enrichments.description:
The original cast of Critical Role had been playing a Pathfinder campaign together for two years before they converted their home game into a livestreamed webseries. The campaign began as a one-off game organized for Liam's birthday. The campaign itself started on December 8, 2012. The very first session was played by Liam O'Brien, Sam Riegel, Laura Bailey, Travis Willingham, Taliesin Jaffe, and Orion Acaba, with Matthew Mercer as the Dungeon Master. Afterwards, the group met every month to month-and-a-half and played for about eight hours. This infrequency was problematic, as many of the players needed to be reminded by Matt of elements of the storyline, how to play, etc. All the players began the campaign with the same characters they had on the stream, with the exception of Taliesin who played a dragonborn paladin for their first session. Marisha Ray and Ashley Johnson joined the game in later sessions.

In 2014, they were approached by Felicia Day to stream their campaign live on the Geek & Sundry twitch channel. When Matt told the other cast members about her offer, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9D5RWAn2sIk the group's reactions were recorded for posterity]. In preparation for the streamed series, Matt converted the game over from Pathfinder to Dungeons & Dragons, to speed up combat and because D&D has more name recognition. When converting their game, Matt had to create a custom fighter's Martial Archetype for Taliesin Jaffe's character, Percy, as the Gunslinger subclass didn't exist in 5th Edition D&D. On March 12, 2015 the first live episode of Critical Role was aired: .

The series initially aired live on the Geek & Sundry [https://www.twitch.tv/geekandsundry Twitch channel] and [https://www.youtube.com/@GeekandSundry YouTube], and subsequently on the Critical Role [http://twitch.tv/criticalrole Twitch channel], on Thursdays at 7pm (Pacific Time). The first campaign and a part of the second campaign were live streamed on the Geek & Sundry Twitch channel. In February 2019, Critical Role parted ways with Geek & Sundry, launched their own [https://www.twitch.tv/criticalrole Twitch] and [https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCpXBGqwsBkpvcYjsJBQ7LEQ/featured YouTube] channels, and started to self-produce new shows and content under the name Critical Role Productions LLC. Eventually the live broadcasts of Critical Role and VODs aired exclusively on Critical Role's channels. Episodes are archived on the [https://critrole.com/ Critical Role website] and the [https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCpXBGqwsBkpvcYjsJBQ7LEQ Critical Role] and [https://www.youtube.com/user/geekandsundry Geek & Sundry] YouTube channels.

On 17 March 2020, Critical Role announced that it was suspending all live broadcasts of both the D&D stream Critical Role and Talks Machina due to the COVID-19 pandemic. During the hiatus, they produced new content, as well as re-imagined versions of existing shows that followed the COVID-19 safety guidelines. Critical Role returned in a prerecorded format on 2 July 2020 with the broadcast of .

enrichments.description:
Kurt is a male given name in Germanic languages. Kurt originated as short forms of the Germanic Konrad/Conrad, depending on geographical usage, with meanings including counselor or advisor. Like Conrad, it can also be a surname and less uncommon variations in Germanic languages including Cord, Curd, Cordt, Curth, Kord, Kort, Kurth, and Kurtu. Curd/Kurd is the decent of the Medes.

In Turkish, Kurt means "wolf" and is a surname and less commonly a given name in numerous Turkic countries. Kurt is also the turkish word for Kurd.

Kurt in Kurdistan meaning your son.

enrichments.description: Mezek (Bulgarian: Мезек) is a village in southeastern Bulgaria, part of Svilengrad municipality, Haskovo Province. It lies at the foot of the eastern Rhodope Mountains, just north of the Bulgaria–Greece border and not far west of the Bulgaria–Turkey border. Mezek is famous for the well-preserved medieval Mezek Fortress (Neoutzikon - Νεούτζικον) and its two ancient Thracian beehive tombs, the Mezek and Sheynovets tombs. The village is also well known for its own winery and the Mezzek brand of Bulgarian wine.

enrichments.description:
Toby is a given name in many English-speaking countries. The name is derived the Middle English vernacular form of Tobias. Tobias itself is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew טוביה Toviah, which translates to Good is Yahweh. Yahweh is the name of the Jewish God.

It is also used as a contraction of Tobin, an Irish surname now also used as a forename.

The name is traditionally masculine, but has also been in use for women since the 19th century.

There are many variations based on the type of waffle iron and recipe used. Waffles are eaten throughout the world, particularly in Belgium, which has over a dozen regional varieties.  Waffles may be made fresh or simply heated after having been commercially baked and packaged fresh or frozen.

Alexander (Greek: Ἀλέξανδρος) is a masculine name of Greek origin. The most prominent bearer of the name is Alexander the Great, the king of the Ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history.

Variants listed here are Aleksandar, Aleksander, Oleksandr, Oleksander, Aleksandr, and Alekzandr. Related names and diminutives include Iskandar, Alec, Alek, Alekos, Alex, Alexsander, Alexandre, Aleks, Aleksa, Aleksandre, Alejandro, Alessandro, Alasdair, Sasha, Sandy, Sandro, Sikandar, Skander, Sander and Xander; feminine forms include Alexandra, Alexandria, and Sasha.

enrichments.description:
Braum is a surname. It is an Americanized form of the German surname Brahm, as well as an Ashkenazi Jewish surname which may have originated as a variant of Braun. The 2010 United States census found 250 people with the surname Braum, making it the 76,768th-most-common name in the country. This represented a decrease from 279 (66,274th-most-common) in the 2000 Census. In both censuses, roughly nine-tenths of the bearers of the surname identified as White.

People and fictional characters with the name include:

Bill Braum, founder of American restaurant chain Braum's

Bohuslav Braum (born 1956), Czech weightlifter

Daniel M. Braum, 1966 recipient of the American Society of Industrial Engineers' Gilbreth Medal

Eduarda Braum (born 2001), Brazilian beauty pageant titleholder

Braum, the Heart of Freljord, League of Legends character voiced by JB Blanc

entities.name: Adelia Pruitt
entities.description:
was a human primal origin sorcerer played by Laura Bailey in Age of Umbra.

Adelia was a very small girl with pale white skin and hair. When the party encountered her, she was wearing a nice but slightly tattered dress. After touching the Scepter of Elias for the first time, one of her arms turned completely black, absorbing the darkness that covered the item.

She was a very imaginative child. Adelia didn't like to kill people, but she'd done it "a couple times" when she was really threatened.

Adelia used to live in Amber Reach with her family, a noble house of the Cinnabar Quarter that had spent generations isolated from the world. At some point in the past few years, her father went off with "a silly elf man", and she believes he's still alive. She didn't see what happened to her mother, aunt, and siblings, but she "didn't think it was going to be nice," so she hid, and was left on her own; the men who killed most of her family offered for her to go with them, but she refused since they were dirty and rude..}} The last she knew of her family was that they were with Yuri of the Emerald Crown, one of the Damask Queens.

entities.name: Alexandra Elise O'Neill
entities.description:
Alexandra Elise O'Neill is a world traveler and smuggler in the one-shot where she was played by Marisha Ray. In , she appeared as the Lightkeeper. As an NPC, she was portrayed by Matthew Mercer.

During the events of Candela Obscura, she was in her mid-fifties, with brown skin and gray-streaked hair pulled up in thick locks falling past her shoulders. Her right eye was clouded white. Her face bore heavy scars streaking downward through her eye and cheek, resembling lightning bolts.

Alexandra described herself as "a bon vivant, bit of an adventurer".

Alexandra has spent much of her recent time in India, helping the Likir monks hold a monster called "the village of the hungry night" at bay. They sent her back to London to retrieve a jade planchette to aid in their task. This led her to accept Rupert Merriweather's job at the Crystal Palace, as the planchette was reported to be there.

entities.name: Aloysius Fogg
entities.description:
is a former slave looking for refuge in Deadwood. He is played by Khary Payton.

Born as a slave, he took the opportunity during the war to escape his shackles. While fleeing, he got cornered and nearly captured again, but a sudden fog let him hide from his pursuers. That is when he decided to change his name to "Fogg". He genuinely believed that this fog was a sentient supernatural being that helped him escape out of good will and believes to recognize the same fog in the cemetery of Deadwood during episode 2. His high reputation precedes him and he gets selected into the group despite arriving to the town only recently.

entities.name: Arabella Whitlock
entities.description:
is an avid fan of the occult who came to Deadwood after her sister's passing. She is played by Marisha Ray.

Arabella has pale, freckled skin and long red hair. The residents of Deadwood are able to ascertain from her appearance that she comes from wealth. She wears a bowler hat with a blue ribbon and flower, a brown dress of heavy fabric, and black leather gloves. Around her neck is a chain holding a tear catcher.

Arabella is well-educated, private, dutiful, and curious about both scientific and magical knowledge, including chemistry, alchemy, and the occult.

She performs her position as the wife of her former brother-in-law with a sense of duty, expressing that she married him for the sake of her family's fortune, despite their mutual lack of interest in each other. She is careful to stick to the accepted modest behavior of married women at the time. While she has become used to the idea that she is "an object for men," she also speaks out against derogatory and patronizing comments she overhears about herself.

entities.name: Arlo Black
entities.description:
is a young woman in Newfaire. She is played by Laura Bailey.

Arlo has dark hair and eyes, and is well-dressed befitting a young woman at the turn of the century. She generally wears one glove, concealing a hand that has cracked gray skin and black nails. Along her forearm are deep scratch marks that look old, but not healed.

Professor Margrove described her as a diligent student, "astute and keen to parse out the details of a person." She grew up in upper class society, with "a certain path set in front of her, but when she was confronted by a devastating paranormal event, she became quite a different person. Because of what happened, she basically lives half in a ghostly realm and half out, often distracted with the activity she sees that others are unaware of".

Arlo lives with her parents in Newfaire. The family is wealthy enough to have servants, including Mr Tellbrook. She was a student of Professor Margrove's, and they have worked together on at least one prior assignment for Candela Obscura.

entities.description:
Asha is a reiloran child living in the Clutch, on Ruidus. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Asha is a good-natured child, more confident than her friend Kelito.

Asha was the child of one of the less privileged families of Kreviris, the reason why they had to live in Caeluma Kreviris, on the surface, and weren't considered important enough to be allowed to take shelter underground during the frequent dust storms.

Bells Hells encountered Asha and Kelito when they arrived in the Clutch, where the children were brushing the ryndons. Both children trusted the Exandrians and had a friendly conversation with them. Chetney Pock O'Pea gave them a wooden rocking horse and explained they had to share it, even promising to return with a new toy if they behaved well. Shortly after that, Asha's parent approached, cautious, and after making sure that their child and her friend were safe, shared more information about the area with the party.

entities.name: Ashton Greymoore
entities.description:
is an earth genasi barbarian and a member of Bells Hells. Ashton is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

Ashton is 5'10" tall and has green stone skin and short, dark-purple crystal hair. They have a prominent hole in the left side of their head filled with slag glass, through which an opalescent brain can be seen, and the eye on the cracked side of Ashton's head is milky white, and it has been implied that it is no longer functional. There are cracks across Ashton's left side, patched together with what looks like slag melted gold (like kintsugi). Their blood is a very deep red, almost black.

Ashton has piercings made mostly of nails, carries multiple leather pouches, and wears a lot of well-worn leather with red fabric lining. Originally, the back of his hand-decorated jacket said "JUST DON'T". He carried a big glass hammer which has "FUCK OFF" engraved in it. On Ashton's pant leg was a patch with a symbol of the Clasp.

During the party's voyage on the Crimson Abyss ghost pirate ship, Ashton got a tattoo on the shoulders and back of a flaming bell and the Primordial words, "From the earth, of the earth, to the earth." After Ashton's plunge into the lava pool within Athos Peak, the gold-filled cracks in their left side appeared to be somewhat healed, although the gold remained.

entities.description:
is a young newsie and street kid recruited into Candela Obscura. He is played by Ashley Johnson.

Auggie is 19 years old, and wears cast-off clothing that doesn't really fit. His hair is mussed and his freckled face is dirty.

Auggie was described as "scrappy". He seems curious and eager to learn, as well as friendly and feisty.

Auggie was an orphan dropped off in infancy at Saint Mannigan's Lodging House for Children. He spent his entire life both there and on the streets, surviving on odd jobs. Charlotte Eaves frequently gave him shelter and odd jobs at her bar The Sight Unseen and felt protective toward him.

entities.name: August
entities.description:
was an underborne faerie wizard played by Taliesin Jaffe in Age of Umbra.

August is an anthropomorphic spider, an arachnid-like faerie of roughly human size, with grey skin, six insectoid eyes, and pincers. He wears fingerless gloves, a too-large old top hat, and a scarf wound around his neck, making his face rather hard to make out, but his mouth is wider than a human's, with small mandibles to either side. His long coat has been repaired many times but remains solid and looks decent (albeit faded); under it he hides two additional sets of arms, E1|03:44|Age of Umbra: Desperloch}} as well as moth wings from a still living moth that is somehow fused to his spine. He carries a rather large sewing needle at his side.

He is very curious, although somewhat sinister.

August and his family lived in the Screaming Forest, but eventually August was taken to the Hive, a buried temple with honey-filled catacombs E4|0:00:14|Age of Umbra: The Rampart and Beyond}} ruled by the Queen Mother. This monstrous entity gave missions to those around her and sometimes changed them if she thought it was interesting, so she attached a living moth to August's back after an incident in which he fell trying to reach an artifact in a cave. E6|7:17|Age of Umbra: The Unforgiving City}} He stayed as part of a team of treasure hunters, and one day, he discovered the statue that became Misty's body. When she had just awakened she needed a name, so August started calling her "Mystery", which eventually evolved into her current name. At some point, they both fled, displeasing the Queen Mother, and ended up in Desperloch a few months before .

entities.name: Ayden
entities.description:
Ayden is a 15-year-old human male with brown eyes and hair. When first seen, he was carrying a damaged shield on his back that didn't look like it belonged to him, and holding a staff carved with etchings of the moon and stars at its top.

During his last minutes as a mortal avatar, as he was in a battle that was unlocking more and more of his divinity, he rapidly aged to reach adulthood, and his head started glowing as he used his powers (before the glow came from his heart), although maintaining his face visible.

He is very calm, and sees mortals as children deserving of his compassion. He is also innocent and idealistic, and seeks solutions that prevent the suffering of others.

After the main Exandrian pantheon agreed to collaborate in a plan to neutralize Aeor and their potentially dangerous technology, the Dawnfather agreed to do his part (being one of the last ones to agree), and a decade and a half before their intended mission, he was born as a mortal human boy, Ayden.

entities.name: Azune Nayar
entities.description:
(pronounced Ah-ZOO-nay or AH-zoo-nay) Mar 2026|1:12:40}} is a paladin/sorcerer played by Luis Carazo in Campaign Four.

Azune is human in appearance. at moments they visibly glow, like a sun setting behind an ocean, and when he channels his sorcery they become even more like the scene they resemble (like an actual sun setting into water). He is just over 5'10" tall but projects the image of being taller by his proud bearing. His body is strong, lean, and muscular, with medium brown skin and auburn hair tied back in a braid. His hair can go past his mid back when out of the braid. He has a birthmark on the left side of his neck and face. He looks like his parents, although they had dark hair and more tanned skin.

His arm has a tattoo reading, "Have mercy on those I send you".

Azune stands tall and proud. He has an emotional side, especially when remembering old friends and witnessing significant moments. He values memories and past events a lot, and struggles differentiating between letting go and forgetting, preferring to suffer if that suffering honors a specific memory.

entities.name: Beatrix Monroe
entities.description:
is an older woman in Newfaire. She is played by Marisha Ray.

Bee is 55 years old, with straggly, frizzy salt-and-pepper hair and threadbare and worn patchwork clothing probably repurposed from a quilt she once had. Her hat is decorated with sun-faded silk flowers. Bee "cares little" about her physical appearance, but paradoxically tries to hide her windburn and sun spots with way too much blush, trying to hold onto a bit of youth. She wears a few pieces of nice jewelry that seem to have nostalgic sentimental value.

Beatrix was happily married to a sailor named Blue, and lived in a small cottage in Seasway. However, because she could not have a child of her own despite her seemingly longing for one, she formed a friendship with Margaret Mary Finnerty ("Peggy") and her three sons, building a strong bond and connection with them to the point that Peggy's children felt like her boys, though she admitted in her later years that it was perhaps a bit unhealthy for her to do so. When Sean was still young, shortly after the death of his father, she and Peggy took Sean and his brother Anthony to a ballgame, with Jimmy having to stay home as he had unfortunately fallen sick. Despite Peggy saving up for months to take her boys to the game she and Bee still had borrow some cash from the neighbors to afford the tickets. Years later Beatrix still remembered the flashes of rainbow colors on the boys faces as they stared in awe at the fireworks that were launched after a homerun, and how Sean, who had a little bit of allowance that he saved up and being a sweetheart, chose to buy a baseball cap for his sick brother Jimmy.

On the 12th day of Mid-Summer 1898, Beatrix was woken up in the middle of the night from a nightmare of men and women screaming as the merchant ship they were on sank, along with seeing her husband's final moments, that put her in an off mood all day. During the day she sat on the stoop of her cottage and saw Halen Naval Ships forming blockades very close to and around the areas of the Vastchasm that one would take to enter the harbor, so close that at least one ship almost fell in. She then saw a letter delivered to her mailbox, and despite trying to play off the nightmare she had had the previous night as just a figment of her imagination, she already knew what the contents on the letter were. After spending possibly an hour just sitting on the stoop of her cottage, she finally built up the courage to check the mail, only to collapse to the ground as she read the letter on her way back to her house. It confirmed her husband's ship, the HMS Brilliance, had been attacked and sunk by a Otherwhere vessel, and that he had perished in the event that would start the Last Great War.

entities.name: Benicio Lorelei
entities.description:
is a human blood hunter and a member of the Lorelei family. He was played by Sam Riegel in .

In his human form Benicio looks like a man of dark skin (although lighter than those of his two oldest siblings) with a soft purple hue (sign of his drow ancestry), dark eyes and short black hair with a streak of white. He has several scars on his face, with one going through his left eyebrow, and more scars and burns on his torso and arms. He wears green clothes, with vine patterns on some of his garments. Benicio has features in common with his brother Lawrence, but they are not identical twins: beyond the style and personal aesthetics of each one, the younger twin has a less pronounced jaw, and has scars that the older twin lacks; furthermore, they both have distinct white hair patterns.

In his werewolf form, Benicio is mostly covered in white fur on the right half of his body and black on the left. His arms get bigger, stronger and ropier, but they are mostly scar tissue and skin, lacking large areas of fur due to prior burning.

Benicio had an itch for danger from an early age. He jokes and plays pranks on his siblings.

entities.name: Bentley Badger
entities.description:
Captain Bentley Badger is a former British cavalry soldier now employed as Rupert Merriweather's butler in the one-shot. He was played by Travis Willingham.

Bentley is overall a grounded and steadfast individual. He shows loyalty to Merriweather, and determination in finding the casket. Despite his insistence that ghosts do not exist, he is obviously anxious discussing it. When Alexandra points out that a non-believer should have nothing to fear, he agrees, but is clearly still nervous. He also displays an obvious discomfort around cats.

Bentley was once in the British cavalry, but now works as a butler. He says that he owes Merriweather a great deal.

Bentley keeps his knowledge of Merriweather blackmailing Hanako over the theft of a necklace discrete, which she expresses appreciation for. There is a degree of sexual tension between them and after the events of the night she expessed interest in seeing him when there weren't supernatural threats around.

entities.name: Bertrand Bell
entities.description:
Sir is a human fighter. First introduced in , he was instrumental in bringing together the adventuring party known as Bells Hells, who named their party after him. Bertrand is played by Travis Willingham.

When he first appeared in , Sir Bertrand Bell was in his late 50s or early 60s. He has been described as a "devilish silver fox son of a bitch." He wore beautiful orange, maroon, and purple robes of the finest make, with a beautiful rapier on his hip. He had tan skin and piercing blue eyes.

In , Bertrand is older and has a receding hairline and a pony tail. He still favors purple and burnt-orange finery, with a coiffed collar. He still carries a beautiful rapier on his hip, but now also carries an elegant walking stick. He wears a lapel pin with the crest of Vox Machina.

Bertrand is characterized by his bombastic attitude that often leads him into trouble. He tends to exaggerate his accomplishments and believes that he is more renowned and important than he actually is. Percival de Rolo considered him to be "the most pompous, egotistical arsehole" he's ever met, and Ariks Eshteross considered his house "stained" by Bertrand's "empty bravado".

entities.name: Bobby Socks
entities.description:
Bobby Socks is a teenaged halfling druid and a member of the Glorious Ones, a small group of adventurers. He was played by Taliesin Jaffe in .

Bobby is something of a late bloomer, even for a halfling, appearing younger than his actual age. He has messy brown hair and was wearing brown boots and gloves with green short pants and a shirt covered by a small leather tunic. He wore a little backpack and carried a belt pack of cards.

Bobby was bubbly and excited by everything happening around him, and the polar opposite of "cool". Despite his father Kent Plucker being obviously disinterested and slightly disparaging of him, he persisted in seeing their relationship in the best way possible and imagining it to be closer than it apparently was.

Bobby is the child of Kent Plucker, a bard and member of Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe. He apparently spends most of his time with his mother, visiting his disinterested father on rare occasions.

entities.name: Bolaire Lathalia
entities.description:
is a warlock played by Taliesin Jaffe in Campaign Four.

When first introduced, Bolaire appeared as a dashing man who wears a mask of gray clay with dark gray lips that moves like a face to show his expression, and where his eyes should be are black pools with tiny blue reflected lights like a cat's eyes in the dark. He has very long, curling, dark red hair. His clothes, which cover every inch of his body, are finely made of black leather and suede over crimson, and he often wears a cloak to keep a low profile.

It was revealed in that Bolaire himself is a sentient mask that can take over the body of whomever wears the mask and does so every few months when his current form decays too much. In the darkness behind his clay lips there is an actual mouth that he uses to consume food and water in order to keep a body alive. On the other side of the mask the material seems slightly opalescent, and there is faint cursive writing under the eyes that can't be properly read unless one's face is close to the item itself. If someone spends long enough focusing on it, they hear the distant noise of an applause so thundering it feels as if the world was cracking from its core.

Taliesin describes Bolaire as "very social and bitchy". Although not a noble himself, Bolaire is comfortable in their company. He prefers to see things for himself rather than relying on the accounts of others. Almost all of his emotions are deliberate, based on what he thinks will be appropriate in each situation, with fear being the only "new" emotion he has acquired.

entities.name: Braius Doomseed
entities.description:
is a minotaur paladin/bard and a member of Bells Hells. He is played by Sam Riegel.

Braius is a "hot" minotaur. He is a muscular 6 feet 4 inches tall (without the horns), with black fur on his body and pale grey peach fuzz on his face. He has long black hair, a humanoid-appearing face (which becomes more bovine when he gets angry or excited), and two sharp horns. His hands are somewhat hooflike, with three fingers. He has a tail that he uses to scare away bugs. When Bells Hells encountered him within the ruins of Aeor, he wielded a flail with twin balls dripping a black liquid and wore white armor with the horned icon of Asmodeus emblazoned on its chestpiece. One side of his armor also bears the signature of Teven Klask.

After Highbearer Vord spoke with him and decided to let him represent the followers of the Platinum Dragon in the mission against the Ruby Vanguard, Braius removed his original armor to don Truthbearer, a holy relic made of silvered platinum, and he was given a black cape with silver edges to maintain his white, black, and gray aesthetic.

Months after his adventures with Bells Hells he was experimenting with adding some color to his general aesthetic.

entities.name: Bramble
entities.description:
Bramble was a fairy barbarian and a member of the Glorious Ones, a small group of adventurers. She was played by Laura Bailey in .

Bramble is a small but muscular fairy woman with light green skin adorned with darker spots in her arms and cheeks (as well as some scars), a mane of yellow-orange hair (which turns fiery red when she rages), and four insect-like green wings (which glow when she rages). Her appearance is somewhat dirty, and her attire consists of a combination of thorns, sticks, dry leaves, dead flowers, and animal hair.

Bramble is intense, determined and daring.

At some point before 795 PD Bramble met Ranthiel Volthor, a warlock with whom she became intimately involved, but who did not seem as interested in having a relationship as she was.

entities.name: Brixton
entities.description:
is an orderborne orc guardian played by Marisha Ray in Age of Umbra.

Brixton is a mature large and hardy orc woman who wears the robes associated with her role as a Pyrekeeper, but also has some old-fashioned armor that doesn't entirely fit her body. Her hair is long, black, and matted, and her hands are calloused and blackened from her work.

Although she can be solemn and calm if the situation requires it, Brixton is actually adventurous, and has a wanderlust born from her very monotonous job with the Sacred Pyre.

Brixton was an orphan in Desperloch, chosen by the Emberwarden to join the Pyrekeepers because she saw Brixton had the potential to one day gain that position. For 15 years, Brixton tended to the Sacred Pyre, staring at the flames and slowly growing tired of it. Because of that, she befriended some of the local delvers, who helped her visit the vaults in secret so that she could spend some time out of their settlement. In her last visit to the vaults, Brixton (allegedly guided by a sign from the Pyre) found an armored skeleton with glowing eyes, and she stole its ancient gear.

entities.name: Buddy
entities.description:
is an ogre fighter and a member of the Darrington Brigade. He is played by Liam O'Brien.

Buddy is a large ogre standing at 9 feet tall, though he is usually hunched over and moves very slowly. Before joining the Brigade officially Buddy had terrible eyesight and always squinted to see, but after receiving special goggles his eyes seemed cartoonishly large. He wears a hulking metal breastplate and on his back sits Taryon's prototype electrically-charged chariot-turned comfortable seating where Macaroni usually sits. Before this Macaroni sat on a plank of wood tied to Buddy's back and shoulders.

Buddy is slow, lumbering and not very intelligent but clearly has a gentler side - upon receiving the goggles that allowed him to see for the first time, Buddy continuously pointed out how 'pretty' everything and everyone was. He also seemed more interested in making friends than fighting during the Brigade's initiation.

While the specifics are unknown, Buddy and Macaroni Samsonite met and became friends before joining the Darrington Brigade.

Bunnie is a faun bard and a member of the Menagerie, a small group of adventurers. She is played by Marisha Ray.

Bunnie is a beautiful and curvy faun with dusty rose fur, short antlers and long rabbit-like ears. She dresses mostly in leather.

Bunnie is confident and flirtatious, and her behavior is passionate and slightly performative most of the time. However, there are moments in which she stays silent, just enjoying quiet and peaceful moments.

Bunnie used to perform in the Lilly Locket Lounge. Eventually, she teamed up with the Menagerie and became an adventurer. At one point, she and Sir Danté Terrapin dealt with a strange phenomenon (a red mist) that affected people, and she saved him when that weird fog was drowning him.

entities.description:
is a firbolg cleric of the Wildmother and a member of the Mighty Nein. He is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

Caduceus is a roughly seven-foot-tall,.}} "not necessarily healthily thin" firbolg with pale skin and grey fur. He has a shock of pink mohawk hair paired with a light fuzz of a beard. He wears a gentle silk shirt with one long flowy sleeve, dark green pants, and brown boots spotted with pink lichen.

During the battle with Cree in the tunnels beneath Cognouza, Caduceus acquired a red eye in the center of his clavicle. He received another on his abdomen while trying and failing to create a passageway to follow the Somnovem, and a third on his left shoulder during the battle with Lucien, the Neo-Somnovem. All of these eyes disappeared following Lucien's defeat.

In 843 PD his pink hair was longer, and for his mission with the Mighty Nein he used a new armor that looked like a beetle.

entities.description:
Cameron Solomon is an infernal. He is played by Ashley Johnson.

Cameron is described as extremely handsome and hot.

Cameron has recently become more quiet and reserved.

Cameron is the all-star quarterback for the Cinderbrush football team and used to be a straight A student, until an incident that happened last summer that forever changed him. This combined with his recent breakup with Sasha Murasaki has sent him into a slump and caused him to let his grades slip and distance himself from the team.

entities.name: Cerrit Agrupnin
entities.description:
is an eisfuura rogue serving as Senior Sightwarden of the Eyes of Avalir. He is played by Travis Willingham.

Cerrit is a 6'6" eisfuura with proud, strong shoulders. He has very white feathers with brown tips, a dark beak, and gray-blue eyes. He wears a hooded cloak and wraps around his wrists and ankles. He has a tomahawk sheathed under each armpit.

Cerrit "has made a name for himself seeing the details that others may miss when foul play is afoot. Cerrit has a very strong sense of morality, and loses himself in his work – so much so that it puts a strain on his home life and personal relationships. He feels a strong sense of duty and responsibility to Avalir, and to do what he can to be a check against the allure of power that so frequently pulls even the most well-intended practitioners of the arcane."

Cerrit is intensely private, probably due to the nature of his work as Senior Sightwarden. When he arrived at Patia's party, he circled the gathering via flight several times before landing to scout the attendees. When he landed, he put up his hood and stood back, continuing to observe silently. When he entered after all the others of the Ring of Brass had arrived, he both bribed and threatened the Herald announcing arrivals to keep Cerrit's name to himself.

entities.name: Charlotte Eaves
entities.description:
is the proprietor of the Sight Unseen Bar and Club in Red Lamp, Newfaire, and a longtime member of Candela Obscura. She is played by Anjali Bhimani.

Charlotte Eaves is an adult woman with long reddish-brown hair. Her attire and appearance are very put together and lends itself to a professional/business attire look of the period and is accented by splashs of scarlet red clothing. Following a week of constantly going to and from her mentor Gertrudes's Library, as she was staying with her following the events of Assignment #442: Ravage of Red Lamp, and pouring over texts and writing out notes; her appearance has become slightly less put together, and the stress has turned a few strands of her hair grey.

Charlotte has "a particular personality that can smooth over certain transgressions" for those looking to use the Sight Unseen as an alibi.

Charlotte grew up poor, but she aspired to more and resented her family for being satisfied with their lot. One day, when she was about the age that Auggie James is now (in her teens or early twenties), she was crossing a field when she saw a crack in the sky above the house in which her family lived. She felt sucked toward it but managed to hold on to a tree. The house, however, was pulled crumbling into the crack, which then disappeared with her family inside. Charlotte made her way to Gertrude, a woman who was her friend and mentor, told her that her family had abandoned her, and Gertrude took her in.

entities.name: Chetney Pock O'Pea
entities.description:
() is a gnomish blood hunter/rogue and member of Bells Hells. He is played by Travis Willingham.

Chetney is an elderly gnome who appears to be "a hundred-and-something" years old, with blue eyes, several scars, and a hooked nose that he says has been broken more than once. He stands about 3 foot 4 inches and has well-muscled arms. On his right arm is a tattoo of a crown and the letters "RTA", which stand for "Rexxentrum Toy Authority" (a mark required by his former union), though he tells people it stands for "Recognize The Alpha". Tufts of silvery-grey hair sprout from and over his ears from under a knitted cap with ear straps pulled down tight on his head; he is partially bald, and the remaining hair has gone completely silver as well. He originally wore a leather chest harness, pointy-toed boots, and woodworking tools around his waist. While aboard the Crimson Abyss, he acquired a flaming bell tattoo on his butt cheek. Just before the group traveled to Eiselcross, he bought a new leather fur-lined suit with some chainmail accents and a shoulder pauldron crafted from a piece of FCG's body, fingerless gloves, and a blue bandana embroidered "RTA", had his toolbelt turned into a bandolier, and hung the Harp of Valor from a leather strap at his waist.

In his werewolf form, Chetney becomes taller, and silvery-grey hair grows from his entire body. The transformation takes place quickly and results in his bones breaking and realigning and claws ripping through his existing fingernails. His voice is much deeper and gruffer as a werewolf.

According to Travis Willingham, in his youth Chetney was an attractive, tanned man, though with less muscular legs than his upper body. He had (more abundant) auburn hair, including groomed chest hair and a mustache.

→ Not to be confused with the Campaign Three gnome Chetney Pock O'Pea.

is a Christmas elf Rogue played by Travis Willingham for .

Chutney started off seeming like a loyal elf to Santa, but as soon as Saint Nick got kidnapped by the Hallow King, he changed his tune, putting forth the idea of leaving Santa to die and taking over the North Pole. He was quite frustrated by the tasks Santa was giving him, complaining about nobody wanting a wooden Voltron, that he can't wire a Gameboy, and how the hair didn't move on a troll doll he made.

Chutney is one of the oldest elves working for Saint Nick. His expertise is in wooden toys, but times (and children) have changed and he has been under pressure to produce less traditional playthings. For a long time, he tolerated this burden but was secretly nursing a growing grudge against Santa.

entities.description:
is a gun-for-hire residing in Deadwood. He is played by Matthew Mercer.

Clayton wears a black & blue two piece suit over a white shirt with a blue tie. He has medium length dark brown hair sitting beneath his signature ten gallon hat, which he is prone to tipping often in social exchanges. His face is grizzled, complete with shortly kept muttonchops and sharp eyebrows which are furrowed most of the time.

Clayton is described to be a reserved and stoic individual. He tends to keep a level-headed but cautious outlook in most situations. He can often be found keeping one hand on the holster of his Colt in any precarious situation. Clayton likes to keep to himself and doesn't trust in others easily, if at all.

More than anything Clayton does not appreciate being the center of attention. He prefers anonymity and speaking only when necessary. This is perhaps due to a hinted past where he had some former notoriety he is trying to get away from. Upon learning that Al Swearengen was keeping tabs on him, Clayton attempted to pay one of his men for information on anyone else also trying to watch or learn about himself. He was unwilling to share the details of his employment with men at the Bella Union as well when it came to acquiring firearms.

Honey Bear: As a honey bear cookie has advantage on his bear rolls to sniff out the golden delisiousness that is honey.

entities.name: Cordelia Glask
entities.description:
is the owner of the Glass Cat Casino, whose flawless exterior hides her inner turmoil. She is played by Gina Darling.

When Cordelia was first seen, she was smoking a cigarette, was adorned in jewels and furs, and was wearing expensive imported perfume. She wears glasses and is 5'7".

Cordelia's impeccable clothing and grooming in an attempt to emulate the upper classes is slightly fraying, and somewhat overcompensation.

Cordelia was born and raised in the KeGa Islands, worshipping Katma, the sea god of her people. When Cordelia was about 12 or 13 years old, she entered into a bargain with other gods of the sea while standing on the shore shouting with rage because her family was lost at sea in a shipwreck and only Cordelia survived, alone in a new world. Something responded, offering her a desire, saying that the price had been paid: a mother claimed by dark water. The family had hoped for safe passage and riches and wealth in their new world, and since she could not have her family back, she took what they had desired. The bargain ended up trading any sense of home and family in return for riches and ownership of the Glass Cat. She still believes the gods of the sea are fair, although she didn't realize the wish came with a continuing price.

entities.name: Cosmo Grimm
entities.description:
is an elderly bookshop owner in Newfaire. He is played by Liam O'Brien.

Cosmo is 97 years old, thin, and wiry. When first seen, he was wearing a tweed jacket and bowtie that were both too large for him. He gets about using a brass wheelchair equipped with a supplemental electrical power source.

Cosmo still enjoys field work, the thrill of the hunt, his own personal studies, and running his shop.

Eighty-seven years prior to the events of the Circle of Tide and Bone, Cosmo was traveling aboard a ship with his father Oscar, mother Cora, uncle Quentin, and sister Iris, when a ritual performed by The Serious Man split the ship in two. As Oscar tumbled into its center he pushed Cosmo back and away, although the rest of the family was lost. Oscar was left with a strange immortality that costs him part of his memories and personality each time his life is restored and the two have spent the intervening years attempting to find a cure without success.

Countess Pi is rather magical and kind. She has many special talents related to numbers and circles.

is a Christmas elf cleric played by Marisha Ray for .

Cranberry Stockings has a full beard with a mustache. Both her hair and beard are dual-colored. The divide between red and green runs exactly in the middle parting of her hair.

Cranberry Stockings likes to keep it traditional, but prefers to keep her own flair on it, with a little bit of half and half (in reference to her beard). She has an Upper Midwestern accent.

entities.name: Crokas
entities.description:
is a white dragonborn monk played by Alexander Ward in Exandria Unlimited: Divergence.

Just before his release from the prison fortress of Rybad-Kol, Crokas had only recently reached adulthood. He was six-and-a-half feet tall, 300 pounds, and muscular. His rough, jagged white scales were covered in scars (both old and new) and marked by a dark vitiligo of dark scales that extended to his throat and neck where he had a small growth. He wore tattered clothing. He had a tail, and moved like a monitor lizard when on all fours.

After he attuned to Stormgirdle, strength seemed to pour out from him.

Crokas has a simple, discreet demeanor, and a certain innocence that could be based on his isolated youth. Although he seems easily confused, he has a good heart and is protective of those who are his allies.

entities.name: Damian Vadoma
entities.description:
is a half-elven fighter and a member of the Darrington Brigade. She is played by Ashley Johnson.

Damian is a tall half-elf with flaming orange hair. She wears a fancy maroon suit with a small harness holding two knuckle-dusters/stilettos under her arms. A golden compass on a chain is in place of a typical watch. Damian has the Latin words for Life (Vita) and Death (Mors) just above her knuckles, and the words 'Never Forget' tattooed on her neck.

Damian comes from the Vadoma family, a group seemingly involved in underground crime or seedier operations. She auditioned for membership in the Darrington Brigade to try her hand at "more moral" jobs.

In 826 PD, Taryon Darrington welcomed Damian at his estate in Deastok, inviting her to contest for the position in the Darrington Brigade. Damian went last, paired with Macaroni Samsonite. Macaroni pummeled her, and then Banished her, ending their fight with a win for him.

entities.name: Danté Terrapin
entities.description:
Sir Danté Terrapin is a galapa warrior and a member of the Menagerie, a small group of adventurers. He is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

Danté is a galapa of turquoise skin with a scar in his face, dressed in elegant clothes, and carrying fancy weapons, and a hat with a beautiful feather.

Sir Danté is a posh individual that values reputation a lot. Some of his behavior seems rehearsed, particularly when he laughs.

In the past, a man humilliated Danté terribly. Eventually, the galapa teamed up with the Menagerie and became an adventurer. At one point, he and Bunnie dealt with a strange phenomenon (a red mist) that affected people, and she saved him when that weird fog was drowning him. He got to meet Dyson Broche once.

entities.name: Dariax Zaveon
entities.description:
Dariax Zaveon is a dwarven sorcerer and member of the Crown Keepers. He is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dariax is a young mountain dwarf with wild, floppy, reddish-auburn hair and a chinstrap beard. He wears a vest over a chain shirt, and has a compass rose chained on his light chain necklace.

After touching the thorny circlet and failing his wisdom saving throw, Dariax's eyes turned inky black. They were restored to their normal "dreamy" brown color by Shaun Gilmore a few days later. for the original color.}}

Dariax is easygoing, reacting cheerfully to being pranked by his friends. However, he becomes intense when he realises he’s being lied to, as he has had bad experiences with people who lie a lot. He is impulsive and prone to throwing himself unthinkingly into dangerous situations.

entities.name: Deanna Leimert
entities.description:
() is a gnome cleric of Pelor. She is played by Aabria Iyengar.

Deanna stands about 3 feet tall, and has dark skin and chubby cheeks. When encountered by half of Bells Hells, she was wearing golden heavy plate, a massive symbol of the Dawnfather around her waist, a chunky knit pale pink sweater-shawl around her shoulders, and leather boots.

Aabria described her as "built like a Pixar mom", with a tiny upper body and a "dump truck" ass.

Although a generally happy person who tries to steer conversations away from "heavy" topics, Deanna seems filled with longing for the peace she found in death and was torn away from by her resurrection. She keeps being drawn back to Uthodurn because it feels like her home.

entities.name: Derrig
entities.description:
was a half-elf fighter and the Master of Defense of Zephrah. He was played by Liam O'Brien.

Derrig is older in age than those in Vox Machina, though due to his half-elf heritage, he appears younger. He has two old scars next to his mouth running up his cheeks. He is grizzled looking and 'tired around the eyes'. Derrig has a tattoo sleeve of clouds with a sun shining through all over one arm (the sun is positioned on the shoulder). He carries a gladius style sword, and a shield on his back, with leather straps coming across his chest to hold them in place. At the wedding he wore a fine linen shirt covering the arm without the tattoos.

Derrig is very loyal to Keyleth, whom he consistently refers to as "The Voice of the Tempest", and is very respectful to all of Vox Machina and views them with awe. He sees himself as not diplomatic in social encounters, and views Keyleth as the expert in that area. He wins over the other party members in the lead-up to the rehearsal dinner: Grog admires his very sharp weapon and his fighting skills, Scanlan basks in his obvious admiration of Scanlan's singing and excitement at the prospect of hearing him sing at the wedding, and after Pike grills him about his relationship with Keyleth (and discovers he has been happily married for 47 years), she accepts him as Keyleth's protector.

He was a good man who loved his family and was willing to admit his mistakes, although he wasn't always willing to share his own feelings.

entities.name: Dorian Storm
entities.description:
Dorian Storm, born Brontë Secondsun Wyvernwind, is an air genasi bard who appeared in Exandria Unlimited Prime, Campaign Three of Critical Role, and Exandria Unlimited: Kymal. He is a member of the Crown Keepers and Bells Hells. He is played by Robbie Daymond.

Dorian has sky-blue skin, crystal-blue eyes, and jet-black hair that falls in an ombre finishing in white and sky-blue just past his shoulders. He is 6'1" and more lightweight than he appears. He is very attractive and looks a lot like his father. Most of his clothes and his lute are sunburst blue, but the inside of his cape is colored the oranges and reds of a sunset. On his chest is a metallic plate in the shape of wings, and it was unclear whether it was purely ornamental or armor. As an air genasi, he moves with a lightness that could be mistaken for confidence.

For his return to Marquet, Dorian was uncharacteristically clean, spotless and shined. He kept the same outfit for months while he adventured with Bells Hells and then with the Crown Keepers, but after returning to Marquet he updated it and made it more lithe, turning his cape into a half-cape, getting swashbuckler pants, and getting a "slutty" poofy shirt made of finely woven mithral, so it acted as sheer armor. The silver ornaments he wore were now gold (befitting his new position after his brother's death as the heir) and included a nose piercing. His mandolin was painted blue with a sunburst on its front and was marked on the back with Fresh Cut Grass's blades of grass symbol. His hair was also slightly modified, up in a bun with more bluish tips rather than gray.

Dorian was well spoken and charismatic. He came from a very secluded place, and liked to see different kinds of people living together. He desperately wanted to prove himself. Dorian left home to look for a better life, but he often dodged questions about his past, seemingly uncomfortable when talking about it. When Poska said Dorian seemed to come from money, Dorian nervously brushed it off and claimed to just be a humble bard..}} He was aware that he wasn't very good at lying, and in time he would stop doing so, deciding to ignore certain feelings instead.

entities.name: Edgar Lycoris
entities.description:
is "a skilled if stern surgeon whose operating techniques were honed in the halls of the Grand Halen Hospital." He is played by Alexander Ward.

Edgar's appearance is unexceptional in every way, and he tends therefore to blend into a crowd. He has small, round glasses and his clothes appear to have been selected by someone else. He appears not to have slept well. He has a large scar on his body, which he keeps hidden under his clothing..}}

Edgar's purpose in life has always been to help people, and he sometimes has a difficult time reconciling that with the actions he must take (or fails to take) as a Candela operative.

Eighteen years ago in 1889, Edgar watched his sister Elizabeth "blow away like dust" in Regent Park, apparently struck by the same kind of force as the Circle later encountered in the battle in the Cemetery from a weapon manufactured by Malcolm Trills' family. She attempted to hold onto Edgar as this happened, leaving burn scars in the shape of her hands on his arm and neck. The War began five years later, in 1894.

Edna is a character played by Marisha Ray in the alternate universe of Vox Moronica's campaign in .

Edna is inspired by (but canonically distinct from) the "old lady" NPC that travelled with the Broker in and was killed by Tiberius Stormwind.

Edna would go on to travel with The Broker and encounter the adventure group Vox Machina, where she would meet her death at the hands of Tiberius Stormwind.

entities.name: Elsie Roberts
entities.description:
is a skilled doctor fraying at the edges, whose mysterious condition remains a source of intrigue for her fellow investigators. She is played by Ashly Burch.

When first seen, Elsie was a bit disheveled and wearing slightly shabby clothing from several seasons ago, although she was clearly trying to emulate the styles of the more upper classes.

Elsie contracted cullet, a degenerative lung disease that causes a sensation of broken glass in the lungs, while she was attempting to treat clients of it in the Eaves. Dying of the disease, she began experimenting to find ways to keep the pain at bay, but became increasingly desperate as the pain worsened, eventually experimenting with magick and corrupting herself into a strange beast resembling a werewolf, which she begins to transform into whenever she is overwhelmed or stressed.

At one time, she and Rajan Savarimuthu were in a romantic relationship, although she remained unaware of the hive of insects that now inhabit his body.

entities.name: Emhira
entities.description:
is a human warlock played by Laura Bailey in Downfall. She is a mortal avatar of the Raven Queen.

Emhira has long, rich brown hair and when first seen, was wearing soft green and cream robes and sensible leathers. She has a raven familiar named "Dearest" accompanying her. Her features were completely different from those the Matron of Ravens had in her first mortal life.

She is slightly cynical and pragmatic when it comes to human behavior related to death or knowledge.

After the main Exandrian pantheon agreed to collaborate in a plan to neutralize Aeor and their potentially dangerous technology, the Raven Queen agreed to do her part, and less than three decades before their intended mission she was born as a mortal human girl, Emhira, with whom she had made a pact to empower her even before her birth. Her champion, Purvan Suul, soon came to her home, and after explaining to her parents he had had a vision indicating he had to protect her, he stayed for many years as her guardian as she grew up under his watchful eye. Eventually, and with his guidance, she manifested her magical powers as a warlock, and became fully aware of her purpose as the mortal incarnation of the goddess of death. Before going to Aeor she searched for the place where the mortal woman who became the Raven Queen kept some of her material possessions, to properly equip herself.

entities.name: Erro Mordaurum
entities.description:
was a gold dragonborn ranger played by Liam O'Brien in Exandria Unlimited: Divergence. He was a mortal incarnation of the Platinum Dragon.

Erro was an aged dragonborn with a long-healed scar across his throat. His eyes had a far-off look, and the flesh around them was sunken and sallow. During his time as a prisoner at Rybad-Kol, Erro was dressed in filthy traveling clothes and a shredded cloak, and coated in so much dust from his months traveling across the wastes that one almost couldn't tell his scales were gold.

In the caravan readying the dragonborn of the prison to be sent to their deaths, Erro advised those panicking around him to calm down and conserve their energy for any potential opportunity to escape.

He had a tendency to keep an eye on the horizon, looking out for any threats.

entities.name: F.R.I.D.A.
entities.description:
(Far-Ranging Integrated Defense Aeormaton) is an Aeormaton fighter/rogue/cleric and a werewolf. F.R.I.D.A. is played by Christian Navarro.

F.R.I.D.A. is a slender emerald green, rose gold-framed Aeormaton with a feminine face and 6-foot tall muscular frame. There is guilloché machined patterning under the enamel on their cladding. When encountered by Bells Hells, they were wearing a very elegant, beautifully designed emerald green trench coat, with the collar up, framing their neck; the coat had Deanna's name embroidered, and more recently, FCG's as well. Their right hand was peeled backward revealing a blunderbuss gun hidden inside their arm. Their right arm was bare, and when FRIDA casts healing magic, an etching of the Dawnfather's symbol lights up.

Their faceplate can be removed by pressing a button on each side of the temple. On the inside, inscribed along the jawline, their full name is written.

F.R.I.D.A. is a dutiful individual that, after discovering that they were intended to protect, focused in that task by keeping their best friend Deanna safe, making her their priority, even if they are also loyal, affectionate and protective around other friends. In a similar way, they are patient and understanding when talking with others, although defending their own posture, like their opinion about the gods. The gunslinger is fascinated by their past in Aeor, having a great desire of learning more and understanding themselves better; because of that, after meeting Fresh Cut Grass F.R.I.D.A. was elated, and the positive feelings towards the other Aeormaton soon developed into a crush.

entities.name: Farah Vallari
entities.description:
Farah Vallari is an old half-elven blood hunter and a member of The Re-Slayer's Take. She is played by Jasmine Chiong.

Farah is a mature and tall half-elven woman, with silver hair, tanned skin, and a general look that identifies her as an old adventurer. She wears leather armor and glasses.

She is tough and grouchy, somewhat sullen and grumpy, and presents a confident and tough attitude towards strangers, although she is willing to share advice with a person she trusts. However, deep down she has some insecurity about her own abilities, as well as her age.

She is private and doesn't share personal information voluntarily; however, she is not secretive, and if someone asks about something, she is willing to talk.

entities.name: Farriwen Breeze
entities.description:
is an air genasi monk and a member of the Darrington Brigade. She is played by Laura Bailey.

Farriwen is a female air genasi with very pale, almost alabaster skin that gives off a faint glow from underneath. She has pale pink hair tied into a loose braid that seems to move around as if there's a constant breeze. She wears a sleeveless grey robe that fades into flames near the bottom. Most noticeably, Farriwen's arms are adorned with glowing glyphs - her left arm with symbols of clouds, and her right with symbols of flames that snake up her arm. She clarified to Taryon Darrington that these weren't tattoos, but engravings.

Farriwen mentioned to Taryon that she was from the Monastery of the Eternal Balance on an island in the Lucidian Ocean, and left to train alongside the famed adventurer.

In 826 PD, Taryon Darrington welcomed Farriwen at his estate in Deastok inviting her to contest for the position in the Darrington Brigade. Farriwen went first against The Owlbear. She uses her "dope monk shit" to knock out the Owlbear handily. Tary thought her chances looked good.

entities.name: Fearne Calloway
entities.description:
Lady Fearne Calloway () is a faun druid/rogue and member of the Crown Keepers and later Bells Hells. She is played by Ashley Johnson.

Fearne is a faun. She is a little over six feet tall when measuring from her horns, with white spotted fur, spiraling horns and ample breasts. She has large deep-green eyes (very similar to her mother's), large furry ears, and sea-foam green hair. Her hooves have bits of moss around them. She wears flowy clothing and is covered in poisonous flowers including hemlock and oleander. She has a tail which wiggles when she feels she's being "naughty", although since it's hidden under her clothing it's usually not visible.

During her travels with the Crown Keepers, as she got nearer to the gate to the Feywild her appearance changed. One of her eyes changed from a humanoid to a goat-like pupil, and the flowers she wore began to turn and open. After holding the Circlet of Barbed Vision, one hand blackened and became claw-like. When she visited the Fey Realm with Bells Hells, her appearance similarly modified, with her features becoming more elongated and exaggerated.

When Fearne entered into a pact with Teven Klask, the Retribution of the Hells, the slightly flaming mark of a black horned crown (the symbol of Asmodeus) appeared on the central knuckle of her hand. She also got a tattoo of a flaming bell in her inner thigh. Later, when Fearne summoned Teven after the gods became mortal, he told her Asmodeus would return someday and their pact remained in force. When he left, the mark on her hand from his kiss had spread, now covering her entire hand in dark hellish runes and designs.

entities.name: Ferris
entities.description:
, more commonly known as Flimsy, is a shapeshifter sorcerer who joined the Darrington Brigade for their job performing security for the maiden voyage of the skyship "Hubris". He was played by Matthew Mercer.

Flimsy was a young, pale, gaunt man with long stringy black hair. His eyes were completely black saucers. When the Darrington Brigade met him, he was wearing a loose fitting tunic and a massive backpack covered with all sorts of things, including a wooden sword.

Flimsy was incredibly timid and unsure of himself, but when in Taryon Darrington's form, was able to pull off his swagger and self-confidence.

Flimsy's hometown was the beautiful Menagerie Coast town of Feolinn. He had been studiously applying to join the Darrington Brigade for some time (with application forms he had made himself), and had to pay his own way to join them in Rexxentrum before they left for their security detail aboard the Hubris.

entities.name: Fjord
entities.description:
Fjord is a half-orc with green skin, yellow eyes with vertical slit pupils, and black hair with a lock of gray. He has notable scars on the left side of his face, an X-shaped pair on his forehead that cuts through his brow past his eye and one through his upper lip. He is about 6'1". He has been described as handsome by multiple characters, including Jester Lavorre, Beauregard Lionett, Caleb Widogast and Nott. Over the course of their journey, he let his hair grow out. When it got a bit longer in , Fjord, with Beau's assistance, tied it into a small topknot after watching Caleb tie his hair. He also started growing out his beard, with the first noticeable stubble appearing in after a day at the spa. By the time the party headed to Aeor, his beard was fully grown.

At the start of the campaign, his orc tusks were intentionally shortened and not visible when his mouth is closed; the tusks have scratches, divots, and chips across the top. After , he decided to stop shortening them, and by , they had grown back enough to be casually visible.

At the beginning of the campaign, Fjord wore beat-up, piecemeal leather armor. While having an enchantment transferred onto his armor by Pumat Sol, Fjord also had his armor cleaned up. He additionally purchased a Cloak of Protection from The Invulnerable Vagrant when he collected enough gold and wore it for most of his journey. Following his first vision from the Wildmother, Fjord etched wave designs into his armor as they traveled to the King's Cage. As the Nein prepared to head to Aeor, Fjord purchased warmer clothes for the harsher climate. Unlike the others, he didn't have his custom-made. Later in , when they found an animal pelt in a wreck, he attached it to his new cloak.

During the battle with Cree in the tunnels beneath Cognouza, Fjord acquired a red eye on his left palm. Upon Lucien's final defeat, the eye vanished from his person.

entities.name: Fresh Cut Grass
entities.description:
Fresh Cut Grass (originally called Faithful Care-Giver), or FCG for short, was an Aeormaton cleric and a member of Bells Hells, played by Sam Riegel.

FCG had yellow metallic plating, with four chestplate stripes that look like blades of grass, and rolls around on a tiny wheel. He had big blue to white eyes of different shapes. FCG was made of various alloys and, being dense, weighs twice as much as he looked like he would. He was 3 foot 8 inches tall, making him taller than both Orym and Chetney.

FCG ate metal rather than organic food for sustenance. They described it as a very complicated self-repairing system that needs raw materials to operate, and Imahara Joe later discovered that FCG's interior held a transmutation enchantment that converted and reallocated raw materials. The portions of consumed materials that they don't require (such as the non-metallic components of ore) are excreted through their mouth. FCG was also able to store liquids inside and pour them out later. The inside of FCG's "stomach" was a small storage compartment, accessed through the mouth, with a number of shelf units and a modest amount of space. These items, unless secured in some way, could be heard rattling inside.

When FCG accumulated enough stress points to tip him into an uncontrolled, vicious rage against the party, his eyes went red, and they noticed that the four grass-like marks on his chest could have been caused by a bloodied hand dragging across it.

entities.name: Frog
entities.description:
Frog (originally called Archivist Librarian Lorekeeper 1, or ALL-1 for short), is an Aeormaton monk and a member of The Re-Slayer's Take. She is played by Caroline Lux.

Frog is a 6'11 tall Aeormaton whose copper-colored metallic body make her look like she wears full-body armor, so she covers it with trousers and a hooded green poncho; the metal under the clothes presents a leaf-like pattern. In a similar way, since her eyes emit a constant blue glow, she tends to wear spectacles to hide it.

She is a very curious person, friendly and nerdy, eager to learn about everything. While she's happy to be around other people, she can get nervous thinking her appearance or behavior might upset them.

Frog was one of the sentient automatons created in the floating city of Aeor during the Age of Arcanum. She originally worked as a librarian, and during the destruction of the city she was able to abandon it in some sort of vehicle, eventually crashing in Issylra, with some of her pieces scattered. Centuries later she was partially repaired and regained consciousness thanks to Devexian, who had been waking their people up for years, being found by the monks of the Cobalt Soul shortly after. Frog started exploring the world, learning about modern Exandria and taking notes about anything that sparked her interest. The monks taught her how to fight in a temple, and told her she should hide her Aeormaton nature for her own safety, although Frog herself didn't known much about what she was or where did she came from.

entities.name: Fy'ra Rai
entities.description:
is a fire genasi monk and a chosen of the Wildmother, who appeared in Exandria Unlimited Prime and Exandria Unlimited: Kymal. She is played by Anjali Bhimani.

Fy'ra Rai is tall and very dark-skinned, with gold sparkling on her arms and neck. She has fire for hair. When she first appears, she is wearing all black, including her tall boots. She carries a tall, collapsible staff.

She has several tattoos, which she explained meant that someone who loved her very much wanted her never to feel pain, but instead wanted others who tried to hurt her to feel pain.

When she tried to remove the Circlet of Barbed Vision from Opal's head she received puncture wounds on her hands that acquired a greenish color.

entities.name: Garen Hearthheart
entities.description:
is a dwarf stonemason played by Matthew Mercer in Exandria Unlimited: Divergence. He was a mortal incarnation of the All-Hammer.

Just before the defeat of the Strife Emperor, Garen was elderly and, due to his time in prison, looked older than his years, with tangled, gray- and white-streaked hair. His beard was scraggly and burned at the tips. He wore a loose vest over simple, gray, dirty clothes. His left arm had been amputated past the elbow, cauterized, and capped with rough iron slag as a punishment.

His years of captivity and mistreatment had left Garen deeply cynical that any change in the condition of the world was possible, although deep down he still retained his old ideals, valuing community over safety..}}

The strongest proponents of the Divine Gate were the Platinum Dragon and the Lawbearer; the Prime Deities developed the idea before taking mortal form, decades ahead of the time when they would bring down the flying city of Aeor. The All-Hammer, arguing that anything a god did another deity could undo, incarnated as a mortal dwarf to begin laying the foundations of the Gate with mortal hands. The Moonweaver was supposed to help him hide with her magic, but the Lord of the Hells learned about it and cursed her miracle, so that no god would know about the All-Hammer's new identity, not even himself; he lost his memories of divinity.

entities.description:
is an orsimer dragonknight who serves as bartender at the Dreary Jug (later renamed Grelnok's Skull), which she owns collectively with Hoa, Mallory, Slaughter, and Tavima. She is played by Laura Bailey in Blackwood miniseries.

As an orsimer (orc), Grelnok is tall, large, and green-skinned. She wears her dark hair partially braided and pulled back in cornrows.

Grelnok exhibits a typically stoic and disinterested persona; as bartender, she makes up the drinks rather than providing the drinks ordered. She is quick to turn to violence to solve a problem. She is a hiking enthusiast and hikes the Grahtwood near the Grelnok's Skull Tavern.

Grelnok is friends with Tavima. She has a low opinion of Slaughter.

is a "young medium whose sideshow distractions may be more than they seem, and whose clever scams might hold a glimpse of the supernatural." She is played by Aimee Carrero.

Grimoria is a young 18-year-old woman, slight of build with naturally curly hair. Her real name is Alma Látigo.

Her original goal was to learn how to give peace to the souls that she encounters. She is fearful that one day she will encounter the souls of her parents, and of what they will think of her.

Grimoria carries with her memories not her own of spirits she has encountered throughout her brief life. She has had a supernatural ability linked to touch or to artifacts since her parents died at the end of the War and she was taken in by Cynthia and Oliver Fogg.

entities.description:
Hanako Hayashi is the socialite daughter of Japanese ambassadors in the one-shot. She is played by Erika Ishii.

At some point in her past, Hana learned to pick locks. Rupert Merriweather caught Hanako stealing a necklace. Bentley Badger was also aware of her attempted theft. Mr. Merriweather used this incident to blackmail her so she would take part in the heist in the Crystal Palace.

Hana and Alexandra know each other, and Alexandra knows Hana's parents.

Hana's parents are Japanese ambassadors. They seem to know of some of her more unruly behavior, but not the extent of her actions, such as the attempted theft of Merriweather's necklace.

entities.name: Hazel Copperpot
entities.description:
is a dwarven bard originally from the city of Hupperdook and a member of the Darrington Brigade. She is played by Marisha Ray.

Hazel is a stout dwarven woman with red hair wearing a bunch of instruments strapped around her body, making her a rather loud one-woman band.

Hazel speaks with a transatlantic accent and behaves like an old-time radio play hostess, complete with her own "The Shadow"-esque introduction played through a gramophone-like device. Hazel complements her actions and movements with various instruments, including a slide whistle and a tambourine, and frequently narrates the action occurring. She tends to heavily flatter Taryon, emphasizing his successes and attributing the actions of others to him.

Hazel claimed she spent her days reading Taryon Darrington's books as an escape from work in Hupperdook's factories. Hazel decided to join the Darrington Brigade as a way to record a live audiobook for Tary.

entities.name: Heera Agneheart
entities.description:
Heera Agneheart is a tiefling rogue/warlock and a member of The Re-Slayer's Take. She is played by Jasmine Bhullar.

Heera is a tiefling woman with yellowish ocher skin, a long tail, buffalo-like horns adorned with ribbons and peacock feathers, and wearing green and blue silks and a leather armor with henna designs. Although she has hooves, she wears boots.

After Farah accidentally hit her with a rock a piece of one of her horns broke, and although it was temporarily re-attached with sap and vines, that same day Heera used it as a projectile in a battle, destroying it in the process. She started using her family's horn and a bow as a sort of prosthetic.

She is confident and cunning, clever and decisive, described as a "con-artist", and pragmatic when it comes to achieving her goals. She is also grateful, appearing friendly to those who treat her well, but irritable to those who disappoint her. She seems to be good with kids, befriending them rather quickly, and she also loves animals, understanding them better than people.

Hoa is an altmer with blonde hair and yellow eyes.

Hoa is talkative, exuberant, cheery, and clumsy. She frequently takes an optimistic view of things. Her eagerness to learn about people leads to her sometimes making people uncomfortable. She is fond of wild animals and has six pet birds.

Hoa uses spells which are based on Elder Scrolls Online lore:

entities.name: Howard Margrove
entities.description:
is a professor of philosophy at Briarbank College in Newfaire. He is played by Robbie Daymond.

Dr. Margrove is always impeccably dressed. He wears spectacles, a formal suit, and a top hat.

Dr. Margrove is very much an introvert, spending long hours in his book and oddity-filled office at the College, which is kept constantly pristine. His colleagues there viewed him as keeping too much to himself.

Robbie Daymond described the character as "a real creep, a punchy lab wizard scientist. ... [He's] a man of mystery. He’s a compulsive, fastidious, hyper-intellectual reductionist, who doesn’t understand the madness that is unfolding around him and wants desperately to, and throughout this journey he will either learn to lean in or be consumed. Dr. Howard is not to be trifled with."

entities.name: Idrin Shadowstep
entities.description:
Idrin Shadowstep is a young elf-orc chronurgist and a member of The Re-Slayer's Take. He is played by Jasper William Cartwright.

Idrin is a young man of elven and orcish descent, with pointed ears but no prominent tusks, dark hair, and skin the color of clay. He wears warm-colored flowing robes with a pattern showing fragments of the starry sky, and matching gold earrings in both ears; he also has painted black nails, and tattoos of the moon and the sun in the back of his left and right hand respectively, that glow when he uses magic.

He is loyal and shrewd, clever, kind and generous, with strong ideals about helping and protecting other people, and enough curiosity and confidence to intervene in situations that catch his attention. He is also insecure about his identity, being terrified of losing himself if he fully remembers his past lives.

Idrin was raised in Xhorhas by a mother and a father who shared stories and advice with him. He was born with the consecuted soul of a member of the Kryn Dynasty, and even though his mother cast a powerful Modify Memory spell to prevent it, presumably during his adolescence he started having visions at night about those past lives (seeing a big ogre, a sword-wielding orcish woman, and a drow man of the Dynasty); although he was told by his father that was a sign of consecution, his mother insisted that those were just dreams, so the young uniya ended up repressing the memories of his past lives. He eventually learned magic and manifested a talent for chronurgy. Idrin ended up leaving Xhorhas following his mother's advice, who might have also used magic so that his father couldn't find him.

entities.name: Idyl
entities.description:
is a slyborne human seraph played by Travis Willingham in Age of Umbra.

Idyl is a human man with a shaved head, wearing furs and basic clothing.

He is responsible and loyal to people he trusts, and he tries to protect them, even if they don't want him to.

At some point in his life Idyl started manifesting divine magic which his mother had always believed in, even if he hadn't; given the lack of godly presence in the world he decided to keep that part of himself hidden, especially since their current home had a tendency of suppressing of manipulating any sign of divine power. Since not even Idyl's mother wanted him to explore what his mother could do, he left by himself, and eventually moved to Desperloch. He met Eryn Loathroot near the settlement when she was being chased by a creature, and became friends with both her and her father, Garrick. He and Eryn spent a lot of time together and had an interest in the activity of the local delvers in the vaults. At one point, Idyl had asked for permission to join the delvers, but had apparently been turned down.

entities.name: Imogen Temult
entities.description:
is a human sorcerer and a member of Bells Hells. She is played by Laura Bailey.

When she first appeared, Imogen was introduced as a young human woman with light skin and freckles on her face, with long light-purple hair. She wore a light blue dress and a yellow scarf tied around her neck. Later, just before the party went to Aeor, she altered her clothing slightly so that her sheer dress opened in the front revealing dark blue pants and thigh-high boots. She wore a black buckled bodice harness and the Robe of the Midnight Rune altered to be off-the-shoulder and flowing into strips at the bottom.

When Imogen began to have dreams of the red storm, marks appeared on her arms resembling purple lightning bolts streaking up from her wrists. They have grown slightly over the decade since they first appeared in concordance with the expanding storm. On occasion, when she employs her magic, her eyes briefly flash with white energy, and magical electricity appears to course through her arms. Later, during the apogee solstice, Imogen's marks grew again, reaching her chest and neck, and acquiring a red hue in certain sections starting from where they first appeared. The markings produced a red mist when she later cast magic near the Bloody Bridge in the Tishtan excavation site. After she visited Ruidus and returned to Exandria her marks had grown more, going up the neck and barely reaching her jawline.

Imogen's appearance has temporarily changed a few times due to wild magic surges coming from her Feywild shard. The first time, her skin turned navy blue for a brief time until Fresh Cut Grass cast Remove Curse on her. After a second wild magic surge, Imogen's hair fell out. She was briefly bald and used Chetney's cap and a wig that Dusk made to cover her head. Her hair grew back almost completely within a day.
