entities.description:
Jamie Wrenly is a human witch. They are played by Taliesin Jaffe.

While Jamie is not really physically described during the Cinderbrush session, official art by Kendra Wells and Taliesin Jaffe's cosplay for the session provides descriptions.

Jamie is of average height, pale, with long black hair with red streaks, one side shaved and choppy bangs. They have pierced ears, and during the events of Cinderbrush they have black painted nails. Jamie wears long, wide-leg black pants with a black belt, a white button-up shirt, and a red and black kimono-type shawl. They also wear a wide-brimmed black hat, a black chest harness, round glasses with red lenses, and a silver spider broach with red gems. Taliesin's cosplay added silver rings on several fingers.

During the rave, Taliesin describes their outfit as "...[their] uniform that says [they're] in business... lots and lots of pockets, lots of flowy stuff, lots of places to hide shit."

entities.name: Jessep Nimblethorp
entities.description:
is a teenaged sorcerer and one of the campers attending Wildemount Wildlings. She is played by Libe Barer.

Jessep is very tall (almost 6 feet), has pale blue skin, ultramarine eyes, and aquamarine hair with pale roots that has grown a bit wild. She wears a monocle.

She is intelligent and somewhat anxious. Despite having excellent health, she is hypochondriac.

Jessep grew up in a very academic household, since both her parents were professors, which made her a very good student. In 844 PD she was sent to the Wildemount Wildlings camp, and even though she had started manifesting magic, she wasn't able to control it. At one point a wild surge of energy caused many people to temporarily lose their hair, making her feel terrible about it. She and Sky became friends, and during a race in which both of them were doing pretty badly, they came up with a song that helped with the sorcerer's anxiety.

entities.description:
Jester Lavorre is a tiefling cleric of the Traveler and a member of the Mighty Nein. She is played by Laura Bailey.

Jester Lavorre is a 5 feet, 3 inches tall blue tiefling with blue hair. She wears a pretty dress and has freckles. She wears a belt with a symbol to the Traveler on her waist. Her voice makes her sound younger than she is.

She sometimes wore a ribbon tied around her left horn. This ribbon was originally wrapped around Jester's map of Wildemount, but Jester kept it because it looked "pretty". She later attached it to a glaive to increase the weapon's value during a trade in Zadash.

As of , Jester has a diamond dust tattoo covering her upper chest and shoulders, resembling clasped hands.

entities.name: Jinnah Basar
entities.description:
Jinnah "Jean" Basar is a surgeon and young woman in Newfaire. She is played by Zehra Fazal.

When first seen, Jean was wearing standard-issue EONS medical clothing. All her clothes are pristine. She wears a long pale green peacoat lined in pink and white gloves.

She is extremely focused and has dark eyes and jet-black hair. "Everything about this woman on first glance is cold, cool, steady." Beneath that exterior, however, those close to her can see the warmth that urges her to heal while trying to maintain balance.

Jean first met Marion Collodi when she accompanied her father, an exorcist, to treat Marion's scar. At some point in her childhood, Jean lost her mother to an illness, and became frustrated with her father's refusal of medicine in favour of magick. Jean was inspired to pursue medicine thanks to this, also swearing off magick. Jean's skill as a surgeon was honed on the fields of war.

entities.name: Julien Davinos
entities.description:
Sir is a human fighter/rogue played by Matthew Mercer in Campaign Four.

Sir Julien is a man with a lanky, compact build and long curling black hair. Although it is not visible at first glance, one of the teeth in his mouth is missing a piece, chipped during a melee. He wears the reinforced leather military uniform of House Davinos: dark purples and gray with red trim. Covering his left shoulder is a dark green short cape with a detailed motif of vine and flowers sewn into it. His armor includes two prominent items of intricate silver: a pauldron on his right shoulder and on his left hand a full gauntlet of dark silver that is heavy enough to make him seem unbalanced. He carries a rapier. After he started traveling with the Seekers he made sure to hide any symbols of his family in his clothes, to avoid unwanted attention.

His shadow looks darker and deeper than normal, a sign of him being cursed.

Julien seems to care deeply about honor, mentioning several times it as a point of dislike towards Thjazi Fang, someone he felt had little honor in his life. Julien indulges frequently in worldly delights such as local taverns and brothels.

entities.description:
is a half-elven teenage rogue and one of the campers attending Wildemount Wildlings. He is played by Aleks Le.

Kai is a young boy of wood elf ancestry, with white hair, blue eyes, a golden earring in his right ear, and a necklace with a blue crystal. He is 5′ 9″ tall.

He is a very "chill" and fun person, rather carefree, although with troublemaker tendencies.

Kai was born in 828 PD; he became an orphan and was raised by bandits. That led to his eventual problems with the justice, which caused him to be sent to the Wildemount Wildlings camp in 844 PD, as part of a court-order rehabilitation plan. He didn't make much progress gaining badges or improving himself, but he took an interest in Padmund Pondhop's project of creating a Mighty Nein-themed card game, so he helped him with that, becoming the illustrator of the project.

is a human ranger played by Robbie Daymond in Campaign Four.

Kattigan is in his mid-40's, standing at 6'4" and 220 pounds. He appears to have led a "weathered" life, and although his abilities are beginning to wane with age, he remains muscular and powerful. When first encountered, he wore scavenged but well-cared-for accoutrements of good quality, all of which were purposeful, including a cowl and hood. He also wears a leather bandolier across his chest, filled with different tinctures and herbs. Kattigan smells like clean but wet dog, with just a little bit of man sweat. Campaign 4 Ep 1-4 Recap]" | vod=https://youtu.be/hdLPwuKMlIY | 10:41}}

Kattigan has facial tattoos that mirror the scars across his wolf companion Wulferic's face. Episode 1 Discussing Up To C4E11|1:28:31}} He lost his right little finger for some hours, and after Thaisha Lloy reattached it to his hand, it left a wood-like mark as a scar.

Kattigan is a man of the wilds, uncomfortable in cities. He is unnerving to be around because of his unpredictable nature, but his wolf companion Wulferic can have a calming effect on him. Teor described him as "a fierce warrior and a good man."

entities.description:
Kexon Peros is a faerie wizard and a member of the Menagerie, a small group of adventurers. He is played by Travis Willingham.

Kexon is a beetle-looking faerie with large mandibles, a blue and purple exoskeleton, blue-green eyes, and translucent light blue wings. He carries a staff, and due to magic he can change his size to appear larger than other faeries.

Kexon is more studious than other faeries.

At one point in his life Kexon teamed up with the Menagerie and became an adventurer.

entities.name: Keyleth
entities.description:
Keyleth () is a half-elf druid member of Vox Machina. She is played by Marisha Ray.

Keyleth was raised in Zephrah as a member of the Air Ashari tribe. When she was a child, her mother Vilya left on a journey to earn the title of headmaster of the tribe, but never came back. After reaching adulthood, Keyleth left her home to attempt the Aramenté herself.

During her adventures with Vox Machina, she became the wielder of a legendary staff, the Spire of Conflux, to fight against the Chroma Conclave. She completed her Aramenté and became the headmaster of the Air Ashari, a position that grants her the title Voice of the Tempest, adding several thousand years to her lifespan.

"A first impression of Keyleth would leave you with little information on the half-elven druid. You might even think that her social awkwardness, due to her sheltered upbringing, is... kind of sweet. Of course, it would be unwise to underestimate her based on first impressions. Under that unintimidating petite frame is a vicious beast waiting to be unleashed, whose natural powers have made even the fiercest of champions pee their pants. Literally.

entities.name: Kingsley Tealeaf
entities.description:
, also known as King Tealeaf, is a tiefling blood hunter/rogue and member of the Mighty Nein inhabiting the same body as Mollymauk Tealeaf and Lucien Tavelle. He is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

Kingsley has the same body as Molly and Lucien, and thus presumably the same overall appearance. He is a lavender tiefling with red eyes, curled horns, and a forked tongue. Multiple tattoos adorn his body, starting with a serpent tattoo that curls all along the length of his right hand and up his arm, then winds into a floral piece on his shoulder, and then into a peacock with tail feathers that run up the side of his face. Between his shoulder blades rising towards the hairline, he has tattoos of an eye within a pyramid, illuminated by another eye above it. Flanking and connecting through it like a mantle, he has a moon and sun tattoo on the back as well.

However, Kingsley does not have the red eye tattoos that Mollymauk and Lucien had.

Kingsley was eager to find out more about the world and about himself. He seemed to think highly of himself, choosing the name Kingsley because he felt like a king.

entities.description:
is a Christmas elf fighter played by Matthew Mercer for .

Klaus has grey hair and bushy eyebrows that are mostly covered by his hooded cloak. His cheeks both have a red swirl in the center and his nose is akin to an arrowhead. He wields two striped candy canes as his main choice of weaponry.

Klaus is a hardy elf, with his main duties keeping watch at the outskirts of the North Pole and fighting away any creatures who trespass into the village.

entities.name: Kurt
entities.description:
Kurt is a male given name in Germanic languages. Kurt originated as short forms of the Germanic Konrad/Conrad, depending on geographical usage, with meanings including counselor or advisor. Like Conrad, it can also be a surname and less uncommon variations in Germanic languages including Cord, Curd, Cordt, Curth, Kord, Kort, Kurth, and Kurtu. Curd/Kurd is the decent of the Medes.

In Turkish, Kurt means "wolf" and is a surname and less commonly a given name in numerous Turkic countries. Kurt is also the turkish word for Kurd.

Kurt in Kurdistan meaning your son.

entities.name: Laerryn Coramar-Seelie
entities.description:
is an elven wizard who served as Architect Arcane of the city of Avalir. She is played by Aabria Iyengar.

Laerryn is tall, lanky, and dark-skinned, with pretty, angular eyes that glow gold. She wears ornate, glowing gold clothing with a purple cape.

Laerryn has no patience for small talk. She is one of the smartest people in the city who took a vital but under-appreciated job working in the basic infrastructure of the city. "If she wanted glory, she could just pick a different job and immediately get the praise her talents would garner. Instead, she dedicated her life to quietly and dutifully protecting the Heart of Avalir, and expanding on the city’s mission statement (travel the ley lines collecting knowledge and magic to share with the world)."

Laerryn's goal was to perfect the Astral Leywright, a new engine that she had created to build a new ley line road through to other Planes of Existence that would allow the city to travel not only across the face of Exandria, but to realms supernal, where a city of mortals might walk as equals with the gods themselves.

entities.name: Laudna
entities.description:
() is a human Hollow One sorcerer/warlock and a member of Bells Hells. is played by Marisha Ray.

When she first appeared, Laudna was fairly young, pale, and gaunt. Her big eyes had dilated pupils, and her lips were dark. Marisha further described Laudna's features as "almost doll-like." She had long, thin, dark hair with a shock of white through her bangs, pulled up in a half-up bun with a rock chisel (depicted as a rock pick in official art). She wore tattered clothes, including a dark red blouse and a black skirt, although after some time traveling with Bells Hells she updated her outfit with a more elegant dress, more lady-like, and also a new hairstyle. She wore pointy gold cuffs on her ears to hide their edges, which were once shorn to points like an elf's. Her belt held various tools, miscellaneous animal remains (which used to include Pâté de Rolo before he became her familiar), and other odds and ends. Later, just before the party traveled to Aeor, Laudna crafted herself (with her mind somewhat absent) a completely new outfit consisting of a black blouse with billowy sheer sleeves and a high collar, a small green gem on a choker chain, tight gloves, a breastplate formed of golden chains resembling a rib cage over a black corset, a long black-purple skirt under a cage-like golden crinoline. Her hair was now worn tied into a tight bun.

Originally, when Laudna used her Form of Dread, her extremities elongated and a black veil came across her face, hiding a stream of black tears pouring from her eyes. After her death and subsequent resurrection, the form altered to embody aspects of the Sun Tree. But when Laudna cast Hunger of the Shadow on Bor'Dor Dog'Son after learning he had betrayed the party, she heard a slow heartbeat start up in the back of her mind, and the faint shimmer of a mourning veil folded over the top of her Form of Dread as Bor'Dor's life essence was sucked into her mouth. Although for some time she managed to keep her Form of Dread tree-themed, whenever she channeled Delilah's essence the veil appeared again. While exploring Whitestone Castle, the image became more definitively that of Delilah, with wider shoulders and wearing her choker, in an overlapping secondary shadow of Laudna. After Delilah was trapped within the soul anchor, Laudna's Form of Dread became more like a generic noble banshee and less like Delilah Briarwood.

Her eyes glow green at times, notably when she uses Eyes of the Runekeeper or Cling to Life.

entities.name: Lawrence Lorelei
entities.description:
is a human blood hunter and a member of the Lorelei family. He was played by Travis Willingham in .

In his human form Lawrence looks like a man of dark skin (although lighter than those of his two oldest siblings) with a soft purple hue (sign of his drow ancestry), dark eyes and long black hair (with white racing stripes starting at his temples) but not quite touching the shoulders; he also has a slight stubble of black beard. He wears black and green clothes, with vine patterns on some of his garments. Lawrence has features in common with his brother Benicio, but they are not identical twins: beyond the style and personal aesthetics of each one, the older twin has a more pronounced jaw, and lacks the scars of the younger twin; furthermore, they both have distinct white hair patterns.

In his werewolf form, Lawrence's head is jet black with white racing stripes coming back from his eyes. The black only extends to his mid-sternum, and the rest of his body is peppered salty gray, black and white, with dappled spots.

Lawrence was studious and serious-minded. He was also often accused of being cowardly by his siblings. While he is willing to offer his family whatever they require, his true love is logic and reason.

entities.description:
(Real name: Raymond Leonared Steedwell. Jr.) is a "bohemian bachelor who moves through the storied echelons of society with an acute journalistic eye for the eccentric and uncanny." He is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

Leo is in his 40s and well put together, although somewhat foppish in manner. His clothes and accessories are of fine quality.

He enjoys writing, and keeping busy is a comfort to him. Although his profession is nominally that of a journalist, he is in fact a professional man of leisure.

Leo and his Aunt Leanna have a somewhat guarded relationship although she said she cares about both him and his estranged father. When she urged him to take the first step to reconcile with him, noting they were both stubborn, Leo refused, saying the favor he was asking for wasn't enough for that.

entities.description:
is a changeling warlock/bard in the city of Avalir. He is played by Sam Riegel.

In his original form, Loquatius has pale gray marble-like skin with shifting black veins, white eyes with dark shading around them, and white hair in an upshock; whenever he transforms the veins in his skin move and colors start changing as if pigments were being taken and added to a painting. He wears a golden jacket with purple lining, and carries himself in a haughty fashion.

Loquatius is flamboyant, larger-than-life, and very much enjoys the life of a celebrity and the perks that come with it.

Loquatius Seelie is a broadcaster in the Herald's Tome of Avalir. He is originally from the Feywild, a member of the Seelie Court and a warlock under the service of Lady Elmenore. He arrived to Exandria as a diplomat working for his court, but eventually decided he liked the City of Crowns and his growing fame, so he stayed permanently; there, he fell in love with a mortal woman, Laerryn Coramar. They married in Domunas during the Replenishment, but despite still loving each other, in less than seven years they divorced due to their differences, with Quay abandoning their home in Avalir.

entities.description:
is a human fighter played by Stephen Colbert in .

Lucky Jack is a human man with dark hair and a prominent scar over his left eye, which he acquired during the attack on the temple of Arioch. He wears a reddish-brown shirt, a gray overshirt, and a black quilted vest.

Lucky Jack feels very responsible for not preventing or stopping the attack on his temple.

When he was younger, Lucky Jack was taken in as an acolyte to a temple of Arioch, Duke of Chaos, in Bladegarden. He swore oaths to Arioch to protect the temple. The temple was attacked by Madrak, who killed his mentor, Laelia, and several of Jack's compatriots, stealing both his dignity and a valuable temple reliquary, the Spirit of Virtue or, colloquially, "Dignity".

is a halfling cleric and a member of the Darrington Brigade. He is played by Travis Willingham.

Macaroni is a small halfling covered in bone-like armor, hides and furs. He wears a skull for a helmet. In Travis's words, he looks like one of "the Lost Boys from Peter Pan".

Macaroni is chaotic, eccentric and quite aggressive at times.

While the specifics are unknown, Buddy and Macaroni met and became friends before joining the Darrington Brigade.

entities.name: Malcolm Trills
entities.description:
is "a former soldier accustomed to conflict now keeping a watchful eye over Red Lamp, with a helpful hand for those in need." He is played by Imari Williams.

Malcolm is "the muscle with a heart of gold." Years of military service have ingrained into him habits of order, neatness, and routine. He deals with stress or trauma by compartmentalization and maintains a stoic, calm demeanor.

Malcolm works at various jobs in the Red Lamp District as a bouncer or ad hoc peacekeeper, but his primary position and home is at the Glass Cat Casino working for Madam Cordelia Glask.

Malcolm's family is old, wealthy, powerful, and not very loving. The men tend to enter the military and the women run the businesses, while the family consolidates its power and prestige in Newfaire by intermarrying with other equally rich and connected families. They are ingrained both in the Periphery and the Ascendancy, and Malcolm's father is a power in the Parliament as well as having an association with EONS, a society seeking to advance and promote alchemy. Much of the family's wealth comes from the manufacture of weapons.

Mallory is an aging Dunmer with white hair and beard. Like all dark elves, he has dark greyish skin.

In his role as cook and chef, Mallory is generally quippy and distrusting. His often dark temperament leads Slaughter to comment, "Every dish you describe sounds like a threat."

At some point in Mallory's distant past ("an old past [he'd] like to forget"), he learned to use a lockpick. He is not on speaking terms with his family.

As a hulking and fatty creature, it has the highest hitpoints among the Champions and protective natural armor. Its arm-cannons allow it to blast humans with fire from a distance and occasionally release gouts of flame in front of it.

is a young man in Newfaire and a veteran of the recent war. He is played by Luis Carazo.

Marion is 5'9" inches tall, with a medium-slim build, dark hair and beard, and an intense look as he focuses not only on what's around him, but on another layer of existence that the eye cannot see. He has a starburst-shaped scar on his chest that pulses slightly when he performs a ritual. He wears a light olive-brown shirt patterned with small flowers, and a nice-for-a-working-man, worn vest, inherited from his father.

Marion cares for his appearance despite having no one to come home to.

After the events of , the existing scar on his chest grew and became more obviously Bleed-based.

Dr. Mason Pocket was an antiquities archivist for the British Museum in the Call of Cthulhu: Shadow of the Crystal Palace one-shot. He was played by Phil LaMarr.

Dr. Pocket is virtually identical in appearance to his player Phil LaMarr in all but his dress. He wears a beige tweed jacket and vest, alongside a simple white shirt and black tie. He relies on a pair of rimless spectacles.

Dr. Pocket is a scholarly man with a strong interest in ancient mythologies. Meek, but polite and personable, he is described by fellow investigator Hanako Hayashi as "a charmer." Being a man of simple means, he is quite overawed by his companions.

Mason Pocket is an antiquities archivist working for the British Museum. He has spent most of his life working on a pamphlet called The Sacred Nightmare of the Ancients, which earned the attention and accolades of Rupert Meriwether, but is disregarded as pure fiction by the general public.

entities.description: Mezek (Bulgarian: Мезек) is a village in southeastern Bulgaria, part of Svilengrad municipality, Haskovo Province. It lies at the foot of the eastern Rhodope Mountains, just north of the Bulgaria–Greece border and not far west of the Bulgaria–Turkey border. Mezek is famous for the well-preserved medieval Mezek Fortress (Neoutzikon - Νεούτζικον) and its two ancient Thracian beehive tombs, the Mezek and Sheynovets tombs. The village is also well known for its own winery and the Mezzek brand of Bulgarian wine.

entities.name: Misty
entities.description:
was a highborne clank bard played by Ashley Johnson in Age of Umbra. Unlike most clanks in the Halcyon Domain, empty or corrupted by the Umbra, she was animated by the soul of a dead girl, Sybil.

Misty looked like a beautiful but imposing stone statue, with humanoid features and four pairs of wings: a relic from the Old World, once a vessel for the spirits and angels of the Veiled Gods and made to worship them, but not empty, like the others upon the gods' departure. Standing eight feet tall, she was stained by years of lichen, dirt, and insect nests, and near the hem of her skirt there was some graffiti left by a child (herself, in fact, as Sybil). She wore a crown and the suggestion of a light veil had been carved into the stone over her face. The statue was originally meant to produce music, and thus it had many hollow sections, making Misty less strong than she looked; E1|8:48|Age of Umbra: Desperloch}} in fact, during a fight part of one of her wings broke, and she lost the top left one completely after a different battle on her way to Amber Reach.

When she magically disguised herself as a human, she looked like a woman in her twenties with wavy brown hair and eyes of the same color, and clothes inspired by the outfits of the rest of the group.

She was kind and curious, although very ignorant about some aspects of humanoid interaction.

entities.name: Mollymauk Tealeaf
entities.description:
Mollymauk Tealeaf is a tiefling blood hunter and member of the Mighty Nein. He is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

Molly first awoke with a red eye tattoo on the right side of his neck, on his right shoulder, two on his upper back, and on the back and palm of his right hand. He integrated and concealed these eyes within a serpent tattoo that curled all along the length of his right hand and up his arm, then winded into a floral piece on his shoulder, and then into a peacock with tail feathers that ran up the side of his face. Although he has tried to tattoo over the eyes, they would not take ink. It was confirmed by Yasha that Molly had nine 'eye tattoos' on his body.

Between his shoulder blades rising towards the hairline, he has tattoos of an eye within a pyramid, illuminated by another eye above it. A moon and sun tattoo flanks it and connects through it like a mantle.

Molly has been described as a "literal and figurative peacock". He frequently tells extravagant lies with little mind for whether or not his audience believes them. He is not visibly affected by insults, as shown by his lack of reaction when the old man in the Old Mud Hole called him a devil and told him to leave town.

entities.name: Morrighan Ferus
entities.description:
is a lagomore paladin and Champion of the Matron of Ravens, formerly a bartender and rogue. She is played by Erica Lindbeck.

thumb|270px| Morrighan is "a really cute bunny girl" standing about 5'10", with bright green eyes and grey bunny ears. When first seen working the bar at The Maiden's Wish casino she was wearing a feathered showgirl outfit, but later wore traditional rogue attire.

During her time in Kymal Mor had a slightly rehearsed demeanor, constantly acting surprised, although appearing more genuine when she gained trust with people. After joining the Crown Keepers and becoming the champion of the Matron of Ravens, she felt somewhat more comfortable around her friends, although when it came to her purpose she blindly trusted the goddess; if the situation she faced did not have a clear solution, she would turn to the Raven Queen to tell her what to do.

Morrighan was born in the Feywild and entered the Material Plane with help from an old woman named Morrigan, to live and grow up in Kymal for the past twenty-six years. She had been a bartender (among other things) for about three years but had only been working at The Maiden's Wish for a few weeks when encountered by the Crown Keepers. Her modus operandi was to work at a casino, siphon off what cash she could, and then after a while move to the next one before they were even aware of what had happened.

is an Uruk in service of Sauron created for Critical Role One-Shot: Shadow of War – Part 1 and 2. is played by Darin De Paul.

Mozuu enjoyed bragging about his personal conversation with Sauron to everyone he met. However, when confronted with a ringbearer, he confessed that he had made up the conversation entirely.

Mozuu always has access to these spells.

In addition to his oath spells, Mozuu has access to 1st through 2nd-level paladin spells. As a 5th level paladin with a +0 charisma modifier, he can prepare 2 of these spells per day.

entities.description:
is a dwarf wizard played by Marisha Ray in Campaign Four.

Murray appears "put together" but is also a little grimy and greasy. She has long auburn hair, a braided chin-strap beard, and a large bust. She wears a long colorful sleeveless duster coat, a wide flat-brimmed hat, and a custom-made quill on her index fingernail. She is missing her three right-front teeth, which have been replaced with gemstones; left-to-right is a ruby, clear/white quartz and purple quartz. She wears a corset.

Murray enjoys a good party, and a good funeral. She cares deeply about fairness in magical education, wanting students of the Penteveral to be allowed equal opportunity to learn and grow, regardless of their background.

Marisha Ray described her as "that friend that everyone has where they are the first person to get sloppy at the bar, even though they're wearing designer clothes, and just when you think they're going to hit the floor, she drops a deep philosophical line, referencing Camus or something." She agrees with the philosophy of the Penteveral that knowledge should be accessible to anyone who is willing to work hard enough for it, and resents the changes being forced on the school by the current government of Dol-Makjar. Murray believes strongly in freedom of all kinds, and will take issue with any threat to or manipulation of those freedoms. Campaign 4 Ep 1-4 Recap]" | vod=https://youtu.be/hdLPwuKMlIY | 12:56}}

entities.name: Nathaniel Trapp
entities.description:
is a veteran of the recent war in Newfaire, and a journalist for the Civil Tribune newspaper. He is played by Travis Willingham.

Nathaniel's clothing looks expensive, although he tries to hide it. He wears a pocket watch, a beard, and two weathered but currently empty leather holsters. He has piercing blue eyes. After the events of , the right eye's vision turned completely white but the only outward sign was a slight discoloration to the pupil and some creeping scarring that he attempted to disguise with makeup. After the attack at the Chapter House in , he carried an officer's revolver in one of the holsters.

When Nathaniel was nine years old, his older brother was caught by waves as he waded out into a river to fetch one of Nathaniel's toys, and instead of helping him, Nathaniel froze and watched him drown.

Nathaniel was Marion and Sean's former lieutenant and commanding officer in the army.

is a Christmas elf wizard played by Ashley Johnson for .

Nutmeg has messy gray hair and two red swirls on her cheeks. Her clothes are covered in purple goop and her striped scarf has holes in it.

Nutmeg speaks with New York accent. She says Macy's is too big, there is too much going on and that there is too much Christmas there. In Macy's, Nutmeg's job was packing gifts, but eventually she was only allowed to place the ribbons as she had an issue with cellar tape.

entities.name: Nydas Okiro
entities.description:
is a human sorcerer/bard who was the Guildmaster of the Golden Scythe in the city of Avalir. He is played by Lou Wilson.

Nydas was 5'10" and stocky. His eyes were hazel flecked with actual gold, and he had a long scar over his right eye and three X tattoos over his left eye. His beard ended with a golden ring, and he had shoulder-length dreadlocks cuffed with gold, over which he wore a floppy cap in the style of a Renaissance merchant. He wore a cape over a red coat with a golden pin with the signature of the Golden Scythe.

Nydas was flamboyant, jovial, and theatrical.

A former pirate, Nydas rose to the position of Guildmaster of the Golden Scythe guild and founded the Sorcerer's University in Avalir.

entities.name: Occtis Tachonis
entities.description:
is a human Hollow One wizard played by Alexander Ward in Campaign Four.

Occtis is a young man, standing 5'11" and thin, with olive skin, dark hair, and bright green eyes. He wears dark, nobleman's clothing that is clean but worn, with various items and implements hanging from his belt or in the many pockets inside his coat, and has a book strapped to his leg. He is accompanied by a small, mostly white fox named Pincushion. After his resurrection he became a little bit more pale and gaunt, and his eyes acquired a supernatural glow that only dims if he is fully unconscious. In the following days he decided to wear more generic clothes instead of the characteristic Tachonis black, although he kept his coat because all of his components were in its pockets.

According to Julien Davinos, ever since he was young Occtis had a certain look that was very distinctive in his family.

As the sole member of his family without sorcerous magical powers, Occtis grew up feeling as though he was unable to fulfill his family's expectations for him. When he joined Thaisha Lloy on her expedition into Venatus, he began to think people cared about him as a human being, but when his family killed him for their own purposes and he became a Hollow One, it seemed that they valued him solely because of what he is, and that he was only a means to an end. It confirmed to him his lifelong sense of loneliness. Episode 2 Discussing Up To C4E18|01:10:46|Tale Gate Episode 2: Discussing Up To C4E18}} Due to his life circumstances, he has never had a way of processing his emotions in a healthy way, although he is slowly learning to do so with his new group of friends, since he feels like they do care for him, even if it is somewhat "conditional" because his skills are useful.

entities.description:
Oppenheimer Betabean, nicknamed Oppy, is a ribbet sorcerer and a member of the Menagerie, a small group of adventurers. He is played by Ashley Johnson.

Oppy is a very short ribbet with slimy sapphire blue skin with yellow freckles and yellow eyes. He wears stripped overalls and clothes made of leaves. He carries with him a sparkling smoking staff that is actually a cigarillo for a larger creature.

Oppenheimer is a happy, polite and enthusiastic individual.

Oppy and Sweetpea were raised together as siblings. Eventually, they teamed up with the Menagerie and became adventurers.

entities.name: Orym
entities.description:
Orym is an Air Ashari halfling fighter and member of the Crown Keepers and later Bells Hells. He is played by Liam O'Brien.

Orym is 3 feet and 3 inches tall, slender, with ropey muscles and fine features. He has a short shock of brown hair less than an inch long. He has a full-sleeve tattoo of swirling winds and clouds on his right arm stretching up onto his chest, and a tattoo of Ruidus cradled within a crescent Catha on his right shoulder, and more recently, a flaming bell tattoo in his left shoulder blade. Originally, he wore green armor with a leaf theme over brown leather, with well-worn sashes with ivy and flower patterns around his waist, and his boots were brown leather with green stone rings laced into his shin guards. His shield was adorned with ivy. Just before the party traveled to Aeor, he altered his appearance slightly. His hair had grown out longer and was now wavy, and he wore newly-purchased antique Zephyr Armor dyed a dark brown and with a shoulder pauldron made from a piece of FCG's body; on his left boot is a jade piece identical to the one Fearne had on her own outfit. Tiny fey spider vines grew over his armor, symbolizing his connection with Nana Morri.

In every version of his outfit Orym wears a green sash of Ashari design, to remind him of his home in Zephrah.

Orym looks a lot like his mother, Alma, and the resemblance becomes even stronger when they smile. According to Allura Vysoren, after his months with Bells Hells he looked much more confident than he had earlier in his life.

entities.name: Oscar Grimm
entities.description:
is impeccably dressed but rough and ready with the scars to prove it. He is played by Sam Riegel.

Oscar is about 5 feet 6 inches tall, and stout, with broad chest and shoulders, weighing about 200 pounds. He has sandy blond hair and a well-groomed mustache. Almost all of his visible flesh bears scars, his fingers appear to have been broken and badly healed, and he walks with a limp. When first seen, he was very well dressed in a sharp three-piece suit with a heavy gold watch chain and a black overcoat. He was constantly sucking on hard candies.

Oscar has said that whenever he is in the presence of strong bleed, his various scars and healed wounds feel better, and he feels stronger, but also feels shame that this is true.

Eighty-seven years prior to the events of the Circle of Tide and Bone, Oscar somehow became immortal. At that time, Oscar was a circus performer calling himself "The Great Grimm", having changed his name for professional reasons. He and his family, including his wife Cora, brother Quentin, daughter Iris, and ten-year-old son Cosmo were on a ship returning from a performance, when The Serious Man suddenly appeared onboard. The Serious Man performed some kind of ritual which split the ship in two, and as Oscar tumbled into the center of the maelstrom, he pushed Cosmo back, away from the edge, although the rest of the family was lost. Oscar was left with a strange immortality that costs him part of his memories and personality each time his life is restored, which feels at the same time both wrong and good..}} He has spent the intervening years attempting to find a cure but has failed, while slowly losing all his memories, and is on the verge of giving up.

entities.name: Padmund Pondhop
entities.description:
is a bullywug teenage wizard and one of the campers attending Wildemount Wildlings. He is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Padmund is a short (2′ 8″) bullywug boy of big eyes and green skin with black dots. He wears glasses and carries his spellbook everywhere.

He is easily distracted, tending to hyperfocus on the things he likes instead.

Padmund grew up in the Menagerie Coast as the son of a rich sailor, in a villa southeast of Nicodranas with several rooms and servants. At some point he became a fan of the Mighty Nein, and when he learned about the Wildemount Wildlings camp his parents paid so he could attend (while they were on vacation) in 844 PD. The original idea was to go there only half of the summer, and to accompany his father in one of his journeys the other half; however, when he overheard him telling his wife that the boy would be a liability on the ship, Padmund pretended to change his mind in order to be at camp the entire season, thus avoiding an uncomfortable situation. When he arrived there he mistakenly believed it was an adventure-themed camp rather than a place in which adventurers were formed, so when he realized he didn't fit in, he focused instead on the activities he started developing a card game about the Mighty Nein, with some help from Kai, who became his illustrator.

Pango Small is a giant guardian and a member of the Menagerie, a small group of adventurers. He is played by Sam Riegel in .

Pango is a 7 or 8 feet tall giant of purple skin, two eyes and a big nose. He wears stolen green clothes.

Pango is somewhat shy, and easily embarrassed, particularly in front of Bunnie.

Pango grew up underground with his family. At some point, a red substance, the "seep", covered his home, trapping many of his people, including his brother Wango. Eventually, he teamed up with the Menagerie and became an adventurer.

entities.description:
(pronounced [ˈpeɪʃə pɔɹˈkoʊ]) is an elven wizard who serves as Keeper of Scrolls and Archmage of the Librarium Incantatum in the city of Avalir. She is played by Marisha Ray.

Patia has clear, ivory skin and somewhat reflective, silvery white hair, threaded through a sun-ray-like fascinator. Around her neck is a rigid golden ring. She wears a collared, breasted coat that stretches down like a gown and has a silken, emerald green sheen. Underneath that is a dress, the color of which depends on how the light hits it: teal, blue, or indigo.

Protecting Avalir in its final hours, Patia touched the Tree of Names to learn its secrets, fusing her right arm with its glowing bark and severing it below her elbow.

"Patia is the epitome of 'boss bitch', who is prepared for anything – and if she isn't, she sure as hell isn't going to let you know that. ... She might be the walking embodiment of 'Fake it till ya make it.'"

Peaches is very big pegasus with a purple coat, pale blue wings, a long pink mane, and eyes in a gradient of pink, gold and blue. Her cutie mark is a half pink, half blue heart with wings. She speaks in a deep voice and carries a flute tied around her neck with a blue ribbon.

She is not very good with directions and cannot tell a lie. She needs to tell everyone how she's feeling at all times.

Peaches plays the flute and is in very high demands, having played for the two princesses before.

entities.name: Poogs
entities.description:
Poogs is a goblin associated with the The Re-Slayer's Take. He is played by George Primavera.

Poogs is a green goblin man who lacks the usual sharp teeth of his people, using instead a false set of very straight teeth.

He is a friendly man, even described as a "gentleman", empathetic and eager, and confident enough to talk about his fake teeth without complex.

Poogs came from the Utesspire Mountains, from a goblin community in which he acted as the squire of a wrathful combat medic. Since he wasn't happy with his life (and the only creature dear to him at home was a pet skull spider) he ran away, eventually finding Timpani Guff; although he tried to steal from him at first, the firbolg showed him only kindness, and eventually Poogs felt how his Curse of Strife was lifted because of it, so he thanked the druid with a cupcake. One of the first things he did after that was to replace his goblinoid teeth (which were already yellow and not very healthy) with straighter ones; he left his mouth without natural teeth, and the spellcaster (Duderonomous) sent him a set of straight human-looking teeth, although somewhat large for his small mouth, which caused him some difficulty in speaking. After that, he was just trying to get by after a very hard life, more peacefully, keeping his stabbing knife but swearing never to use it again. He stayed with Timpani while the firbolg was still trying to join the Slayer's Take, and although he supported him, his presence never made a difference in the druid's chances of entering the guild.

is a human blood hunter and a member of the Lorelei family. She was played by Laura Bailey in .

In her human form Portia looks like a woman of dark skin (although lighter than those of her two older siblings) with a soft purple hue (sign of her drow ancestry), dark eyes, and a mane of black hair that reaches a little past the shoulders and is white on the underside. She wears black and green clothes, dark purple lipstick, and tinted glasses.

In her werewolf form, Portia is two or three inches taller and muscular, covered in black fur on top with a stark white underside, resembling a skunk but with reversed patterns.

Portia is described as accomplished and driven. She was shown to be very headstrong, demanding to undergo the Taming two years early and charging into a large group of skeletons without knowing if she'd get reinforcements.

entities.name: Rajan Savarimuthu
entities.description:
is criss-crossed with scars and runic tattoos from his travels, a suave archaeologist. He is played by Noshir Dalal.

Rajan is almost six feet tall and scarred on one side of his face, with the other side covered in runic tattoos. He is always dressed head-to-toe in finery. He wears gloves whenever possible, and when he closed a door, he wiped his hand with a handkerchief afterwards. Rajan is brash and sometimes obnoxious. Beneath his fine jacket and shirt, he has a hive full of locusts built into his chest.

After he unleashed his insect swarm upon the Serious Man, Rajan's right eye began changing to resemble the black compound eye of an insect. Eventually, the transformation was complete and the eyelid fell off.

In his youth, Rajan's mother Vimala became very ill. The Serious Man saved her with Oldfairen artifacts, but his sister Atheka became the thrall of The Maw. In the form of a beautiful nun, Rahema, it offered the family comfort, allowing Rajan's sister to improve and giving the grieving family much hope. One night, Rajan followed his sister to a dark neighborhood in the city, finding her digging before she turned into something monstrous and attacked him. He tried to use a nursery rhyme to protect them, but fumbled a single word and saved only himself, losing his sister to The Maw, the monster that hid behind the nun's beautiful face.

entities.name: Ranthiel Volthor
entities.description:
Ranthiel Volthor is a human warlock and member of the Glorious Ones. He was played by Sam Richardson in .__TOC__

Ranthiel Volthor is a human with braided hair tied back with a blue headband and a cloak that covers a fine bit of hide armor. He is very sexy and charming, and loves to drink. A very young and naive Scanlan Shorthalt looked up to and admired his cavalier attitude and ability to pick up women, and tried to emulate him.

Ranthiel was in Drobanagos on the island of Athova-Rae at the time of the Musetide Festival some time prior to about 795 PD. There, he came to the aid of an Elder of the village who got involved in a bar room brawl, and along with several others, was hired to provide security for the festival. The group was approached by an apparent young woman who sought their aid rescuing her sister from a sea cave. Once there, the women revealed themselves as sirens attempting to perform a ritual to awaken and control a gargantuan, unconscious crab. The party killed the women and the crab, but later discovered the creature was a protective guardian of the town. To avoid unpleasantness, Ran joined Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe in taking ship for Tal'Dorei, with Dranzel being interested in having the warlock as their promoter.

At the beginning of , Ranthiel denied repeatedly that Bramble was his girlfriend, although they had apparently had some form of romantic encounter which he referred to as a "situation-ship". Throughout the episode, she continued to say he was her boyfriend and was in love with her, and he continued to deny it. He flirted back with Lygeia, the disguised siren, as they traveled, and the two made a date to meet after their quest was completed. However, when Ranthiel bisected Lygeia during the battle, he told her, "I've got a girlfriend," thrilling Bramble.

He wears a purple fedora with a pair of (presumably) race tickets sticking out of the hat band.

entities.description:
is a half-elf nurse and cleric played by Celia Rose Gooding in Exandria Unlimited: Divergence.

Rei'nia was young, with dark brown skin and silver white locs that she tried to keep from fusing. She saw herself as very observant, and tried to hide her intense hope that things would someday be different while keeping the workers functional as long as possible. She was naive enough to believe that she knew better than those who had been beaten down by years of experience.

In the years following the Divergence she became more confident, left her hair grow slightly longer, and started wearing silver, white, and blue clothes.

Rei'nia grew up during the Calamity with her younger sister Liana. They were both friends of Luz, a tiefling that shared stories about Sehanine the Moonweaver, causing them to develop their own personal beliefs connected to the goddess and Catha.

entities.description:
is a pious man who came to Deadwood to rebuild the local church. He is played by Travis Willingham.

Reverend Mason is described as "a big man" by Miriam Landisman. He has dark, shaggy, short hair, a 5 o'clock shadow, and a vertical scar on his right cheek. He wears a brimmed hat, a clerical collar, and a heavy leather coat given to him by Clayton Sharpe.

Reverend Mason is a deeply pious man, often turning to prayer when the strange and supernatural happenings of Deadwood become too much for him. He seems a little naive to the ways of outlaws and combat in general, with Miriam Landisman often needing to go out of her way to protect him. Reverend Mason seems kind and compassionate to everyone in Deadwood despite the camp's hostility, illegal activity and the occasional naysayer.

When the group were given their arcane abilities, the Reverend viewed it as a sign of God.

entities.description:
is an Aeormaton sorcerer/warlock played by Abubakar Salim in Downfall. He is a mortal avatar of the god Corellon, the Arch Heart.

SILAHA is beautiful, with a dark frame that is difficult to see where it begins and ends, like a painting sprinkled with golden freckles that occasionally move, and orange eyes that occasionally glow green. He holds himself regally, and moves more fluidly when he is among friends..}}

As the Chosen One, the golden freckles cover his whole body, and his eyes turn green.

He is a charismatic and socially savvy individual, well respected. He is vain, hedonistic, and enjoys attention and beauty in every form, but deep down he's sorrowful because of the knowledge that his godly self, the Arch Heart, is directly responsible for Aeor being so advanced and dangerous, causing the Aeormaton to even contemplate the possibility of giving up existence.

entities.name: Salty Pete
entities.description:
Salty Pete is a dwarven rogue and member of Vox Moronica, also known as the Good, the Rad, and the Nubbly. He is played by Dan Casey.

"So I'm Salty Pete, the First Mate of the Obsidian Helen. A sailor by trade. A scoundrel by nature. The captain gambled with the ship, so I fed him to a long beaked squid with razor sharp teeth. I've spent time on pontoons, cigarette boats, skiffs, whoring, snoring, and deploring across the land. I'm married to the sea, but me best friend is a hermit crab named Terrence. The only leftover I have from the Helen is her flag, which I wear like a cape.

I've bet many friends over a buttery glass of chardonnay, sailor's choice. But I've lost many more. If you step to me, you best come correct. I'm on a quest to reclaim the Helen. I play for pink slips. Looking for clues at the bottom of a glass, oh, you bet your ass I did. And now I fell in with a fell warlock named the Snugglelord.

Salty Pete strikes an imposing figure, wearing a battered leather jerkin and rich woolen pants to get him through those salty nights on the open seas. He has a velvet doublet "because you've gotta treat yourself right every now and then." He's never seen without his signature black cape, which was once upon a time the flag of the Obsidian Helen, the ship that he lusted after. He has a grizzled beard.

entities.name: Sarge
entities.description:
Sarge is a drummer, halfling ranger, and member of Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe who joined the Glorious Ones. He was played by Tony Hale in .

Sarge has platinum white hair and vari-colored eyes: one dark blue eye and one light blue. He is accompanied by an enormous white tiger named Ethel.

Sarge used to be the jester of the Uludan family of Nicodranas, and was very loved by them. Despite this, when one of the relatives of the marquis killed a merchant, during or before 790 PD, in order to avoid controversy, the family used Sarge as a scapegoat, forcing him to dye his hair and flee (and involuntarily causing the vengeful soul of the murdered to end up bound to the halfling). It was during his time as a fugitive that the ranger encountered Ethel, bonding with the tiger, which became his companion.

At some point before 795 PD Sarge was hired, along with other mercenaries, to protect the people of Drobaganos during the Musetide Festival. They became an adventuring group that the halfling dubbed "the Glorious Ones". Although initially there was a slight cautiousness with the group (and Bramble even used her Speak with Animals to ask Ethel if Sarge was a nice guy), eventually they warmed up and, while trying to help a local woman called Ligeia, Sarge shared his traumatic past in Nicodranas. While they were talking, the ranger noticed angelic chanting nearby, and found the Grove of Enlightenment, where there was a particularly impressive apple; although he was suspicious at first, he took it, and the fruit told him that it would grant him strength when he needed it. Shortly after some kobolds attacked the Glorious Ones, and when the fight was over Sarge saw the ghost of the murdered merchant that was haunting him.

entities.name: Scanlan Shorthalt
entities.description:
Scanlan Shorthalt is a gnome bard member of the group Vox Machina. He is played by Sam Riegel.

Scanlan spent a portion of his life travelling with Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe to support his single mother, Juniper. During his years of travel, he encountered a gnome named Sybil, who later gave birth to his daughter, Kaylie, without his knowledge. At one point, he witnessed his mother's death at the hands of a goblin.

During his adventures with Vox Machina, Scanlan came into possession of the legendary sword, Mythcarver, to fight the Chroma Conclave. After meeting his daughter and going through hard times, Scanlan left Vox Machina. He later returned and earned the blessing of Ioun, becoming the Champion of Ioun, to face Vecna.

"Oh, you haven't heard of Scanlan Shorthalt? Well, gird your loins, ladies, because he has his eye on you. A talented musician, master of disguise, and dashingly handsome in his own mind, Scanlan sings songs almost as much as he sings his own praises.

entities.name: Sean Finnerty
entities.description:
is a veteran of the recent war in Newfaire and a younger soldier. He is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Sean is currently in his mid 20s. His easily replaced clothing is clean, although the more expensive items (such as his suspenders and shoes) show more wear. Generally, he appears healthy and fit, but also clearly has no one to go home to.

Sean's mother is Margaret Mary Finnerty ("Peggy"), now an inmate at the Grayslate Sanitorium. Beatrix Monroe, an employee, visits her there regularly and brings Sean letters from her. Sean was Peggy's youngest son. His older brothers, Anthony and Jimmy, were closer in age. Anthony was a war hero even before the Last Great War, having taken a fort in a prior colonial conflict. Anthony was engaged to a woman beyond his station, Jane Windermere, an aristocrat, whose main suitor was another aristocrat named Nicholas Clyburn, whose father, General William Clyburn, transferred Anthony to another platoon, all of whom lost their lives in a battle where the artillery never showed up. Jimmy accused his commanding officer, Douglas Vanderfeld, of a conspiracy, before being court-martialed for espionage and executed. With both brothers dead, Sean returned to find his mother committed to Grayslate Sanatorium and his house seized.

Sean voluntarily and illegally enlisted in the war at a very young age (16 or 17). Both of his brothers were killed in the war.

entities.name: Septimus Goodfellow
entities.description:
Septimus Goodfellow was an actor masquerading as a celebrity spiritualist in the one-shot. He was played by Liam O'Brien.

Like the rest of the cast, Septimus is the spitting image of his actor, Liam O'Brien, with the only discernable difference being his garb. Septimus is depicted in a smart, white button-up with a cravat, overlayed by a black-and-grey striped vest and completed by a black tailcoat. The only adoring he appears to wear is a blue and silver pin on his left breast-pocket connected to a chain that crosses over his chest and under his right collar.

Septimus Goodfellow is the alias of the Irish charlatan Archie Orlick. He found fame masquerading as an English spiritualist, but he is in fact a fraud deep in debt. He carries a substantial debt to the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, an esoteric secret society whom he is implied to have defrauded at some point in the past.

Septimus was hired by Rupert Merriweather to retrieve a casket during a Cat Show at Crystal Palace. He ventured into Crystal Palace with Alexandra O'Neil, Captain Bentley Badger, Hanako Hayashi, Dr. Mason Pocket and Ida Codswell. He placed a bet that his cat would win the Cat Show, but only did so because he had previously bribed the judges to ensure that it would win.

is a Goblin in service of Sauron created for Critical Role One-Shot: Shadow of War – Part 1 and 2. is played by Travis Willingham.

As a small and weak Goblin trying to survive in Greater Mordor, Skak has learned to use crossbows and alchemy experiments to defeat larger, more ferocious creatures. His magical abilities are flavored as alchemical devices.

As a 5th-level Arcane Trickster, Skak knows three wizard cantrips and four 1st-level spells from the wizard spell list.

entities.name: Skreev
entities.description:
was a slyborne human nightwalker rogue played by Liam O'Brien in Age of Umbra.

Skreev was a very gaunt, very tall and pale human man with scraggly white hair, one side shaved, wrapped in leather and black cloth strips except for a diamond-shaped window revealing a large silver ring threaded through the skin of his chest. Smaller rings were similarly threaded in his arms. He maintained a scrunched and skulking stance at most times. His leather hand wraps or gloves had iron claws protruding from them.

He displayed an erratic, chaotic, and extravagant behavior. However, he also had moments of unusual sweetness and formality, especially around Adelia. He seemed to have a sense of balance and compensation, treating others as he was treated and expecting the same in return. Despite his past psychological and physical trauma he tried to weaponize those feelings and sensations, owning his pain as a way of feeling in control.

Skreev used to live in Amber Reach, where he was abused and tortured by Farrah of the Ruby Crown, one of the Damask Queens. One day, in the ruins beneath the city, he met Adelia, a young girl who had been left alone and had been hiding there; he became her friend, protector, and "pet", and they started traveling together. Around a year later and about a week before the events of Age of Umbra, the two of them attended a revival meeting held by Sanctifar the Enlightened, a "holy man", and witnessed how he and his allies tricked people to join them and then allegedly killed them. Apparently to silence Adelia and Skreev, the Enlightened locked them up in cages, not far from Volkoru.

entities.name: Skullcrusher Bloodforge
entities.description:
, better known as Sky, is a halfling teenage barbarian and wizard apprentice, and one of the campers attending Wildemount Wildlings. She is played by Eden Riegel.

Sky is a short (2' 8") halfling girl with curly red hair and a naturally muscular built. She wears glasses and a cape, and carries her spellbook everywhere.

She rejects her natural anger and idealizes the possibility of using magic instead of violence to solve problems.

Skullcrusher was born in about 829 PD, and grew up in Othe as a member of the violent Bloodforge family, known for their barbarians. When she was about 10 years old, she saw some bullies bothering a little girl and breaking her unicorn figurine; before Sky had time to react, the bullies left, and she saw a wizard approach the child, comforting her and using a spell to summon an actual unicorn to protect her. Since then, Sky decided she wanted to be a wizard, rejecting the violent tradition of her own family, and in 844 PD she was sent to the Wildemount Wildlings camp. Although she was very willing to become a wizard there, the process of learning magic was rather slow, and her strength sometimes worked against her, making her break wands while she tried to use them. She and Jessep Nimblethorp became friends, and during a race in which both of them were doing pretty badly, they came up with a song about a zorbo that helped Jessep's anxiety.

entities.name: Slaughter Grimm
entities.description:
is an argonian necromancer who serves as waiter at the Dreary Jug (later renamed Grelnok's Skull), which he owns collectively with Grelnok, Hoa, Mallory, and Tavima. He is played by Sam Riegel in the Elder Scrolls Online: Blackwood trilogy.

Slaughter is an argonian and is referred to by customers as a "lizard". He has reddish and blue scales and yellow eyes. At first his body was covered all over in sharp spines; these are normally lost on a fifty-year cycle by argonians, but the traumatic experience of "Death & Taxes" caused Slaughter to prematurely molt, so that by "A Faulty Foundation" he no longer had any spines.

Slaughter is excitable, exuberant, and polite. He often stammers in his eagerness to please others or to do well at a task.

Slaughter Grimm was raised in a multi-generational family of necromantic torturers who worked for "despots and tyrants". His father is Massacre Grimm, and his mother Felony Grimm-Lebowitz; they work as semi-retired freelancers. He has two siblings, brother Homicide and sister Agony. Unlike his family, he finds no pleasure in torture and has instead pursued his "dream" of working in the food service industry. He has described himself as "on the outs" with his family.

entities.description:
was a ridgeborne faun ranger played by Sam Riegel in Age of Umbra.

Snyx was a young, lanky faun resembling a mountain goat, with one of his horns broken off. After traveling a lot through natural spaces he had started "collecting" beetles that stayed on his person.

He was kind and curious, but not very brave, and felt safer when surrounded by strong people. He also had some youthful pride that made him boast about dangerous situation to cause a better impression.

Snyx used to be a member of the Phantom Stride, a group in Amber Reach that made dangerous deliveries for Ash Lord Agu-Vathala. However, at some point Snyx stole a package from him and never returned, so he kept moving to avoid the assassin he knew would be sent after him. E8|7:55|Age of Umbra: The Tomb of the Heretic Saint}}

entities.name: Taryon Darrington
entities.description:
Taryon Gary Darrington is a human artificer, former member of Vox Machina, and founder of the Darrington Brigade. He was played by Sam Riegel.

Taryon is a handsome human male with shoulder-length, feathered, dirty blonde hair. He has blue-green eyes and a well-groomed goatee adorning his dashing smirk. His frame is svelte and he is adorned in a set of polished immaculate breastplate armor that looks to be barely used, with numerous satchels all around him as well as jewelry and adornments. He has a silver helmet that shines with many embedded gems, including diamonds and opals.

By 826 PD (roughly a decade after the Darrington Brigade was first founded), Tary's once-golden hair is cut short and shows signs of graying, but despite being over 40 he always claims he is closer to 33. Taryon's adventuring gear shows signs of use - his golden armor and Rod of Mercurial Form have scuff marks and his Robe of Useful Items have largely been used up, with the used spaces being replaced with commemorative patches like "Kill a Dragon".

Tary's somewhat more youthful appearance is due to his injection of an unspecified "bovine toxin" into his face.

(pronounced "tuh-VEE-muh") is a redguard templar who serves as bouncer at the Dreary Jug (later renamed Grelnok's Skull), which she owns collectively with Grelnok, Hoa, Mallory, and Slaughter. She is played by Aabria Iyengar in The Elder Scrolls Online: Blackwood miniseries.

Tavima is large and muscular. She has dark skin, and a scar runs across her right eye. She wears a fluffy red hair tie and a "weird ruffly outfit" that she despises. In her role as bouncer, she regrets that she is legally not allowed to carry a sword.

Tavima is intimidating, aggressive, and hungry for a fight. Despite similarities to Grelnok, she seems to be friendlier and less careless.

Tavima considers Grelnok to be her best friend.

entities.name: Teor Pridesire
entities.description:
is a nama paladin played by Travis Willingham in Campaign Four.

Teor is very tall and powerfully built, and has a tattoo running up his upper-left arm. He has dark silver fur and a braided mane. He wears a golden breastplate with purple vestments and cape (hiding many pockets), along with a shield on his back. He carries a giant, heavy, golden flail and more recently, the Bracers of Oak and Birch and a double-headed axe originally given by Ingrid Einfasen to Sir Julien Davinos, who loaned it to Teor..

Loza described Teor as "loyal, shrewd and a fine warrior". Teor is very protective of his friends and comrades, yelling for them to take cover while in battle and disregarding his own safety and well-being to heal them.

Travis Willingham described Teor as having been "the shield for so many people for so many years, it's second nature to him. What happens if there isn't anyone else left to protect? What does that mean for Teor?" Teor felt a great deal of guilt for not having been in town when Thjazi Fang was executed because he realized how much it would have taken for that to happen, and that there must be massive machinations at work. "Teor is wondering what will he be able to do in order to put a claw on the scales of justice." Campaign 4 Ep 1-4 Recap]" | vod=https://youtu.be/hdLPwuKMlIY | 09:31}}

entities.name: Thaisha Lloy
entities.description:
(pronounced TIE-sha /[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English `taɪʃə]/) is an orc druid of the Circle of Ancients played by Aabria Iyengar in Campaign Four.

Thaisha is 6'4" tall and appears to be in her mid-to-late 30s due to her aging being slower than normal, with desaturated green skin and long, curly, dark (but graying) hair. Her eyes are completely black with red-ringed silver irises. The tips of her fingers are red and black, with metallic ends on each of her nails and a red decorative pattern on her hands. She wears fine clothing with those same colors, associated with her family. In one of her ears she has a steel spine piercing through two different points. She also has visible metal plates where her vertebrae are, and they seem to warm up and turn red hot when she's angry or tense.

She is honest, fierce, and ferociously protective and maternal toward those she considers family. She is also very proud of her status as a Lloy. She hopes "that she can heal the lands that were damaged by the death of the Shapers, and in so doing, lead the world and the people who still miss the weight and heft of divinity to realize that that's always existed within the world and within themselves." When she returns home, she's always surprised "by how much her family has changed without her, and feels the disconnect between her mission and the thing she gave up to pursue it." Campaign 4 Ep 1-4 Recap]" | vod=https://youtu.be/hdLPwuKMlIY | 08:26}} She tends to be more cheery around nature, and whenever she leaves the city, she spends a brief period of "mourning" for a couple of days leaving behind the personality she displays around her friends and family there.

Having been born as part of a remarkable family and being in a position of influence as a druid of the Circle of Ancients, Thaisha has never had the need to lie about herself and isn't very skilled at it; moreover, the combination of her good intentions and her privilege creates in her a certain expectation that people will be nice to her. Her biggest flaw is that she believes that her wisdom makes her able to see and understand everything perfectly regardless of perspective. Episode 2 Discussing Up To C4E18|1:33:39}}

entities.name: The Emissary
entities.description:
→ This article is about the character in Downfall. For the Unseelie representative in Campaign Three, see Cashadoor.

was an earth genasi barbarian played by Noshir Dalal in Downfall. He was the herald of the goddess Erathis, the Lawbearer.

The Emissary was brought aboard the skyship Venatoria in a crate in the back of Asha's supply wagon. When the crate was opened, the group of gods saw a slab of ice-covered stone that appeared to pour out and pool at Asha's feet. A light built in the stone and a massive icy figure slowly took shape, with no mouth or eyes, and rocky plates like a carapace over his shoulders and chest. The ice forming the figure appeared windswept. The Emissary was about eight feet tall. On his chest there were Celestial runes carved by the Lawbearer herself, symbolizing "refusal," "abjurance," "denial," or "no."

When The Emissary took form after being inside a crate for transport, the gods in mortal form surrounding him could feel his loss, confusion, and heartbreak. When the Emissary saw Asha, however, the confusion subsided. The behavior and vocabulary of the herald was simplistic, but despite his child-like innocence he was good at reading people. Only after he died did he became more eloquent, while still retaining a behavior that showed how young he was.

entities.name: The Owlbear
entities.description:
is a human barbarian/rogue and a member of the Darrington Brigade. He is played by Taliesin Jaffe.

As of 826 PD, the Owlbear was a human man in his late 30s. When he arrived at the Darrington Estate he clearly hadn't shaved in a few days. He wears an Owlbear cowl with a brown tunic underneath and brown boots. Multiple daggers dangle from his belt and he wields two claw-like weapons in each hand. His mask has apparently two overlapping pieces, one for the owl and the other for the bear.

The Owlbear is a "serious and brooding" figure.

In 826 PD, Taryon Darrington welcomed the Owlbear at his estate in Deastok inviting him to contest for the position in the Darrington Brigade. The Owlbear went first, paired with Farriwen Breeze. Farriwen used her dope monk shit to knock out the Owlbear handily. At the end of her duel, Hazel Copperpot healed her opponent (Buddy) and the Owlbear.

entities.name: Tiberius Stormwind
entities.description:
Tiberius Stormwind was a dragonborn sorcerer and a former member of Vox Machina. He was played by Orion Acaba.

"Greetings and salutations. I am Tiberius Stormwind. I hail from a town called Tyriex, located in the heart of Draconia, born from a politically respected family.

At the age of 15, I succeeded in passing the Sorcerer's Rite, showing prodigy-like control of my magic. The judges and the Draconian high council were amazed at how powerful my spells were for how long I had been training. At 20 years old, I was the youngest appointed member of the magic guild in Draconian history. For the next few years, I almost went mad from the malaise of being a guild member, as it's rather boring.

However, one day I happened upon a chamber, unused for quite some time. In the room were stacks of books and maps of the surrounding cities and areas around the known world. For months I would frequent the chamber, and learned of artifacts from legend. After a long period of research, I made a list of artifacts that caught my eye. I brought these findings to the high council and was told that all of the information in the chamber I stumbled upon was either believed to be fiction or unsolvable mysteries and hence were lost forever. I found those answers to be unacceptable.

entities.name: Timpani Guff
entities.description:
Timpani Guff is a firbolg associated with the The Re-Slayer's Take. He is played by Nick Williams.

Timpani is a robust firbolg man, with skin covered with bluish hair, red-headed, and with a lush mustache of the same color. He has gained weight in the last century, and in the recent battles he has lost a couple of teeth.

He is a cheerful man, bumbling and sincere, and described as a "crackpot", with a certain sense of spectacle.

Timpani came from the Dwendalian Empire, but he traveled to Vasselheim and tried to join the Slayer's Take at some point before 636 PD, failing because he didn't have the right skills. He tried multiple times, unsuccessfully, with the last attempt being around 739 PD, period during which he visited Shoresight Isle when he was still "in school" and with ties with the guild; there he befriended Duderonomous. After returning to Issylra and being rejected again, he chose to live a life of isolation, traveling to many places, although keeping an apartment in Vasselheim where he was occasionally joined by hia cousin Pumat Sol, who visited last around 829 PD. He, however, ended up noticing strange phenomena involving monsters once defeated by the guild, so he started taking notes about the subject to show it to them, although he wasn't believed, making him suspect they knew something and were covering it. He met Gurt Stumpstuck during this time, and together they designed a magical way to access the dwarf's bog, using a specific tree with a special password, and protecting it against non-magical damage. At one point, while traveling through the Utesspire Mountains, he met Poogs, a goblin who had ran away from his community; although the latter tried to steal from him, Timpani showed him only kindness, which caused the Curse of Strife to be lifted. Very thankful, Poogs gave him a cupcake, and they became friends.

entities.name: Toby
entities.description:
Toby is a given name in many English-speaking countries. The name is derived the Middle English vernacular form of Tobias. Tobias itself is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew טוביה Toviah, which translates to Good is Yahweh. Yahweh is the name of the Jewish God.

It is also used as a contraction of Tobin, an Irish surname now also used as a forename.

The name is traditionally masculine, but has also been in use for women since the 19th century.

entities.name: Trinket
entities.description:
Trinket is a bear played by Matthew Mercer in and . He is a parody version of the bear Trinket featured in the canonical Critical Role series. Trinket's appearance in the first two Honey Heist games, as well as his co-stars', have the characters resemble the ensemble of the Ocean's film trilogy, starring George Clooney. Trinket himself resembles Clooney's character, Danny Ocean.

Trinket is nearly identical to his appearance in Campaign One: Vox Machina.

Trinket's history mostly remains the same as in Campaign One: Vox Machina, up until two years after the defeat of the Chroma Conclave. He is a member of Vox Machina, saviors of Tal'Dorei and beyond, and has picked up the skills of a thief from his owners Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia.

On the day of the annual Hazel Festival, Vex, knowing full well of Trinket's love of honey and how he had cleared out the Slayer's Cake honey stash the previous two festivals, leads him away from the festival and towards the edges of the Bramblewood Forest. There, he meets three bears, Peddy Tuxpin, Cookie, and Waffle, and a honey badger named Liam Las Vegas, and the five proceed to come up with a heist to steal the honey from the Hazel Festival using both their skills and Trinket's knowledge of the festival.

entities.name: Trist
entities.description:
is a human paladin/cleric played by Ashley Johnson in Downfall. She is a mortal avatar of the goddess Sarenrae, the Everlight.

Trist is an ordinary-looking human woman in her late thirties with greying dark brown auburn hair, tanned and freckled skin, and kind eyes. When first seen, she was wearing her husband's very large overcoat.

Trist is gentle and kind, although she also encourages smart naughtiness, as a teacher and a mother. She has some difficulty trusting people.

After the main Exandrian pantheon agreed to collaborate in a plan to neutralize Aeor and their potentially dangerous technology, the Everlight agreed to do her part, and less than four decades before their intended mission she was born as a mortal human girl, Trist. She grew up and eventually became a teacher and met Amaris, a firbolg that would become her husband and the father of her two children, Haylie and Topher. Her husband may have been aware of her connection with the divine, agreeing for her to go on the mission to Aeor believing she would return in a few days. By then the family had kept a teenager boy with them for some time: Ayden, the mortal incarnation of Pelor, who after spending some time with Trist and realizing who she was decided to become a cleric of the Everlight.

Trixie loves inventing the best gadgets ever. She really wants to be a caped crusader superpony and help everybody.

entities.name: Tyranny
entities.description:
is a demon warlock played by Whitney Moore in Campaign Four.

Tyranny is a beautiful woman standing at 5'3" (not including the horns). She has bubblegum-colored skin, white hair with blunt bangs, goat-like ears with a single silver arrow piercing, a forked tongue, long tail ending in a heart-shaped spade, hooves, and yellow goat-like eyes. She wears teal and white ruffled vestments that mark her as an Aspirant to the Candescent Creed of the House of Halovar. She has a distinctive and interesting odor somewhat like warm chocolate chip cookies mixed with sulphur.

Tyranny claims to always be honest, but being brand-new to Aramán's plane of existence is totally unaware of social norms and has little concept of morality. She is extremely sociable, and loves meeting new people.

Whitney Moore described her as: "Tyranny is just a girl in the world trying her best and she's very led by impulse. Tyranny is the most unfiltered version of myself, horny and sad, period. Aramán for her, it's a feast for the senses. It's unlimited opportunities of things to experience, both good and bad. Every demon represents a certain ancient archetypal energy. Tyranny does not know what that is inside of her. It is something that isn't quite sitting right with her, but it is one of those drives that is going to be pretty impossible to ignore." Campaign 4 Ep 1-4 Recap]" | vod=https://youtu.be/hdLPwuKMlIY |05:26}} Despite her confidence in other areas she is notably sensitive about this, being particularly affected when she's being judged for impulses she cannot control.

entities.name: Ulfgar Fireforge
entities.description:
Ulfgar Fireforge is a dwarven fighter and member of Vox Moronica. He is played by Ify Nwadiwe.

"Yo, dis is Ulfgar Fireforge. I'm a sellsword, ex-pit fighter. I'm slow to trust and quick to kill. Money talks, bullshit walks. Just so ya'll know, I'm in it for the money and I play a mean flute that's sharpened at the end. If you get too close, I might stab you in the neck. Just know, I'll do anything for a buck. Anything."

Ulfgar has a grayish stone skin and "a Kimbo Slice beard going on." He wears an iron chain around his neck at all times over his chainmail, and carries a stein with brass knuckles as the handle. He always wears his gold sack out, "so people know how much money I'm rocking with."

Ulfgar often points out that he will do anything for money, and will put his or other people's lives in jeopardy while searching for money.

Revvetha "Veth" Brenatto (née Smyt'hh) is a halfling rogue/wizard and a member of the Mighty Nein. She took on the anagrammatic name Nott the Brave for a period of about two years while cursed into the form of a goblin girl. She is played by Sam Riegel.

Originally, Nott was a halfling woman named Veth Brenatto, who had a plump face, dark skin, and braided hair.

As a goblin, Nott had green skin, green hair, and yellow eyes. Her clothes were not in great condition, much like her traveling companion, Caleb. She hid her face with a hood and a porcelain mask. Nott was three feet tall. In , she got an aquamarine tattoo highlighting her eyes and temples.

In , Nott regained her halfling form and began using her original name, Veth Brenatto, though she retained the piercings and tattoos she acquired as Nott.
