entities.name: Wicander Halovar
entities.description:
Wicander "Wick" Halovar is an aasimar sorcerer played by Sam Riegel in Campaign Four.

Wicander is a beautiful man, 5'11" tall. He has teal and white hair and pearlescent shimmering tattoos made with Filament covering about half of his face. He wears teal and white robes and carries a cane with the symbol of the Candescent Creed. According to Thimble his teeth look bigger up close.

Although he is a member of one of the foremost Sundered Houses of Dol-Makjar, Wicander is generally unsure of himself, nervous, and has led a somewhat sheltered life.

Sam Riegel described Wicander as "an acolyte of the Light, a true believer, a fancy lad, and in way over his head. Wick had really been drinking the Kool-Aid with all things Candescent Creed, and to be told the origins are not what he thought they were was a shock, to learn that his family and his grandmother had actively and knowingly betrayed him for his whole life was shocking, but mostly I think he was just scared and confused. How can so much goodness come from such a monstrous source? He's slowly realizing that his name, which he's worn with pride for his whole life, it's not a crutch, but it is a weight." Campaign 4 Ep 1-4 Recap]" | vod=https://youtu.be/hdLPwuKMlIY | 04:22}}

Xarlo Grandall is a simiah seraph and a member of the Menagerie, a small group of adventurers. He is played by Liam O'Brien.

Xarlo is a 4 feet tall simiah with orangish brown fur (with a shock of white in the head), a regal-looking mustache, and a very active tail. He wears pants and satchels going diagonally across his chest.

Xarlo is a fun and kind man, very fond of animals, who likes acting on impulse.

Xarlo was a worshiper of Ondra who lived in isolation, interacting only with animals, until the ranger Wild Cullen encouraged him to seek connection. That, among other reasons, led the simiah to team up with the Menagerie and become an adventurer.

entities.name: Yasha Nydoorin
entities.description:
Yasha Nydoorin is an aasimar barbarian and member of the Mighty Nein. She is played by Ashley Johnson.

Yasha Nydoorin is a 5'11" tall, muscular woman with very pale skin. When she joined the Mighty Nein, her matted hair was black fading to white as it reached the tips, and was styled with various dreads and braids. When she used her Necrotic Shroud, her eyes and the parts of her hair that were white both turned jet black, and her wings were black and skeletal. Her clothes were slightly tattered and she was a bit of a mess. Yasha has heterochromia, with one eye being light greenish-blue and the other violet. She wears a symbol of the Stormlord on her waist. She is rarely seen without her dark-blue shawl, which she never takes off.

After a series of visions from the Stormlord, Yasha's formerly skeletal black wings became full and feathered, and capable of brief flight. A few days later, Caduceus noticed that her black hair was returning to its former silver-white color at the roots. By the time of the Nein's excursion into Eiselcross, her hair has returned to its silver-white coloration. According to Ashley Johnson, Yasha does not know that she is an aasimar, believing that she is just "weird".

After Traveler Con, Yasha received an enchanted tattoo from Orly Skiffback that stretches from behind her left ear to the tip of her left middle finger. The tattoo is a two-toned green color, the deep verdant hue of emerald dust and the lighter shade of residuum, that features various vines and flowers woven around large runes spelling out "Orphanmaker".

entities.name: Zerxus Ilerez
entities.description:
is a paladin who served as First Knight of the city of Avalir. He is played by Luis Carazo.

Zerxus was 6 feet tall and muscular, with broad shoulders. He has medium tan-brown skin, amber eyes, and dark, wavy hair.

Zerxus has a troubled expression, and sometimes emptiness behind his amber eyes. The death of his husband Evandrin has weighed heavily on him, and that, coupled with the extremely isolated life of The First Knight, has resulted in "an often stoic and serious Zerxus, whose demeanor is most often softened by the humor of his long time friend Nydas."

Originally from a town near Cathmoíra, some time prior to the events of Exandria Unlimited: Calamity Zerxus met and married the love of his life Evandrin. Evandrin had arrived in Cathmoíra with his infant son, Elias, who looked like a younger version of his father, and rose to become First Knight of Avalir, a title given to a legendary hero tasked with slaying monstrous threats and defending the city. During that time Zerxus trained in the Hall of Prophecy, where he learned healing magic and befriended Sofyra, a future oracle; he had oracle leanings himself, but wasn't aware of it, focusing more on the martial field.

entities.description:
Dockmaster Abban is in charge of the docks of Emon. As an NPC, Abban is played by Matthew Mercer.

Abban has dark reddish-brown skin. He is shaved completely bald with no facial hair, and has piercing blue-gray eyes. When Vox Machina met him, he wore a billowing white shirt, well tailored pants, and mid-rise boots.

Abban was noted for a his bright white smile, and greeted Vox Machina with an air of charisma and mild impatience. He was friendly and cordial with a dry sense of humor, but had a matter-of-fact attitude towards any business-related conversations.

Vox Machina encountered Abban while seeking a ship to escort them to Vesrah in order to complete Keyleth's Aramenté. Abban referred the party to Captain Adella.

His name is synonymous with generosity and business savvy; Abdar's Promenade, a marketplace district in Emon, was named after him. The street has been mentioned on-stream multiple times, but Abdar himself has neither been mentioned nor appeared on Critical Role.

entities.name: Abrianna Mirimm
entities.description:
Skysybil is an ancient goblin in the court of the Bright Queen. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Abrianna is a withered, ancient, elder female goblin with strings of hair that dangle down two and a half feet almost to her toes, wrapped in wrinkled and billowing dark blue and black robes. In The Tales of Exandria: The Bright Queen, she is depicted with clear eyes, and white hair. Her hair, though still long, is shorter than described in the campaign and goes down to her mid-back. She paints her face in vertical lines crossing over her eyes and horizontal lines outlining her chin, and she has numerous earrings, including plugs and ear cuffs.

Abrianna is a trustworthy woman who patiently guides many Kryn teenagers through the process of anamnesis. She is understanding and empathetic, and fights for those causes that she considers just.

Abrianna is titled "Skysybil", and is an important figure in the court of the Bright Queen. She has lived nearly as long as the Bright Queen, through several lives, and she is the Keeper of the History. The Bright Queen looks to her on matters of lore. In her most recent reincarnation, less than a century ago, the Skysybil was reborn as a goblin, and despite the respect she commands, she has also become an object of ridicule in some court circles. This experience, far from embittering her, has given her a greater perspective and she has become an advocate for goblinkin rights on the Lucid Bastion council.

entities.description:
. The transcript for this episode alternately spells the name "Acastrial" or "Acastriel", unlike the previous episode, in which it is spelled consistently "-el".}} was one of the angelic lieutenants of the Dawnfather who fought in the Calamity and abandoned his god during the divine truce.

Acastriel is about seven-and-a-half feet or eight feet tall, and gorgeous.

Acastriel was one of the solars who acted as the lieutenants of Pelor at the beginning of the Calamity. However, when the gods stopped fighting and reached a truce, this angel learned about their plans of incarnating as mortal avatars to infiltrate Aeor. After sharing this information with other angels, Acastriel and other divine servants, equally disappointed in the way their leaders were handling the war, decided to abandon the cause of the pantheon, traveling to Aeor and giving them information. In that process he received the subtle assistance of the disguised avatar of Asmodeus, who gave him a glass emblem containing the sealed avatar of Ioun, after which the Betrayer himself, through his illusion of Father Milo Cowst, shared rumors and gossip about the angel with the other avatars. That same day Acastriel and one of his followers, Garathran, met in the Ars Elysia, and barely twenty minutes after the solar left, SILAHA and Emhira (avatars of Corellon and the Raven Queen) found Garathran and interrogated him about Acastriel and his cause.

Later that same day the solar was protecting the Factorum Malleus with Adamar Cadrow and Selena Erenves when SILAHA approached them to speak with the latter. Acastriel, suspicious, used his powers to determine that the Aeormaton was, in fact, one of the mortal avatars that had infiltrated the city, and a battle ensued. During the fight, the very angered angel didn't hold back, attacking Ayden and cursing the Dawnfather, and trying to kill Emhira, without success. When SILAHA cast Meteor Swarm, his spell caused a lot of deaths, including Acastriel's.

entities.name: Acek Orattim
entities.description:
Acek Orattim was a priest of Tharizdun, the Chained Oblivion, during the Age of Arcanum and the Calamity. He has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

During the Age of Arcanum, Orattim made his base in Gatshadow Mountain, under which the Chained Oblivion had been imprisoned since the Founding. The priest channeled Tharizdun's power, causing Gatshadow to grow notably in height compared to the other Cliffkeep Mountains and grow a maze of tunnels within. From Gatshadow, Orattim spread his evil corruption until the Chained Oblivion's defeat by Pelor, the Dawnfather. The Chained Oblivion retreated to the mountain, but was chased by the Dawnfather, who shackled and banished Tharizdun beneath Gatshadow. Acek was rumored to be so suffused with his master's power that his master's divine banishment tore the priest's body apart.

One suggested scenario in the Critical Role: Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting, set in 812 PD, is for a supposed Vecna cultist known as the Nameless to flee to Gatshadow after stealing her master's "secret knowledge", seeking the spirit of Acek Orattim.

Category:Followers of the Chained Oblivion Category:Priests
entities.short_description: Acek Orattim was a priest of Tharizdun, the Chained Oblivion, during the Age of Arcanum and the Calamity. He has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Adamar Cadrow
entities.description:
Prince Chancellor Adamar Cadrow was one of the archmages of the city of Aeor, and one of the three lead designers of the Factorum Malleus. As an NPC, Adamar was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Adamar was a very influential figure in the city of Aeor as the Prince Chancellor of the Cogence. He was also one of three archmages who held enough knowledge of the Factorum Malleus project to be able to recreate it.

Umleta recorded a meeting between two archmages, Adamar and Primarch Selena Erenves, and celestial forces led by Acastriel. The celestial explains the gods' plan to them and the recording shows the moment they learn the Obtenebrator has been destroyed and that the Factorum Malleus is in danger with Acastriel insisting the group must move to trigger the weapon quickly. The watching mortal avatars of the gods realize they must act immediately.

Adamar then joined the Aeorian forces in defense of the Factorum Malleus at the heart of the machine. During the ensuing brutal battle, he used Wish to cast Finger of Death, and even though S.I.L.A.H.A. succeeds on his save, the mortal avatar took massive damage. Later in the battle, S.I.L.A.H.A. cast Meteor Swarm which Adamar's failed to Counterspell; S.I.L.A.H.A. then successfully Counterspelled Selena's Counterspell. While Selena is badly injured by this spell, both Adamar and Acastriel are killed and three upper wards of the Latimus Princeps fail which turned the tide of battle in favor of the gods.
entities.short_description: Prince Chancellor Adamar Cadrow was one of the archmages of the city of Aeor, and one of the three lead designers of the Factorum Malleus. As an NPC, Adamar was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Adeen Tasithar
entities.description:
is a drow male, formerly the Taskhand for the Bright Queen's court. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

When Fjord talked to him in the Dungeon of Penance, he was bloody and beaten, with one eye swollen nearly shut and his hair tattered and matted. He wore tattered, ragged Rosohna-style clothing, very costly at one point but now torn and dirtied.

Adeen was allegedly captured in the Ghostlands while fleeing the city of Rosohna after the defeat of Obann and the disappearance of Vence Nuthaleus. While he had confessed to giving two Luxon Beacons to the Dwendalian Empire and being involved in the Angel of Irons cult, he was terribly confused, saying that he had done these things, but he didn't remember how or why. He recognized Vence (being impersonated by Fjord), but didn't know how. He said he felt as if he were going crazy, and knocked himself out banging his head against the wall. The party was convinced he was the victim of some form of mind control, but was unclear as to who had done it to him, and how.

On the night of the party before the Mighty Nein set sail to the peace talks between the Dwendalian Empire and the Kryn Dynasty, Essek Thelyss confessed that it was he who gave the two beacons to the Empire, in return for their promise to share their research and knowledge with him.
entities.short_description: is a drow male, formerly the Taskhand for the Bright Queen's court. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Adelaide Bluebutton
entities.description:
Adelaide Bluebutton was the grandmother of Devan Bluebutton. As an NPC, she was played by the Dungeon Master, Liam O'Brien, in .

"This is Adelaide Bluebutton, better known as the Shrew. Adelaide is a rather successful businesswoman here in Emon. She buys and sells exotic curiosities from all the far-flung corners of the world, mostly on the black market. Oh, and she's really good at money laundering, too, which the Clasp would know; they've used her extensively in the past. Had a bit of a falling-out in recent months, though. The Clasp invited her to join them, but Adelaide wasn't interested, and with her business growing the way it was-- well, the Clasp prefers people they can control. And by the way, if you're by any chance wondering how she came by the moniker "The Shrew," she earned it. Bluebutton is as mean a son of a bitch as you will ever meet. A visiting merchant once tried to get the drop on her and steal her wares. She ripped his arms off without lifting a finger. But a mark is a mark, and Spireling Shenn wants something specific. Earlier this year, Adelaide acquired an emerald as big as a cantaloupe: Tagmut's Eye. Priceless. That is a substantial amount of capital that the Clasp could bend to its purposes. That's where these guys come in."

Category:Articles needing appearance verification

entities.name: Adelaine
entities.description:
is a barmaid in The Nestled Nook Inn. As an NPC she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Adelaine has red hair that she keeps pulled back with a bit of fabric.

Not much is known of her, though she is always polite in her interactions with the Mighty Nein. She likes patrons that order a Trost with their breakfast, and if asked, will choose a Von Brandt among the ales they have on offer.

entities.name: Adella
entities.description:
Captain Adella is the captain of the Drensala Vis. As an NPC, Adella is played by Matthew Mercer.

Adella is a dark-skinned woman with a long mass of dark hair, crimped, curled, and tattered by the sea air. Her hair has been sun-bleached to the point where the tips are lighter. When Vox Machina encountered her, she looked spry and young, probably in her late twenties or early thirties. Her skin was weathered from the days spent at sea, with crow's feet beginning to form at her eyes, but she had a bright smile. She wore a light brown coat that hung just past her calf-high boots.

Twenty years later, she had long wild graying sea-tattered hair and dark wrinkled skin. She still wore a calf-length light brown coat.

The Marquesian name of her ship and her darker complexion suggest that she may originate from Marquet, but this has never been confirmed. Also, Adella has a Tal'Dorei accent as opposed to a Marquesian one.
entities.short_description: Captain Adella is the captain of the Drensala Vis. As an NPC, Adella is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Adon Zeenoth
entities.description:
Zeenoth is a delicate-looking elven male with shoulder-length, curled, blond hair.

In The Mighty Nein, he is a stout older elf, with grey hair and a thick beard.

Around 833 PD, Zeenoth was bribed by Thoreau Lionett to kidnap Beauregard Lionett and take her to the Cobalt Soul.

During the carnival of curiosities zombie incident, Law Master Norda called upon Archivist Zeenoth to help identify from what sort of entity the head of Kylre had come, which he later confirmed was indeed a nergaliid from the far east.
entities.short_description: Zeenoth is a delicate-looking elven male with shoulder-length, curled, blond hair.

entities.name: Adra
entities.description:
Adra is the owner of the Iron Hearth Tavern in the upper district of Kraghammer. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Adra is a dwarven woman whom Vox Machina first seen behind the bar of her tavern with a towel over one arm.

Adra seems to be very strict when it comes to her business, as her all-male staff of barkeeps looked to be run ragged.

Shortly after Vox Machina entered the Iron Hearth Tavern, Vax'ildan pulled out a sack of gold and called out to the bartender to buy a round for everyone in the room. All eyes turned to Adra, who was standing behind the bar and staring at Vax in confusion. After a short pause she loudly praised the half-elf's generosity and announced the round to the room. Vax asked her to bring an entire cask of ale for Grog and Adra went off to the back room to retrieve one. She returned a moment later and began passing out drinks.
entities.short_description: Adra is the owner of the Iron Hearth Tavern in the upper district of Kraghammer. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Advik
entities.description:
() is a human man who runs Advik's Wandering Curiosities and Collections in Elder's Post. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Advik is a thin human man with black hair, which he wears side-parted and slicked back into a long ponytail. He has a thin pencil mustache which extends beyond the corners of his mouth, and good posture. When the Bells Hells first met him, he wore a button-down shirt with a weatherbeaten cloak over it.

Advik is somewhat theatrical in his interactions, and tells long anecdotes about how he procured the items he has for sale.

Some time ago, Advik claimed to have walked in the outskirts of the Heartmoor of Oderan Wilds and met a young herbalist named Amarash. After a night of drinks, he began to regale Advik with the tales of his family's great technique in brewing the finest of herbal remedies, which he lost over a game of cards that night.
entities.short_description: () is a human man who runs Advik's Wandering Curiosities and Collections in Elder's Post. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Aedla
entities.description:
Aedla was a squire of Lady Diassa Kwynn, paladin of (presumably) the Lawbearer. At some point during their squireship, Kwynn explained to them how, in her youth, she had discovered the extent and severity of the dangers in the world, and warned Aedla to stay close to her, be safe, and to bury her curiosity. Aedla has neither appeared nor been mentioned on Critical Role.

Category:Squires Category:Followers of the Lawbearer

entities.name: Aetheon
entities.description:
is a feral angel of Tansul. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Aetheon, as a captive, was 30 feet tall with claws and several rows of teeth like a shark, although not pointed. His body was shining and his bodily fluids glowed. His wings were plucked, and his face was ravaged by pain and misery.

Aetheon was the servant of Tansul, one of the Shapers and god of the sun; his task was to look after the Halovar family, the House of Flame in the Obridimian Empire. When Tansul was slain, Aetheon, like other celestials, went feral. Eventually he was captured by the Halovars, being secretly turned into the base of their new religion, the Candescent Creed, and the source of their Filament..}}

Aetheon has spent decades imprisoned, tortured, and mad. His existence was revealed to his younger grandson, Wicander Halovar, after he started making questions about the Light, and the Photarch used the feral angel to help him understand the true nature of their faith. During the conversation, Aetheon was constantly making tortured noises, trying to move and attack those outside the Prismatic Retort.
entities.short_description: is a feral angel of Tansul. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Agatha
entities.description:
was a night hag and the foster mother of Xella Blacktongue.

She was a woman of mottled blue skin with long greasy hair, and she behaved rudely even when she received compliments.

In the past, Agatha lived in the Utesspire Mountains under an ancient dead willow tree, using her magic to control nature, and even cast a powerful curse to that end. Not long before 809 PD, she made a deal with a couple, and took their human child. She raised him as her own in a small room in her lair, and took him with her occasionally when she had to deal with people; one of those times, the hag found the home of Professor Alexander Ward, who had found her heartstone, and traded a bag of oats for it. Over time, her magical influence transformed her adoptive son into a hexblood, a fey being, and he eventually left, becoming an artificer and merchant known as Xella Blacktongue.

At some point before 839 PD, the Slayer's Take defeated Agatha near her lair, although they weren't able to find her heartstone. Even after she was gone, her curse activated, animating many twigmen that attacked people and stole the sap from the local trees.
entities.short_description: was a night hag and the foster mother of Xella Blacktongue.

entities.name: Agony
entities.description:
Agony is a demon aspirant in the Candescent Creed, and one of the three sisters of Tyranny. As an NPC, Agony is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Agony is smaller than her sisters and has bright blue skin. She wears spectacles and her robes are monkish and hide her figure. She seems to be clumsy, frequently tripping and hurting herself. She appears to be the least assertive of the three sisters.

Tyranny met all three of her sisters at the Villa Aurora the day after Thjazi Fang's execution. Agony was the concerned about how Tyranny was doing, but when she learned she had made a friend of Thaisha Lloy, asked immediately if they would be able to "use her to our ends".

Agony was present in Riesingürtle when the Seekers arrived there. Her sister Enmity had encountered the group at a biergarten, posing as a ditzy missionary of the Candescent Creed, and learning from Thaisha Lloy her real name and that she had met both Tyranny and Wicander Halovar at the Lloy family estate. When Enmity joined her sisters at the Candescent Cathedral, she told them what she had learned from Thaisha. The sisters, who were searching for Wicander and Tyranny, suspected that Occtis Tachonis was actually Wick in disguise, and that Vaelus was Tyranny. They returned to the biergarten in search of the group, who had by that time left it.
entities.short_description: Agony is a demon aspirant in the Candescent Creed, and one of the three sisters of Tyranny. As an NPC, Agony is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Agztash Splitknuckle
entities.description:
is one of the local representatives of the Revolutionary Council of Dol-Makjar. He occupies the seat reserved for the orcish Wall Clan and was a legendary hero of the Shapers' War who got his nickname from punching out an angel during the Shapers' War. "He was once a radical, but he has more recently become aligned with the rest of the council – even voting for the Revolutionary Council's neutrality in the Falconer's Rebellion." His seat represents the Dol-Makjar districts of Silverhill, Shafira, the Rookery, and the Tanners.

In his youth, Agztash was a legendary hero of the Shapers' War who was elected to the Revolutionary Council shortly thereafter. During the War, he was hit at the edge of an area of effect by one of Azgra's spells and survived, adding to his legend. As the years went on, when asked if he was going to step down from his Council seat he responded he was still healthy and had no plans to do so. He had a "prodigious" constitution. After Azgra died, he led the charge to help the other nations that were still fighting their gods. He was hit by an arrow from a celestial designed to kill all mortals on contact, and he finished the battle and then pulled it out afterwards.

He is now 99 years old, very ill and constantly attended by his nurse, Jayan Nathir, a Candescent Creed member who heals him with the Light, keeping him alive. He was one of the three Council members to whom the Schemers sent an invitation to attend a performance of "KoTher'ai" at The Hallowed Round.
entities.short_description: is one of the local representatives of the Revolutionary Council of Dol-Makjar. He occupies the seat reserved for the orcish Wall Clan and was a legendary hero of the Shapers' War who got his nickname from punching out…

entities.name: Ajit Dayal
entities.description:
Ajit Dayal () is a member of House Dayal, a Mahaan house in Jrusar, and oversees the Dayal Hall. Gurge Kisgregg instructed Chetney Pock O'Pea to find Ajit, who could further connect him to the Gorgynei.

Ajit is described by Gryz Alakritos, a socially nervous friend, as suited for large social occasions like balls and "much better at this". Gryz also felt that Ajit was "a good man". He is described by Eshteross as "a philanthropic sort" and as having almost "too good" of a reputation within the city, which Eshteross felt made him a target.

When Bells Hells visited him at Dayal Hall, Ajit wore a dark colored sherwani coat. He has deep brown skin, short dark hair, kind eyes, and a friendly and open manner.

Ajit is a member of House Dayal, a Mahaan house in Jrusar. He oversees the Dayal Hall, an educational center located in the Core Spire. He was a student of Daramon.

entities.name: Akami Rowe
entities.description:
is the Guildmaster of the Navigator's Guild and the Helmswoman in the flying city of Avalir. As an NPC in Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

The day before the Calamity and 10 minutes before sunrise, Akami connected with Laerryn Coramar-Seelie via Sending to report on the status of their flight. The city would be right above Cathmoíra and in position to start its descent sometime shortly after 1:00 in the morning and should be terrestrial about 10 minutes before sunrise.

Around 1:00 in the morning, Akami connected with Laerryn once again to report that Avalir was in position over Cathmoíra (at the intersection of all three leylines) and the automated protocol of descent had begun. She intended to stay and oversee the entire process, but began choking on her last words as she was attacked by an unknown assassin.

Category:Unspecified Humanoids Category:Dead Characters Category:Avalir

entities.name: Alamads Haddou
entities.description:
Alamads Haddou is the current marquis of Port Zoon and head of the Silverbone Smithing Guild, which operates throughout the Menagerie Coast. A former Shore Warden and an immensely skilled ironsmith, he is greatly respected. He is nicknamed Ironpuss but is referred as such only out of his hearing.

So far, Alamads Haddou has not been mentioned on Critical Role.

Alamads is known for his iron will, sense of duty, and honorable character. He is passionate about Port Zoon and its people, and he performs his job as marquis with clear intent, quickly punishing those who break the law or endangers the people of the city. He trains the local Zhelezo, with whom he works closely, to distrust idle hands, and convicted criminals are forced into manual labor for the local guilds to perform the harshest job in each industry. He is also described as crotchety and ornery.

Alamads is a former Shore Warden who cultivated a respected reputation with a war hammer in battle. He is also considered a legendary ironsmith and a master of ironworking, which has earned him an equally respected reputation as a smith. These together earned him the nickname Ironpuss, spoken only out of his hearing.

entities.name: Alasterre de Vitrevos
entities.description:
Alasterre de Vitrevos is a blood cleric of the Matron of Ravens and the director of Tal'Dorei's Claret Order as of 836 PD.

Alasterre is a human man with a slim build, pale skin (except for a red vertical line that crosses his chin), and long black hair that falls to his shoulders and is partially held in place with a red ribbon. He wears a light robe with red and dark blue fabrics edged with turquoise; his sandals are the same dark color that reddens at the height of the cufflinks, where it ends with a design of red wings. He has both of his forearms covered with red ribbons, but the right one has over them a metal armband with feathers design. His right shoulder is also covered by a metallic protective shoulder pad with a wing design; this piece is fastened with leather straps that cross his chest, where they are fastened beneath a symbol of the Raven Queen; furthermore, his belt buckle bears the symbol of the Claret Order.

Alasterre is very calm and sanguine, a young and confident man whose self-assurance helps him make decisions without hesitation, combining aggressive strategies with a general relaxed demeanor that is useful in battle, but makes it challenging for others to work with him as equals. Alasterre is meticulous and orderly, and very determined, trying to do what is best for his order and for his goddess' wishes. He desires to achieve all of his goals and get recognition in the process, thus being willing to accept whatever good or bad thing that comes to him as consequence.

Alasterre joined Tal'Dorei's Claret Orders at some point in his youth and showed a talent for hemocraft as a blood cleric of the Matron of Death. He was mentored by Teresa Dulamar, director of the Orders and a fellow worshiper of the Raven Queen.
entities.short_description: Alasterre de Vitrevos is a blood cleric of the Matron of Ravens and the director of Tal'Dorei's Claret Order as of 836 PD.

entities.name: Alba Davinos
entities.description:
Alba was born as the daughter of General Raimond Davinos, head of the Vassal House of Davinos, and his wife, Lady Maya. She has an older brother, Julien, the heir of the house.

In the year 71 after the Shapers' War Lady Maya and her daughter Alba had been staying in the Golden Orchard with the Royce family, while General Raimond and Sir Julien were in Dol-Makjar with Lady Aranessa Royce after her husband, Thjazi Fang, was sentenced to death. However, in the following days, after the Palazzo Davinos was attacked, the safety of both noble families was compromised, and Sir Julien, when he had the chance in Riesingürtle, wrote a letter to his mother, wondering if she and Alba were ok, and asking them to look for a safer place to stay in, somewhere only he could find them.

When the Golden Orchard was attacked, Alba was amongst the survivors after the demiplane fell; however, during the fight against the Tachonis forces, one of the latter, Koral Tachonis, used the "Wraith's Touch" (a necromantic curse) against her, running away with the focus but being himself targetted by a curse that forced him to dance to a Davinos tune. When her mother, Maya, described her situation to Julien she told her that Alba's fingers were starting to become ghost-like, and that she would die in less than a year if the curse wasn't lifted, fully turning into a spirit.
entities.short_description: Alba was born as the daughter of General Raimond Davinos, head of the Vassal House of Davinos, and his wife, Lady Maya. She has an older brother, Julien, the heir of the house.

entities.name: Aldageam
entities.description:
Aldageam is mistrustful of her friend, the tabaxi pirate Three Earrings, but she is happy to help her in times of need. She's even willing to sell certain items, such as Potions of Water Breathing, to adventurers hired by her at half price.

At some point in her youth, Three Earrings saved Aldageam's life. She eventually became a druid and an apothecary while settling in Brokenbank.

Aldageam uses the Druid statblock from the Monster Manual, making her a 4th-level spellcaster with certain spells prepared and a quarterstaff equipped. In addition, she would have the racial abilities of sea elves.

entities.name: Aldor
entities.description:
Aldor was a member of the Slayer's Take in Vasselheim. As an NPC, he was played by Matthew Mercer.

Aldor was a human with short, dirty blond hair and a little bit of stubble on his chin. He carried a symbol of Erathis around his neck.

A member of the Slayer's Take, he found his fellow bounty hunter, Lyra, had an obsessive crush on him. Lyra claimed that they slept together once.

Aldor and several other members of the Slayer's Take confronted Vox Machina as they battled a hydra just outside the walls of Vasselheim. When the adventuring band slayed the beast, Aldor angrily explained the contract system of the Slayer's Take and took the group to the guild hall for further explanations and punishment.
entities.short_description: Aldor was a member of the Slayer's Take in Vasselheim. As an NPC, he was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Aldreda Tavelle
entities.description:
Aldreda Seriblo, previously known as Aldreda Tavelle, is a tiefling woman and the younger sister of Lucien Tavelle.

Aldreda was a beautiful tiefling woman with red eyes, magenta skin and black hair styled in braids through which her horns speared.

In her youth Aldreda had a dreamy nature, and aspired to build a successful life. Over the years, she became more suspicious, protecting what she had achieved and distrusting possible changes.

Aldreda was born in 811 PD as the third and youngest child (and the only daughter) of a married couple of the Greying Wildlands. She had two older brothers, Elric and Lucien, the latter being only one year her senior. Their parents were artists who usually played music while their children danced, sang or performed plays, Aldreda being particularly good and singing and dancing, twirling for minutes without getting dizzy; however, their parents were abusive, hitting Elric despite being the best performer, while Lucien tried to protect himself and his sister. Things got worse after Elric was killed due to a debt with the Jagentoth family, and Lucien's parents, obsessed with getting their best performer back, talked to a witch in the Savalirwood, Azrahari, who turned Elric's corpse into a strange puppet that his parents kept around, horrifying their other two children, and even using the puppet to support their arguments, like when Aldreda criticized how they performed a certain play.thumb|200px| At some point Lucien couldn't stay there any longer, so he burned down the caravan with his parents and the puppet inside, and he left with his sister. She, eventually, travelled to Rexxentrum under the promise of working cleaning houses until she could find a powerful husband or lover; she wrote to Lucien from time to time, and he expected to eventually move in with her when the time was right.
entities.short_description: Aldreda Seriblo, previously known as Aldreda Tavelle, is a tiefling woman and the younger sister of Lucien Tavelle.

entities.name: Alexander
entities.description:
Alexander (Greek: Ἀλέξανδρος) is a masculine name of Greek origin. The most prominent bearer of the name is Alexander the Great, the king of the Ancient Greek kingdom of Macedonia who created one of the largest empires in ancient history.

Variants listed here are Aleksandar, Aleksander, Oleksandr, Oleksander, Aleksandr, and Alekzandr. Related names and diminutives include Iskandar, Alec, Alek, Alekos, Alex, Alexsander, Alexandre, Aleks, Aleksa, Aleksandre, Alejandro, Alessandro, Alasdair, Sasha, Sandy, Sandro, Sikandar, Skander, Sander and Xander; feminine forms include Alexandra, Alexandria, and Sasha.

entities.name: Alfarr Lorelei
entities.description:
, also known as The First Wolf, was a nobleman and a member of the Lorelei family. He was mentioned by Liam O'Brien in .

Alfarr was a persistent man, who, despite being near madness after becoming a werewolf, endured the experience and kept his sanity.

During a near-fatal encounter closer to the end days of the war between Julous Dominion and Dwendalian Empire, Alfarr Lorelei was bitten and cursed with lycanthropy. The curse burned into Alfarr's blood in a relentless fever that almost drove him mad, but he persisted. He had a daughter, Grenya, who fought the curse as well, and so did her sons, and so on. Early on the family considered lycanthropy a curse, but gradually younger generations saw it as a gift to be wielded responsibly. They created a ritual known as "The Taming" to help control the inner beast and used it to help their family.

When Alfarr died, he was buried in the Lorelei mausoleum, where a small monument was built for him.
entities.short_description: , also known as The First Wolf, was a nobleman and a member of the Lorelei family. He was mentioned by Liam O'Brien in .

entities.name: Algar Dyomin
entities.description:
is a powerful man in Nicodranas and a client of the Ruby of the Sea. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Algar is a muscular man with a wide neck and sun weathered skin. He is well dressed and has shoulder length hair fashioned in a tangled bowl cut style that is unkempt at the shoulders. After encountering the Mighty Nein, he is now missing his left hand.

Algar is prideful and has a quick temper. Despite his high status in the Clovis Concord, he lacks any real social graces and can be very possessive. He enjoys spending his wealth on luxuries such as drink, clothing and furniture, as well as the companionship of the famous courtesan Marion Lavorre. Marion describes Algar as a boring conversationalist and a boastful man.

After his capture and interrogation by the Mighty Nein, Algar is left a broken man. He is deeply traumatized by the experience and acts cowed and in shock. He is eventually sent away from Nicodranas, told never to return by the group.
entities.short_description: is a powerful man in Nicodranas and a client of the Ruby of the Sea. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Allura Vysoren
entities.description:
Arcanist Allura Vysoren is a human wizard. She is famous throughout Tal'Dorei as a powerful arcanist and former adventurer. Allura is a member of the Council of Tal'Dorei and one of Vox Machina's principal contacts within Emon. Her home was the Ivory Tower, in Emon's central Cloudtop District. It was Allura who tasked the party, shortly before the Critical Role stream started, with travelling to Kraghammer to find Lady Kima of Vord.

As an NPC in Critical Role, she is played by Matthew Mercer. In The Legend of Vox Machina, Allura is voiced by Indira Varma.

Allura has long, golden hair which she usually keeps braided. She is often seen wearing blue robes. In 843 PD, even after several decades, she still kept her preferred hairstyle, although her hair had gone mostly grey, with only some blond remaining.

Allura Vysoren is one of the kindest and most loyal allies of Vox Machina. She has been shown to carry a lot of pressure on her shoulders as both a member of the Arcana Pansophical and holding the position of Master of Arcana for the Kingdom of Tal'Dorei. Allura is headstrong, forgiving, and willing to do anything to protect the ones she loves. While one of the most powerful and well-respected arcanists in Exandria, with that responsibility comes a certain loneliness as well as isolation from the realm she works so hard to protect. Her reunion with Kima sparked joy and vitality she had not felt since destiny had drawn the two apart fifteen years prior.

entities.name: Alma
entities.description:
is a halfling midwife and member of the Air Ashari in Zephrah. As an NPC, Alma is played by Matthew Mercer.

Alma is a halfling woman in her sixties, with slightly hunched shoulders and strong legs. She has long reddish brown curly hair with streaks of white, and pale blue eyes. She and Orym look alike, especially when they smile. When Bells Hells encountered her, she was barefoot and wearing a flowing white and green dress.

Alma is a sweet and good-natured woman, and a very proud mother.

At some point in her life Alma became one of the few midwives of Zephrah, a position that made her very valued in her community. Between 806 and 807 PD she was involved with another halfling, surnamed Tarrintel, and she became pregnant, but by the time she gave birth the man had left town and had no contact with his son.
entities.short_description: is a halfling midwife and member of the Air Ashari in Zephrah. As an NPC, Alma is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Alogar Fang
entities.description:
is the oldest son of Thaisha Lloy and Halandil Fang.

Alogar is an orcish warrior. He is 27 years old as of the beginning of Campaign Four. Nov 2025|47:43}}

According to Sir Julien he is smart and skilled with weapons, and has great intuition. He is also very sociable and loves to drink with other soldiers in the Barrowguard.

When Alogar was still a child he climbed a ginkgo tree but fell and broke his neck; his mother reached him, feeling his death and using druidic magic for the first time to cast Spare the Dying, saving him just in time.
entities.short_description: is the oldest son of Thaisha Lloy and Halandil Fang.

entities.name: Alonne Frith
entities.description:
Alonne Frith is a Hollow One and cultist of Ceratos.

Alonne hails from Rotthold in Blightshore, where he works as a scholar of the Far Realm. In 835 PD during the War of Ash and Light, Alonne traveled to Brokenveil Marsh find eldritch relics. While there, he was captured by the Righteous Brand soldiers stationed at Fort Venture, where his undead nature was noticed by the sadistic Inquisitor in charge, Parson Pellinost. Pelinost took interest in Alonne and had him imprisoned so he could be studied and experimented on.

When Bol'bara, another prisoner at Fort Venture, went on a rampage after becoming posessed by her shadow demon patron Trush, Alonne was left alone in his cage as the sole survivor. When the adventuring party hired to resuce Bol'bara arived, he descirbed to them how her powers caused the guards to turn against each other. If freed, Alonne could be convinced by the adventuring party to help find the possessed Bol'bara, but with difficulty.

entities.name: Aloysia Telfan
entities.description:
(pronounced like "ah-LOY-see-uh TELL-fin") is an elf agent of the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream.

When encountered in Bazzoxan, Aloysia is gaunt and wearing scarlet robes. She is described as tall and pale, and illustrated with shoulder-length, light-colored hair that drapes over her left eye.

Aloysia is ambitious in her pursuit of knowledge and power. She is described by an agent of a rival organization as cold-blooded, and indeed, she is willing to kill to get what she wants. But she is not so cynical as to avoid being shocked when she is betrayed.

She has at least a superficial charm: she is polite and pleasant while she still thinks she can persuade people to cooperate. But she quickly reveals a haughty manner with those who turn down her offers. To those who achieve enough initial success in tasks for the Consortium to be offered membership, she says she hopes to see them rise through its ranks.
entities.short_description: (pronounced like "ah-LOY-see-uh TELL-fin") is an elf agent of the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream.

entities.name: Altradler
entities.description:
is a giant eagle using the aerie in the city of Riesingürtle as his home. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Altradler is a massive and very old 30-foot-tall giant eagle with white plumage that darkens to a soft gray around the edge of his beak and around the socks of his leg plumage near his talons. He has an old healed injury over one eye that remains "a little bit weepy."

Altradler has flown across the skies of Helvar for four decades.

Altradler was awakened in the middle of the night to carry the Seekers from Riesingürtle to Castle Torch. When Thaisha Lloy cast Speak with Animals on him, she promised him a cow if he would transport the party to Gerwyn. Altradler was worried about being so near the darkness that he knew was near the city, and promised to fly slow so they wouldn't land in the dark. The party boarded the wooden carriage placed on his back, and rested during the flight. In the morning, they awakened to find Altradler circling the city, and at their request he landed them safely. Instead of the promised cow, there were many goats that he promptly began eating, and Thaisha sought out their owner and reimbursed him. Altradler then headed back to his home in Riesingürtle.
entities.short_description: is a giant eagle using the aerie in the city of Riesingürtle as his home. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Alyson Paij
entities.description:
is the human captain of The Ill Hand and a pirate of the Revelry. She is a rival of Captain Avantika. As an NPC, Alyson is played by Matthew Mercer.

Alyson is a woman with curly, shoulder-length blonde hair and a scar over one eye that keeps the eye closed. She wears a tattered black coat.

Alyson is a fierce and abrasive woman whose demeanor makes Beauregard seem friendly. Enjoys a good brawl as much as she appreciates a stiff drink. Possesses an uncompromising sense of moral duty to the downtrodden.

Prior to the Mighty Nein meeting her, Alyson had been a rival to Avantika for some time. Avantika claims she had crossed paths with her multiple times, and that Alyson has previously embellished information to gain favor with the Plank King. While a pirate, she never raids civilian vessels and does her best to rein in the Revelry's cruelest captains and focus their efforts on those who deserve to have their goods stolen.

entities.name: Alyxian
entities.description:
, dubbed the Apotheon, was a mortal champion blessed by three of the Prime Deities in the Calamity.

Alyxian was born a human with olive skin and curly brown hair. As a child, he was dirty and untidy in appearance; as a teenage hunter he was slender. He carried a sword as a young man and apparently for much of the Calamity, and as an adult he was granted the Jewel of Three Prayers, initially a golden amulet on a golden chain.

Late in the Calamity he had soft features worn by pain. Then, and in visions long afterward, Alyxian is often shown with a spear, leather armor, and a red cape, and he appears with items representing his connection to the three deities who gave him their blessings. He carries a shield emblazoned with the icon of Sehanine (a crescent moon strung like a bow), a brooch with the golden profile of Avandra, and a dagger in a sheath bearing the crested moons of Corellon's symbol. Just before his final confrontation with the Ruiner, he wielded a spear, and he glowed with a silver-and-green aura representing the blessings of Sehanine and Corellon, and the golden light of Avandra's power flared as he blocked the Ruiner's spear. In visions, he may still appear with a tattered red cape over leather armor, and carrying a shield.

After centuries in the Netherdeep, Alyxian's appearance changes depending on his form. As Alyxian the Tormented, he is a huge, many-eyed monster with a thick, pale white hide pierced and scarred by many blades; it has dozens of arms, six of them capable of grappling enemies. As Alyxian the Callous, he has an angelic form with gleaming feathers and a cold, expressionless face; he is armored in half plate and surrounded by a halo of spears, and he wields a brilliant radiant spear. As Alyxian the Dispossessed, he is a hunched, weary old human man with gray hair, again wearing leather armor and carrying a shield, spear, and magic dagger. When he is redeemed, he maintains much the same appearance, but there is no dagger.
entities.short_description: , dubbed the Apotheon, was a mortal champion blessed by three of the Prime Deities in the Calamity.

entities.name: Alyxian Aboleth
entities.description:
The is a mutated creature that, due to ruidium corruption, believes it has the soul of the ancient champion Alyxian.

This mutated creature differs in appearance from an typical aboleth in that it has a second warped face and has veins of ruidium crossing its pale green hide. It has the delusion that it is trapped in this alien body as a divine punishment for failing to save the world during the Calamity.

By 836 PD the Alyxian Aboleth had spent decades in Cael Morrow near the rift to the Netherdeep, and the aboleth's psychic influence was partly responsible for clouding the mind and memories of a neighboring sea elf named Olara. The ghost of Hadarai, an ancient priest of the Arch Heart, was aware of the aboleth and could warn friendly adventurers about it.

As of 836 PD, during the Netherdeep crisis, the Alyxian Aboleth resided in Cael Morrow; its lair was in a kelp forest there. A number of aboleth spawn also lived in the area, bound to the Alyxian Aboleth and guarding its treasure. The corpse of an explorer of the Allegiance of Allsight could be found around the lair.

entities.name: Amaris
entities.description:
Amaris was the firbolg husband of Trist and the father of her children during the Calamity. As an NPC, Amaris is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Amaris was a firbolg man with fuzzy ears that his children inherited, and smelled of petrichor and pine.

He was a kind man and loving husband who supported his wife and wasn't afraid to be at risk if that meant helping her.

During the first century of the Calamity Amaris met Trist, a human woman, and they got married, having two children together, Haylie and Topher.
entities.short_description: Amaris was the firbolg husband of Trist and the father of her children during the Calamity. As an NPC, Amaris is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Amariya Cormoray
entities.description:
Lady Amariya Dacen Cormoray is a member of House Cormoray. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Amariya is a "very bejeweled" middle-aged woman with dark skin, hair wrapped in braided rings like a crown set with gold, and dressed in resplendent white robes with long ivory fingernails painted white to match her gown..}}

She was professional and polite when speaking to a new acquaintance. However, she was also prideful and daring regarding her position and her knowledge and understanding of things.

Amariya was a member of House Cormoray of the Sundered Houses and, as others in her bloodline, manifested powerful sorcerous abilities. At some she married Lord Dacen. During or shortly before the beginning of Campaign Four, she was appointed by the Chamber of Lords-Advisory to represent them in specific tasks.
entities.short_description: Lady Amariya Dacen Cormoray is a member of House Cormoray. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Amelia
entities.description:
Amelia is a young woman from Westruun. She is the daughter of Reginald. As an NPC, Amelia is played by Matthew Mercer.

Amelia is a young woman in her late teens or early twenties with long brown hair

Amelia was languishing and starving in the abandoned Iron Stockade when Grog went there to search for survivors. Grog freed her, but did not tell her of her father's death.

Grog recounts his encounter with Amelia to the party, who then seek her out among the remaining citizens of Westruun. She was found sleeping in the tavern. She wakes up due to the celebration and is approached by Vex and Pike, with Grog staying just behind. Amelia thanks the party for freeing her, and for defeating the dragon. Vex recounts her fathers bravery and fate. She joins them in a toast and Grog gifts her 400 gold, from her father. She accepts, stating it could help a lot of them here in Westruun.
entities.short_description: Amelia is a young woman from Westruun. She is the daughter of Reginald. As an NPC, Amelia is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Amido
entities.description:
is a quanikka connected to the Volition. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Amido is tall, somewhat older, and covered in pale grey-white fur, although his head is balding.

In 843 PD, after Bells Hells located the most recent safe house of the Volition in Kreviris, they met Amido, who at first didn't trust them and questioned them about why they were there, getting increasingly nervous when the Exandrians started acting suspicious. However, when they proved they weren't aligned with the Imperium, Amido relaxed and allowed them to go meet the members of the Volition, mentioning the relevant figures the adventurers would have to meet. He received several blueberries Druidcrafted by Orym as a thanks.

Amido welcomed Bells Hells and the Mighty Nein to the Delta Dust Pit but was cautious and nervous, saying he no longer was a part of the Volition since "the last attempt".
entities.short_description: is a quanikka connected to the Volition. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Amry Talter
entities.description:
Doctor is a professor and a cleric of the Totality. As an NPC, Amry is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Amry is a halfling woman with a mousy face and brown hair, who wears spectacles as well as a blue and white academic gown and vest.

She is enthusiastic about her field of study and wants to help people with it, although she is also very insecure about the possibility of failure or mistakes.

Amry became a member of the Totality and started dedicating herself to the ideas of knowledge and truth in order to channel that divine domain as a cleric would. As an academic, she also specialised in celestials, being fascinated by their biological origins.

entities.name: Andica
entities.description:
Andica was a historical figure of the Menagerie Coast.

By 831 PD, she was remembered in stories as a vain queen, the wife of King Daldred, and when the evil Taeleron the Cleaver demanded her death in order to spare the kingdom, the peasants believed that Andica would never choose them over herself, but the queen, in a noble sacrifice, took her own life; the tragedy ended with Daldred lamenting his loss.

Lucien Tavelle, who knew the story well, believed a local lord or chief named Daldred had in fact had a wife who made a great sacrifice. However, their story had been altered and popularized in plays and retellings in both the Greying Wildlands and the Dwendalian Empire.

entities.name: Aniko Seremai
entities.description:
Sir was a knight of House Seremai. As an NPC, he was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Aniko was a powerful knight of impressive appearance: 6'9" in height, broad-shouldered, with a forked tongue and snake-like eyes; his features became even more reptilian when he used his powers, which produced a poisonous green glow. He was skilled with spear, longsword, and shield, and carried those with him, the latter displaying the coat of arms of his family.

He had a dark and sadistic personality, mocking people for the losses he had caused, and being fascinated with the idea of facing his enemies again in the Underworld. However, Aniko preferred murder to combat.

Aniko was born as a member of the Vassal House of Seremai, and as such, he was at the service of House Tachonis. As other members of his lineage he eventually manifested sorcerous powers, and in time, also became a knight. He had experience with basilisks and worked in Obrimus Manor for a time (later focusing on working specifically with Segundus Tachonis's children), where he learned things about them, including a "trick" that he eventually shared with his liege lords.
entities.short_description: Sir was a knight of House Seremai. As an NPC, he was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Anna Ripley
entities.description:
Dr. Anna Ripley was a follower of the Briarwoods. After the Briarwoods seized control of Whitestone, Percy attempted to kill Dr. Ripley in Stilben, but he was captured by her guards, tortured, and interrogated. Dr. Ripley began gathering intelligence about Percy's weapons and experimenting with firearm construction, losing a hand during one of her experiments.

As an NPC in Critical Role, Dr. Ripley was played by Matthew Mercer. In The Legend of Vox Machina, Ripley was voiced by Kelly Hu.

thumb|270px| When Vox Machina first met Ripley in the dungeon beneath Whitestone Castle, she was disguised as an old woman, looking to be in her seventies. She had very deep, sunken wrinkles, weathered skin, mostly whitish-gray hair with a bit of remaining red and brown, and was wearing ragged clothing.

When the magic disguising her was dispelled, she was revealed to be a woman in her early mid-forties, with jet black hair pulled into a tight ponytail. She was wearing nice travel clothes with a long duster-like coat. Her right hand was missing. Her face was a little weathered from travel and she had dark lines at the sides of her face, whether from smiles or frowning.

entities.name: Annaline
entities.description:
is a human weretiger. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

When first encountered by Bells Hells, Annaline was in the form of a wide-shouldered deep red-orange weretiger standing six and a half feet tall and carrying a massive iron-headed hammer. She wore dark grey-brown hide armor and a jet black hood. In her human form, she was a woman in her late 40s with short dark red hair with gray streaks, an intense expression, and a severe, perpetually clenched jaw.

In her past life, before she became a lycanthrope, Annaline's name was Divaasheela. She was a student at the Dayal Hall in Jrusar and therefore knew the Dayal family. She was sent to retrieve a mislabeled delivery from her uncle in the northeast Oderan Wilds when she was attacked by a lycan (which she suspects was connected in some way with the Ivory Syndicate). When the curse found her, she left the city, took the name "Annaline", and was trained in the ways of the Gorgynei by Ometho, one of the founders of the group.

She told Chetney if he ever encountered the lycan who transmitted the curse to her, a pale, brown-haired elf named Dorao with amber eyes and a scar under his mouth to the left, Chetney should kill him immediately for her.
entities.short_description: is a human weretiger. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Anni Aughta
entities.description:
() is an uniya musician living in the Krook House in the Core Spire of Jrusar. As an NPC, Anni is played by Matthew Mercer.

Anni appears young and wears rough clothing.

Anni is somewhat crusty but benign; she expresses mild impatience with other members of the Krook House for not bringing in income, and she does not enjoy Fresh Cut Grass's bright, friendly encouragement or appreciate Ashton Greymoore saying they believe in her. Her normal attitude is somewhat "devil-may-care".

As Ashton and FCG left the Krook House on the day they met the rest of the group later named Bells Hells, Anni greeted them. She was practicing a new, fine-looking lute of uncertain provenance, hoping to pull something together for an audition at Stuvan's Dreamscape Theater.

entities.name: Anola
entities.description:
is the woman who handled the mass cooking for the village of Vo on Rumblecusp. As an NPC, Anola is played by Matthew Mercer.

Anola is a very squat, muscular-looking humanoid woman in her fifties, with thinning hair and an intense smile with very bright teeth.

Caduceus and Beau helped Anola and the other villagers prepare the feast that was held the evening they arrived, partially in order to keep an eye on what went into the food.

When Anola recovered her memories, she decided to stay on the island since she had spent most of her life on Rumblecusp. She began trying to offer comfort and counseling to the others. While she remembered her original name had been Wenthal, she elected to continue to be known as Anola.

entities.name: Apple Pie
entities.description:
was an automaton member of the Division of Public Benefit, an adventuring party with Fresh Cut Grass and Dancer.

Apple Pie had a relatively simple set of responsibilities for the Division.

Apple Pie may have been slightly smaller or wider than Fresh Cut Grass.

Dancer created Apple Pie, who—like all of Dancer's automaton creations—was named after one of Dancer's favorite smells.
entities.short_description: was an automaton member of the Division of Public Benefit, an adventuring party with Fresh Cut Grass and Dancer.

entities.name: Aradrine
entities.description:
Master Aradrine the Owl (pronounced like "AWR-uh-dreen") is a goliath sorcerer and one of five co-leaders of the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream.

When Aradrine is first encountered in 836 PD, she is wearing a red robe and carrying a silver-bladed ruidium dagger. She is also showing signs of ruidium corruption: pulsing ruidium-colored veins are webbed across her forearm. A week later, while wearing a simple, sleeveless tunic instead of her robes, crimson growths and crystalline spines are clearly visible on her arm. (See the Trivia section below for what this implies.)

Occult silvertongues like Aradrine are charismatic leaders. However, exposing themselves to alien mysteries can make them mistrustful and anxious, and lead to hallucinations and imagined conspiracies to usurp them.

Aradrine has little tolerance for failure from her subordinates, and despises obsequiousness. She is manipulative enough to feign vulnerability to gain trust. Her living quarters reflect a degree of obsession and paranoia.
entities.short_description: Master Aradrine the Owl (pronounced like "AWR-uh-dreen") is a goliath sorcerer and one of five co-leaders of the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream.

entities.name: Arakki
entities.description:
is the orcish leader of the Koshtask clan of the Iothia Moorland between 835 PD and 855 PD.

Arakki was described in 835 PD as a fire-scarred orc. By 855 PD he looked like a mature man of tanned, age-marked skin with scars, black eyes and long black hair. He is corpulent and wears armor.

Arakki was a cunning and strategic leader who made alliances to ensure his clan's survival, but being able to betray and destroy those same allies without hesitation. He's devout of the Ruiner, and he actively asked for his forgiveness before accepting the faith of the Kryn Dynasty.

Arakki was the leader of his clan for at least two decades, between 835 and 855 PD. During that time, he tried to keep Koshtask independence against the Kryn Dynasty and the cult of the First Radiance with its increasing popularity in Xhorhas; due to this, Arakki was hostile towards missionaries of the Luxon.
entities.short_description: is the orcish leader of the Koshtask clan of the Iothia Moorland between 835 PD and 855 PD.

entities.name: Aramond Tuestrel
entities.description:
was the Grand-Conservator of the city of Molaesmyr, who spearheaded the investigation into the crystal well that was the natural magic fount of power upon which the city was founded. He theorized the well was a gift from the Arch Heart that was lost in the Calamity and rediscovered when the city was founded within the Veluthil Forest. Others (including Ezradan), however, believed the well to be arcane in nature, and most probably fallen from one of the ancient floating cities, such as Aeor.

Aramond and the other researchers were delving deeper and deeper into the caverns below their city, hoping to learn the nature of the well's power, when the corrupting, toxic miasma that eventually destroyed the city and the entire surrounding Veluthil Forest was unleashed while Ruidus was ascendant during an Apogee Solstice.

entities.name: Aramue
entities.description:
Aramue is a dryad of the Wildmother who lives in the Vermaloc Wildwood.

Aramue is a devout fey woman, following the Wildmother and protecting her domain; she defends her own forest as well, not fearing asking for help when necessary.

Aramue was born/created at some point before 835 PD. She grew up and became a follower of Melora, the goddess of the wilderness; she even developed magical abilities connected with her devotion to the goddess. Eventually the dryad became a protector of the Vermaloc Wildwood.

At some point after this, the peace in Aramue's territory was disturbed: an ettercap, wanting to gain Lolth's favor, took control of several of the local giant spiders that now attack settlements near the forest to bring victims to their master, who sacrifices them to the Spider Queen. The screams of the ettercap's prisoners disturb Aramue to the point of keeping her awake, so she is seeking the help of other followers of the Wildmother sending them dreams.

entities.name: Aranessa Royce
entities.description:
Lady is the head of the Sundered House of Royce, and the widow of Thjazi Fang. As an NPC, Aranessa is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Lady Aranessa is an elegant woman in her forties. When she attended the funeral of her husband Thjazi Fang, she wore a gown of gleaming green adorned with jewels. She carried her wedding ring with her despite not having been together with her husband for a long time. In the days after her husband's arrest and execution, followed by the attack against House Royce, the noblewoman had lost a lot of weight due to stress.

Despite her status as a noble lady, Aranessa is close to those she considers trustworthy, no matter who they are, and is in touch with her emotions to the point where she breaks protocol.

Lady Aranessa was born as the granddaughter of Lord Royce less than three decades after the end of the Shapers' War. When she was still a child she attended the wedding of Lord Otto Einfasen, arriving to Riesingürtle in a sky carriage. As she grew up, she became friends with Julien Davinos, the son of a vassal house, who was born when she was a teenager. Episode 2 Discussing Up To C4E18|1:02:30}}

entities.name: Arcadia Cerenvetorix
entities.description:
Arcadia Cerenvetorix was an archmage of the Magestri of Aeor during the Calamity. As an NPC, Arcadia is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan. The true Arcadia was a mortal avatar of the goddess Ioun, the Knowing Mentor, although the Arcadia known to the other Prime avatars at the time of the Fall of Aeor was actually Asmodeus in disguise.

Arcadia was a beautiful woman with deep black skin, long braids, and gleaming white eyes, wearing a golden headpiece and red and white robes with geometric patterns.

She was focused and intelligent, although she seemed to be doubtful about certain aspects of her plans if she wasn't certain of how they would go.

After the main Exandrian pantheon agreed to collaborate in a plan to neutralize Aeor and their potentially dangerous technology, it was agreed that the Knowing Mistress would act as the scout, infiltrating the flying city first in order to understand it. Thus, she was born as a human girl, Arcadia Cerenvetorix, and when she grew up and understood her duty, she traveled to Aeor and integrated into its society. Presumably due to her arcane merits, she became an archmage within the magocracy, and with her cover well established, she started investigating, eventually finding an abandoned temple (the Chamber of Seasons) that she magically protected although she was pretty sure that Aeorians had completely forgotten about it. She was soon joined by another mortal god in the city, since Corellon had also decided to live among those mortals as an aeormaton, SILAHA.

entities.name: Archibald Desnay
entities.description:
Archibald Desnay is a well-respected philosopher in Whitestone and was once the chancellor to Frederick de Rolo, Percy's father. As an NPC, Archibald was portrayed by Matthew Mercer.

Archibald Desnay appeared in The Legend of Vox Machina, where he was re-imagined as a young rebel leader voiced by Dominic Monaghan.

Appearance Archibald Desnay is a very elderly man with a very thin, frail form. His weathered skin is dark and leathery, with liver spots all over his nearly hairless scalp. One of his eyes is clouded over in white. When Vox Machina first met him, he was wearing ragged robes draped over his body.

Personality Archibald speaks with power, resonance, and confidence, giving off the impression that he is a man of great power and respect. He is stern and can be crotchety at times.
entities.short_description: Archibald Desnay is a well-respected philosopher in Whitestone and was once the chancellor to Frederick de Rolo, Percy's father. As an NPC, Archibald was portrayed by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Archmage Kohlesturm
entities.description:
is a noble high sorceress serving and advising House Einfasen, and attending Lord Otto specifically. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

The archmage is a polite woman dressed in robes as black as coal, adorned with red and orange spiked pauldrons shaped like flames; by her appearance alone she looks like a full caster.

At some point in her life this woman manifested sorcerous abilities, and eventually became the archmage of House Einfasen at their court in Riesingürtle.

Days after the execution of Thjazi Fang, in the year 71, Archmage Kohlesturm was present at Castle Klippenblicke when the Seekers visited it. She was presumably present during the meeting Lord Einfasen and his ministers had with Lady Aranessa Royce, in which the latter explained how House Tachonis had attacked her and House Davinos.

entities.name: Arethusa
entities.description:
Arethusa is a female nymph and resident of the Frostweald, where she keeps watch over a cluster of three mirror-like pools that form a pathway into the Feywild, each one leading to the forest of a different Archfey. Suspicious of all mortals, she requires both her trust and a favor before she grants passage through her domain. She was active as of 812 and 836 PD.

Arethusa has not appeared or been mentioned onstream on Critical Role.

Arethusa uses the Mage statblock, available in the Monster Manual, 5th Edition (2014), p. 347.

entities.name: Ariks Eshteross
entities.description:
Lord Ariks Eshteross () was an orc nobleman and former mercenary living in Jrusar, Marquet. As an NPC, he was played by Matthew Mercer.

Lord Eshteross was an older orc with grayish skin. He had gray, receding hair that was bald on top and a well trimmed Van Dyke goatee and beard on a scarred face. He stood about 6'2" and had broad shoulders and a wide neck. He was also described as handsome with a cunning look in his eyes.

He walked with a cane, and when first encountered, he was wearing a pair of spectacles, a deep crimson-burgundy high-collared robe, and a scarf around his shoulders.

He was described by Bertrand Bell as having a strange manner. Bertrand also believed that Eshteross was "interested in preserving the good folk of Jrusar" and wanting to see good done in the city.
entities.short_description: Lord Ariks Eshteross () was an orc nobleman and former mercenary living in Jrusar, Marquet. As an NPC, he was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Armand Treshi
entities.description:
() was the head of the Mahaan house Treshi in Jrusar. He was originally believed by Lord Ariks Eshteross to be a member of the Chandei Quorum. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Armand is tall for a dwarf, dark, and handsome. He has short black wavy hair and a well-kept goatee. When seen by Gurge, he wore a fancy blue and gold sherwani coat with a buttoned high collar, shiny pants and a lot of jewelry. He wore a platinum ring on his left thumb, which the soon-to-be-named Bells Hells were tasked by Ariks Eshteross to swap with an identical ring that had been enchanted to be traceable.

Armand values business and connections, and his house has a hand in many different guilds throughout the Oderan Wilds. Lord Eshteross suggested he might be interested in expanding his political power by sending contingents of Paragon's Call to locations beyond Jrusar.

Knowing that Armand Treshi was going to be attending a masquerade ball for the upper echelon of Jrusar, Bells Hells, cooperating with Ariks Eshteross, developed a plan to get as physically close to Armand as they could to exchange his cherished ring with a tracking device that was a perfect replica of that ring. It would allow Armand to be located when the investigation of his operations was completed.

entities.name: Arrideo and Cor
entities.description:
were Issylran followers of the Platinum Dragon, and the parents of Erro Mordaurum.

Arrideo and Cor were honorable and devout people that followed the tenets of their god and helped people in need. Cor was a fearsome warrior with bright gold scales.

Arrideo and Cor were followers of Bahamut living in Seagate, a city in Issylra during the Calamity. Arrideo was a cleric with knowledge of the intricacies of the draconic language, and Cor was a fearsome scimitar-wielding paladin, a member of the Order of the Last Banner, and the bearer of Honor's Last Stand. They raised a son together, and although life was hard for them, they helped refugees whenever they could.

During a battle in which Asmodeus was involved, his fiendish forces invaded Seagate; Arrideo was killed, but Cor managed to escape with their young son. Along with a man called Skoll, they traveled to Gwessar, where they stayed for a time with Skoll becoming like an uncle to Erro and teaching him about survival. They made a brief return to Issylra, but they couldn't find any refugees, so they decided to stay in Gwessar Cor, however, didn't live to see her son grow: when Erro was about eleven, a sickness killed the people of the small settlement they had found, including his mother. The young dragonborn stayed with Skoll.

entities.name: Artagan
entities.description:
Artagan is an Archfey from the Feywild. He posed as a satyr named Garmelie to travel with Vox Machina for his own amusement before eventually revealing himself, and later became a minor deity known as the Traveler. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer in Critical Role. He is played by Billy Boyd (as Garmelie) and Matthew Mercer in The Legend of Vox Machina, Season Two.

Artagan was very tall and thin, walking chest-forward and regal-poised. He appeared almost elflike but still had exaggerated fey-like features and long ears that curled past his small head, with a pointed chin, almond-shaped, verdant-emerald green (and sometimes cat-like) eyes and wild, curly orange hair like a lion’s mane going down to his lower back. He wore sleeveless silk vestments of blue and green billowing freely behind him. One of its pockets contained an extra dimension.

While posing as the satyr Garmelie, Artagan played a mischievous and self-centered character that enjoyed amusing himself by drawing immature caricatures of people, stealing items that caught his eye or imagination, and playing pranks. He greatly valued his possessions, sometimes disproportionately to their actual value. Wearing his heart on his sleeve, Garmelie's capricious emotional state was typically easy to read due to his exaggerated and dramatic reactions, even when he tried to hide his feelings. When his impulses were stymied by external forces, he became frustrated easily, but his mood could just as abruptly shift again, seemingly without holding a grudge.

Garmelie preferred to avoid direct confrontation, choosing to run or hide when such situations arose. He also expressed a strong dislike and distrust of "the theatre" on multiple occasions.

entities.name: Artana Voe
entities.description:
() is an uniya bounty hunter who was hired to arrest Gurge Kisgregg. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Artana has piercing light-brown eyes, with elven ears and orcish features, and is described as "strikingly beautiful". She is very slender, and when first encountered by the Bells Hells she was wearing dark leather armor, a very dark green cloak, and a heavy belt holding multiple pouches and tools.

Artana has a years-long reputation in Jrusar's criminal circles as a mercenary for hire known for successfully hunting those that are hard to find. Gurge Kisgregg was one of her targets. With the help of Keledon, the head of the wardens in the Smolder Spire of Jrusar, she brought Gurge to Vali Dertrana in exchange for the bounty.

Shortly after Artana completed her contract, the party picked up her trail, which brought them to the Soot and Swill. While investigating a kitchen in the back of the establishment, Chetney, Dorian, Orym and Ashton found a secret room. When they broke in, they found Artana waiting for their entrance with a crossbow. She shot Orym immediately, but the party was able to talk her down, and after begrudgingly paying her 160 gold, the group learned that after Artana received Gurge from the Wardens, she handed him over to Vali Dertrana in the Moon Tower.

Artenn Gitelle was the human leader of the Relic Seekers guild in Stilben, Tal'Dorei. In an adventure hook in the original Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting, set in 812 PD, a sect of the Remnants has been infiltrating the guilds of Stilben, and Artenn's corpse is discovered buried in the K'Tawl Swamp. Despite this, an entity previously thought to be Gitelle is still alive and well.

So far, Artenn has neither appeared nor been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Arthur
entities.description:
Arthur was a member of the Nameless Ones in Emon in late 842 PD. As an NPC in Exandria Unlimited Prime, Arthur is played by Aabria Iyengar.

Arthur had very pale blue, almost gray, eyes and carried several daggers and a big rapier inside his cloak.

Once Charmed by Opal, Arthur was friendly and willing to go get a beer with her. When she proposed tying him up, he told her he was "into new stuff."

Arthur was one of two cloaked, extremely shady figures lurking at the southern gate of Emon when the Exandria Unlimited party approached. He succumbed to Opal's Charm Person spell, and she chatted with him while the remainder of the party fought the other cloaked figure that he referred to as his friend. He told her that they were members of the Nameless Ones who had been sent to kill her whole squad, but she convinced him to go off with her to get a beer instead. Arthur told Opal he was most familiar with the Dock area of Emon.
