entities.name: Ashann
entities.description:
is a gnome sorcerer working for the Consortium of the Vermilion Dream.

Occult extollants like Ashann typically have a thirst for knowledge that drives them into risky investigations of ancient lore. Like other female members of the Consortium who are not infiltrating other organizations, Ashann wears red robes and a floppy red hat, similar to the hat Master Vrill wears to shield herself from the sun.

Ashann is highly motivated to acquire a fenced ruidium shortsword, to the point that she will attack anyone who outbids her for it. On the other hand, if someone tries to take it from her after she's already purchased it, she prefers to flee, and will only fight if caught. In any case, if she's badly hurt, she will surrender.

By the time of the crisis around the Netherdeep in 836 PD, Ashann is among the middle ranks of the Consortium, and she is sent to Old Man Kruuk, who fences stolen goods out of a bakery that he uses as a front. If the Player Characters in Call of the Netherdeep attempt to join the Cobalt Soul after arriving in Ank'Harel, one of their early missions to gain membership requires that they prove that Kruuk is illegally selling dangerous magic items and confiscate said items, and it is on this mission that they may encounter Ashann, who has an appointment to meet after the bakery closes for the evening to purchase a ruidium shortsword.

entities.name: Asharru
entities.description:
Mistress Asharru was a merchant warrior from Ank'Harel and one of the previous owners of Cabal's Ruin.

Mistress Asharru was a woman in her mid-to-late forties. She had black hair with white streaks throughout it. Her left eye was ruined and sealed closed with a scar. She wore ornate scale mail armor that was black and purple.

After Vox Machina passed Kamaljiori's test, he told them of the current wearer of Cabal's Ruin: "a merchant-warrior with a missing eye in the walls of Ank'Harel."

Anna Ripley, who had been able to listen in on Vox Machina through an enchantment on her old pistol that Percival de Rolo was carrying, tasked Kynan Leore with quietly killing Mistress Asharru, but he failed at the last moment to cut Asharru's throat, so the rest of the party had to rush in and kill her in a less stealthy manner. Worried about detection, the party fled the city quickly, gaining as much distance as they could before the body was discovered.

entities.name: Assum Emring
entities.description:
Seeker Assum Emring is a halfling ranger who held the title of Master of Information on the Council of Tal'Dorei in Emon. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Assum wears ranger garb, a fine mail shirt, and a thick, dark, black cloak. He has tattoos covering one side of his face. Normally, his head is shaved bald, but since the attack of the Chroma Conclave, his hair has grown in and acid scarring has covered some of his tattoos.

Assum used to be a member of the Clasp, but was able to leave and erase almost all trace of his membership of the theives' guild. In his first meeting with Sovereign Uriel Tal'Dorei II, Assum's defiant demeanor almost had him arrested. However the next day, the sovereign instead offered Assum the position of Master of Information on the Tal'Dorei Council.

Assum appeared alongside the other members of the Council of Tal'Dorei to decide what to do with the Horn of Orcus that Vox Machina brought back from the Underdark. Assum said little during the discussion, but his body language indicated that he had heard of illithid before and, like the rest of the Council, was worried about the Horn.

entities.name: Astrid Becke
entities.description:
Astrid Becke is a human Volstrucker, and current Archmage of Civil Influence. She was a student of Trent Ikithon alongside Eadwulf Grieve and Caleb Widogast. As an NPC, Astrid is played by Matthew Mercer. In The Mighty Nein, Astrid is voiced by Ivanna Sakhno.

Caleb originally described Astrid as she was when she was eighteen years old, because that was the last time he had seen her. She was short, about 5'3", with short dark brown hair about four to five inches long, and brown eyes. She had scars on her arms similar to his. She was slight, with attractive but severe features. When Jester asked Caleb if she was pretty, he answered that she was "handsome".

In her mid-thirties, Astrid has dirty blond hair, extremely short in the back but long and side-combed in the front, framing the right side of her face to just past the chin. She has a scar running down her face from the top of one brow to the bottom of her chin, a burn scar on her neck, and a hard look in her eyes. She has black maze-like tattoos on her arms.

In 843 PD Astrid hadn't changed much, and wore ornate form-fitting clothes under a green cloak. However, when she went into hiding she did so under the guise of a half-elf in her mid-twenties wearing a loose peasant blouse, with the same color of hair, but curly, and round rosy cheeks.

entities.name: Atakan Cormoray
entities.description:
Lord is the head of House Cormoray. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Lord Atakan is a handsome old man with a well-groomed salt and pepper beard, hair in dreadlocks adorned with rings, and dark skin with a slight reddish hue. His eyes were tired but serene and happy, indicating a wise, contented life. He had "fire at his fingertips", and wore deep orange and red robes held with a golden belt.

Lord Cormoray was present at the meeting of all the then-extant Sundered Houses called in Dol-Makjar by Lord Otto Einfasen to discuss the apparent machinations of House Tachonis. Atakan arrived in the form of a purple and red meteor. His main concern was initially with his missing daughter, Lady Amariya Dacen Cormoray, who appeared shortly thereafter, allaying his fears. Later, he became uncomfortable when Primus Tachonis brought up the celebrations at the old Kalystra quarries over the "grant at the Penteveral" going through.

Following the meeting, Lord Cormoray quickly accepted Primus Tachonis' offer of 10 million gold pieces in addition to land and titles in Telmora as recompense for his machinations to become the new imperial ruling house over the others. The following day the Cormorays started increasing their security at their estate, since most of their delegation was going to stay in the city for some time.

entities.name: Ataro
entities.description:
Ataro is a shadow dragon or undead dragon, referred to as "a dragon of death", who reached out to aid the celestial Acastriel in the rebellion of the celestial ranks against the gods when many of them were absent infiltrating Aeor during the late Calamity. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Ataro was first seen standing on the top of the Factorum Malleus along with several other of the defending mages. During the battle, he leaped down, transforming into a shadow dragon in the air, and engaged in battle with the mortal avatars of the gods, effectively utilizing his Frightful Presence and Shadow Breath. However, he was very badly wounded by SILAHA's Meteor Swarm, and killed by Ayden's Sunburst.
entities.short_description: Ataro is a shadow dragon or undead dragon, referred to as "a dragon of death", who reached out to aid the celestial Acastriel in the rebellion of the celestial ranks against the gods when many of them were absent…

entities.name: Athesias Uludan
entities.description:
Lord Athesias Uludan is a human mage and a member of the Cerberus Assembly, filling the role of Archmage of Diplomatic Union. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Lord Athesias Uludan is a human male with slightly long salt and pepper hair that curls slightly and is pushed to one side. He wears a long black robe with silver and blue detailing on it.

Athesias Uludan carries himself with a "practiced, very smooth, tailored persona" that lends to charismatic and persuasive interactions. He wears a half-cocked grin and gives off the impression of wanting to make a good impression socially. His charming and bombastic personality helps him in diplomacy, but his narcissistic and showy nature led others in the Cerberus Assembly to distrust him with secrets. Yussa Errenis described him as "a buffoon".

Athesias was originally employed as a teacher at the Soltryce Academy; he was considered effective in that position, but he was felt difficult to trust with state secrets because of his narcissism and fondness for spectacle. As a result, he was promoted to Archmage of Diplomatic Union of the Cerberus Assembly as soon as the position became available.
entities.short_description: Lord Athesias Uludan is a human mage and a member of the Cerberus Assembly, filling the role of Archmage of Diplomatic Union. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Athion Zathuda
entities.description:
Sorrowlord was a powerful fey prince in the service of Sammanar. As an NPC, Zathuda is played by Matthew Mercer.

Zathuda is seven feet tall, with very pale skin, elongated ears, and black brows extending into the edges of his thick wavy long black hair. His eyes are dark grey, with big black pupils. He has magical tattoo markings framing his face, and wore dark armor with a hollow in it. The shoulders of the armor were wider than those of the ordinary guards present and clearly denoted someone of higher status. The Fatestitcher described him as "incredibly darkly handsome." His eyes and cheekbones were similar to those of his daughter.

When Bells Hells saw him again in Ruidus, the Sorrowlord was still wearing his dark armor, and he had some unkempt facial hair. When he was defeated by the adventurers in the Shrine of Gilded Gifts he lost part of his right leg due to Laudna's Disintegrate spell.

After his body was used in Morrigan's Loom, he became a pale tapestry that showed his face, but with empty eye sockets, framed by some of his hair. In this form he was able to speak, and the more he does the more personality and volume his face gains, even moving slightly in the tapestry itself.
entities.short_description: Sorrowlord was a powerful fey prince in the service of Sammanar. As an NPC, Zathuda is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Athodan
entities.description:
was an arcane researcher of the flying city of Aeor, who became famous among his people after finding a strange relic whose properties were used in necromantic and rejuvenation experiments.

His first tests involving the powers of his discovery involved reversing the aging process of overripe fruit, and although the results were messy (the fruit ended up liquefied and tossed all over), led to the accidental creation of a tasty drink that other Aeorians recreated to celebrate and taunt the researcher at various celebrations. Athodan, however, continued his experiments, and eventually he collaborated with Archmage Ayoshadaf, using the artifact to develop a form of time travel, allowing someone to travel to the past while leaving a shadow of themselves anchored in the present. Athodan was in a privileged enough position to have an area of the Genesis Ward dedicated solely to his team and his project, and was only accessible by using a bracelet.
entities.short_description: was an arcane researcher of the flying city of Aeor, who became famous among his people after finding a strange relic whose properties were used in necromantic and rejuvenation experiments.

entities.name: Athudashionus
entities.description:
Athudashionus is an ancient silver dragon and a guardian of the Platinum Sanctuary in Vasselheim. As an NPC, they are played by Matthew Mercer.

Athudashionus is a massive silver dragon who almost looks like a statue when not moving.

As an ancient dragon, Athudashionus was born at least eight centuries ago. A follower of the Platinum Dragon, as of 843 PD they had spent centuries as a protector and guardian of the Platinum Sanctuary in Vasselheim and the worshippers there.

After the apogee solstice of 843 PD Athudashionus was present in the Dawn City during an important meeting of the Exandrian Accord. The silver dragon stayed outside, watching the city. When Bells Hells and their friends were walking nearby, Athudashionus looked almost like a statue until the tail moved, surprising the adventurers.
entities.short_description: Athudashionus is an ancient silver dragon and a guardian of the Platinum Sanctuary in Vasselheim. As an NPC, they are played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Atrix
entities.description:
While Atrix's political climb was a bit aggressive, he since grew to be a formidable leader. He had also been known to take personal delight in the occasional celebration, allowing himself to relax publicly. Friendly in demeanor, though strict in law, Margrave Atrix was not one to cross.

When the Chroma Conclave attacked Westruun, followed immediately by the invasion of the Herd of Storms, Margrave Atrix lost control of his city. Kevdak killed Atrix, had his head impaled on a barricade as a warning symbol, and took the Margrave's house as his own.

entities.name: Atz Yuminor
entities.description:
Atz Yuminor was a heroic wizard who lived during the Age of Arcanum. In his lifetime, he assisted in killing the crazed wizard Clemain Astural and took with him many of Astural's scrolls, which were brought back to his house in the Dividing Plains. He is the namesake of Westruun's Yuminor Observatory and the Scions of Yuminor, which is funded by the headmistress of the Westhall Academy, Yuminor's descendant Estella Ladimar.

entities.name: Audra
entities.description:
Audra is an Ashari druid and one of Keyleth's students. She was a friend of the children of Vox Machina.

Audra is a girl of grey eyes and ash-blond hair.

She became Keyleth's protegee as a child, and the archdruid sometimes took her with her in her journeys. During a visit to Whitestone Audra was introduced to Vesper, the eldest daughter of Percival de Rolo and Vex'ahlia, and they became playmates, along with Juniper and Wilhand'ildan (the children of Pike Trickfoot and Scanlan Shorthalt).
entities.short_description: Audra is an Ashari druid and one of Keyleth's students. She was a friend of the children of Vox Machina.

entities.name: Augustus Valian
entities.description:
King , known simply as Gus by his former war comrades, is the ruler of the Kingdom of Timmony.

Gus is a tall (about 6'4") and muscular man with thick arms and a broad back, the obvious build of a mercenary even years after he became king. He has salt and pepper hair and beard, and scars that include a big one that runs over his left eye and into his cheek (which looks like it should have killed him) and a burn from a fire poker. When the Schemers encountered him in Dol-Makjar, he was wearing a leather vest and a broadsword whose pommel was a snarling dog.

Despite his position as monarch, Augustus remembers his origins and shows a certain level of gratitude and closeness to those who fought alongside him. He is known to favor the commonfolk, and spends time with them when he can, since he doesn't like talking and hearing news exclusively from politicians. To Bolaire Lathalia, he introduced himself as a former soldier who'd now gotten himself involved in politics.

Augustus was born in the nation of Argosia, in the region that would later become his kingdom. There were rumors about him being a bastard, but he was in fact the trueborn son of a noble. Augustus's biological father was a lord of Argosia, whom he described as "a cruel, egotistical tyrant, a monster" who believed he had visions of the shapers after they died. Seemingly fearing for his safety under such a man, the midwife at Augustus's birth got him out of the room and brought him to be raised by the lord's kennel master; during this period of his life he grew very fond of hounds and their loyalty and believed his surname to be "Kennel" for the first eighteen years of his life. However, at some point his true nature was discovered and his adoptive father and uncles were hanged, most likely by order of Augustus's father. In response, Augustus killed his father and took his throne and his title.
entities.short_description: King , known simply as Gus by his former war comrades, is the ruler of the Kingdom of Timmony.

entities.name: Auld Connaught
entities.description:
Auld Connaught is a hunter and gamesman based in Tal'Dorei. At some point, he warned someone about the bears native to the Mooren River Run, noting that river's wildlife are not what they appear to be and are best left alone.

So far, Auld Connaught has not appeared or been referenced onstream.

entities.name: Auntie Mama
entities.description:
Chidra the Blue Rose, better known as , was a human smuggler from Shadycreek Run.

Auntie Mama was a human in her fifties, with a wrinkled face, rouged lips, a bit of chin hair, and gray hair. She used to wear layers of brown-and-green housecoat and floppy felt slippers ended in points, and she always had rings on her fingers.

Auntie Mama was a determined woman who had hardened over the years, becoming smart and mean, and while she showed some compassion, it ended where her own well-being began.

Chidra was born around 772 PD, growing up and eventually marrying a goliath man called Lazak Oakbender, the Dark Forge, who was so famous that was even known in the Menagerie Coast. The couple settled in the North Clover area in Shadycreek Run, and had three children together: a daughter, Brevyn, and two sons, Narath and Vik. While Lazak was a nice father for Brevyn, who loved to spend time in the forge with him, listening to his stories, the goliath was a violent man and cruel husband who beat his wife. Chidra, eventually, poisoned him, causing the goliath to fall into the forge, burning to ash. Brevyn and her brothers, Narath and Vik, were sent away.
entities.short_description: Chidra the Blue Rose, better known as , was a human smuggler from Shadycreek Run.

entities.name: Ava Endlewood
entities.description:
is an elven shopkeeper and proprietor of the Plexus Post. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Ava has wide shoulders and fine, thin, and long grey-green hair, along with a faint grey-green mustache. She dresses in a patterned frock of Marquesian make, under a cotton robe.

Ava runs the Plexus Post trading shop in the Deliberation Disc of Uthodurn. She apparently rents a house to Reani through a trading arrangement. mentions that she has to pay rent.}}

The Mighty Nein recovered from the Tumblecarve residence the red spiral ring requested by Ava in exchange for her refined residuum. Before they decided to return it to her, Caleb identified it as "a ring used to implant dreams in someone's mind", and the party decided that was innocuous enough that they were comfortable giving it to her.

entities.name: Avandros
entities.description:
Avandros was a female archdruid of the Dawn Circle. In the adventure hook Shard of the Shadebarrow, a wraith claiming to be the spirit of Avandros animated an army of ghasts and ghouls and conquered the Silvercut Crossroads. This adventure hook appears in both the Critical Role: Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting sourcebook, set in 812 PD, and the Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting Reborn, set in 836 PD.

So far, Avandros has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Avantika
entities.description:
is an elven pirate, the captain of the Squalleater, and a fanatical champion of Uk'otoa. As an NPC, Avantika is played by Matthew Mercer.

Avantika is an elven woman with fine features, light brown skin, and wild red hair that falls in clustered strings across her face. She wears a sleeveless coat with a high collar, a thick scarf, heavy, elbow-length gloves, and weathered knee-high boots. She has a tattoo of an eye representing Uk'otoa on her sternum, hidden under her scarf. She wears gloves on her hands to hide the Cloven Crystal embedded in her right hand.

Her appearance changed when she returned in undead form: signs of her broken neck were apparent, her skin was pale and clammy, and her eyes glowed faintly blue. She wore a large brimmed hat with a plume of feathers.

Avantika is snarky, confident, and astute. She has a commanding presence and a penetrating gaze that has seen through a thousand lies. Avantika is a fervent believer in Uk'otoa and sincerely wishes to free him in the hope that she would be rewarded. Avantika is willing to remove, sometimes by murder, anyone who she sees as getting in the way of this goal. Despite this fanaticism, Avantika is no fool and shows a remarkable amount of wisdom regarding the people she interacts with. She intentionally built a reputation for being a little bit crazy, knowing that would make people less likely to interfere with her and her plans. She is also extremely protective of her weapons, especially her dagger. She went so far as to kill Frumpkin for landing on its hilt while she was assumed to be asleep. The same caution extended to her quarters on the Squalleater; she trapped her journal's hiding place with a gas that induces Confusion when inhaled.
entities.short_description: is an elven pirate, the captain of the Squalleater, and a fanatical champion of Uk'otoa. As an NPC, Avantika is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Ayo Jabe
entities.description:
is a water genasi of orc parentage and the de facto leader of the rival adventuring party in Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, set in or shortly after 836 PD.

Ayo is impulsive; she likes decisiveness in others and has a low opinion of its opposite. She also despises insincerity. As the adventure begins, her goals are to make a friend around whom she can be her true self, slay a legendary monster, and become a hero like those she's read about. When Ayo is first encountered in Jigow, she speaks with a brash voice. She takes pride in giving her all, respects determination and courage, and prefers to compete fairly rather than accept an unfair magical edge. She doesn't like taking orders.

Chris Perkins described Ayo as a Captain Kirk type of character who "is basically the struggling leader archetype, the one who is always moving forward, but not always with both feet on the ground".

Ayo's family lived in Jigow for generations, and she was born at sea in the Emerald Gulch during a powerful storm. She worked as a hunter for the town of Jigow, and learned some combat skills along the way. She had a dream to form an adventuring party. Three weeks before the adventure begins, mercenary Maggie Keeneyes came to town, and Maggie immediately became loyal friends with Ayo and Dermot. Soon after that Ayo met two more visitors to town: first Irvan Wastewalker, and then rounding out the party, dunamancy wizard Galsariad Ardyth. At the time the adventure begins, her party has been doing odd jobs for a few weeks.
entities.short_description: is a water genasi of orc parentage and the de facto leader of the rival adventuring party in Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, set in or shortly after 836 PD.

entities.name: Azmog
entities.description:
was the vampiric hobgoblin commander of the garrison of the Steel Keep, a prison camp in Rybad-Kol near the end of the Calamity. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

When he appeared on the walls of the fortress prison addressing the prisoners, Azmog wore black armor. He had coiffed hair and distinctive ears..}}

Azmog was cruel and ruthless, willing to kill casually and seeing the prisoners as cattle to be controlled, used up, and disposed of.

Sundering Lord Azmog addressed the thousand assembled prisoners on their knees before him, telling them that soon they would be marching to fight in the final defeat of the Prime Deities in the forces of the Strife Emperor. The All-Hammer, the Platinum Dragon, and the Moonweaver were already dead, and soon the rest would be, too. The hobgoblin prisoner in his grasp, a secret follower of the Changebringer who had preached the hope for change, was forced to recant under the threat of his family being killed before his eyes, but Azmog cruelly killed him anyway, licking the viscera from his fingers before sending the prisoners back to work.
entities.short_description: was the vampiric hobgoblin commander of the garrison of the Steel Keep, a prison camp in Rybad-Kol near the end of the Calamity. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Azrahari
entities.description:
Azrahari looked like a beautiful ageless woman, with a prominent and refined nose, a graceful neck, blue eyes, ringlets of icy-blond hair, and two gray horns that swept back from her forehead. She wore a black robe and a gold amulet shaped like a face, with two silver needles stabbing it diagonally.

During her fight with Lucien she rapidly aged, although maintaining her beauty, and her hair spreaded out around her.

Azrahari lived in a dark-red cottage in the Savalirwood, in an area around which the ground was pocked with inky-black mushrooms. The animal sounds and general sensation in that place suggested a false sense of security. She used her magic and her amulet to kill people and turn their skin in puppets, sometimes inanimated, and sometimes not so much.

At some point before 822 PD two parents came to her: they were artists who, due to a debt with the Jagentoth family, had lost their first born, Elric Tavelle. Even though they had been abusive towards the child, the couple were obsessed with having him back, and Azrahari granted them their wish, creating an animated puppet of the child that made the parents happy, but terrified their other two children, Lucien and Aldreda; at some point the remaining living brother couldn't stay there any longer, so he burned down their caravan with his parents and the puppet inside, and he left with his sister.

entities.name: Babenon Dosal
entities.description:
Babenon Dosal, known to most as only The Gentleman, is a water genasi and the former crime boss in Zadash, working out of the Evening Nip tavern. A couple years after 836 PD, he faked his death to reconnect with Marion Lavorre, allowing Ophelia Mardoon to take over his operation in the city. As an NPC, The Gentleman/Babenon was played by Matthew Mercer. In The Mighty Nein, The Gentleman is voiced by Nathan Fillion.

The Gentleman has light teal skin, a dark goatee, and shoulder-length, jet-black hair with a steep widow's peak. He usually wears a deep-blue coat and leather gloves. His skin seems to be perpetually moist with an ever-present layer of condensation on it.

The Gentleman oozes confidence and, despite inciting fear in many who hear his name, he has a cheerful and approachable personality. He treats the Mighty Nein with respect and generosity and has proved on several occasions that he is a man of his word. The Gentleman runs his operations in Zadash with a certain amount of meticulousness and places a great deal of importance on luck. During most waking hours, The Gentleman is engaging in deals and revelry in equal measure. Despite his calm, flirtatious and charismatic exterior he is still the head of an extremely dangerous criminal syndicate and quite dangerous himself.

The Gentleman claimed, when his credentials were questioned, that he had lived and worked in the underbelly of Zadash since 820 PD and had never been caught. He later revealed to Jester that he was in fact her father, Babenon Dosal. He was previously a merchant sailor out of Feolinn until meeting Marion, Jester's mother. Although he loved Marion, he felt unworthy of her and left to find fortune. His ship was attacked at sea, he was captured, and this led to him spending an extended period of time in Darktow where he became a skilled criminal. When he felt his success had brought him unwanted attention from the Plank King, he left to begin his criminal empire in Zadash.

entities.name: Badran Esparad
entities.description:
was the captain of the Golden Scythe guild of Avalir. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

As a part of his duties to the Golden Scythe, Captain Badran was responsible for transmitting a payment to the mercenary group the "Stormbringers", who had helped the guild on the coast of Issylra. He was told by the guildmaster Nydas Okiro to forestall their payment until just after the Replenishment, as the guild was experiencing a cash flow problem. Before this, the Captain had arranged a fireworks show for Nydas, involving the students of the Sorcerer's University.

When the growing chaos of the Calamity took over the streets of the city of Avalir, Badran, several sailor-marines of the Harvest Moon, Alessander Kyrus, and Daenyria barricaded themselves in the Vault of the Golden Scythe. When Guildmaster Nydas arrived, he conveyed to him a message from the Ring of Gold that required the ships of the guild at the top of the city to evacuate the wealthy and elite of Avalir. When Nydas refused, in favor of the more vulnerable populace, Badran and Alessander then suggested they take care of the gold in their vault. However, Nydas denied its value in the face of the global disaster and continued to insist on saving anyone they could, flying as far as they could from both Avalir and Vasselheim.

As soon as Nydas finished speaking and turned to deal with other matters, Badran, caring more about the guild's gold then people, stabbed him in the back, piercing through his stomach. In retribution, Nydas stabbed him three times in succession and let Sha'korzhan deal the final blow.
entities.short_description: was the captain of the Golden Scythe guild of Avalir. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Baernie
entities.description:
is a half-elf herbalist and druid of the Air Ashari in Zephrah. As an NPC, Baernie is played by Matthew Mercer.

Baernie is a half-elven woman with vibrant brown eyes and blonde hair (like her sisters Leeta and Maeve) that she wears in a pixie cut.

Baernie was born at some point before 813 PD as the daughter of Derrig and Nel. She was one of triplets, having two sisters, Leeta and Maeve, and a younger brother called Will. She eventually became a druid, although she focused on more areas of training, including the herbalist profession.

Circa 837 PD Baernie lost her father and her brother during an attack on Keyleth in Zephrah, since both were part of Keyleth's defense team as the Master of Defense and a member of the Tempest Blades respectively.
entities.short_description: is a half-elf herbalist and druid of the Air Ashari in Zephrah. As an NPC, Baernie is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Balan
entities.description:
Balan was wearing an apron when he met Vox Machina.

Adra called Balan over to show Vox Machina where Greyspine manner was. He lead them outside and to the edge of the outer walkway of the ring of Kraghammer they were in. Balan pointed across the way to where a series of marble pillars were outlining what looked like a residential district. He gave them directions to House Greyspine, telling them it was the house with dark black marble tinted with gold, a wrought iron black gate topped with pikes, and a statue of Ironkeeper Gradim Greyspine in the front yard.

Scanlan thanked Balan for his helpfulness. The dwarf then requested that he fill out a form saying how helpful he had been. Vox Machina gladly accepted, so Balan handed over a single piece of handwritten parchment. Tiberius requested that they each be given one to fill out, but Balan only had the one.

Keyleth and Percy spent the rest of the day making some more comment cards for him. Vox Machina later filled out the homemade cards and turned them in for Balan. Percy and Keyleth also made a few extras for him to hand out to other.
entities.short_description: Balan was wearing an apron when he met Vox Machina.

entities.name: Balgus
entities.description:
Balgus is an older, grizzled dwarf with long gray hair that is pulled into straight braids in the back. He has a big bushy beard. His grin looked like a "railroad of terror."

Balgus has a hunched posture, but when he flexes his rippling muscles become apparent.

Balgus is a frequent drinker; he owns his own brewery and is a regular at the Iron Hearth Tavern. Incredibly tough, Balgus laughed off a strong hit that he didn't see coming from Vax'ildan.

Vox Machina first encountered Balgus while he was passed out drunk at the Iron Hearth Tavern in Kraghammer. Grog and Scanlan went up to Balgus, where the goliath tried to get his attention by showing off the scar on his chest. Scanlan played some music on his flute to cast a Healing Word spell on Balgus to wake him up. The dwarf awoke, wondering where the music was coming from and pawing towards the flute.
entities.short_description: Balgus is an older, grizzled dwarf with long gray hair that is pulled into straight braids in the back. He has a big bushy beard. His grin looked like a "railroad of terror."

entities.name: Balthasar Bleakskull
entities.description:
Balthasar Bleakskull is a goliath bard and performer from Westruun.

Balthasar is a surprisingly slim goliath of angular face. His skin has the characteristic whitish tone of half-giants, but on his face he also wears eyeshadow and black lipstick that contrast with said paleness. He wears elegant burgundy, dark blue, and white clothing with silver trim, puff sleeves, a cape, and dark boots. He also carries with him a humanoid skull and a burgundy and gray zither adorned with another skull, silver and of the size of his fist.

In his youth Balthasar was a boy who enjoyed theater and followed his passions. After the incident that marked his arrival to adulthood he became tortured by the repressed emotions of that event, preferring to channel that anguish into moving performances that mark the public instead of facing his own pain.

Balthasar was born in Westruun, being raised by two loving (and equally massive) goliath parents: one of them was a warrior, and the other was an astronomer of the Yuminor Obserbatory. The child grew up being exposed to both the adventuring and academic lifestyle, but from an early age he was drawn to the theatre, and it was towards it that he turned his passion, studying in one of the city centers that offered drama training. During that time, the young goliath developed his dramatic skills, and learned about the magic that bards weave in their art.
entities.short_description: Balthasar Bleakskull is a goliath bard and performer from Westruun.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Barbithrix
entities.description:
is a human warlock, or something close to those descriptors, in service of the Strife Emperor at Rybad-Kol in the closing days of the Calamity. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Barbithrix is overall a horrifying sight. He is gaunt, with a magically stretched skull. Emerging from his back is an additional pair of arms with poor fine motor skills but long claws suited for violence. He wears black robes, leather, and shaped bone, with a collar made of upward-facing skeletal claws.

Barbithrix is cold and calculating, quick to kill any person as soon as their value in service to the Strife Emperor is not worth their upkeep, but no sooner; he is a stickler for detail, and allows himself to be held to his word on deadlines. He demands the same of those who work for him.

Barbithrix visited the infirmary to ensure that any patients who were not recovering fast enough to be worth maintaining would be promptly killed. Rei'nia Saph, the nurse at the infirmary, assured Barbithrix that her patients were all recovering before the deadlines; he pressed her to make sure she was only advocating for her patients insofar as they were of value to the Strife Emperor. He tasked his servant with sending soldiers to kill a patient if he did not recover by nightfall.
entities.short_description: is a human warlock, or something close to those descriptors, in service of the Strife Emperor at Rybad-Kol in the closing days of the Calamity. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Bark
entities.description:
is a human pirate and member of Avantika's crew aboard the Squalleater. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bark was one of the crew on watch during the first night of the Squalleater crew's stay on Darktow. He kept watch from the crow's nest when Nott cast Phantasmal Force upon him, making him believe the crow's nest is on fire. After calling out in panic and initially trying to beat out the perceived flames to no effect, he in desperation jumped from the crow's nest to the deck below, breaking his leg in the process.

A short time after his fall Caduceus, seeking out the cause of the commotion on the docks, found Bark in his injured state being helped by some of the guards from the dock. Seeing the severity of Bark's broken leg, he set the bone back in place and cast Cure Wounds, successfully healing the injury. Caduceus after hearing Bark explain what he experienced tried to explain the hallucination as being caused by psychedelic effects of the mysterious fruit he had picked from Urukayxl and apologetically "confessed" he may have accidentally left some in the ship's kitchen, though Bark seemed unconvinced.

With his leg healed, Bark made his way to the Bloated Cup with Caduceus, which is where he is last seen until the next day as the Mighty Nein retired to their rooms for the night. The following morning Bark was amongst the crew summoned to the Squalleater by Captain Avantika where he once more explained his involvement in events from the previous night. This left him on the deck when Caleb cast Wall of Fire.
entities.short_description: is a human pirate and member of Avantika's crew aboard the Squalleater. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Baron Visco
entities.description:
is an ogre butcher in Asarius. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Baron Visco is an ogre who wears a monocle.

Baron Visco hired a hunting party of bugbears, including Gluzzo, to go into the Wastes and bring back food. He planed to sell what they brought back to the Kryn Dynasty for the war effort.

Gluzzo describes Baron Visco as "super smart" and "kind of a douche."
entities.short_description: is an ogre butcher in Asarius. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Barthie
entities.description:
is an Elder of the Bormodo village of Razora on Ruidus; his cytaa is Chu. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Barthie walks with the aid of a long gnarled stick he leans on. He has long, stringy gray-white hair, deep wrinkles, and deep-set eyes. When he smiles, his intense expression melts into grandfatherly warmth.

Barthie bonded with Chu when the cytaa was young, and they have stayed together ever since, taking care of each other. Around 803 PD the bormodo visited Kreviris, the capital of the Imperium. In recent times he has had contact with the Volition, and it is strongly implied he may be a member or at least a collaborator.

In 843 PD Barthie shared much information about the history and philosophy of the inhabitants of Ruidus with Bells Hells, after Dono introduced them to him. After a long conversation in which both parties learned about their respective worlds (and during which the Elder confirmed that Otohan Thull and Ludinus Da'leth had been seen in the area weeks before) Barthie (despite Chu's caution) expressed willingness to help the adventurers meet Zhesh, an agent of the Volition, but before they could do so Willmaster Edmuda arrived at his house and a battle ensued.
entities.short_description: is an Elder of the Bormodo village of Razora on Ruidus; his cytaa is Chu. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Baryn Vestisho
entities.description:
is a female half-elven doctor of Exandrian history from Othanzia. As an NPC, Baryn is played by Matthew Mercer.

In 843 PD when Bells Hells encountered her, Baryn was thin, had thick black shoulder-length hair, thick glasses, and silver elven scroll tattoos around her eyes. She was wearing pants and a green blouse. She appeared to be in her 40s.

Baryn is a doctor of Exandrian history from Othanzia, and specializes in research on The Founding and The Schism - in other words, the most ancient of histories. She was one of three people who sometime before 843 PD became aware of inconsistencies in the promulgated histories of Ruidus, the other two being Arnold Drot and Janina. She and the others broke into the temple of Erathis in Vasselheim and stole secret ancient texts referring to the two forgotten gods Vordo and Ethedok, their destruction by the entity Predathos, and Predathos's subsequent imprisonment in the newly-created red moon Ruidus. Drot was captured during the break-in and likely remains in the hands of the Platinum Sanctuary, while Baryn and Janina escaped to Marquet. Baryn believed that the judicators that had recently arrived in Yios were looking for them.

Baryn was with Ebenold Kai in the cellar of his home when Bells Hells broke in. They fled to Planerider Ryn's office in the Elemental Plane of Fire, and were left there without a means of escape when Ryn was later turned to stone while scouting the Tishtan excavation site. After the apogee solstice, Ebenold, who had been with Baryn, was present in Whitestone.
entities.short_description: is a female half-elven doctor of Exandrian history from Othanzia. As an NPC, Baryn is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Bautha Dyrr
entities.description:
Bautha Dyrr is a drow priest of Xalicas at Bazzoxan.

Bautha is a drow woman who wears a cloak with a black pin in the shape of a wing. As a priest, she presumably generally wears this over a chain shirt.

Bautha is dedicated and selfless, devoting much of her time and magic to healing the wounds of those in need. She is cultured and careful, especially with matters related to the Betrayer Gods. She also shows a pragmatic attitude towards the Kryn Dynasty's quest to fully reclaim Bazzoxan, seeing it as a source of unworthy suffering.

Despite living in the Kryn Dynasty, which is generally devoted to the Luxon, Bautha became a priest of Xalicas, a solar who served the Arch Heart. Bautha can recall legends spoken in the temples of the far-away cities of Ank'Harel and Vasselheim, including that of the story of Alyxian. By 835 or 836 PD she became a healer in the infirmary at Bazzoxan, and while she, as a follower of Xalicas, disapproves of the government's obsession with controlling the city and the amount of military presence they dedicate to it, she supports the effort to hold back the demonic forces, and uses each spell slot she has to heal whoever may need it.
entities.short_description: Bautha Dyrr is a drow priest of Xalicas at Bazzoxan.

entities.name: Beedle
entities.description:
Beedle is a surname or given name which may refer to:

People:

Ashley Beedle (born 1962), British DJ, producer and remixer

Ernest A. Beedle (1933–1968), American lawyer and politician

Martin Frosty Beedle (born 1961), British rock drummer

George E. Beedle (born 1964), American politician, member of the Wisconsin State Assembly from 1903 to 1906

William Beedle Jr., real name of actor William Holden (1918–1981)

Fictional characters:

The title character of J. K. Rowling's The Tales of Beedle the Bard

Beedle, in The Legend of Zelda series

The Japanese name of Weedle, a Pokémon species

entities.name: Belana Zolaed
entities.description:
Belana Zolaed is a drow priest of the Luxon at Jigow.

Belana is a devoted woman who takes care of her deity's temple and her fellow worshipers' ceremonies.

Belana joined or was born as a member of Den Zolaed, one of the twelve noble Dens of the Kryn Dynasty. She became a priest of the Luxon with divine magical abilities.

When the city of Jigow officially became part of the Dynasty around 735 PD, the cult to the Luxon also extended to the city. By 836 PD a dodecahedron-shaped temple had been built there, and Belana maintained the temple and conducted its ceremonies. A part of the local population still mistrusted these new beliefs, which they felt were suffocating the preexisting culture.
entities.short_description: Belana Zolaed is a drow priest of the Luxon at Jigow.

entities.name: Ben
entities.description:
is a bugbear who works as a bodyguard for Maruo. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Ben is a bugbear. He is a generic character who wears a cloak of invisibility.

There is no background information for Ben.

Ben is employed by Maruo as a bodyguard.
entities.short_description: is a bugbear who works as a bodyguard for Maruo. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Benathar
entities.description:
is a powerful mage defeated by Beauregard Lionett and Caleb Widogast as well as potentially other members of the Mighty Nein between Campaign Two and Campaign Three (between 836 and 843 PD).

All that is known of Benathar is from an offhand comment by Beauregard, when Caleb mentioned that many powerful mages feared Ludinus Da'leth. Beauregard responded, "Oh bullshit! We fucked up Halas. We fucked up Trent. We fucked up Benathar. Just another mage to add to the tally. Right? Just mark another tally piece."
entities.short_description: is a powerful mage defeated by Beauregard Lionett and Caleb Widogast as well as potentially other members of the Mighty Nein between Campaign Two and Campaign Three (between 836 and 843 PD).

entities.name: Benjamin Cole
entities.description:
Benjamin Cole is a human book merchant operating in Vasselheim. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Benjamin is quite wry, and no-nonsense. He seems to take his job, and the hobby of book collecting, very seriously.

Benjamin is an employee of a bookstore in Vasselheim.

While looking for information on the Raven Queen, Vex'ahlia met Benjamin while attempting to read a book without buying it. He insisted that she purchase the book if she were to read it, and upon realizing that she had no intention of doing so, took the book from her and declared that there would be no sale. Vex caved and paid full price, giving Benjamin the honor of being the first person to ever make Vex pay full price.
entities.short_description: Benjamin Cole is a human book merchant operating in Vasselheim. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Bentha Tamalos
entities.description:
is an innkeeper, beekeeper, and the owner of the Bisaft Meadery. As an NPC, Bentha is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bentha is a heavyset woman in her late 50s to early 60s with beautiful brown skin and a wide smile.

Bentha is warm and talkative and is more than happy to entertain the many tourists who visit Bisaft Isle. She also comes across as an even tempered woman, clearly keeping her composure as Jester mimics her distinctive accent.

As well as being the proprietor of the Bisaft Meadery, Bentha keeps bees on the island with which a sweetened honey mead is brewed and offers tours of the hives to tourists.
entities.short_description: is an innkeeper, beekeeper, and the owner of the Bisaft Meadery. As an NPC, Bentha is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Berin Abenard
entities.description:
Berin Abenard is a minor noble and officer of the court of law in Westruun, and Vex'ahlia's stalker.

Berin is a pale human man with shoulder-length, ash-blond hair and piercing blue eyes. Around 807 PD, he appeared to be older than Vex'ahlia, "in his late twenties at most." When they met, he was wearing a finely tailored "sleek gray coat trimmed with gold," "stylish boots," a hat, gold bracelets, and several rings, and was carrying a purse, with no weapons.

Around 807 PD, Vex'ahlia saw Abenard at a jeweler's shop in Westruun trying to buy a silver bracelet. He followed her throughout the day, and eventually introduced himself in a bookstore. After overhearing that she was researching dragons, he offered to bring her to the Cobalt Reserve and introduce her to his contacts there. Vex'ahlia declined the offer, but Abenard continued to insist, invading her personal space and threatening her verbally. Vex'ahlia responded by threatening him in turn with a knife. He left his hat and purse behind as he stormed off; Vex'ahlia stole his coins.

The following day, Vex'ahlia saw someone resembling Abenard in the market, and hid from him. That evening, as she visited the Scholar Ward on her own, she was followed and attacked from a distance by Lyre, a Clasp member. When Vax'ildan confronted the man, he told him he was fulfilling a Clasp contract for Spireling Gideor. Gideor told Vax'ildan that the person who put out the contract to kidnap his sister was "a minor nobleman who has requested [the Clasp's] services before" and "a good customer." He did not name Abenard, but Vax'ildan inferred that it was him. Unwilling to cancel the contract, Gideor instead made a deal with Vax'ildan. He transformed Lyre into a copy of Vex'ahlia and tore out his tongue. Gideor told Vax'ildan that he would give the Vex'ahlia copy to the nobleman "[f]or as long as our gentleman contractor has use of him."
entities.short_description: Berin Abenard is a minor noble and officer of the court of law in Westruun, and Vex'ahlia's stalker.

entities.name: Bertholt
entities.description:
Bertholt is the dragonborn servant of the Darrington Family. As an NPC, Bertholt is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bertholt is a very tall, thin, brass-scaled dragonborn. He has no tail, which speaks of his Ravenite lineage.

Category:Deastok Category:Ravenites Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: Bertholt is the dragonborn servant of the Darrington Family. As an NPC, Bertholt is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Bertrand Dwendal
entities.description:
King Bertrand Dwendal is the king of the Dwendalian Empire in Wildemount and was one of the targets listed on Ripley's gun, "Animus". As an NPC, Dwendal is played by Matthew Mercer. In The Mighty Nein, Bertrand Dwendal is voiced by Graham McTavish.

In 835–836 PD, Bertrand Dwendal was a tall human male in his late sixties. He had wavy, dark grey hair falling past his shoulders, a long, thin beard tied from beneath, and he wore the golden crown depicted on the bottom of the crest of the Dwendalian Empire.

Bertrand Dwendal is a dark, clever, and often paranoid king - and a lonely one since his wife's death. Fiercely nationalistic and proud of his heritage, the king harbors a disdain for outsiders and their challenges to imperial rule. Whilst he does genuinely wish to protect the lives of his people and be remembered as the best of his bloodline, the increased pressures of civil unrest and the inability of his son to produce an heir have made him fearful his family line will come to an end, an obsession which drives him to seek out a way to prolong his own life.

Bertrand Dwendal is known for being a mighty and authoritarian ruler. Due to his disdain for religious practices and the extensive taxes levied on the Dwendalian citizens, tensions have begun to brim beneath the surface of Western Wynandir as whispers of dissent continue to grow.
entities.short_description: King Bertrand Dwendal is the king of the Dwendalian Empire in Wildemount and was one of the targets listed on Ripley's gun, "Animus". As an NPC, Dwendal is played by Matthew Mercer. In The Mighty Nein, Bertrand Dwendal…

entities.name: Besh Turmin
entities.description:
is the duergar owner and proprietor of Turmin's Tinctures and Tonics in Rosohna. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Turmin is a duergar dwarf with even gray skin, a permanent scowl on his face, and almost pupil-less white eyes. His hair is a deep red maroon color parted in the center, and he has a puff of red for a beard.

While somewhat combative, Turmin is willing to sell almost anything, at a substantial markup, even if he has to go elsewhere to buy it.

Turmin grew up in the Shadowshire of Rosohna.

entities.description:
was a kobold. As an NPC, Bex is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bex, alongside Spurt, was tasked with following the Mighty Nein. After being discovered Bex snuck away while the Mighty Nein talked to Spurt.

entities.name: Birdie Calloway
entities.description:
Birdie Calloway is a fey woman and Fearne Calloway's mother. As a NPC, Birdie is played by Matthew Mercer.

Birdie is a faun, and she's often described as bearing a strong resemblance to her daughter (especially in the eyes), although she is visibly a little bit older, slightly shorter, and stockier. She has blue-green eyes and bushy auburn brown hair that has got blonder because of the sun, flowing down to her mid-back. When she was first seen by Bells Hells she was wearing a thick leather jacket and riding goggles.

According to Dusk, Birdie is very kind. When she spoke with Imogen Temult through the Sending spell, she seemed to be cautious. Imahara Joe considered both her and Ollie nice and jovial.

Birdie appeared to be either exceptionally trusting or exceptionally pragmatic. She stated she knew nothing of Ira Wendagoth's past evil deeds and brushed them off as probably being done at someone else's behest, and said that although he had done bad things in the past, he was the only person who could help them save the Feywild. Later, however, it appeared that Ira might have tampered with some of both her and Ollie's memories, which might account for her attitude toward him.
entities.short_description: Birdie Calloway is a fey woman and Fearne Calloway's mother. As a NPC, Birdie is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Black King
entities.description:
The Black King is the name of a statue of Westruun's founder Palest Westruun, mockingly named after the black dragon Umbrasyl, who briefly conquered Westruun during the Chroma Crisis. Both Westruun and the Black King statue were blessed by a High Priest of the Lawbearer when it was unveiled on the one-year anniversary of Westruun's freedom — when the city is threatened, the statue is supposed to animate into a stone golem and defend the people of Westruun.

entities.name: Blemmy
entities.description:
was the dwarven leader of the crew that had won the Hour of Honor three weeks in a row before Mighty Nein's victory. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Ol’ Blemmy was a dwarf with a giant gash down his face, and a snow-blind eye in the eye socket under the gash. His gray-black, salt-and-pepper beard is so unkempt that it is difficult to see his mouth.

Originally, he was an ice sailor on the Frigid Depths out of Icehaven, but he retired ten years before the Mighty Nein encountered him in Hupperdook.

entities.name: Blenton Zuurthom
entities.description:
Blenton Zuurthom is a male dwarven architect and a member of Kraghammer's House of Zuurthom. Known between 812 and 836 PD as one of the older and kinder dwarves and an architectural savant, he tries to oversee every major construction project in Kraghammer's Bottom Slab.

So far, Blenton Zuurthom has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.
entities.short_description: Blenton Zuurthom is a male dwarven architect and a member of Kraghammer's House of Zuurthom. Known between 812 and 836 PD as one of the older and kinder dwarves and an architectural savant, he tries to oversee every…

entities.name: Bluud
entities.description:
is a minotaur bodyguard of Marion Lavorre. He protected Marion at the Lavish Chateau in Nicodranas since her daughter Jester was a baby, and he continues to serve as her guard decades later. He was often found at his watch post outside of Marion's door when Jester and the rest of the Mighty Nein visited the Chateau.

As an NPC, Bluud is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bluud is a massive, dual-horned minotaur with thick fur. In The Mighty Nein Origins: Jester Lavorre, he is depicted with brown fur, lighter brown hair, and dark brown horns like that of Cape buffalo, and he wears his hair and a goatee in braids.

When Mighty Nein met him in , he wore a very fine shirt and no pants. In The Mighty Nein Origins, he wore a studded leather garment similar to a bases around his waist but no shirt. He has a septum and nipple piercings, in which he wears gold rings, and wears two golden bangle bracelets on each wrist and one on each bicep.

entities.name: Bodo Icozrin
entities.description:
is the drow administrator of the Deepriver Mining Camp. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Foreman Bodo is a middle-aged drow with shoulder-length hair and a straggly goatee. He has hard facial features and is somewhat plump. Bodo dresses in good quality clothing and is bedecked with a large amount of expensive jewelry.

Under ordinary circumstances, he is a rather officious individual and very arrogant in his dealings with people, especially those he considers to be subordinate. However, when challenged by a stronger personality the facade soon crumbles.

Very little is known of his background, although he is fairly important within Den Icozrin due to his being placed in charge of such an important installation. He is also known to be married, but is involved in an affair with another woman, known only as V.

entities.name: Bogrey
entities.description:
is a promising lizardfolk artificer and an ally of Thjazi Fang. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

He is a crocodile-like lizardfolk with a long tail, who wore canvas-like overalls and a wide strawhat.

Bogrey is described as a man with too much confidence, to the point in which he shows a lack of interest for remarkable things and places if they don't align with his methods or interests.

At some point during his youth Bogrey learned about magic and developed a talent for it, focusing on the most physical aspect of it as an enchanter and a creator of arcane devices.
entities.short_description: is a promising lizardfolk artificer and an ally of Thjazi Fang. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Bol'bara
entities.description:
is a goblin warlock and elder seer of Urzin.

Bol'bara is an elder of the mobile village of Urzin. She was alive during the reign of Ogre Lord Buhfal I, and acts as seer and chief loremaster for the town. She also is one of the most trusted councilors to Buhfal II, who rules in the absence of Urzin's Champion, Sunbreaker Olomon.

In 835 PD during the War of Ash and Light, Bol'bara journeyed out of the village within Brokenveil Marsh to a ritual stone in order to gather spell components and commune with her patron, the shadow demon Trush. However, Bol'bara was captured by a garrison of Righteous Brand soldiers lead by the Imperial Inquisitor Parson Pellinost, and taken to the Imperial outpost Fort Venture for questioning and torture. With her rite interrupted, Bol'bara became host to Trush.

At Fort Venture, Pellinost, a cultist of Vesh the Bloody Siren tortured Bol'bara by killing her each day then resurrecting her with the spell Revivify. On the third day of this torture, Bol'bara became fully possessed by Trush. With this power granted, the demon-possessed goblin was given enough power to kill Pellinost and wreak havoc across Fort Venture and escape, killing everyone at the fort save for another prisoner, Alonne Frith.
entities.short_description: is a goblin warlock and elder seer of Urzin.

entities.name: Bolo
entities.description:
was the plus-one of Loquatius Seelie at the pre-Replenishment party hosted by Patia Por'co. As an NPC was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Loquatius Seelie initially described her as gorgeous, but later told Laerryn Coramar-Seelie Bolo was "just some arm candy". Loquatius was a friend of a friend, and they were "sort of set up" -- Patia's party was the second time they'd met.

Bolo was born in Aeor as one of the three daughters of Gorus and Vitalio Maximus, an illustrious couple of the floating city.

She presumably met Loquatius Seelie during a meeting between Avalir and Aeor, and since she wanted to be a reporter like him, he took her under his wing and was helping her in this goal, bringing her to a party in Patia Por'co's home, where Bolo explained that in Aeor it was sometimes illegal to ask probing reporter-like questions.
entities.short_description: was the plus-one of Loquatius Seelie at the pre-Replenishment party hosted by Patia Por'co. As an NPC was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Bosun
entities.description:
, also known as Bo the Breaker, is a half-orc member of The Fletching and Moondrop Traveling Carnival of Curiosities. As an NPC, Bo is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bosun is a tall, masculine half-orc man with a well-groomed handlebar mustache that curves out to the sides. He wears a billowing white silk shirt and black trousers.

When Lestera died Bosun cried a lot, although he mentioned hers was the happiest corpse he had ever seen, which cheered up his friends a bit.

Bo the Breaker accompanied the carnival to Nogvurot between 834 and the first half of 835 PD, when Molly scammed a lawmaster who was scamming his own people; he and the Fire Fairy performed for the locals.
entities.short_description: , also known as Bo the Breaker, is a half-orc member of The Fletching and Moondrop Traveling Carnival of Curiosities. As an NPC, Bo is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Bouldergut
entities.description:
is an ogre pirate and Captain Avantika's personal bodyguard on board the Squalleater. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Bouldergut is a massive female ogre with yellowed teeth and greasy gray hair that falls in her face. She wears a simple leather tunic, and wields a large greatclub made from the mast of a ship.

Bouldergut is simple minded but obedient and loyal, particularly to Captian Avantika. She often comes across as jovial and even friendly despite her fearsome appearance, but shows great enthusiasm for acts of violence when given the chance. As an ogre she is often used as an enforcer and muscle by the crew due to her size and strength.

Prior to meeting the Mighty Nein, Bouldergut had served under Avantika as her bodyguard for approximately a decade. Avantika claims Bouldergut fell into her service towards the start of her pirate career.
entities.short_description: is an ogre pirate and Captain Avantika's personal bodyguard on board the Squalleater. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Bram Gulchswattle
entities.description:
Watchmaster Bram Gulchswattle is a gnomish guard who serves as Watchmaster for the Crownsguard in Hupperdook.

Around 835 PD during the War of Ash and Light, Sken Zabriss was broken out of Gearhole Prison by Huron Stahlmast's kobold minions, briefly encountering an adventuring party in the Ironlot streets. Bram and several Crownsguard arrived on the scene shortly afterward, questioning the party on the events that transpired. Recognizing them as adventurers, he hired the party to investigate and re-capture Sken, offering a bounty of 500 gold pieces, with 250 gold payed up front. He also gave the party a badge to show that they were working for him.

After the party located and captured Sken, he rewarded them the rest of the bounty. After telling Bram about Stahlmast and his lair behind Silver Falls, he offered to extend their bounty for the capture or elimination of Stahlmast, as well as evidence of his plans. For Stahlmast he would reward 1,500 gold pieces, and an additional 300 gold for recovering his plans and 150 gold for the letter confirming his dealings with Den Hythenos of the Kryn Dynasty.

Category:Watchmasters Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: Watchmaster Bram Gulchswattle is a gnomish guard who serves as Watchmaster for the Crownsguard in Hupperdook.

entities.name: Brandon Zimmerset
entities.description:
Brandon Zimmerset is the former margrave of Westruun, Tal'Dorei. He was appointed after the Chroma Crisis and held the position until 822 PD.

After his appointment as margrave, Zimmerset planned to restore Westruun to his former glory and had worries he shared with his councilors about the level of organization of the Ravagers.

Appointed after the Chroma Crisis, in the peace that followed, Zimmerset wanted to restore Westruun to its former glory, a plan resented by some rebellious Westruunian students and traders who believe Westruun was never "glorious" under the rule of a margrave. Zimmerset resides with his family in the Margrave's Keep in Westruun's Opal Ward.

In the adventure hook Counter-espionage in the Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting, which is set in 812 PD, Zimmerset is nearing the end of a three-year investigation into the Clasp's headquarters in Westruun, with information on Spirelings Gholesh, Oalan, and Fetch. However, unbeknownst to the margrave, he has been given misinformation by secret Clasp plant Winston Destwiler, and the Clasp leaders, aware of his investigation, have set into motion a plot to ambush and assassinate the margrave.
entities.short_description: Brandon Zimmerset is the former margrave of Westruun, Tal'Dorei. He was appointed after the Chroma Crisis and held the position until 822 PD.

entities.name: Brashaar
entities.description:
was an important human mage and architect of great influence in the flying city of Aeor during the Calamity.

Brashaar was a human woman who dressed and adorned herself in a way that denoted her status and importance. Before Aeor's fall she wore a multilayered cloak and mantle adorned with details, tethers, and tassels.

She was proud, powerful, ambitious, and filled with ideas that she shared with the others Aeorians. She was also confident, even in dangerous situations.

Brashaar arrived or was born in the city of Aeor during the Calamity, and despite the violent and dire historical context, she became a successful figure in the magocracy, a respected architect. She had many thoughts and ideas shared by her fellow Aeorians, although that same ideology made her own people blame her for drawing the ire of the gods upon their city.
entities.short_description: was an important human mage and architect of great influence in the flying city of Aeor during the Calamity.

entities.name: Braum
entities.description:
Braum is a surname. It is an Americanized form of the German surname Brahm, as well as an Ashkenazi Jewish surname which may have originated as a variant of Braun. The 2010 United States census found 250 people with the surname Braum, making it the 76,768th-most-common name in the country. This represented a decrease from 279 (66,274th-most-common) in the 2000 Census. In both censuses, roughly nine-tenths of the bearers of the surname identified as White.

People and fictional characters with the name include:

Bill Braum, founder of American restaurant chain Braum's

Bohuslav Braum (born 1956), Czech weightlifter

Daniel M. Braum, 1966 recipient of the American Society of Industrial Engineers' Gilbreth Medal

Eduarda Braum (born 2001), Brazilian beauty pageant titleholder

Braum, the Heart of Freljord, League of Legends character voiced by JB Blanc

entities.name: Brazilda
entities.description:
Mother is a very old woman who serves in The Zenith in the Whitestone. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Brazilda is an old woman with a gentle smile, thinning gray hair, and a wrinkly forehead that leaves her eyes partially hidden.

At some point of her life Brazilda became a follower of Pelor, and ended up working in his temple in the Greyfield of Whitestone. Eventually she became a revered clergyperson, being titled "Mother".

When Imogen Temult visited The Zenith in 843 PD, during the apogee solstice, Mother Brazilda greeted her. Since the sorcerer seemed confused about how to pray, the priest gave her some advice, explaining how faith worked for her and how even the smaller things in life could be seen as miracles. Brazilda also suggested leaving an offering if it felt right. Shortly afterwards, she returned to her spot in the temple, where she started eating strawberries.
entities.short_description: Mother is a very old woman who serves in The Zenith in the Whitestone. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Bren Brenatto
entities.description:
Bren Brenatto is the second son of Yeza and Veth Brenatto. As an NPC, Bren is played by Matthew Mercer.

At some point prior to Fjord and Jester's wedding, Yeza and Veth conceived a second child.

Days after Fjord and Jester's wedding the Brenattos were preparing the crib for their new child, although according to Veth the pregnancy was still in its early stages (about two months); because of that, when Essek told them that Caleb was trapped in the Folding Halls of Halas, Veth joined the mission. It ended up becoming challenging, because Caleb had been corrupted by an entity known as the Ego Leech, and when they finally faced him, they had to fight the wizard. He, in order to keep the adventurers distracted, used Wish to cause Veth's pregnancy to move forward in time, so that labour started in the middle of the battle. As people were fighting around them, Veth tried to deal with the birth, receiving the assistance of Jester and even trying to cast magic on her own body to encourage her baby to come out faster, unsuccessfully.

When Caleb finally regained his senses and was freed, the Mighty Nein returned with Veth to Exandria, and she was brought home, where she finally gave birth. Both Yeza and Luc were happy for the arrival of the baby halfling boy, and Veth declared his name would be Bren.
entities.short_description: Bren Brenatto is the second son of Yeza and Veth Brenatto. As an NPC, Bren is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Brevyn Oakbender
entities.description:
was a half-goliath blood hunter and a member of The Tombtakers.

Brevyn was a tall and muscular woman with brown eyes and blond wavy hair pinned up with a gold hairpin. She had a butterfly tattoo in her chest.

She cared about her friends, and about her family, even when she didn't show it to them. She had a temper and found it hard to give up control, but her charisma allowed her to command respect in others.

Brevyn was one of the three children (and the only woman) of Chidra the Blue Rose and Lazak Oakbender, known as the Dark Forge, a goliath who, despite living in the Greying Wildlands, was known even in the Menagerie Coast. Brevyn grew up in Shadycreek Run and loved to spend time in the forge with her father, who told her a lot of stories; however, Lazak was a violent man who beat his wife, and Chidra, eventually, poisoned him, causing the goliath to fall into the forge, burning to ash. Brevyn and her brothers, Narath and Vik, were sent away.
entities.short_description: was a half-goliath blood hunter and a member of The Tombtakers.

entities.name: Brimscythe
entities.description:
Brimscythe, the Iron Storm was a blue dragon from the Chroma Conclave. His human form was General Krieg Tristan, an identity he stole after killing the real Krieg to gain the manor in the Cloudtop District of Emon and the position of the Master of Law on the Tal'Dorei Council. Brimscythe was the first dragon killed by Vox Machina in his lair.

As an NPC, Brimscythe was portrayed by Matthew Mercer. He appears in The Legend of Vox Machina, voiced by David Tennant.

As General Krieg, he had brown hair and was attractive enough to earn the attention of many of the ladies in Emon.

As General Krieg, he had an approachable personality, behaving in a friendly manner towards Vox Machina and showing interest in the information they presented to him. He seemed sad to hear about the death of fellow Council member Sir Gregory Fince.

entities.name: Briyakar Jurrell
entities.description:
, better known as just Jurrell, was an elf member of the Claret Orders that later became one of The Tombtakers.

Jurrell was an elven woman with brown skin covered in piercings. As of 831 PD her head was shaved, and she had runics tattoos. Her teeth were filed to points and she had an immense jewel pierced into her navel.

She had a refined behavior acquired in proper cities, around proper folk. She used to brag about her talent stealing. She was ambitious.

Jurrell was born in Yardel, in a community of elven jewelers that soon became impoverished. She and her family moved to Nogvurot seeking a better life. She maintained an interest in jewelry, and at some point began to steal it, increasing her mastery of the activity to the point where she infiltrated Rexxentrum as a handmaiden of Queen Duvia Dwendal, stealing an immense royal jewel from her, and becoming wanted by imperial decree.
entities.short_description: , better known as just Jurrell, was an elf member of the Claret Orders that later became one of The Tombtakers.

entities.name: Brom Goldhand
entities.description:
Arbiter Brom Goldhand is a human member of the Tal'Dorei Council, the former captain of the guard, the Master of Law, and the head of the Watchful Hall. As an NPC, Brom is played by Matthew Mercer.

In 810 PD, Brom is a built and armored man, the tallest of the Tal'Dorei Council. He has a thick square jaw that is unshaven with short black hair. He suffered extensive burn scars from the Chroma Conclave's attack on Emon.

By 836 PD, Brom's hair has turned gray and he maintains a stoic lack of expression.

Brom Goldhand took up his position in the Tal'Dorei Council three months before he met Vox Machina. The position had previously been held by General Krieg.
entities.short_description: Arbiter Brom Goldhand is a human member of the Tal'Dorei Council, the former captain of the guard, the Master of Law, and the head of the Watchful Hall. As an NPC, Brom is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Brookmeadow
entities.description:
is a nixie living in the Dahapshanee Wood. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Brookmeadow is a small brook fairy, about seven inches tall.

She was cautious around big people, but was kind and helpful with other fey like herself. She became particularly emotional over gifts.

Brookmeadow was one of the fey living in Hawthorn's Glade ten years after the doors of Faerie closed, leaving them stuck in Aramán. She spent some time in one of the streams of the forest to warn fey like her of how to find their way to a safe haven.

entities.name: Bruel Sunderchin
entities.description:
Bruel Sunderchin was a Dwarven male entrepreneur and founder of the Brawlers' League.

As an entrepreneur, he was described as a "rough-and-tumble"; indeed, as he was one of multiple strong, charismatic "ruffians" who took advantage of the dire social status of the Kingdom of Drassig to gain social power for themselves.

Bruel Sunderchin was a dwarven male from Kraghammer who was born in the era of the Kingdom of Drassig, during which many of the social elite in Emon would use their wealth to pay the lower class to fight to the death for their amusement. Sunderchin was one of many "ruffians" who used this to his advantage by reaching out to his network of criminals and becoming the ringleader of an annual gladiator tournament that catered to the wealthy elite of Exandria known as the Brawlers' League.

Sunderchin has at least one descendant, Oben Sunderchin, who was alive during the time of the Chroma Crisis.
entities.short_description: Bruel Sunderchin was a Dwarven male entrepreneur and founder of the Brawlers' League.

entities.name: Bryce Feelid
entities.description:
Watchmaster Bryce Feelid is a genderfluid half-elf guard. They served as a watchmaster for the Crownsguard in Alfield. As an NPC, they are played by Matthew Mercer.

They have elven features, shoulder-length blond hair, were adorned in somewhat ornate armor with a helmet when the party first encountered them, and wielded a morning star in battle.

When the Mighty Nein arrived in Alfield, Bryce was in their fourth year as Watchmaster of Alfield. Bryce had at one point spent three years in the West Outersteads of Zadash, and it was from there that they had joined the crownsguard and been sent to Bladegarden for training.

While exchanging volleys with the gnolls during the attack on Alfield, Watchmaster Bryce sustained injuries to their midsection and thigh area. Hunkered down behind a wall with four crownsguard, they received medical attention, cursing in pain through gritted teeth as bandages were applied to their wounds.
entities.short_description: Watchmaster Bryce Feelid is a genderfluid half-elf guard. They served as a watchmaster for the Crownsguard in Alfield. As an NPC, they are played by Matthew Mercer.
