entities.name: Buhfal II
entities.description:
Ogre Lord Buhfal II is an ogre and acting leader and protector of Urzin while the town's Champion, Sunbreaker Olomon is away.

In 795 PD Buhfal's father and leader of Urzin, Ogre Lord Buhfal I, was killed by Sunbreaker Olomon after the Kryn warrior issued a challenge for leadership of the mobile city. Ever since, Buhfal II proudly takes the role of Urzin's leader and protector when Olomon is away.

In 835 PD during the War of Ash and Light, Bol'bara, a goblin warlock, elder seer, and trusted councilor to Buhfal, disappeared after a routine trip into Brokenveil Marsh. Buhfal and his advisores suspected that the nearby Imperial outpost was responsible for her kidnapping. However, he knew that sending the goblinkin that lived in Urzin to advance on the fort would result in reprisal, so he sought outside help.

Three days after Bol'bara's disappearace, Buhfal hired an adventuring party that had come into town, offering them a reward of 200 gold pieces for Bol'bara's return, as well as promised to provide "premium weapons", which were actually of rather shoddy quality. After being outfitted with necessary provisions, he sent the party on their way into the marsh, guided by the hobgoblin scout Morgid.
entities.short_description: Ogre Lord Buhfal II is an ogre and acting leader and protector of Urzin while the town's Champion, Sunbreaker Olomon is away.

entities.name: Bulray
entities.description:
was a bugbear elder and leader of a group of goblin, hobgoblin, and bugbear peasant refugees in Torm's Hill at the beginning of the Divergence. As an NPC, Bulray was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Bulray was older and his body bore traces of what appeared to have been public discipline sustained under the rule of the Strife Emperor. He had unusually long arms that extended past his knees.

A long time ago when Bulray was young, he believed in the Strife Emperor "because it's what we were allowed to believe in". Then a beautiful young female bugbear came to the village and taught him the difference between a ruler and a leader: the former goes on top, while a leader goes underneath and holds the weight others cannot, by being sturdy and strong. Bulray was later taken from his family and sent to work in the ash fields by soldiers of the Strife Emperor.

Bulray was seen speaking with Klasara Bandy and Nez Pilch, the leaders of Torm's Hill, about what was to be done when the refugees from Rybad-Kol arrived there. Later, he had his men learn from Garen how to build a wall to protect the village from floodwaters, and was placed in charge of the distribution of tools and supplies. He survived the attack on the village and had his troops check to ensure the slain soldiers had been acting alone.
entities.short_description: was a bugbear elder and leader of a group of goblin, hobgoblin, and bugbear peasant refugees in Torm's Hill at the beginning of the Divergence. As an NPC, Bulray was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Burning Oak
entities.description:
Burning Oak is a male lizardfolk druid and, as of 812 and 836 PD, was the 500-year-old leader of the Scions of Flame, a tribe of black-scaled lizardfolk ruling the Ashen Gorge. His magic is responsible for keeping the other tribes of the gorge at bay, but it is known to them that the druid's frailty makes him vulnerable to attack.

So far, Burning Oak has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.
entities.short_description: Burning Oak is a male lizardfolk druid and, as of 812 and 836 PD, was the 500-year-old leader of the Scions of Flame, a tribe of black-scaled lizardfolk ruling the Ashen Gorge. His magic is responsible for keeping the…

entities.name: Byron
entities.description:
Byron is a thin gnome, with tousled, greasy black hair that hangs past his shoulders, covering his bedraggled and bearded face. He wears hides, roughly crafted leathers, and furs.

Byron came upon a young roc in the Cliffkeep Mountains, the last surviving member of its clutch, its mother having been killed by giants. He decided to care for the creature, relocating it and helping it find food.

Vox Machina encountered Byron when they were chasing after the roc that had been stealing cattle from the farms north of Emon. The druid was immediately wary and distrustful, believing that they had come to slay his roc. Over the course of a very tense conversation, Vox Machina—mostly thanks to Keyleth and Scanlan—managed to convince Byron to take the roc to Vasselheim, where it could hunt freely in the Vesper Timberland and possibly live under the protection of the Slayer's Take.

When the morning came, Vox Machina left two cows on the outskirts of the farms as provisions for the roc. They saw the giant bird swoop down, pick them up, and fly off over the Ozmit Sea towards Othanzia.
entities.short_description: Byron is a thin gnome, with tousled, greasy black hair that hangs past his shoulders, covering his bedraggled and bearded face. He wears hides, roughly crafted leathers, and furs.

entities.name: Byron Anders
entities.description:
Professor Byron Anders was Percy's former tutor. He assisted the Briarwoods in the seizure of Whitestone and became one of Percy's targets for revenge, appearing on The List.

As an NPC in Critical Role, Anders was played by Matthew Mercer. In The Legend of Vox Machina, he is voiced by Stephen Root.

Anders is an older gentleman with short grey hair and a little bit of facial hair. During the battle with Vox Machina in the Critical Role stream, he wore a breastplate.

In the streamed campaign, Byron Anders was a devoted cultist of Vecna and acted as an inside man for the Briarwoods to take Whitestone castle. In the animated series, Byron Anders's betrayal was motivated by his frustration over the ambitions that he believed had been shattered by the de Rolo family, and working under their wing as teacher to the de Rolo children.
entities.short_description: Professor Byron Anders was Percy's former tutor. He assisted the Briarwoods in the seizure of Whitestone and became one of Percy's targets for revenge, appearing on The List.

entities.name: Cadigan
entities.description:
is a man who had previously captured Twiggy and the prior owner of the Happy Fun Ball or Heirloom Sphere. He never appeared in campaign.

Sir Cadigan was described by Twiggy as twice her size, which would put him at medium humanoid height, and very skinny. He wore a big ring with a green gem.

Twiggy referred to Sir Cadigan as a "mean man" and a "rascally man". He seemed to be connected in some way to the Exalted Collection Auction House in Port Damali. At the time of the Mighty Neins run in with Twiggy, Sir Cadigan was searching for the Heirloom Sphere.

He would stick his fingers through the bars of the cage Twiggy was held in to scare her.
entities.short_description: is a man who had previously captured Twiggy and the prior owner of the Happy Fun Ball or Heirloom Sphere. He never appeared in campaign.

entities.name: Cadmus Leeland
entities.description:
is a pirate operating in the Menagerie Coast of Wildemount. The captain of the Widow's Embrace, he worked under the guise of a shipping merchant frequently moving between ports. However, those who work in the shipping lanes know him to be a thief who "skims off the top". In recent months before Cuersaar in 835 PD, his business slowed considerably and rumors held that he turned to outright piracy.

He was mentioned by Adella to Fjord, who was familiar with the rumors about Cadmus, as someone that Sabian worked with a few months prior in Nicodranas. She described Cadmus as a "lowlife" and "a right fuckface", warned Fjord away from him, and cautioned that Sabian's association with Cadmus suggested that Sabian was up to no good himself.

entities.name: Calastro and Rulius Mercanaud
entities.description:
were twin demonic warlocks and the owners of the Mercanaud Coturier in the city of Dol-Makjar.

Calastro and Rulius look like well-dressed older men wearing long, curly wigs (the former's is gold, while the latter's is platinum), which hide crystalline heads inside of which fire seems to be constantly burning. Their eyes don't reflect external light, and they use illusory magic to add that effect in order to look more normal.

The twins seem cordial and polite but are quite merciless in their job, displaying a savage and professional attitude for it. The only true compassion they had was for each other.

The Mercanaud twins started a business in Dol-Makjar at some point after the Shapers' War. Their couturier, however, hid more sinister activities: due to their connection to Ksha'aravi they had deals with House Halovar, eliminating people for them and providing souls (which they took after cutting away their shadows to turn them into fabric) for the office of Lady Zebani; moreover, they also gave the resulting corpses to House Tachonis.
entities.short_description: were twin demonic warlocks and the owners of the Mercanaud Coturier in the city of Dol-Makjar.

entities.name: Calhoun
entities.description:
Calhoun is an elven member of the Fire Ashari. He protected the village of Pyrah from trespassers. As an NPC, Calhoun is played by Matthew Mercer.

When Vox Machina met him, Calhoun was a bald elven man with dark tattoos around his eyes. His entire left arm was covered in a long-healed but horrible burn scar. He was dressed in the dark brown and black hides and leathers typical of the Fire Ashari.

He seemed to be the leader of the lookout group of about ten individuals, who guarded Pyrah from unwelcome beings.

Vox Machina was traveling towards the Fire Ashari village when suddenly, large walls of stone surrounded them. Calhoun spoke with the group to determine their intention. Persuaded by Keyleth, the Fire Ashari released Vox Machina and showed them the path to the Flamespeaker.
entities.short_description: Calhoun is an elven member of the Fire Ashari. He protected the village of Pyrah from trespassers. As an NPC, Calhoun is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Calis Krishtan
entities.description:
Calis Krishtan was an entrepreneur from Ank'Harel who founded The Maiden's Wish casino in Kymal.

Around 766 PD, Calis moved to Kymal and opened a small casino called The Maiden's Wish, giving the rural city's stagnant economy a needed boost. As of 812 PD, Krishtan operated the casino and had a son, Jaktur Krishtan, margrave of Kymal and heir to The Maiden's Wish. By 836 PD, Jaktur had inherited the ownership of the casinos previously managed by his father.

Category:Entrepreneurs Category:Unspecified Humanoids Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: Calis Krishtan was an entrepreneur from Ank'Harel who founded The Maiden's Wish casino in Kymal.

entities.name: Callowyn Royce
entities.description:
was the younger brother of Lady Aranessa Royce.

Callowyn was described as a jovial, happy, and wonderful man with broad forearms.

Callowyn was born as the grandson of Lord Royce around three decades after the end of the Shapers' War. He had an older sister, Aranessa, who eventually became the head of their family, having connections with the heir of House Davinos, Julien, and marrying a war hero that ended up becoming a rebel, Thjazi Fang.

Callowyn, on the other hand, spent time in their house's estate in the Golden Orchard, and eventually became the owner of a family heirloom: a pair of bracers the fair folk of Hallow had given them long ago, which gave whoever used them the strength and might of oak and birch.
entities.short_description: was the younger brother of Lady Aranessa Royce.

entities.name: Camellia Springshower
entities.description:
Camellia Springshower is a druid nomad who wandered the Dividing Plains as of 836 PD.

Camellia is a firbolg with curly red hair. Her traumatic experience altered her appearance, turning the mottled dun fur of her skin to a pale gray, with her hands darkening. Her once-brown eyes are now milky white, and although her hair retains its color, it is now unkempt, with the withered remains of flowers and branches entangling it. She wears a tattered, dirty green dress, with an apron and shawl that were once white, but now appear yellowish. She carries with her a wooden staff with withered flowers.

Camellia was once a cheerful and happy young woman who enjoyed the beauty of the world and loved to explore. After her traumatic incident, she became more sad and melancholic, although she still tries to be kind, even in her sinister state.

Camellia was part of a family that traveled across Tal'Dorei. When they were in the Dividing Plains, she left the group to explore, and entered the bleak depths of Shadebarrow, where she found the monolithic henges used once by the sun-worshipping druids of the Dawn Circle, who aided Zan Tal'Dorei during the Scattered War and were slaughtered by Trist Drassig because of it. One of the specters that dwelled in that area found Camellia as she was trying to escape and touched her chest, cursing her and marking her magic as it connected her to that unhallowed territory. The effect was immediate, and the flowers that Camellia carried in her basket withered away as she ran.
entities.short_description: Camellia Springshower is a druid nomad who wandered the Dividing Plains as of 836 PD.

entities.name: Camilla
entities.description:
was a musician playing in the Grumpy Lily. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Camilla was a female goliath with a well kept hair and no tattoos.

Category:Performers Category:Articles needing appearance verification
entities.short_description: was a musician playing in the Grumpy Lily. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Canaith
entities.description:
is a performer and the former owner of at least one magical instrument.

According to Dariax Zaveon, Canaith is a douchebag, and "kind of a total dick" who pretended to be a professional musician.

In 843 PD, Canaith was traveling and performing in different places, and in Byroden he met Opal and Dariax, who, since they didn't like him, decided to steal his mandolin, thinking it would be a good present for their friend, Dorian Storm. However, they didn't kill Canaith, who was still alive last time they checked.

Eventually, when the three friends reunited with their group in Kymal that same year, Dariax surprised Dorian with the new instrument, explaining he thought it would be better in the genasi's hands; however, when Dorian tried to attune to it, he discovered not only that his new instrument was magical, but that it would magically damage him if he did not attune to it properly, which he eventually managed to do.
entities.short_description: is a performer and the former owner of at least one magical instrument.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Captain von Eitel
entities.description:
Captain von Eitel was a pirate active during the 9th century PD.

He abandoned his family to become a pirate, and boasted about it often. Farah Vallari met him, and years later, around 839 PD, she met an adventurer, Gavain von Eitel, who had both the looks and the surname of the captain, correctly guessing Gavain was his son.

Category:Unspecified Humanoids Category:Pirates Category:Menagerie Coast
entities.short_description: Captain von Eitel was a pirate active during the 9th century PD.

entities.name: Carlos Remedi
entities.description:
is a bartender at the Lavish Chateau in Nicodranas. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

He has a thick mustache and combed-over hair.

Carlos quickly covered for Beau when she brought a cart full of fireworks to the Lavish Chateau, followed by suspicious Zhelezo. While he seemed a little perturbed he was now a conspirator in this, he let her bring them in with no hesitation, just asking she not stash them near the lantern oil, and helped her hide them.

entities.name: Carolle
entities.description:
is a human receptionist in the Aydinlan Seminary of Yios. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

When Bells Hells encountered her, Carolle was a pale human woman in her 40s with a short, blonde bob cut. She wore a pin with the green-blue leaf symbol of the Seminary.

Carolle had been working at the Seminary for about about five or six years in 843 PD. She found the work not terribly challenging, but with nice benefits. She enjoyed meeting interesting people and "seeing the new students come every year and watching them progress and get involved in their own particular dramas and the whispers that come through. She admitted, however, that the students didn't love her.

She also admitted to a side business buying and selling knick-knacks. At least once, she stole a small statue from a professor's office, and when it wasn't missed, sold it as well.
entities.short_description: is a human receptionist in the Aydinlan Seminary of Yios. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Carthol
entities.description:
was an employ of the Meatman and a forger. He was mentioned in but has not appeared onstream.

entities.name: Cary
entities.description:
is a human barkeep in Kamordah. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cary is a rather rotund heavy-set figure of a gruff man with strong stubble across his heavy squared jaw. His hair is receding in the back, like a Friar Tuck bald spot where he has a bit of a bowl cut around the sides. He has a series of minor scars and one discolored eye on the right side of his face.

Cary grew up in Kamordah and is the owner of the Gemmed Hearth Inn, a seedy inn with three rudimentary sleeping rooms upstairs. It looks like a mud-spattered warehouse built of simple, bland woods. It has five tables and a beautiful, well-polished curved bar.

The Mighty Nein rented rooms at the Gemmed Heart for the night following Beau's confrontation with her family in .

entities.name: Cashadoor
entities.description:
Cashadoor was a fey elven man who acted as an emissary of the Unseelie Court. As an NPC, Cashadoor is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cashadoor was a gray-skinned fey elf with shallow cheeks, sky blue-to-white eyes, somewhat sharpened teeth, and gray with silver hair with black streaks on the sides and a pointed goatee curved at the end. He wore ornamental but effective armor, and had two expensive rings with jewels.

At some point in the past Cashadoor became an emissary of the Unseelie Court, having undergone special training to resist mental manipulations.

After the apogee solstice of 843 PD he and some guards were sent to the ruins of Pravenier to meet with Sorrowlord Athion Zathuda and Ludinus Da'leth, since the latter felt like the Unseelie Court hadn't been respecting his alliance with the Ruby Vanguard. They met in the Shrine of Gilded Gifts, an old temple of the Arch Heart, where Cashadoor assured the archmage that his people still believed in his cause, but their specialty was to wait and strike their enemies in the right moment, instead of lending constant support; although displeased by this, Ludinus was satisfied, and told the emissary to tell his superiors to prepare an attack against the forces the Exandrian Accord would send to the Tishtan excavation site. Shortly after, however, a battle started when Bells Hells attacked the temple, and after Da'leth's Simulacrum form was destroyed, the Unseelie agreed to speak to the adventurers. One of them, Fearne Calloway (who was Zathuda's Ruidusborn daughter), addressed Cashadoor telling him about Ludinus and his past crimes against the fey. Athion, however, dismissed this and focused instead on the possibility of the Unseelie Court betraying the Vanguard so that Fearne could take control of Predathos; when she showed hesitance Cashadoor expressed disappointed, since their court had put their hopes in her, although the Sorrowlord assured him that she would learn. When the Unseelie were preparing to leave Bells Hells attacked them again, managing to knock the Unseelie fey unconscious.
entities.short_description: Cashadoor was a fey elven man who acted as an emissary of the Unseelie Court. As an NPC, Cashadoor is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Casimir and Marsa
entities.description:
were followers of the Moonweaver living during the last days of the Calamity, and the parents of Rei'nia Saph.

Casimir and Marsa were devout people who cared about both of their daughters, and were thankful to those who helped return their daughter Rei'nia to them. Casimir was a human man who was starting to get salt-and-pepper hair during the Divergence, and Marsa was an elven woman with long white locks.

Casimir and Marsa lived during the Calamity as followers of the Moonweaver, with Marsa being a priest of the goddess. They had two daughters together, Rei'nia and Liana (who, unbeknownst to them, was the mortal incarnation of the Moonweaver). They raised their children in an environment in which they could be open about their religion, but at some point towards the end of the Calamity they were separated from Nia and Liana. The half-elven sisters ended up traveling across Gwessar with other companions in order to find them, and eventually Liana decided to go out and search by herself, agreeing with Nia to meet up at Torm's Hill. Casimir and Marsa had been in that town for a time, meeting Luz, a family friend, there, but they left before Liana arrived, and moved to Vasselheim.

Months later, Rei'nia and her friends, after receiving a divine mission from the Moonweaver, arrived in the Dawn City themselves. When Casimir and Marsa saw Nia they were thrilled. When they asked about Liana, Nia explained she had actually been a goddess, but her parents seemed so confused that one of her friends, Crokas, showed them a magic orb with recorded memories of Liana, to explain things faster. Casimir asked if this meant that he, Casimir, was a god himself, and when Crokas denied this, Casimir thanked him. Marsa, on the other hand, was happy that one of her daughters was safe and immortal, but that made her worry even more about Nia's mortality. They thanked Erro Mordaurum for helping their child when he was introduced.
entities.short_description: were followers of the Moonweaver living during the last days of the Calamity, and the parents of Rei'nia Saph.

entities.name: Casimir Gavendale
entities.description:
is a former member of the Torn Banner, a smuggler, a member of the Crow Keepers thieves' guild in Dol-Makjar, and an indirect participant in the plot to save the life of Thjazi Fang. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Loza Blade described Casimir as the quiet type. Years later, however, he had become more blunt and impatient.

Casimir was a young mercenary in the Torn Banner, working in the mess hall. There, he became friends with Thjazi Fang, who convinced him to join the rebellion, in which he saved the orc's life at one point during a battle. Later, he became a smuggler and member of the Crow Keepers thieves' guild. After some time he started resenting his participation in the Falconer's Rebellion, since his life hadn't become much better despite the promises of the rebels.

By the year 63 he was still in touch with Thjazi and told him about rumors he heard regarding other falconers.

entities.name: Cassandra de Rolo
entities.description:
Lady Cassandra Johanna von Musel Klossowski de Rolo is the head of the Chamber of Whitestone, the youngest sister of Percival de Rolo's six siblings, and only other surviving member of the de Rolo family. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

"One day, a mysterious couple, named Lord and Lady Briarwood, came to the court. During a feast held in their honor, the Briarwoods violently took control of the castle, killing or imprisoning everyone who would stand in their way. Percy awoke chained in the dungeon, only to be freed by his younger sister. Together they fled, chased by the Briarwoods' men. As they ran, Percy's sister took several arrows to the back and fell."

Cassandra is a young human woman in her late teens/early twenties. She has dark brown hair with a few streaks of white at her temples, most likely due to her mental and psychological hardship.

By 843 PD, Cassandra was in her late forties to early fifties. Her hair was still dark brown although more than half was grey, and she still bore a resemblance to her brother Percy.

entities.name: Cassida Previn
entities.description:
Archmage Cassida Previn was one of the wizards of the city of Aeor, and a member of the Society of Primes. As an NPC, Cassida is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

When first seen in Trist's vision of the person who had recently prayed to The Everlight in the abandoned temple within Aeor, Cassida was wearing the high-collared dark cloak of an archmage of the city.

Cassida grew up in the Opus Ward, a working class neighborhood where she witnessed a lot of deaths due to unsafe working conditions, and worked her way into becoming one of the elite wizards of the city. Her upbringing gave her a firm belief in the gods, and she also believed she could help to end the Calamity by saving the Prime Deities. She devoted her life to this project, becoming a wizard of intense focus and dedication.

She was one of three archmages who held enough knowledge of the Factorum Malleus project to be able to recreate it.

entities.name: Catlyn Delafin
entities.description:
is the half-elven owner of Catlyn's Clothier, a high-end clothing shop on the Volition Disc of Uthodurn. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Catlyn was a half-elf woman in her forties, with her blonde hair worn with a large curled wave to one side, and square glasses. She wore a sharp business blazer and "immaculate" make-up.

Catlyn was initially very suspicious of the party but when shown the warrant from the King and Queen covering the costs of the clothing they ordered, she became warm and welcoming. Everyone got a new custom outfit, signed unobtrusively with Catlyn's name.

entities.name: Cedargaunt
entities.description:
Cedargaunt was an ancient treant. In the adventure hook Seed of Life in the Critical Role: Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting, set in 812 PD, he was deceased; his last bloom, the Seed of Life, was being used as decoration around the neck of a pet remorhaz of an unidentified frost giant jarl.

So far, Cedargaunt has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Celdria
entities.description:
was a blue female dragonborn child held (with her mother Celeste and brother Celwyn) in Rybad-Kol prison as of the final battle of the Calamity. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Celdria was wide-eyed and expectant while in the caravan of dragonborn being sent to The Scaled Tyrant, in contrast to her brother who was withdrawn and vacant.

Celdria, her mother, and her brother were part of a caravan of dragonborn being assembled at the prison to be sent to The Scaled Tyrant, either to fight on the front lines or to be eaten by her. They happened to be seated next to Crokas and Erro Mordaurum, and when Rei'nia Saph arrived with a convincing story that Crokas was contagious, they were part of the group taken to the prison's oubliette in order to minimize the risk of illness being spread. Thus, they survived the battle between the Strife Emperor and the Prime Deities that took place above them, and termed the damage it caused, "Nuts!" They were part of the group of twelve that began the trek northward in its aftermath. The two children in the party suffered from exhaustion and dehydration along with the others, and after several days, Crokas took them on his back and began walking on all fours, like a monitor lizard, carrying them. When The Stormlord's rain began falling, the children opened their mouths to suck in the life-restoring water, and they were part of the group that witnessed the Stormlord's farewell and gift of Stormgirdle to Crokas.

Celdria reached Torm's Hill with the rest of the party, and was present when soldiers of the Strife Emperor arrived and were bloodily defeated. Seeing Crokas still lost in battle frenzy afterwards, Celdria and her brother approached and embraced him, telling him, "You don't have to be scared."
entities.short_description: was a blue female dragonborn child held (with her mother Celeste and brother Celwyn) in Rybad-Kol prison as of the final battle of the Calamity. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Celeste
entities.description:
is a blue dragonborn mother of two, held in Rybad-Kol prison until the Strife Emperor's defeat near the end of the Calamity. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Celeste spent most of her time concerned about her children and in keeping them calm under extremely frightening conditions, although she herself was also terrified. She wore a peasant's gown with a shawl over her shoulders.

Celeste and her children were part of a caravan of dragonborn being assembled at the prison to be sent to the Scaled Tyrant, either to fight on the front lines or to be eaten by her. They happened to be seated next to Crokas and Erro Mordaurum, and when Rei'nia Saph arrived with a convincing story that Crokas was contagious, they were part of the group taken to the prison's oubliette in order to minimize the risk of illness being spread. Thus, they survived the battle between the Strife Emperor and the Prime Deities that took place above them, and were part of the group of twelve that began the trek northward in its aftermath.

During the journey Crokas continued carrying Celeste's children so that they wouldn't get tired, but the mother carried one of them on the last leg of the journey so that Crokas could carry Fiedra. When they reached the refugee center of Torm's Hill, Celeste was in terrible shape from the journey but told Crokas he was now family to them because of his aid carrying the children on the way. She then left to find some food, leaving Celwyn and Celdria with Coswald.

entities.name: Celia Ovesso
entities.description:
is a human woman and a follower of the Traveler. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Celia is well-dressed, with shoulder-length blonde hair.

Celia was impatient when she arrived at Rumblecusp for Traveler Con, accompanied by her goliath bodyguard Trudo. She corrected Kellbast rather snootily when he referred to Trudo as her buddy. She projected a general air of believing herself to be too good for the accommodations and the other followers of the Traveler. She reacted in shocked horror when told to bathe in the ocean, saying she'd find "the proper water." Jester immediately took a dislike to her, which Kellbast hinted he shared.

When talking to the Traveler, Jester expressed her opinion about Celia, and the Traveler agreed she was "a bit of a bitch, but that cruelty makes for some fun pranks on occasion." He said they weren't always directed at the right targets, but she was learning.

entities.name: Celindar
entities.description:
Celindar is an Elven warrior, Verdant Lord and head of the Verdant Guard of Syngorn.

As of 812 PD and 836 PD, Celindar was Verdant Lord of Syngorn, one of the titles of the Wardens of Syngorn. As Verdant Lord, he commands the armies of Syngorn and Beryl Keep, the fortress-district that houses the Verdant Guard.

If Celindar was Verdant Lord around 800 PD, he had a daughter, who was pickpocketed by Vax'ildan in the Tarn Thoroughfare. The Verdant Lord also later sent a letter to Syldor Vessar informing him of his son's illegal activities.

If Celindar was head of the Verdant Guard in early 811 PD, that was during the time of the Siege of Emon, in which Syngornian forces fought alongside the Tal'Dorei military to take back Emon from Thordak the Cinder King and his lizardfolk army. While their equivalent in the Tal'Dorei military, Warmaster Mikael Daxio, was present, Vox Machina did not meet Celindar.

entities.name: Celwyn
entities.description:
was a blue male dragonborn child held (with his mother Celeste and sister Celdria) in Rybad-Kol prison as of the final battle of the Calamity. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Celwyn was vacant and crying to himself while in the caravan of dragonborn being sent to The Scaled Tyrant, in contrast to his sister who was wide-eyed and expectant.

Celwyn, his mother Celeste, and his sister Celdria were part of a caravan of dragonborn being assembled at the prison to be sent to The Scaled Tyrant, either to fight on the front lines or to be eaten by her. They happened to be seated next to Crokas and Erro Mordaurum, and when Rei'nia Saph arrived with a convincing story that Crokas was contagious, they were part of the group taken to the prison's oubliette in order to minimize the risk of illness being spread. Celwyn was very impressed that a lie had worked to give them a chance at freedom. Thus, they survived the battle between the Strife Emperor and the Prime Deities that took place above them, and termed the damage it caused, "Nuts!" They were part of the group of twelve that began the trek northward in its aftermath. The two children in the party suffered from exhaustion and dehydration along with the others, and after several days, Crokas took them on his back and began walking on all fours, like a monitor lizard, carrying them. When The Stormlord's rain began falling, the children opened their mouths to suck in the life-restoring water, and they were part of the group that witnessed the Stormlord's farewell and gift of Stormgirdle to Crokas.

Celwyn reached Torm's Hill with the rest of the party, and was present when soldiers of the Strife Emperor arrived and were bloodily defeated. Seeing Crokas still lost in battle frenzy afterwards, Celwyn and his sister approached and embraced him, helping him to calm down. When Celeste approached and started whispering in Draconic, Celwyn realized that Crokas couldn't understand the language, so he translated for him, telling him that he had saved them.
entities.short_description: was a blue male dragonborn child held (with his mother Celeste and sister Celdria) in Rybad-Kol prison as of the final battle of the Calamity. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Champ
entities.description:
is a human man who works at The Landlocked Lady, a brothel owned by the Mardoon Family. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Champ is a human man in his late 30s with a very short hair starting to show signs of male pattern baldness and a well kept handlebar mustache that curves out very wide over a van dyke beard. When he met Mighty Nein he was wearing a vest and a light green, billowing shirt with a white collar

Champ was manning the front desk at the Landlocked Lady when the party arrived. He offered them rooms and "companionship". Beau rented a room for the night and a companion for an hour, and the rest of the party (Caleb, Nott, Nila, and Keg) spent the night in two separate rooms. Champ also told them that the Mardoon family was currently at their estate.

entities.name: Charlie
entities.description:
Charlie is a bear and child of Vex'ahlia's animal companion Trinket.

Charlie is a brown bear. In 832 PD he was a cub, smaller than a half-elven child, but by 843 PD he already looks like an adult bear.

Charlie was born in or before 832 PD as the child of Trinket.

Charlie is a playmate to Vex'ahlia and Percival's children.

entities.name: Chessia Wakiam
entities.description:
is a famous elf entertainer in Port Damali who is involved with the Myriad. She has not appeared on-stream.

Chessia is an alluring woman known across the Menagerie Coast as a talented dancer and singer with a sweet voice.

As of 835 PD, Chessia uses her charm to allay suspicions as she insinuates herself into the lives of guild masters and politicians of Port Damali and maneuvers them to the Myriad's benefit.

entities.name: Chloroxodon
entities.description:
Chloroxodon is a young green dragon from the Ashen Gorge, in Tal'Dorei.

Less than a century ago, Chloroxodon hatched from one of Tatterwing's eggs. At some point between 812 PD and 836 PD the young dragon, along with two of their siblings, Toxoshuul and Snagglefang, moved to the Ashen Gorge, where several factions fight over the territory and treasure that once belonged to Thordak, a powerful red dragon who dubbed himself "the Cinder King". Chloroxodon longs to plunder Thordak's lost vaults for their own hoard, and so do their siblings, but in the meantime the three of them act as mercenaries for other factions in the Ashen Gorge (but only in exchange of some sort of tribute).

If by any chance Chloroxodon or any of their siblings are on opposite sides of a skirmish, they honor the blood they share and never fight each other, choosing to annihilate the humanoids beneath them instead.

Assuming Chloroxodon is typical of green dragons, they are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition, and they can breathe air and water. They have a breath weapon that cause poison damage in a conic area.
entities.short_description: Chloroxodon is a young green dragon from the Ashen Gorge, in Tal'Dorei.

entities.name: Chu
entities.description:
is a cytaa symbiotically linked to Elder Barthie of Razora. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Chu has an iguana-like body, but her tail is long and curves up from her back into a tight spiral.

Barthie described her personality as "uppity" and "a firecracker".. }} Chu appeared to be more suspicious and skeptical than her symbiote, telling Bells Hells that despite Barthie's trust and sharing of information, she thought they might be a danger to all of them.

Chu bonded with Barthie at some point when she was young, becoming his constant companion.
entities.short_description: is a cytaa symbiotically linked to Elder Barthie of Razora. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Cidrick Gillsman
entities.description:
When Grog first met Cidrick, he was dressed in a fine velvet maroon tunic and carrying a small satchel by his side.

In 843 PD, Cidrick's hair was grey but he still wore a curved moustache and a Van Dyke goatee. He also had several fine rings adorning his fingers.

Grog first met Cidrick in Vasselheim where he was selling potions from a tent along the road. The two of them bartered, with Cidrick offering a Potion of Stone Giant Strength in return for all fourteen of Grog's dragon teeth and two vials of dragon blood. The goliath then haggled the price up to all of the teeth and three blood vials, which the merchant gladly accepted.

Grog later told Vex'ahlia what he had done, and the furious ranger cast Hunter's Mark on the merchant so that she could find him again later.

entities.name: Cinna Brightbow
entities.description:
is a dwarven jeweler from Byroden. She is narratively treated as an NPC, but she was played by Liam O'Brien, a non-DM player.

Cinna is a dwarven woman; during the Gem of Byroden pageant, she wore her blonde hair "with a bit of a little bump in the front and all tied back perfectly", and had "the barest bit of sheen of sideburn" down to her jaw. She usually wears "a lot of rhinestones and glass jewelry" as well as one genuinely pricy piece.

Cinna is very confident and self-assured.

Cinna runs a jewelry shop in Byroden. Her family has lived in Byroden for about a hundred years. She won the Byroden Forever pageant about fifteen years prior to the 22nd Annual, which took place in 842 PD; for the talent portion she sculpted an ice statue of Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia. She is a very accomplished axe thrower. According to her, she cannot dance or sing well.
entities.short_description: is a dwarven jeweler from Byroden. She is narratively treated as an NPC, but she was played by Liam O'Brien, a non-DM player.

entities.name: Clara Lionett
entities.description:
is the mother of Beauregard Lionett. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Clara is a human woman with darker olive skin and blue eyes like her daughter Beauregard. Her hair is put up into a very tight bun with a bit of pony tail that dangles behind. When Beau visited her, she wore a deep green dress that was very nice for being casually at home, but appeared comfortable.

Beau believes that her mother is passive and will not stand up to her father, Clara's husband Thoreau Lionett, even when he is in the wrong. In his presence, Clara takes her cues from him. But when he is not, she was stated to be a far more caring parent.

Unlike her husband Thoreau, Clara came from a wealthy family. The vineyards owned by the family in Kamordah have prospered and they are now very wealthy themselves.
entities.short_description: is the mother of Beauregard Lionett. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Clarabelle
entities.description:
is Caduceus' moorbounder. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Clarabelle was the youngest and smallest of the three moorbounders purchased by the Mighty Nein.

Clarabelle acted the most like a kitten, such as when Caduceus tried to get it to sit and it instead gave him a big lick up the side of his face.

Clarabelle was raised by Zorth, a goblin who trained moorbounders for a living in Asarius, the City of Beasts, in Xhorhas. She was bonded to and trained by Caduceus.

entities.name: Clarabelle Clay
entities.description:
is a firbolg living at the Blooming Grove and the sister of Caduceus Clay. Like most others in the Clay family, she left her home to find a way to protect it from the advancing corruption of the surrounding Savalirwood. She traveled alongside her brother Colton, and the pair were petrified at the Whitedawn Lagoon, where they remained until restored in 836 PD by Caduceus. She returned to the Grove with the rest of her family.

As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

In 836 PD, she was in her mid-teens, bright-eyed with long stringy hair past her shoulders stained in a variety of different colors. She was described as the "unkempt wild kid of the family". Caduceus affectionately described her as weird.

Clarabelle lived in the Blooming Grove in the Savalirwood of the Greying Wildlands with the rest of the Clay family. She, like all in the family, is a worshiper of Melora and spends her time administering burial by interment. She left the Grove in 828 or 829 PD with her brother Colton to visit the temples at Kravaraad and the Whitedawn Lagoon in search of a way to stop the corruption of the Savalirwood from progressing into the Grove. She was petrified by a gorgon at the White Dawn Lagoon, where she remained for seven or eight years.

entities.name: Clarota
entities.description:
Clarota was an arcanist mind flayer (or alhoon). As an NPC, he was played by Matthew Mercer.

Clarota was a purplish-blue illithid, dressed in rags, with a giant scar across one of his eyes. He constantly wore his helmet to guard his mind against any outside influence.

Clarota did not view himself as being able to be friends with anyone but was willing to see himself as an ally to the party. The party frequently attempted to call him Clarence due to his odd name, but he quickly grew angry and insisted that they call him by his real name. He ultimately betrayed them after fulfilling their role in helping him reconnect with his hive, stating that it was time to feed.

Clarota seemed interested in others who could also wield magic, as shown when speaking with Tiberius .

entities.name: Claudia Sheed
entities.description:
Claudia Sheed is a drow woman and the former owner of the Leaky Tap in Zadash. In her appearances during the campaign, she used illusion magic to disguise herself as a non-drow elven woman. As an NPC, Claudia Sheed is played by Matthew Mercer.

Using illusion magic, Claudia appeared as a non-drow elven woman, who looked to be, by human standards, in her 40’s. While working she was graceful if a bit disheveled, wearing a simple apron and having her hair pulled back and tied into a small haphazard bun. When off-duty, she wore a maroon silk robe and had her hair in a high bun.

She was not judgmental when it concerned which patron or deity a person chose to follow, even if it happened to be unsanctioned by the Dwendalian Empire, going so far as allowing the Knights of Requital to hold their meetings in the cellar of The Leaky Tap.

Claudia was a refugee from conflicts of the Kryn Dynasty. The man who owned the tavern offered to take her in, but badly mistreated her. She killed him, hid his skeleton, and got forged documents from The Gentleman to take over the tavern.

entities.name: Cleff Tinkertop
entities.description:
Master Maker Cleff Tinkertop is an eccentric gnomish tinkerer in Hupperdook, responsible for constructing the Gear Warden and the Tinkertop Bolt Blaster 1000. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cleff is an eccentric inventor of things ranging from harmless trinkets to semi-sentient war golems. He is not portrayed as a "mad scientist", however; he was remorseful of the events that led his golem to killing several Crownsguard and submissive when his daughter insulted his faulty creations. When the Mighty Nein destroyed the clockwork warden, he was appreciative and generous, following through with his promise to give Nott his prototype crossbow and expressing a wish to seem them again.

Around 833 PD, Cleff was hired by the wardens of the Gearhole Prison to build a clockwork warden to watch over some of the more dangerous prisoners. Unfortunately, the automaton appeared to be faulty and started killing everything it encountered. The wardens managed to seal off the section of the prison it was in, leaving it trapped. Cleff had to pay a fine for the damages caused by his rogue automaton. Ever since the wardens have come round to Cleff's shop - Tinkertop Inventions - to constantly remind him of his failure. It has been a black spot on the Tinkertop family name, resulting in his daughter Rissa being picked on for it by other gnomes like Ashton and Fitz.

The Mighty Nein entered Tinkertop Inventions with Cleff's daughter, Rissa. He welcomed them in, pleased to see Rissa had made friends. Mollymauk expressed interest in seeing his inventions and Jester wanted to find toys for Kiri. He offered them a miniature bolt thrower, which misfired and nearly hit Beauregard's head. Instead he gave Kiri a music box with a tiny metallic bird with wings that flapped up and down. Jester bought it for three gold pieces.
entities.short_description: Master Maker Cleff Tinkertop is an eccentric gnomish tinkerer in Hupperdook, responsible for constructing the Gear Warden and the Tinkertop Bolt Blaster 1000. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Clemain Astural
entities.description:
Clemain Astural was a powerful arcanist who lived during the Age of Arcanum. According to legend, he was known as the Sight Shepherd and went mad after a pact with an otherworldly entity he called The Sightless, who fueled his power. This power allowed Clemain to devastate southeastern Tal'Dorei until he was defeated, buried in the rubble of his tower, Wrettis.

According to legend, after encountering The Sightless, Astural was driven mad and wrote pages of paranoid, half-crazed ramblings.

Clemain Astural lived during the Age of Arcanum. According to the few legends that survived history, known as the Sight Shepherd, he was a powerful arcanist who had peered into a realm beyond the Planes of Existence in search of power that would allow him to cease war around the world. He found an entity he called The Sightless, whom he made an agreement with, mistakenly believing that The Sightless would serve him. Astural's sanity subsequently crumbled, but his power, fueled by The Sightless, grew, allowing the mage to sweep devastation over southeastern Tal'Dorei.

During his reign, Astural wrote thousands of pages of parchment with writings that would later become known as the Astural Scrolls. Earlier notes ranged from alchemical formulas, spells, and star charts, but his later notes descended into paranoid ramblings. At some point, Astural made his tower, Wrettis, his base of operations, containing his secret creations.

entities.name: Colton Clay
entities.description:
is the elder brother of Caduceus. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Colton wanted to be the hero of the family. The experience of being rescued from being turned into a statue at the Menagerie by his little brother was humiliating. He felt taken down a few pegs and wore it "like a shamed dog."

In 828 or 829 PD, Colton left the Blooming Grove with his sister Clarabelle, seeking a way to stop the corruption of the Savalirwood from progressing into the Grove. He made his way to the Cinderrest Sanctum and then eventually The Menagerie where he and Clarabelle were petrified by a gorgon.

Colton's petrified form was found shielding the also petrified Clarabelle. The next day, Caduceus cast Greater Restoration on him, curing him of the petrification. He was immediately defensive of Clarabelle before he realized what was going on and relaxed. He was begrudgingly thankful to Caduceus for saving them.

entities.name: Conessa Berg
entities.description:
is an undead frost giant jarl of Eiselcross in northern Wildemount.

At some point after 300 PD Conessa became jarl, ruling over her people from an enormous and beautiful ice castle.

She was very interested in the ruins and relics from the fallen city of Aeor, so she started collecting them, and others brought similar artifacts in order to please her. Around 635 PD one of those objects was brought to the fortress, but its unstable nature caused an arcane burst, with necromantic and cold energies transforming every giant inside the castle into rime-infused zombies.

Conessa and her subjects stayed in their frozen home, that would end up being called the Fortress of the Dead Jarl because of her, but not many knew about their current undead existence. However, in or before 836 PD, something caused a breach in the ice fortress, allowing some of the giants to escape their home and start attacking people in Eiselcross.

entities.name: Constance Clay
entities.description:
is the mother of Caduceus, Clarabelle, Colton, and Calliope. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Constance is an older female firbolg with hair short on the sides almost like a soft mohawk that braids into a single long braid down the back.

In 827 PD, Constance left the Blooming Grove with Corrin, seeking a solution to the encroaching corruption. She reached the Cinderrest Sanctum on Kravaraad, then made her way to the Menagerie, where she was ultimately petrified by a gorgon.

The Mighty Nein found the petrified forms of Constance, Corrin, Cornelius and Calliope.

entities.name: Cordell
entities.description:
Cordell was one of the guards at Greyskull Keep. As an NPC, he was portrayed by Matthew Mercer.

Cordell was a half-orc. He had short, black hair, with no notable scars on his face.

Cordell was one of the guards on duty when Vox Machina returned from the Underdark. Shayne shouted for him to open the gates as they approached, and he welcomed them home.

When the members of Vox Machina woke the next morning, Shayne and Cordell were just finishing their guard shift, sharing a meal together before leaving.

Cornelius is a former bookbinder from Westruun. After Umbrasyl and the Herd of Storms attacked the city, Cornelius took up a leadership position among the refugees. As an NPC, Cornelius is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cornelius is a man in his mid-forties. He has blondish hair and a scruffy beard. His calloused hands give him the appearance of a working man. He has a bright white toothy smile.

entities.name: Cornelius Clay
entities.description:
is a firbolg living at the Blooming Grove and is the father of Caduceus Clay. Like the others in his family, he left the Grove to find a way to protect it from the advancing corruption of the surrounding Savalirwood. He traveled alongside his daughter Calliope, and the pair were petrified at the Whitedawn Lagoon, where they remained until restored in 836 PD by Caduceus. He returned to the Grove with the rest of his family.

As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cornelius is a large older firbolg, similar in appearance to his son Caduceus Clay, though a bit thicker and portlier. His hair is gray and braided on either side of his face, dangling in tufts at the bottom decorated with a bit of jewelry. He is described as "a little more cartoony variation" of Caduceus' appearance.

Cornelius is characterized as pleasant, warm, and friendly. Though he is often easily confused in conversation, he is also wise, speaking well and patiently to others on death and making arrangements for burial rites. He does not particularly pay attention to dates or the passing of time, and he is unaware of the existence of Rexxentrum.

entities.description:
is a firbolg living at the Blooming Grove. She is aunt to Caduceus Clay, sister to Constance Clay, and the eldest of the Clay family at the Grove. Like the others in her family, she left the Grove to find a way to protect it from the advancing corruption of the surrounding Savalirwood. She traveled alongside her sister Constance, and the pair were petrified at the Whitedawn Lagoon, where they remained until restored in 836 PD by Caduceus. She returned to the Grove with the rest of her family.

As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

She has fading pink hair and pink skin. She is the eldest of the Clay family living at the Blooming Grove. After she was shattered as a petrified statue and ultimately restored, she became stiff and locked into a specific posture.

Corrin lived in the Blooming Grove in the Savalirwood of the Greying Wildlands with the rest of the Clay family. She, like all in the family, is a worshiper of Melora and spends her time administering burial by interment.

entities.name: Coswald
entities.description:
was a green dragonborn prisoner in the Calamity-era prison at Rybad-Kol when it was destroyed in a battle between the gods. As an NPC, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Coswald was a brawny green dragonborn with an exceptionally long and draconic neck.

At some point in his past Coswald was caught stealing and sent as a prisoner to Rybad-Kol.

Coswald was part of a caravan of dragonborn being assembled at the prison to be sent to The Scaled Tyrant, either to fight on the front lines or to be eaten by her. He happened to be seated next to Crokas and Erro Mordaurum, as well as Celeste and her frightened children. Coswald told Marlath, another frightened dragonborn, to keep his fear to himself, and attempted to comfort the children by telling them he'd been in scarier situations before this. He agreed with Erro when he was told they might get one opportunity, and to make it count. When Rei'nia Saph arrived with a convincing story that Crokas was contagious, Coswald concocted a convincing lie that he'd lunged for the children and had spit all over them. He was part of the group taken to the prison's oubliette in order to minimize the risk of illness being spread, and was grateful to Erro for having a friend buy them some extra time to live.

entities.name: Covak
entities.description:
Covak is a very old gnoll who worships the Traveler. As an NPC, Covak is played by Matthew Mercer.

Covak is a very elderly, frail-looking gnoll whose fur has become mostly white and grey, or fallen away to reveal heavily wrinkled skin. He walks hunched-over with a cane. Covak is even missing a few teeth, and has noticeably bad breath.

Covak is an elderly gnoll resident of Asarius. He was approached by the Traveler after his partner was killed by a Gloomstalker in the south, and helped him bring back some joy into his life by deal with loneliness through pranks and irritating his neighbor. The Traveler promised gifts in the future should Covak continue to pester and bring a little chaos to Asarius. Though he doesn't visit often, Covak still thinks of the Traveler as his only friend.

After the Mighty Nein's escapades beneath the well, Beau and Jester met Covak after recognizing the Traveler symbol outside his ramshackle hut and inquiring. Covak shared his history with the Traveler and Jester did the same, although his sense of humor is somewhat more earthy than Jester's (for instance, he thought defecating in four of the public wells in the city was a funny joke). The old gnoll seemed disheartened and bitter when Jester boasted about her closer relationship with their god. Before leaving, Jester created a small figurine of the Traveler for him to pray to and Covak seemed excited about the upcoming gathering of Traveler believers. He did, however, light Jester's cloak on fire as she left.
entities.short_description: Covak is a very old gnoll who worships the Traveler. As an NPC, Covak is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Craven Edge
entities.description:
is a sentient two-handed greatsword once wielded by Sylas Briarwood and then by Grog Strongjaw before being thrown into the pocket dimension of the Dread Emperor. Imbued with dark arcane power, Craven Edge drains strength from the foes it strikes, absorbing their blood into its blade, but potentially consuming the soul of its wielder. As an NPC, Craven Edge is portrayed by Matthew Mercer in both Critical Role and The Legend of Vox Machina.

Craven Edge is a large, onyx, two-handed greatsword.

Craven Edge constantly seeks the thrill of battle and the taste of blood on its blade.

Percy gave Craven Edge to Grog, as Grog was the party member best suited to wield a greatsword. When Grog first took hold of it, the sword asked him if he was to be the wielder. Grog was surprised, and immediately asked Craven Edge if it had a female setting or if he could rename it "Bacon". Craven Edge seemed somewhat exasperated by this, but asked Grog to pledge his acceptance of the sword, which Grog did.

entities.name: Cree Deeproots
entities.description:
Cree Deeproots was a tabaxi cleric (Blood Domain) and a member of the Tombtakers. She previously worked for The Gentleman, a crime boss in Zadash. As an NPC, Cree was played by Matthew Mercer.

Cree was "a muscular panther-like female of dark brown/black fur and yellow eyes." When the Mighty Nein first met her, she was dressed in maroon and dull grey robes.

Much later during the Mighty Nein's encounter with the Tombtakers in Eiselcross, Cree wore heavy leathers and furs, and a necklace around her neck with a red circular polished orb in the center of it. On closer inspection, Beau noticed it contained a red liquid. Cree bore five eye tattoos on her body, only seen by the Nein during their final battle.

After her death at the hands of the Mighty Nein, Cree was transformed into a monstrosity of mangled flesh and bones. Her face could still be seen within the pile of flesh.

entities.name: Cressida Holt
entities.description:
Cressida Holt is a new expositor of the Cobalt Reserve in Tal'Dorei as of 836 PD.

Cressida is a tall orc with a muscular build (although she would be considered slim by orcish standard), with dark eyes, light green skin and dark brown hair shaved on the sides and pulled back in a braid held in place by a simple gold ornament. They usually wear a Cobalt Soul blue outfit trimmed in gold and a lighter blue, with a yellow fabric belt and dark boots with gold metallic; however, whenever she has to assist to a social event she wears a finer suit instead, although keeping the cobalt-blue coloration. Their weapon appears to be a stylized version of a gold metal rope dart with a white string.

Cressida is a charismatic, suave and stylish individual that combines her great social skills with a blunt, merciless coldness, which makes them the perfect agent for any type of mission.

Cressida joined the Cobalt Soul being young, and underwent demanding training, learning the ways of a monk of this order. Having recently been appointed expositor, she has been accepting infiltration and espionage missions that have taken them to different locations on the continent, such as Kymal or Westruun. On these missions, designed to find political corruption, Cressida has been seen at parties and/or gambling places of potential high-society corruption, subtly seducing and interrogating potential targets, as well as using her license to kill when necessary.
entities.short_description: Cressida Holt is a new expositor of the Cobalt Reserve in Tal'Dorei as of 836 PD.

entities.name: Cruelty
entities.description:
is a demon aspirant in the Candescent Creed, and one of the three sisters of Tyranny. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Cruelty is slightly shorter than her sister Tyranny, but stunning, with ruby red lips, small pronged silvery horns, and a whipping tail. Tyranny believed she was "very, very smart."

Tyranny met all three of her sisters at the Villa Aurora the day after Thjazi Fang's execution. Cruelty was pleased that Wicander had appeared at the funeral of someone the Sundered Houses had just executed, saying that it sent a clear message about their values. She found it amusing that Wicander truly believed and held true to the Tenets of the Whispered Light.

Cruelty was present in Riesingürtle when the Seekers arrived there. Her sister Enmity had encountered the group at a biergarten, posing as a ditzy missionary of the Candescent Creed, and learning from Thaisha Lloy her real name and that she had met both Tyranny and Wicander Halovar at the Lloy family estate. When Enmity joined her sisters at the Candescent Cathedral, she told them what she had learned from Thaisha. The sisters, who were searching for Wicander and Tyranny, suspected that Occtis Tachonis was actually Wick in disguise, and that Vaelus was Tyranny. They returned to the biergarten in search of the group, who had by that time left it.
entities.short_description: is a demon aspirant in the Candescent Creed, and one of the three sisters of Tyranny. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Crute
entities.description:
is the dwarven owner of the Feed and Mead inn located in Alfield. As an NPC he was played by Matthew Mercer.

Crute had tousled white-gray hair and a single tuft of beard that dangles down down toward the bellybutton before it hit a ring of gold.

Crute was ornery and salty-looking, and, in conversation, tended to look above or at person's shoulder due to his poor sight.

After the Mighty Nein returned to Alfield after defeating the Knolls, Bryce told them that Crute had rooms for them at the Feed & Mead Inn.

entities.name: Crysa-Thul
entities.description:
When encountered by Vox Machina, Crysa-Thul's form resembled a large, undead fetus.

In Vox Machina's first adventure, the group was hired by Fendril Vas in Stilben to investigate the seemingly dubious and dangerous new business conglomerate called "the Myriad". Vox Machina eventually entered a chamber housing a planar rift that pulled the group into a room with Crysa-Thul. Fendril was actually a worshipper of the stillborn god and had intended to feed the party to this deity like many previous mercenary groups. Vox Machina destroyed Crysa-Thul and returned to slay Fendril for his treachery.

In the comic version of the story, Crysa-Thul only made a brief appearance as the party took him down. It seems that Fendril Vas was not present in this storyline, as Vex'ahlia mentioned that they were being paid "a very small amount" by the town of Stilben to take care of it. They fought it in a forest outside of town.

entities.name: Culpasi
entities.description:
is one of the Somnovem of the mutated Cognouza Ward of the city of Aeor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Culpasi's appearance, age and race prior to the flight of Cognouza into the Astral Plane and its subsequent transformation are unknown.

When Lucien was just resurrected Culpasi appeared to him in a dream, at first as a shapeless figure made of black sand, but soon after taking a more solid male form. During their conversation four white eye-like dots appeared in his head. He wore an embroidered gray robe.

Culpasi was one of the nine leaders, the Somnovem, of the Aeorian neighborhood called Cognouza. Those leaders led the ward to escape the destruction of Aeor by the gods and transport themselves into the Astral Sea, where they encountered a "psychic storm that wracked every mind and spirit and shattered them until they became one with their own city." "Thousands of people and the Somnovem that guided them were broken, and over time slowly reformed, powerful, the instinct of their dreams driving them, in a place where they could will their dreams to be, were their will not so fragmented."
entities.short_description: is one of the Somnovem of the mutated Cognouza Ward of the city of Aeor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Curator Tasha
entities.description:
is a Curator of the Cobalt Soul in the Dwendalian Empire in The Mighty Nein (animated). She does not appear in Campaign Two: The Mighty Nein, and is played by Zehra Fazal in the animated series.

Curator Tasha is a dark-skinned humanoid with long pink hair worn in a single braid. She wears both glasses and earrings with her cobalt blue robes.

Tasha participated in the arrest of Trent Ikithon for treason, along with Vess DeRogna. She and DeRogna were both watching while Ikithon was later being tortured for information. However, when Ikithon later convinced King Bertrand Dwendal of his usefulness, Tasha was beheaded publicly while DeRogna escaped.
entities.short_description: is a Curator of the Cobalt Soul in the Dwendalian Empire in The Mighty Nein (animated). She does not appear in Campaign Two: The Mighty Nein, and is played by Zehra Fazal in the animated series.

entities.name: Curtis Uleas
entities.description:
was the Holy Curator of the temple of the Lawbearer in Vasselheim in 812 PD. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Curtis was squat, bald, and mousey-looking.

In 812 PD, Holy Curator Curtis Uleas is mentioned as the representative of the Quadroads of Erathis in a meeting to discuss how to stop Vecna's march on Vasselheim. He objected to Allura Vysoren's offer to transport a strike team to Thar Amphala.

In 843 PD, Curtis Uleas was not mentioned as the Holy Curator at the meeting of the Exandrian Accord in Vasselheim after the fall of the base of the Bloody Bridge in the Hellcatch Valley of Marquet. At that time, there was a Holy Curator named Adona., a figure steps forward identified first as "High Curator Adona" and then as "Holy Curator" and expresses very similar sentiments as the person in the previous episode.}}
entities.short_description: was the Holy Curator of the temple of the Lawbearer in Vasselheim in 812 PD. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Cymie
entities.description:
is a guard at the Vergesson Sanatorium. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cymie was wearing Vergesson guard armor.

Cymie was on guard in the basement of the northwest tower of the Vergesson Sanatorium when Team Firestorm consisting of Caleb, Jester, and Veth broke in searching for the Amulets of Proof against Detection and Location that they knew were stored there. Jester used Fast Friends on Cymie, instructing him to stay in the first room and ignore the sounds of battle that began coming from further inward, sit at the table, and start counting. When Jester moved out of the room to join her teammates in battle and cast Invoke Duplicity, it broke her concentration on Cymie's spell. Beau saw him racing away from the tower in search of help a few minutes later.

Category:Unspecified Humanoids Category:Articles needing appearance verification
entities.short_description: is a guard at the Vergesson Sanatorium. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Cyrillia
entities.description:
is the undead navigator on the Crimson Abyss, a ghost ship sailing the seas around the Shattered Teeth. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cyrillia was first seen as a female smoldering skeleton holding "some station" within the crew. She had a blue flame flickering in one eye socket, but the other was dark and vacant. She had little veins of smoldering light in between her bones. After she shared her warmth with Captain Novos, the glow of her smolder became a light grayish purple.

Cyrillia was morose and protective of her territory, although somewhat shy expressing her emotions.

While she was alive, she removed her own eye to prove that she was still good at her job, and even after dying she was good at it, being the only one able to see through the Fool's Curtain with the aid of a spyglass.
entities.short_description: is the undead navigator on the Crimson Abyss, a ghost ship sailing the seas around the Shattered Teeth. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Cyrulia
entities.description:
Lady was a follower of the Betrayer Gods just before the Divergence. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Cyrulia was a woman of pale greyish skin (almost corpse-like), clawed hands, and hundreds of very sharp and translucent fish-like teeth. She was dressed in a beautiful, shiny black gown.

She behaved politely and sinisterly at the same time.

Lady Cyrulia was a servant of the Betrayer Gods who, during the Calamity, acted as an ally and dignitary among the followers of other evil gods, even obtaining a privileged position in Rybad-Kol.
entities.short_description: Lady was a follower of the Betrayer Gods just before the Divergence. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Cyrus
entities.description:
Cyrus is one of the refugees from Westruun and the younger brother of Cornelius. As an NPC, Cyrus is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cyrus is a man in his late twenties or early thirties with shaggy brown hair and a bit of a puffy goatee.

Cyrus is described as a lazy man by his brother Cornelius.

Category:Westruun Category:Articles needing appearance verification
entities.short_description: Cyrus is one of the refugees from Westruun and the younger brother of Cornelius. As an NPC, Cyrus is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Cyrus Hume
entities.description:
was a warden of the stockade in Emon. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Cyrus Hume was a gentleman with a well-kept mustache, thick over the top lip and slicked black hair that curled up in the back in a small poof. He was wearing a breastplate and was standing with an appearance of self-importance.

Cyrus Hume was first seen speaking to Dr. Dranzel inside the stockade of Emon. Percival de Rolo and Scanlan Shorthalt, after a short negotiation with the warden and hearng of the fines caused by Kaylie, Scanlan's daughter, attempted and failed at bribing to release her. He had Scanlan arrested.

Category:Unspecified Humanoids Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: was a warden of the stockade in Emon. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Cyrus Wyvernwind
entities.description:
was Dorian Storm's brother. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer in Critical Role and by Aabria Iyengar in Exandria Unlimited.

Cyrus had blue skin, light green eyes, wavy shoulder-length black hair, and a square jaw. He wore a gold septum piercing and was burlier and taller than his younger brother. He had consistently worn a light grey cloak, a heavy hood, full-body studded leather armor, and gauntlets. He was 6 foot 3 inches tall.

Cyrus was good-natured, but somewhat naive, a man who easily got into trouble. He was also proud, and liked people guessing how important his family was.

Cyrus was born before 816 PD as the eldest son of the rulers of the Silken Squall, and was followed by a younger brother, Brontë, born in 816 PD. They frequently would get into physical fights, hitting each other until they returned to their parents bleeding and crying; that, however, didn't stop them from doing the same again, since it was one of the ways the two of them bonded.
entities.short_description: was Dorian Storm's brother. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer in Critical Role and by Aabria Iyengar in Exandria Unlimited.

entities.name: Dagen Underthorn
entities.description:
is a dwarven explorer hired to escort the party on Foren. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dagen is an extremely grizzled-looking male dwarf, his face a mess of tanned, leathery skin framed by a mane of jet-black hair that tumbles thick past his shoulders meshing with a rats' nest of a beard. Tattoos wrap his arms extending under his sleeves. He moves via an intricate chair of scuffed metal and wood with slanted wheels on its side. There are numerous tools and plates bolted onto it.

He carries a battle-axe that has a massive thick leather hilt and a dark metal blade that he named Sheila.

Oweda described him as "a beast" who had been up and down most parts of Foren, but was respected. She would want him on her side in a battle. He appears to largely be unconcerned with the politics of the Empire and Dynasty, and will gladly work for anyone who pays him money no matter what side of the conflict they are on.
entities.short_description: is a dwarven explorer hired to escort the party on Foren. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Dagon
entities.description:
Dagon is the co-owner of the Midnight Breath Tavern in Vasselheim. As an NPC, Dagon is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dagon is an older human man with a patchy red-and-brown beard. He has a few scars, but they seem to be more of a result of living in the harsh landscape of Vasselheim than from any battle.

Dagon has a brother in Muldire, more than two days' horseback ride northwest of Vasselheim.

To be pardoned by the Slayer's Take, Vox Machina had to kill an adult white dragon. They found Dagon, who told them where he had encountered such a creature.
entities.short_description: Dagon is the co-owner of the Midnight Breath Tavern in Vasselheim. As an NPC, Dagon is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Dairon
entities.description:
is an elf monk working for the Valley Archive of the Cobalt Soul, a library in Zadash. Her monk archetype is the Way of the Cobalt Soul, published in Critical Role: Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting. As an NPC, Dairon is played by Matthew Mercer. In The Mighty Nein, Dairon is voiced by Ming-Na Wen.

When Dairon first appeared, they were hooded and wearing baggy grey pants. All Beauregard Lionett could see of them was a thin, muscular figure, neither particularly masculine nor feminine, and dark skin. Dairon later lowered their hood to reveal elvish features and a bald head.

Dairon is very direct and blunt. She maintains focus despite distractions. She is committed to the Cobalt Soul and willing to die to accomplish a mission.

Dairon has shared little of her background, but mentioned that she had been hurt by people in power. She told Beau that in the past, she had been emotionally driven and vengeful, with unfounded prejudices, but that spending time within the Kryn Dynasty had made her realize how little difference there was between people trying to survive and be happy on both sides.
