entities.name: Daldred
entities.description:
Daldred was a historical figure of the Menagerie Coast.

By 831 PD, he was remembered in stories as a king, and when the evil Taeleron the Cleaver demanded the death of his wife Andica in order to spare the kingdom, the peasants believed that the vain queen would never choose them over herself, but the queen, in a noble sacrifice, took her own life; the tragedy ended with Daldred lamenting his loss.

Lucien Tavelle, who knew the story well, believed a local lord or chief named Daldred had in fact had a love who made a great sacrifice. However, their story had been altered and popularized in plays and retellings in both the Greying Wildlands and the Dwendalian Empire.

Category:Unspecified Humanoids Category:Dead Characters Category:Characters in The Nine Eyes of Lucien Category:Rulers Category:Menagerie Coast
entities.short_description: Daldred was a historical figure of the Menagerie Coast.

entities.name: Dale
entities.description:
Dale is a citizen of Emon who escaped to Whitestone and helped fight Thordak. He is good friends with Kashaw Vesh, but hadn't seen him for many years until the battle against Thordak.

Dale and Kashaw were close friends when they were younger, but hadn't seen each other in many years before Kashaw met Vox Machina. When they knew each other, Dale met Anne who Kashaw knew as well.

When the Chroma Conclave attacked Emon, Dale managed to escape, but Anne was killed by the dragons. Dale joined the Alliance of Tal'Dorei in order to avenge her loss and was placed in a war camp near Greyskull Keep.

Dale was preparing for the attack on Thordak later that day when Vox Machina, Zahra Hydris, and Kashaw walked past. Kash instantly recognised his old friend and they greeted each other warmly. Dale sarcastically said that he was preparing to die today, and his friend asked about Anne. Dale revealed Anne's death upon which Kash comforted him and the pair talked about killing the dragons. Kashaw then said goodbye, remarking how strange it was they met after this long.
entities.short_description: Dale is a citizen of Emon who escaped to Whitestone and helped fight Thordak. He is good friends with Kashaw Vesh, but hadn't seen him for many years until the battle against Thordak.

entities.name: Dame Morgaine
entities.description:
Dame Morgaine is one of the hounds of the King of Timmony. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Morgaine is a beautiful mountain herding dog similar to a collie with black, white, and brown fur in splotches, as well as an unusual shade of deep, rich blue..}}

The dame is a professional and polite individual, very formal, although with occasional moments of casualness.

The souls of the Hounds of the King were once knights of Timmony fighting for their homeland against the gods in the Shapers' War, who swore an oath to defend their king in this world and the next. After their deaths, with no afterlife to receive them, they learned from the Druids of the Stag that souls can return many times to the world. The Hounds asked to return and serve a king once more, and were reborn in their dog forms.
entities.short_description: Dame Morgaine is one of the hounds of the King of Timmony. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Damon
entities.description:
Damon served in the Crownsguard for the Dwendalian Empire, stationed in Trostenwald when he encountered the Mighty Nein, although they had not yet adopted the name. As an NPC, Damon was played by Matthew Mercer.

Damon wore slightly-tarnished, brass scale mail armor consisting of a chestplate and armplates with a maroon robe. He carried a basic longsword.

After an old man transformed into a husk zombie during the show at The Fletching and Moondrop Traveling Carnival of Curiosities in Trostenwald, the Crownsguard locked down the carnival and its crew. The next night, Damon was sitting in a chair, dozing off while guarding the site, when he noticed Jester sneaking between tents. She subdued Damon with a Charm Person spell, and he sat back down.

Shortly thereafter, as Kylre fled from the scene, Damon and a fellow guard transformed into the same type of undead monster that had ravaged the carnival the previous night. Their flesh split open and fell to the ground, their blood spilling as dust and sand rather than liquid. They began approaching the adventurers.
entities.short_description: Damon served in the Crownsguard for the Dwendalian Empire, stationed in Trostenwald when he encountered the Mighty Nein, although they had not yet adopted the name. As an NPC, Damon was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Damon
entities.description:
Captain Damon is the captain of the skyship Deera. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Captain Damon is described simply as "more adorned" than his crew, wearing a "captain's uniform."

The next time Vox Machina met Captain Damon was in Ank'Harel, when Scanlan and Grog were attempting to steal an airship. Instead, they earned themselves free passage on Captain Damon's, thanks to the badge given to them by J'mon Sa Ord. Damon seemed pleased to see them again, and agreed to help them reach the Isle of Glintshore to hunt down Anna Ripley. He revealed that since the Chroma Conclave attack, he and his men had gained significantly more autonomy and no longer had to pay taxes and fees.

After the encounter with Ripley on the island, and Percy's untimely death, Vex'ahlia notified Damon that their group was using another method to leave the island, so the skyship and its crew could head back to Ank'Harel. As the ship turned to leave, Vex stopped Captain Damon and asked if he would like to join the fight against the Chroma Conclave. After some initial hesitation, he agreed, and Vex directed him and the skyship towards Whitestone where their other allies were gathering.
entities.short_description: Captain Damon is the captain of the skyship Deera. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Danas
entities.description:
() was a female gnome who managed Prudaj Textiles in Jrusar. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Danas had a strong will and a forceful personality befitting her managerial position.

Danas was at first helpful to the party later named Bells Hells when they arrived at Prudaj Textiles, greeting them with a bright smile and offering to answer any questions while they looked around even as she kept a close eye on the workers there to make sure they weren't slacking off while she was occupied. As the encounter continued, she grew increasingly suspicious of the party's motives, and more urgent to get them out.

After the party left and evening arrived, she was the last to leave the warehouse, scuttling between the crates which had been tampered with, gathering things from them and reclosing their lids with a jittery energy. Imogen and Sir Bertrand pursued her at a distance, but she noticed and nervously confronted Imogen. Eventually, she entered the Weary Way Tavern and disappeared into the crowd. Meanwhile, the rest of the party found evidence at the warehouse that Danas had been covering up the ongoing pilferage from the warehouse stock.
entities.short_description: () was a female gnome who managed Prudaj Textiles in Jrusar. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Dancer
entities.description:
is a tinkerer from Bassuras who allegedly built Fresh Cut Grass and other automatons. FCG learned later that apparently she had acquired him already fully assembled, though inactive.

Dancer has jet black hair, "olive skin with a bit of fuzz fur on the edges", and a star tattoo on her cheek. Her eyes are light brown. Since the attack that led Fresh Cut Grass to believe Dancer was dead, she acquired a metal arm. Her voice is low, gravelly, and world-weary.

According to Fresh Cut Grass, Dancer frequently attended parties at which she got drunk and he would have to pick her up and take her home to sleep after she passed out. She would often curse when passing the shop of Imahara Joe, because she was jealous of his popularity among the other inhabitants of the area.

Esmer described Dancer as a "complicated person", but in comparison to most of the inhabitants of the neighborhood, "shining".
entities.short_description: is a tinkerer from Bassuras who allegedly built Fresh Cut Grass and other automatons. FCG learned later that apparently she had acquired him already fully assembled, though inactive.

entities.name: Daramon
entities.description:
Daramon is an old teacher of the Dayal Hall. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Daramon is a very old man, with a bald head and a big white beard that makes him look like all his hair moved down his face.

Daramon used to be a teacher, and he became Ajit Dayal's mentor, who eventually decided to dedicate himself to teaching too. When Daramon became too old, his former student started taking care of him, although he still stayed in the Dayal Hall, being a valued member due to his knowledge.

During the apogee solstice of 843 PD Chetney, Fearne and Orym visited the Dayal Hall to learn about the current situation in Jrusar, and took the chance to ask about a very old magical harness they had found in Molaesmyr. Ajit decided to bring Daramon to them, since he would be the only one who might have knowledge about such ancient arcane matters; however, after inspecting the device the old man confirmed he knew nothing about it, and left to finish his soup.
entities.short_description: Daramon is an old teacher of the Dayal Hall. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Darius
entities.description:
Darius is the husband of Shaun Gilmore. He helps Shaun with his work in Marquet. Darius has not appeared in Critical Role or Exandria Unlimited thus far.

Darius is a handsome elf with light skin and shoulder length blond hair. He is shy in public, "a perfect counterbalance" against his husband's outgoing personality, and it is rare to see him at Gilmore's Glorious Goods. Darius's singing voice and lyre playing are said to move any listener to tears.

Darius and Shaun are married and he helps him with his affairs in Marquet. Shaun refers to Darius as "lovely" when speaking about him to Fearne Calloway.

entities.name: Darmin
entities.description:
is an old man patronizing the Gemmed Hearth in Kamordah. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Darmin is very, very old, with an almost folded face, missing all of his teeth. His jaw scoops forward and overlaps the front a bit.

When the Mighty Nein encountered him at the Gemmed Hearth in Kamordah, it was difficult to tell if he was deaf or just disinterested in them.

When the Mighty Nein entered the Gemmed Hearth Inn, Darmin was the only patron seated at one of the five tables available. Fjord tried to speak with him from a distance but Darmin didn't respond. Fjord then tried to get closer but when Darmin saw the half-orc, he got very scared so Fjord backed off directly. Caleb Widogast asked Darmin about the news in Kamordah, but the old man understood the word "noose" instead and replied there hadn't been hanging in town for about four years.
entities.short_description: is an old man patronizing the Gemmed Hearth in Kamordah. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Darrow Allocke
entities.description:
is a human mercenary and the leader of The Stubborn Stock. As an NPC, Darrow was played by Matthew Mercer.

Darrow is a tall man in his thirties, standing a little over six feet tall. He is very strong-looking with dark skin and long jet black hair that is braided into a single thick braid that goes past his waist. He wears partial scale mail across the chest and part of the shoulders and a dull gray leather heavy waistband that's almost a foot thick.

Darrow comes off as friendly, welcoming, and genuine in his interactions with the Mighty Nein. Though his faith keeps him from partaking in some particular vices Darrow seems to revel in the thrill of combat, contrasting with his usual laid-back demeanor.

Darrow approached Yasha after she won an arm wrestling competition and offered her a place in his mercenary group. He told her the group was out of Gwardan on the Menagerie Coast.
entities.short_description: is a human mercenary and the leader of The Stubborn Stock. As an NPC, Darrow was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Dashilla
entities.description:
Dashilla is a sea fury who inhabits the Lucidian Ocean. Her lair is located within the Swavain Islands region of the Menagerie Coast, in a place known as the Diver's Grave. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dashilla has aqua green skin and a bulbous, unnaturally proportioned form. At the end of her arms are long vicious claws. Her long dark hair often falls across much of her face which has no nose and a mouth full of protruding angler fish-like teeth. Often glaring from behind her hair can be seen two yellow eyes, one half closed and one wide open.

Dashilla, as with all hags, is vicious and cruel. She has a penchant for collecting the shiny objects from the ships she sank and hoarded them within her lair. She also displayed great cunning and patience through many of the actions she took, such as baiting the front of her lair with treasure and flickering light to attract merrow prey for use in her rituals, and by remaining hidden whilst ensorcelling multiple members of the Mighty Nein during their travel through her lair. Upon being grievously injured she had the presence of mind to flee and hide until the danger had gone.

Dashilla has plagued the Diver's Grave for an unknown length of time, but it has been long enough for myths and legends of her to spring up in the folklore of the Menagerie Coast such as the poems Jester Lavorre had read and the sea shanty Sorris Cade sang. She preys on the local merrow population to power an ancient but very powerful magical ritual to summon fierce storms above the waters of the Diver's Grave, sinking countless ships over the time she has inhabited the area.
entities.short_description: Dashilla is a sea fury who inhabits the Lucidian Ocean. Her lair is located within the Swavain Islands region of the Menagerie Coast, in a place known as the Diver's Grave. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Davia Redtresses
entities.description:
Davia Redtresses was a provisoneer and merchant of Emon, Tal'Dorei. At some point, she talked to a group of adventurers, offering them wares to aid in a mission.

So far, Davia Redtresses has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.
entities.short_description: Davia Redtresses was a provisoneer and merchant of Emon, Tal'Dorei. At some point, she talked to a group of adventurers, offering them wares to aid in a mission.

entities.name: Davies
entities.description:
(possibly an alias) is the half-elven proprietor of Natural Remedies in Trostenwald.

"Davies" is a tan-skinned, half-elven man with dark hair that is a bit ratty and clustered.

"Davies" is a rather shady individual and it is implied he uses his own supply of drugs and performance-enhancing fungus.

Category:Shopkeepers Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: (possibly an alias) is the half-elven proprietor of Natural Remedies in Trostenwald.

entities.name: Davin
entities.description:
is an older dwarf from Westruun. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Davin is an elderly, crotchety, half-blind, one clouded eye dwarf. He is wrinkled and his hair was bright white.

Davin is very crotchety and blunt. He demanded to be fed and let out before any other prisoners in .

Davin was thrown in the Iron Stocks for an unknown reason, but was drunk at the time he was arrested.
entities.short_description: is an older dwarf from Westruun. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Dayana Prucine
entities.description:
Dayana Prucine was the High-Richter of Zadash. As an NPC, Dayana Prucine was played by Matthew Mercer.

She was an older female half-elf with dark red-purple hair that was short on the sides and brushed to one side, almost to a point. She had a gaunt, angular appearance. In her duties as High-Richter, she sometimes wore elaborate ceremonial gold-and-white armor.

For the pre-harvest gala on the 18th of Fessuran 826 PD, and at the moment of her death, she wore a beautiful, elegant, dark green dress.

Prucine was ill-tempered, prejudiced against tieflings and dwarves, and even disliked puppies.
entities.short_description: Dayana Prucine was the High-Richter of Zadash. As an NPC, Dayana Prucine was played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Deezma Simmin
entities.description:
is the tabaxi proprietor of Meandering Treasures in the Restless Wharf of Nicodranas. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Deezma is a male tabaxi with green eyes.

Deezma is the owner and proprietor of Meandering Treasures, a sort of general store in the Restless Wharf area of Nicodranas, which sells partly scavenged and partly pawned or fenced items. It holds a smell of mildewed wood, dry rot, and textiles.

Deezma sold Fjord and Yasha Nydoorin ten vials of alchemist's fire and two healing potions. He also offered a ring of fire resistance, and told a story about its previous owner not returning for a long time to reclaim it. Fjord grew curious and offered 50 gold for the name of the previous owner, but Deezma was initially reluctant to be indiscreet. Fjord left without the ring, but soon returned and offered to buy the ring if he could have the name of the previous owner; Deezma found the offer persuasive, and revealed that it was Diedric Sutan.

entities.name: Deirdre
entities.description:
Deirdre ( DEER-drə, -⁠dree, Irish: [ˈdʲɛɾˠdʲɾʲə]; Old Irish: Derdriu [ˈd̠ʲerʲd̠ʲɾʲu]) is a tragic heroine in the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology.  She is also known by the epithet "Deirdre of the Sorrows" (Irish: Deirdre an Bhróin).

Deirdre is a prominent figure in Irish legend.  American scholar James MacKillop assessed in 2004 that she was its best-known figure in modern times.

entities.name: Deirdrik Greyspine
entities.description:
is the Dwarven ambassador to the Tal'Dorei Council from the city-state of Kraghammer in 836 PD.

Although 70 years old (in 836 PD), Deirdrik is considered young for a dwarf. He is ambitious and something of a romantic idealist, generally supporting progressive ideas and policies without always thinking through the potential consequences of his actions.

As the youngest son of House Greyspine, and therefore virtually assured never to inherit a ruling position there, Deirdrik opted to pursue political success outside his home town of Kraghammer. He now serves as an ambassador with voting power on the Tal'Dorei Council, representing the interests of the sovereign city-state of Kraghammer there.

Rumors have begun circulating within Kraghammer that negotiations may be underway to have Kraghammer join the Republic of Tal'Dorei as a constituent city-state.

entities.name: Deirta Thelyss
entities.description:
Deirta Thelyss is the mother of Essek and Verin Thelyss, and the leader of one of the three ruling dens of the Kryn Dynasty. In The Mighty Nein, Deirta is voiced by Anjelica Huston.

In her most recent life Deirta is a drow woman with pale hair, purple skin, and green eyes, wearing silver and red jewelry.

She is "deeply steeped" in Dynasty culture.

Deirta was consecuted a long time ago, becoming a follower of The Luxon and living multiple lives, reincarnation after reincarnation, until she became an Umavi, a "perfect soul" revered in the Kryn Dynasty. During her most recent life, which started at some point before the 8th century after the Divergence, she is the leader of Den Thelyss, which wishes to see the Dynasty established within the world and respected by others.

entities.name: Deity
entities.description:
Deities are extremely powerful beings that represent and control aspects of reality, having because of this followers and servants among mortals.

Many of the known gods in the pantheon of Exandria fled from their original home, Tengar, the Eternal Palace, when it was attacked by a destructive force against which they were defenseless, the god-eater Predathos. They traveled through the cosmos and eventually arrived on Exandria, which at that time was at least partially a scene of elemental tumult and constant shifting change, inhabited by the Primordials and eidolons, although portions of the planet were ordered and beautiful. It is rumored that at that time, souls would return and be reborn to new life after death, consistent with the mythology of the Luxon which holds that Luxon beacons were scattered during the age of the Primordials to enact just such a cycle of rebirth.

The newly-arrived Protean Gods and the Primordials apparently existed in peace for some time, during a period known as the Founding in which the gods brought order to the chaotic portions of the world and then brought forth mortal creatures to also inhabit Exandria and which worshiped their creators. Rumors say the cycle of rebirth was broken for these creatures, whose souls now went to dwell with the god they worshipped after death. However, the major deities eventually split into two groups: the Prime Deities (who are generally seen as good- or neutral-aligned), who granted magic to mortals and who battled the Primordials who did not wish mortals to attain that much power; and the Betrayer Gods (who are generally evil-aligned) who embraced the Primordials' chaotic destruction of the mortal races following their gaining knowledge of magic.

In the late Age of Arcanum, a mortal woman ascended to godhood and replaced the god of death through a ritual they devised together. In fear of the Raven Queen's achievement, the remainder of the pantheon swiftly destroyed and prohibited her rites, and she herself took measures to ensure no one would be able to replicate it. However, another powerful mage of the Age of Arcanum, Vecna, reconstructed an altered version of the Ritual of Seeding and attempted it, but the ritual was interrupted and he was all but destroyed (although he would succeed many centuries later, in 812 PD). The Raven Queen's ascension also inspired the megalomaniacal malconvoker Vespin Chloras to try to replace the Lord of the Hells as a less destructive deity, but in his failure to replicate her act he released the imprisoned Betrayer Gods back into the Material Plane, leading to the Calamity.

entities.name: Delilah Briarwood
entities.description:
Lady Delilah Briarwood is a powerful human necromancer from Wildemount, former Archmage of Antiquity for the Cerberus Assembly, and a zealot of Vecna, The Whispered One. She is played in Critical Role by Matthew Mercer and voiced by Grey Griffin in The Legend of Vox Machina.

When Vox Machina first met her, Delilah was a beautiful woman with dark auburn hair, pulled up into a tight braided bun, and blue eyes (lavender in the series). She wore a blue-and-black gown that had a long, billowing skirt which tapered up to be form-fitting at the waist and bodice; the neckline rose nearly to her jaw. She also wore gloves.

During her time as an undead warlock patron she appeared often as a wraith-like entity made of dark and purple energy. After she was sealed inside the Pinion of Service, her appearance was that of a frail woman in a tattered dress chained to an invisible wall, with glowing purple eyes.

Delilah is incredibly cunning and intelligent as well as ruthless, cold, and willful. She is strategically minded, clearly being the mastermind behind the Briarwoods' plans in Whitestone. Despite this ruthless nature, she is genuinely loving and devoted to her husband, willing to do anything to preserve their life together.

entities.name: Demedan Baumbauch
entities.description:
is a business owner of the Baumbauch Family Brewery in Trostenwald. He has not yet appeared on Critical Role.

In their pre-stream Session 0 organized by the DM Matthew Mercer, Beauregard Lionett, Fjord, and Jester Lavorre took a job moving boxes for Baumbauch Brewing in Trostenwald. Something happened during the job that caused Beau to form a grudge against them. Beau said in they kind of swindled their employee, and the three companions didn't leave in the best of terms after that.

Beau convinced a courier in Trostenwald to give her three packages meant for the Baumbauch family.

Beau shows Jester the coded letter to Demedan from The Gentleman. She believes the code means the Baumbauch family is ordering a plant called bloodroot (which can be used as poison) from someone called "The Gentleman". Jester agrees with Beau's doodle on the note calling Demedan a douche.

entities.name: Demid Sunlash
entities.description:
Demid Sunlash is a gnome archivist of the Cobalt Soul. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Demid Sunlash is a male gnome, with a curly mop of red hair and blue eyes, wearing Cobalt Soul attire and a pair of large wide spectacles. He is tiny, even for a gnome, and slightly hunched in the shoulders.

The Mighty Nein encountered Demid in the Vellum Steeple Archive in Uthodurn, working with the Woodset Auditors to see if there was some information that might have been recovered from the ruins of Molaesmyr regarding the moons of Exandria, particularly the smaller, dimmer moon, Ruidus. Demid speculated that it was either "a pre-creation, back when the elements themselves were consuming all of Exandria," or that it may have been a creation by the Betrayer Gods that was cut short during the end of the Calamity.

Beau and Caleb met Demid at The Broken Stool and listened to him talk more about his studies of Ruidus and Catha in an effort to ingratiate themselves with him.

entities.description:
is an imp that lived with Sprigg. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Demistrik is a red imp, and like other imps, he is a tiny, winged creature.

Demistrik's master was killed by a trap when they tried to enter Sprigg's home near the Pools of Wittebak. Sprigg let the imp stay in his home for 19 years.

When Vox Machina arrived at Sprigg's homestead, Sprigg was surprised and delighted to hear they were real, then promptly told them to go away, Demistrik appearing to slam the door in their faces. Through the door, Vox Machina heard Dimistrik arguing with Sprigg about who should leave, Sprigg telling Demistrik to go become a circus performer in Kraghammer, before he let them in. Sprigg introduced himself as Sprigg "the Obnoxious", which Demistrik thought was an appropriate epithet.

entities.name: Demodus Blix
entities.description:
is a gnome illusionist and a graduate of the Penteveral of Dol-Makjar. As an NPC in Campaign Four, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Demodus is a young and handsome gnome with dark brown skin and ice-cream-swirled "fwoompy" hair. He has a curious condition that makes his irises supernaturally translucent, in a way that makes them look the color of whatever is behind his head. He wears a Penteveral vest holding school spirit badges, and a dark blue chest binder emblazoned with wizard stars.

He is beloved by many, and considered to be funny, hard-working, and enthusiastic. He is somewhat naïve, and grateful to a fault, to the point of trying to buy drinks for people who had given him money as a thanks, using that same money. He tries to show his own independence so that people that helped him in the past can be proud of him. He always gives people the benefit of the doubt.

Demodus was dropped off by his parents at the Penteveral when he was only 12 years old. Despite his age and lack of financial support from his family, he fell in love with the boarding school and wanted to eventually become a professor there. In the following decade he learned magic and became known as an illusion savant, a brilliant student with high school spirit; he was involved in many activities and events, fundraising money for specific dares and magical acts he couldn't fund by himself otherwise. He had an additional source of income from busking and doing small illusion shows in the Ogrimok Marketplace, but he had to stop when it became illegal to use magic in such spaces.

"Oh, hi, I just wanted to meet everybody. My name is Denalia. I'm making meals. I'll be right over here cooking if you need me. If not, I'll be probably sleeping."

entities.description:
Depherad Kolios is a wedding planner in Zadash. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Depherad is a half-elven woman with long blonde hair, very pale skin and dark eyes even in the sclera.

When Jester and Fjord met her, she was wearing a very well buttoned over suit with a sash that has many beads hanging from it.

Depherad met with Jester and Fjord in Zadash, asking them numerous questions and offering suggestions and alternatives regarding the couple's wedding plans. Throughout the process, the half-elf took notes, remaining impartial and professional no matter how unusual what she heard was; the only time she showed any nervousness was when Artagan showed up unexpectedly and began appearing and disappearing in the room while contributing to the plans. Despite everything, the meeting ended successfully.

He wears the buttoned-over uniform of a captain of the Dwendalian Empire which has a number of decorations on the front of the lapel.

Fjord introduced himself to Captain Deremi at the party at the Marquis Demesne in Nicodranas. Deremi was marginally polite, and seemed to see that Fjord was not as experienced as he was attempting to project.

Desavon is an older, very well-dressed male dwarf on the rotund side. When Bells Hells encountered him, he was leaving the throne room of the king and queen, flanked by two bodyguards, and dressed in long purple velvet robes with gold and red inlays. He wore jeweled rings on every finger and in his beard.

The Team Wildemount half of Bells Hells encountered Desavon outside the throne room of the Uthodurnian king and queen. Fearne picked up a conversation with him and he responded gallantly, not noticing that she pickpocketed a very expensive jeweled ring from his beard during the conversation.

Garen was an amiable leader. He grew somber at the mention of Uthtor..}}

entities.name: Desmond Moondrop
entities.description:
is a founding member of The Fletching and Moondrop Traveling Carnival of Curiosities, which he runs alongside Gustav Fletching. As an NPC he is played by Matthew Mercer

Desmond is a bald man in his late 30s. He was first seen wearing a frilled frock coat of bright red, his face adorned with vibrant orange makeup to look like the setting sun. During the performance, he first wore an outfit and makeup matching the deep blue of the tent, and was later seen to don an outfit of deep-set black.

Under the makeup, Desmond's face is heavily scarred, appearing to have been shredded at some point in the past.

Desmond has a melancholic presence to him that contrasts with his colorful performances on stage. He is extremely talented at playing the violin and even shows some acrobatic ability. While a calm and stoic person, Desmond does seem to genuinely care for the members of the circus and is forgiving of his business partner, Gustav.

entities.name: Desmond Otham
entities.description:
Desmond Otham was the carriage driver for the Briarwoods until he was captured and imprisoned by Vox Machina. When the de Rolos restored their rule in Whitestone, Percy granted him the position of a messenger between Whitestone and Emon. As an NPC in campaign one, Desmond was played by Matthew Mercer. In The Legend of Vox Machina he is voiced by Max Mittelman.

In confrontation with Percy, Desmond lost a large part of the upper part of his right hand and most of his fingers (index, middle and ring). After Pike healed him with her divine magic, the wound closed entirely, and the thumb and pinky grew complete and functional.

His father was a messenger during the de Rolo's rule. He vanished on the night of their fall. His mother was taken by madness and passed away in 810 PD. Since Desmond possessed a decent knowledge of the roads between Whitestone and Emon, he was hired as a coachman for Count Tylieri, who misused the power and titles that the Briarwoods gifted unto him by abusing his staff and many citizens of Whitestone, including a teenaged Desmond. After seeing the harm Tylieri had wrought, Sylas Briarwood took the boy under his wing, hiring him as a coach for him and his wife.

Seriously hurt in their fight with Vox Machina at the Palace of the Sovereign, the Briarwoods attempted to escape via the carriage, which Desmond was driving. The party toppled the carriage, but the Briarwoods managed to teleport away. In anger, Percy shot off Desmond's hand and knocked him unconscious to further interrogate him at Greyskull Keep.

Desona was described as a half-elven female in her forties with piercing green eyes and long, fine brown hair that reached just past her shoulders. Like other scalebearers, Desona wore silver and blue robes.

Much later, Vox Machina discovered Scalebearer Desona's body hanging in a torture chamber within the Tower of Entropis in Thar Amphala.

entities.description:
Devana Vessar is an elven cartographer who lives in Syngorn with her husband, Syldor Vessar, and their daughter, Velora Vessar. She is also the stepmother of Syldor's half-elf children, Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia. As an NPC, Devana is played by Matthew Mercer in Critical Role, and by Toks Olagundoye in The Legend of Vox Machina, Season Two.

Devana is described as having bright blonde hair that she keeps braided and tied up.

In Vox Machina Origins, she is depicted with dark brownish gray hair tied in a loose bun. She has tan skin. When Vox Machina met her, she was wearing a dark teal dress with loose sleeves over a purple blouse.

Similarly, in The Legend of Vox Machina she also has darker skin, black hair and dark purple eyes.

entities.name: Devexian
entities.description:
Devexian, also known as "D", is an Aeormaton who the Mighty Nein found in the ruined city of Aeor. He was given the name Charlie while he couldn't remember his true designation after being found by the Mighty Nein. Later, as "D", he sold Fresh Cut Grass to Dancer. As an NPC, Devexian is played by Matthew Mercer.

Devexian is tall, masculine-presenting (and generally described as handsome), and roughly humanoid in form, made of dull, brass-like metal with intricate filigreed engraving and gold trim. He has no nose, but does have eye sockets, a mouth, and jaw, and a "deepish" voice. When the Mighty Nein found him, his legs had been heavily damaged.

In his guise as "D", Devexian passed for an organic humanoid, wearing a "really intricate metal mask" (which was actually just his face) and a dark hooded cloak. He walked alongside a crawler-pulled cart and wore leather boots., Imogen used Detect Thoughts on Imahara Joe to actually view his memory of seeing D.}}

He is serious and professional, but has a fondness for those who seek knowledge like him. He isn't used to be the center of attention.

entities.name: Diassa Kwynn
entities.description:
Diassa Kwynn was a female paladin of (presumably) the Lawbearer. So far, she has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

In her youth, Kwynn was rebellious and struck out into the world, confident in her wit and faith in her goddess. However, after realizing the extent of the dangers of the world, she appears to be more cautious and willing to bury her own curiosity in preference of safety.

In her youth, Kwynn was rebellious and struck out to explore the world, using her wit and faith to protect herself. Eventually realizing the extent of the dangers harbored in the world and how they are not always easily cast away, she grew more cautious and willing to bury her own curiosity in preference of safety. At some point in her life, she became a paladin and took on a squire named Aedla, to whom she passed on her wisdom of caution.

The single source of information about this character is a quote in the original Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting sourcebook, and it twice uses the name "Changebearer" to refer to the god Diassa serves. This is an apparent portmanteau of "Changebringer" and "Lawbearer", two goddesses with contrasting commandments about striking out into the unknown. The Lawbearer commands her followers to tame the wilds and defend against the darkness, so this page presumes the sourcebook intended to refer to her.
entities.short_description: Diassa Kwynn was a female paladin of (presumably) the Lawbearer. So far, she has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Diedric Sutan
entities.description:
, possibly spelled Suutan, is the head of the Sutan family. He has been mentioned but not appeared on Critical Role.

The Mighty Nein first learned of Lord Sutan when Dolan Thrym, speaking in a meeting of The Knights of Requital in Zadash, named the house of Sutan as having taken over his physician practice, placing the son of the house, Ren Sutan, in charge of it. When the party decided to work with the Knights in the plot to take down the High-Richter, part of the plan involved breaking into the Sutan residence to steal a wax seal and a sample of his handwriting in order to falsely connect him to the Myriad and bring down the Sutan family as well.

The plan was executed, more or less successfully until the unexpected return home of the High-Richter and the simultaneous attack on the Zauber Spire by Xhorhasian spies. Afterward, the party heard that Lord Sutan was already in chains.

At Meandering Treasures in Nicodranas, Fjord purchased a Ring of Fire Resistance that had been put on an installment payment plan by Lord Sutan "a year or so ago". He was never heard from again by the pawnbroker, because he was in prison.

entities.name: Dieter
entities.description:
"Dieter" is the nickname the Mighty Nein gave to a dragon turtle that they encountered in the Lucidian Ocean near Urukayxl. The name is derived from the first two syllables of "D. Turtle," short for "dragon turtle." As an NPC, Dieter is played by Matthew Mercer.

After the peace talks concludeed the Mighty Nein made their way towards Rumblecusp to attend Traveler Con on the Zenith, the 26th of Unndilar, 836 PD. Fjord decides to go towards Rumblecusp via south of Urukayxl. During the journey Caduceus Clay notices a small island trailing the Balleater, after bringing it to the attention of the crew, Fjord recalls from old sailor stories and marine mythology that the island that was trailing them was this dragon turtle.

The dragon turtle gave chase to their ship, and the Mighty Nein engaged in combat, firing at it with their cannons. Jester Lavorre successfully Polymorphed the dragon turtle into a sea turtle and combat subsided. However, Caduceus realized that the dragon turtle was still pursuing them in its sea turtle form as this form was in fact faster than its original form. The party decided to send in its two clerics alongside its wizard to Polymorph the dragon turtle into a form which would not be able to chase them. With Caleb Widogast's magic, he Polymorphed it into a sea slug.

After the Mighty Nein escaped the dragon turtle's wrath, Jester used Sending to contact the dragon turtle, asking "are you looking for your mate?" to which the dragon turtle ominously responded with “I need no mate. I take what I want.”

entities.name: Dimble Thaydeen
entities.description:
is a goliath woman who lives in Rexxentrum. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Thaydeen is a large goliath woman with red frazzled hair, described as being similar to Merida's from the movie Brave.

Thaydeen is described as being a showman, especially when she gives Caleb and Caduceus business cards for her establishment.

Thaydeen is the owner of Thaydeen's Endless Emporium of Enchanted Eccentricities, having taken over the family business from her father after he passed.

entities.name: Dispater
entities.description:
Dispater is one of the archdevils of the Nine Hells and the Lord of the Second in the Iron City of Dis. Also known as the Iron Duke, he is considered a master of politics and manipulation. He uses the Iron Tower in Dis as his throne.

In one depiction of Dispater, he looks like a humanoid male with slicked long hair that goes to about mid-back. His face is very chiseled and handsome, with two hooked horns at the top of the forehead, continuing upward. He does not stand on two legs, but rather has one singular cloven hoof at the bottom of his torso, and he is adorned in fine robes.

Dispater is described as worried and paranoid, obsessed with keeping his city in a perpetual state of change and reconstruction.

Dispater became the ruler of his layer at some point after Asmodeus became the ruler of Baator, turning celestials into the first devils, and other Betrayer Gods imposed order on demons to create more of them for their armies.

entities.name: Diven Leson
entities.description:
is an altmer with multiple regulatory professions. As an NPC, is played by the GM of each of the Blackwood specials: Matthew Mercer, Marisha Ray, and Liam O'Brien.

Diven is an altmer with light brown hair who wears fine clothing and who powders his face.

Diven is somewhat fastidious and demanding.

Diven arrived at the tavern (then known as the Dreary Jug) late in the evening and asked for wine. He spoke with Hoa Sen and at Mallory's recommendation ordered the Plowman's Special as well, then asked to see the group's ledgers, claiming that the previous owners of the tavern were behind on their taxes. When the party could not produce the ledgers nor the back taxes, he told them they needed to pay a 300 gold fee to delay their payment, initially asking for it immediately but eventually agreeing to wait until the morning after threats from Tavima. He then nailed a sign to the door of the tavern saying it was closed until the back taxes had been paid.
entities.short_description: is an altmer with multiple regulatory professions. As an NPC, is played by the GM of each of the Blackwood specials: Matthew Mercer, Marisha Ray, and Liam O'Brien.

entities.name: Dobby Kingsman
entities.description:
is the halfling innkeeper of the Sodden Grange Inn in Heartmoor Hamlet. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dobby is very old and looks somewhat rough. He is a heavy pipe smoker, and has a very thick, bushy gray beard. Dobby's ears are large, and his gray hair is curly.

Bells Hells met Dobby when they bought rooms at the Sodden Grange Inn. Once asked by Imogen and Orym, he provided the party with plentiful information about the people and sights of Heartmoor Hamlet, including Isha Sabanis, Estani, and the Twilight Mirror Museum. Dobby specifically cautioned about coming on too strong to the townsfolk and to not take offense when residents seem distant or mistrustful; the Heartmoor Hamlet is far from large cities and has seen outsiders attempt to take advantage of this by engaging in unlawful activity. He offered a small amount of his pipe tobacco to Ashton, on request.

Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: is the halfling innkeeper of the Sodden Grange Inn in Heartmoor Hamlet. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Dolan Thrym
entities.description:
Dolan Thrym is a human man and the High-Richter of Zadash. He was also the de facto leader of The Knights of Requital. As an NPC, Dolan was played by Matthew Mercer.

Dolan is a short, thin man with greying unkempt hair, small spectacles he wore on the edge of his nose, and unshaven stubble on his chin. He wore a nice white shirt he had tucked in.

Dolan seems polite but harbors ambitions of wielding influence that he keeps somewhat secret. When situations turn dire, Dolan's response is to protect Horris from harm.

At some point in his past, Dolan earned an art degree.

entities.name: Dominox
entities.description:
Dominox, the Grand Demon of Loathing, also known simply as the Dominox, was a powerful and very ancient demon once sealed in Aeor.

Dominox had massive red muscular clawed arms, impossibly large shoulders with hooks protruding from their fleshy armored plates, burning red eyes, a toothy lizard-like mouth of putrid scent, massive horns curling outward, and a long tail with a second reptilian head at its end. The creature stood 15-16 feet tall and its long arms scraped the ground when it stood. When he bled, his demonic ichor transformed into chains.

When he didn't want to look threatening, Dominox took the form of a young girl, five or six years old, with pale skin, strong and vibrant red hair, and a black dress that resembled armor. However, even in that form, moments of anger would make the grand demon show glimpses of glowing energy and his true form.

His symbol is two overlapping circles of different sizes, with lines forming a strange sigil.

entities.name: Donaea
entities.description:
was a dragonborn cleric of the Moonweaver, and the partner of Erro Mordaurum.

She was a dragonborn woman with scales as white as snow. She had a holy symbol of the goddess of the moon carved from gray-white stone.

Despite living in an apocalyptic world, she believed that change was coming.

Donaea lived during the Calamity as a cleric of the Moonweaver, and had a very hard life. She met Erro Mordaurum, an equally exhausted dragonborn man, next to a lake in Gwessar, and they stayed together for a year, becoming partners and making the lake their home even if they traveled together several times.

entities.name: Dono
entities.description:
is a Bormodo farmer and rancher in Razora on Ruidus; his cytaa is Kaniey. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dono was described as hulking-looking and round-backed, with arms like tree trunks, an elephantine nose with thin nostrils, and thick brows.

Dono seemed to struggle with decision-making, and was upset and anxious because his symbiote cytaa Kaniey was too young to offer advice. However, even through his fear and anxiety on encountering Bells Hells unexpectedly, he was also curious. He described himself as "simple farm folk".

Dono had recently lost his symbiote cytaa, and was raising a new one named Kaniey, who was still very young and unable to speak as yet.

entities.name: Doolan Tversky
entities.description:
is the Archmage of Dysology for the Cerberus Assembly. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Doolan Tversky is an old gnomish woman. When she hired the Darrington Brigade, she was dressed in a finely-crafted blue-green travel outfit of leather and fine silks. She has an intense-looking face, though she has a smile that prevents her from appearing too stern.

Doolan Tversky is an "absent-minded yet brilliant gnome who is obsessed with all beasts, aberrations, and creatures of legend." She resents the Cobalt Soul, as they have barred her from their libraries due to her reputation.

When she hired the Darrington Brigade to recover the meteor that had fallen in the Cyrengreen Forest, she did not care how they brought her the object/creature, as long as it was brought to her. She accepted Taryon's price of 10,000 gold without protest, but insisted on "10,000. No more." when Macaroni attempted to add "per hour" to the billing. She believed that adventurers had their purpose.

entities.description:
was an employee of the Meat Man. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Doran is a 22–23 year old, scrawny-looking boy with completely shaved head and tanned skin.

entities.name: Dorao
entities.description:
Dorao is a pale elf with brown hair, bright amber eyes, and a scar under his mouth to the left.

While Annaline was traveling through the Oderan Wilds, she encountered the "temporarily unleashed" weretiger Dorao, and she believed that his release involved the Ivory Syndicate from what Ajit Dayal told her later. Dorao bit her, transmitting his lycanthopy to her.

Annaline requested that if Chetney ever encountered Dorao, to kill him immediately.
entities.short_description: Dorao is a pale elf with brown hair, bright amber eyes, and a scar under his mouth to the left.

entities.name: Dork the Ox
entities.description:
Dork the Ox was an ox purchased by Vex'ahlia that Vox Machina attempted to place into their bag of holding during their pre-stream home game. When they later retrieved Dork, they learned that living creatures do not survive within the confines of the bag of holding.

Keyleth once used Speak with Animals to converse with Dork, although apparently the conversation didn't go well.

entities.name: Doron
entities.description:
was one of the members of the dwarven family who gave up their home in the Vo village on Rumblecusp to the Mighty Nein. As an NPC, Doron is played by Matthew Mercer.

Doron was eager to give up his family's modest home in a broken-off hollowed-out giant tree to the party for the night, saying that it would be nice to have a bit of a change of pace.

He was originally from Wildemount, where he had a relationship to which he was not eager to return after recovering his memories.

Doron appeared briefly as the Mighty Nein were being ushered into his home to stay the night.

entities.name: Doset Tachonis
entities.description:
is the former Baron of Sloak, and a cousin of Occtis Tachonis. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

He was described by Talcydimir Pridesire as a "pretty boy."

Doset was born as a member of House Tachonis, although not into the main branch: he was the second child (and only son) of Lady Nausha Vachari and Segundus Tachonis, younger brother of Lord Primus Tachonis, and had two sisters, Univere (the older) and Tertia (the younger). At some point after he reached adulthood, around the year 69, his family started making moves to control land in Timmony. As part of it, Doset was chosen to become the husband of the Baroness of Sloak, who had inherited the titles and lands of her predecessor, her previous husband; this new and marriage was very short, lasting only nine months, and ended with the death of Lady Sloak, which left Doset as the only heir of the barony in the year 71. Although there was some expectation in Timmony about him becoming the ruler of the region, he ended up designating Casimir Gavendale as his successor (as a way for House Tachonis to pay him for granting them the means to execute Thjazi Fang. The true purpose of Univere and Doset's time in Timmony was harvesting and relocating stolen calcidion.

Lord Doset and his sister Univere had a meeting with the new Baron of Sloak in his new, ruinous castle, giving him the deed of title that had been stolen from him by Talcydimir Pridesire. Casimir was very disappointed with his reward and the fact he didn't get to punish the thief, and spoke rudely to his benefactors, causing Doset to coldly point out that Talcydimir was no longer concern of him, and that Sloak, disappointing as it might be, was more than he deserved.
entities.short_description: is the former Baron of Sloak, and a cousin of Occtis Tachonis. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Dr. Fitzwaggle
entities.description:
Dr. Fitzwaggle is an eccentric potionmaker from Josgren's Hollow. As an NPC, he is played by Nick Williams.

Dr. Fitzwaggle is a short man of white beard and half-moon glasses, dressed with clothes covered in colorful stains.

He seems slightly distracted all the time, but always very enthusiastic about his products

Dr. Fitzwaggle was one of the potionmakers of Josgren's Hollow, but he wasn't very appreciated, and his products were deemed less than reliable; because of this, the place he got during Potion Con in 839 PD was very bad, and when the whispers attacked he was immediately killed.

entities.name: Drake Thunderbrand
entities.description:
Elementalist Drake Thunderbrand is a dwarven wizard and friend of Allura Vysoren, as well as a member of the Arcana Pansophical. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Drake has short, black hair with a beard "trimmed fairly fine." When he first encountered Vox Machina in late 810 PD, he was wearing red leathers and was apparently unarmed, though carrying a gnarled, curved wand. The wand almost spiraled, in a messed-up sort of way, with a well-treated surface.

Somewhat exuberant in personality, Drake can also be quite soft—both concerned and supportive—toward Lady Allura.

Drake Thunderbrand is one of the eldest of House Thunderbrand in Kraghammer.

entities.name: Dranzel
entities.description:
is a half-orc violinist and the leader of Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Dr. Dranzel is a rowdy-looking but well-dressed half-orc. He keeps his black hair slicked back. He has a rough-looking, angry chin. His general appearance leans more towards the orc side than the human side.

In this semicanonical one-shot set sometime prior to 795 PD, Dr. Dranzel and his troupe, including Kent Plucker and a young and inexperienced Scanlan Shorthalt, were in the northern Shattered Teeth attending the Musetide Festival of Drobanagos, in the island of Athova-Rae. After the celebrations the troupe sailed to Tal'Dorei, and Dranzel allowed Scanlan's new friends (Sarge, Bobby Socks, Ranthiel Volthor, and Bramble) to go with them.

Vox Machina visited the Diamond Nest tavern and there encountered Dr. Dranzel and his Spectacular Traveling Troupe, who were in the middle of putting on a performance. Scanlan joined them with his flute, and played a duet with Kaylie, finishing the band's set. Scanlan caught up with the troupe, and while they were talking a young halfling boy named Samson delivered to Dr. Dranzel the spoils of his thievery. Vox Machina introduced themselves to the troupe, and Dranzel deemed their name too formal, so Vex told him to call them the Shits.

entities.name: Drath Mephruhn
entities.description:
(spelled "Mephrun" in an earlier work) was a shade or dying mage who briefly achieved lichdom by placing a phylactery in Grog Strongjaw's chest. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Pike identified Drath as a "shade" Indeed, Drath's appearance and behavior resemble those of a "lich shade" from Pathfinder, which was used early in the pre-stream home game.

When he possessed Grog's body, the violet glow of his eyes was transferred to Grog.

Drath looked down on others to an extreme degree, describing the adventurers who interrupted his ritual as "worthless cattle". He called Grog's body "this behemoth's shell", and in his final fight he gloated and expressed contempt for his opponents constantly.

entities.name: Dread Emperor
entities.description:
The Dread Emperor was one of the major enemies that Vox Machina fought prior to the stream. He was a deviation of the "Dread Emperor" example villain from Dungeons & Dragons, 3rd ed. As an NPC, he was played by Matthew Mercer.

In the Material Plane, the Dread Emperor used magic to appear as a child with black hair and golden eyes, but upon dropping the illusion, he appeared as a grown man with long, black hair, wearing gold armor.

The Dread Emperor enjoyed the presence of children because of their innocence and naïveté. However, when his own life was at stake, he was willing to use those same children as a means of defense, even at the cost of their lives. He also killed the children that grew too old.

The Dread Emperor was a being that lived on a large island, which held a giant gothic castle surrounded by a bramble forest, floating through either the Astral Plane or a pocket dimension. The Dread Emperor abducted children, chaining them by the neck to his armor, gaining power from them. When the children became too old, he would kill them and put their bodies in the castle basement.

entities.name: Dreef
entities.description:
is a human blacksmith in Nicodranas. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dreef is a tan skinned, heavyset, burly looking fellow, human, with a smooth bald head, a split lip that healed with a big scar that gives him a little bit of character.

Dreef apparently is both well-read (being able to produce a book and identify Caduceus's sword hilt as Uthodurnian) and playful. Noticing that Beau was carrying a bo staff, he produced a bow which he tied on the staff, so it would be Beau's bo bow.

Dreef is the owner of Ingots and Hammers, a humble-sized blacksmith shop in Nicodranas.

entities.name: Drekkit
entities.description:
Drekkit was one of the leaders of a goblin clan that lived in the Marrow Valley.

Drekkit was a goblin man with green skin who wore armor and a hood adorned with a small metal skull, and wielded an axe. Only his right eye, was visible, the left was covered by a bandage, suggesting an injurie or the lack of the eye.

At some point around 833 PD Drekkit and his mate, Khaaz, led their goblin clan to Felderwin, attacking their inhabitants and taking several prisoners, including Veth and Yeza Brenatto, as well as their young son, Luc.

The clan kept the prisoners for weeks, weaker and weaker, until the halfling family was able to escape, using bone toothpicks that Khaaz had left within reach to force the lock on their cage. While Yeza and Luc ran ahead, Veth lured their captors away, eventually being confronted by them. She tried to attack them (Drekkit catched the crossbow bolt she fired at him), and ended up throwing a vial of acid in the leader's face, killing him. Khaaz witnessed it, and once Veth was recaptured, the goblin widow used the help of a witch, Isharnai, to torture Drekkit's killer.
entities.short_description: Drekkit was one of the leaders of a goblin clan that lived in the Marrow Valley.

entities.name: Drez Vina
entities.description:
Drez Vina is a mysterious elf that hired Vox Machina in Westruun to infiltrate Realmseer Eskil Ryndarien's Greystone Tower and steal a brass box with a pearl-topped lid. He works for Master Quall, who required this relic. As an NPC, Drez Vina is played by Matthew Mercer.

Drez Vina is an elven man with long brown hair that he keeps slicked back and tucked behind his ears.

Drez Vina first approached Vox Machina at an inn in Westruun and hired them to infiltrate an archmage's tower to retrieve a certain brass box. The party agreed to the job, but upon reaching the top of the tower they decided not to steal from Eskil Ryndarien, and instead asked for his aid in removing a lich's phylactery from the chest of Grog Strongjaw.

After Vox Machina abandoned their theft mission, Drez Vina found them within their chambers at the inn, very unhappy that the items provided (and used) in the mission are gone, and the deal was not kept. While his Master was very unhappy with the group's previous behavior, Drez said, "He sees potential, and is offering another mission to both wipe clean your debt, and make some more gold on the side." He then hired the party to infiltrate a druid's barrow called the Shadebarrow, delve into the Tomb of Driag, and return with an arcane cortex embedded within some rumored construct within. This time, the party completed the mission and delivered the cortex to Drez, who happily paid for their services.

entities.name: Drixlitch Ovana
entities.description:
is an elven toymaker in Uthodurn. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Drixlitch is a tall elven gentleman, young to middle-aged with curly blond hair and a very long pointed nose. When encountered by Bells Hells, he wore ostentatious clothing and a tall top hat. He used a cane and walked with a slight limp.

Drixlitch repeatedly stressed that he was the majority owner of the business. Matt compared him to "a snide Willy Wonka". Chetney Pock O'Pea described Drixlitch as "a son of a bitch", and while Oltgar told the party he was "a unique individual who has a good mind for business," he was secretly thinking "this fucking son of a bitch," who had crushed not only his spirit but that of all the other toymakers in the shop.

According to Chetney, Oltgar Dradegon was a brilliant master craftsman and maker of fine wooden toys. Chetney had worked with him as his second in his shop in Uthodurn for years. When Drixlitch arrived, he was all about metal toys, and overnight, Oltgar sold part of the store to him, which Chetney viewed as a total betrayal. Eventually Chetney's hostility escalated to the point where he stabbed Drixlitch in the knee and Oltgar in the hand before fleeing. Drixlitch had to use a cane because of that injury, but he lied about its origin, saying he was wounded in a war.
entities.short_description: is an elven toymaker in Uthodurn. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Drunneq Bronzegrip
entities.description:
Drunneq Bronzegrip was a master smith and a member of House Bronzegrip, one of the five ruling Houses of Kraghammer. At some point, he became fed up with what he regarded as "smoke-brained tavern tales" regarding rare, pre-refined metals left in the remains of deceased cinderslag elementals. He once explained that anyone thinking of seeking out a cinderslag elemental would only get themselves killed.

So far, Drunneq Bronzegrip has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Dryca
entities.description:
Dryca of Ghostwall is a gnome who lived in the Ghostlands of Xhorhas as late as the early 840s PD.

Dryca is a male nether gnome with a stocky build, a bald head, and purplish grey skin marked with angular tattoos on his arms, torso, and neck. He wore simple clothing: a white shirt and dark pants.

Dryca is a mysterious and secretive individual, and also cold-minded, able to make difficult decisions in order to protect his people. He also was somewhat loyal to the Bright Queen, even if not very devoutly.

Dryca was part of a nether gnome community in the Ghostlands. At some point in the last three centuries he met one of the last members of a lineage of champions of Kord that warded a passage to the Dreadnest, Lolth's layer in the Abyss. After the extinction of that line of trusted heros, Dryca became the only one with knowledge of said passage.
entities.short_description: Dryca of Ghostwall is a gnome who lived in the Ghostlands of Xhorhas as late as the early 840s PD.

entities.name: Dryden
entities.description:
Rockcaller Dryden is a half-orc member of the Earth Ashari. She is one of the central sentinels of Terrah. As an NPC, Dryden is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dryden is a short and stocky female half-orc wearing furs and leathers. Her hair is woven in thick braids that are pulled up and back into a sort of topknot. Her jaw protrudes a bit, exposing her two lower fangs.

Dryden, flanked by two humans, approached Vox Machina as they entered Terrah. She recognized Keyleth from her previous visit to Terrah. Keyleth asked her how the Earth Ashari had fared over the past few months that the Chroma Conclave had been active. Dryden explained that they had hunkered down and focused on making sure their elemental rift did not experience the same tear as the one in Pyrah. Keyleth then informed her that the Chroma Conclave had been slain and Dryden said she would pass the news along. Keyleth requested to speak with headmaster Pa'tice in order to get information on the Water Ashari. Dryden mentioned that she could answer any questions about the Water Ashari, but Keyleth really just wanted to see Pa'tice while she in the area. Dryden and her companions then led Vox Machina to Headmaster Pa'tice.

entities.description:
was a young woman with scrying abilities. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Duala is young mousy woman of red-brown skin. Her eyes are snow-blind. She has big black curls that trail down to her middle back.

After Vox Machina cleared out the platinum mine, Korshad called on Duala to confirm that all conditions were met. She cast a spell similar to scrying to verify that job had been done.

entities.description:
is a captain in the Righteous Brand, commanding troops at the Wuyun Gates. As an NPC, Captain Dualla is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dualla wears the silver and dark-crimson armor of the Righteous Brand. Her hair is a reddish-brown and a bit sun bleached at the tips. She keeps her hair pulled into a high ponytail.

entities.name: Duasad Keef
entities.description:
Duasad Keef () is a human noble of the Keef family from the Clovis Concord, and a member of the Golden Grin. He is a transgender man. Duasad is known for his empathic skills, which he uses to help people to go through their psychological challenges.

Duasad is a human man with an "acrobatic" build and a friendly smile. When Dorian first met him, Duasad wore his hair in a bun pulled to one side, and had on a shimmering bronze outfit over a light blue shirt.

In the summer of 843 PD, Duasad Keef appeared at the ball held by the Chandei Quorum in Jrusar attended by Bells Hells.

entities.name: Dugger
entities.description:
() is a dwarf involved in the criminal activities at the Prudaj Textiles warehouse in Jrusar. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dugger had a pale sallow face, greasy pulled-back hair, and a patchy, nasty-looking chin beard. When Bells Hells saw him, he wore a dark cloak.

In his mutated form, Dugger's veins were blackened and oozed glistening oily film. The eyes were almost completely black.

Dugger was cold, demanding, and generally agreed upon to be creepy.

entities.name: Dulgrim Smeltborne
entities.description:
was a fabled dwarven weaponsmith who lived from approximately 430 to 832 PD.

Dulgrim was a somewhat squat dwarf with broad shoulders, black hair that was thin in the front but thick and heavy in the back, a bulbous nose that looked like it had taken a few hits in his youth, and piercing bright light blue, almost grey-white eyes.

Dulgrim was a fabled Uthodurnian weaponsmith who had been called to create implements of war by the elves of Molaesmyr. He reforged and strengthened Dwueth'var, the Star Razor, after it was sundered in a terrible battle deep within the ruins of Molaesmyr within the Savalirwood.

Dulgrim's son Umagorn Smeltborne has carried on his father's work and operates his forge in Uthodurn.
entities.short_description: was a fabled dwarven weaponsmith who lived from approximately 430 to 832 PD.

entities.name: Duncan
entities.description:
was one of the members of a team that had won the Hour of Honor three weeks in a row before Mighty Nein's victory. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer

Duncan was a gnomish gentleman with a patchy beard with missing centerpiece on his chin.

entities.name: Durent
entities.description:
is a dwarven Waverider of the Water Ashari. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Durent was a very dark skinned, stocky dwarf with very short, dirty blonde hair and an unkempt, tattered and knotted beard. He wore goggles and a throat bead.

Durent escorted Vox Machina beneath the ocean to the Aerie of Torrent, the underwater rift into the Elemental Plane of Water. He showed them three lodestones so that they would know what to look for, and told them they were mostly found buried. He also urged the party to abandon their quest if it went badly, and told them that returning safely was the most important thing.

When Grog, Percival, and Taryon staggered back through the portal after battling the Kraken, Durent escorted them safely to the surface, enquiring anxiously about Keyleth.
entities.short_description: is a dwarven Waverider of the Water Ashari. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Durmas
entities.description:
is the main stablehand in Alfield. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Durmas is a hardy, rotund and strong female dragonborn with black scales and no tail.

Durmas outfitted the the Mighty Nein with a new cart as the previous one had carried many of the dead. The new cart belonged to somebody in Alfield and was given to the party out of appreciation. It was a well-made cart, larger than the previous, and it didn’t smell of blood and feces.

entities.name: Durrom
entities.description:
Durrom of the Emerald Eyes was the lord of the aboleth city of Salar and master of its surviving brood of dozens or perhaps hundreds of aboleths. As of 836 PD, it oversees the brood as it expands its army of thralls and learns about the surface world, with the ultimate goal of shattering the forgotten Pillars of the Earth that support Emon and collapsing the city into its subterranean domain.

So far, Durrom has not appeared or been mentioned onstream.

In the original Tal'Dorei Campaign Setting, set in 812 PD, this character was called "Overseer Durrom", and the Pillars of the Earth were said to support the surface of Tal'Dorei, rather than clarifying that, with Salar being directly underneath Emon, and the twisting pillars coming up from Salar, only Emon would be affected.

entities.name: Durth Mirimm
entities.description:
Taskhand is a drow soldier in command of the Kryn Dynasty's forces at Jigow.

Durth is very loyal to the Kryn Dynasty, but neglects the needs of the town he is assigned to, causing a strained relationship with local leaders.

Durth joined or was born as a member of Den Mirimm in the Kryn Dynasty, being therefore a nobleman of notable influence due to his family contacts. At some point before 836 PD his military merits helped him achieved the rank of Taskhand, and he was given charge of the Aurora Watch in Jigow.

This city, as part of the Kryn Dynasty, needed an intermediary between its elders, Colbu Kaz and Ushru, and the government, and Durth was supposed to act as such. However, his priorities always favored the Kryn Dynasty, and he only cared about how Jigow could benefit the nation, which, combined with his controversial judgments, causes tensions and challenges from the elders, and particularly from Colbu Kaz, who enjoys thwarting Durth and other Kryn representatives.
entities.short_description: Taskhand is a drow soldier in command of the Kryn Dynasty's forces at Jigow.

entities.name: Dust titan
entities.description:
The dust titan, known by other names such as the Rolling Danger or the Thunder that Comes, is an elemental titan composed of dust, sand, and cyclonic winds.

The dust titan had two eyes of perpetual green glow, and a huge body whose winds carried elements of its environment. In addition to its titanic, sandstone-like form, this primordial was capable of taking on the appearance of a tornado.

The dust titan was very aggressive, and relentless while chasing a target.

The dust titan was one of the primordials, ancient beings of chaotic elemental power that existed before the Exandrian Founding. At some point this specific titan began to prowl the plane of Pandemonium, using its power to attack and destroy life forms and their buildings, such as a citadel made of dark metal.

entities.name: Duvia Dwendal
entities.description:
Queen Duvia Dwendal was a noblewoman of the Dwendalian Empire, and the consort of its ruler, King Bertrand Dwendal, until her death.

Duvia was a human woman who kept her husband company while she was alive.

Duvia was a noble of the Dwendalian Empire who, when she reached an appropriate age, married Bertrand Dwendal, who became ruler of the Empire in 790 PD. Together, the couple had at least one son, Prince Eidys Dwendal, who became his father's heir. Queen Duvia died around 826 PD, following which the king became a lonely man, and had not married again, through at least 835 PD.

entities.description:
is a gnomish employee of The Gentleman. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dweez is a crazed looking young gnome with big mound of curly blond hair and big chinstrap beard.

Dweez is a "not-bright sorcerer thief with the Gentleman, extremely loyal."

entities.name: Dwelma
entities.description:
Before the battle at Glory Run Road, Keg described Dwelma as the "creepiest and the craziest" of the Iron Shepherds, as well as "pretty gnarly" to the remaining Mighty Nein.

A group of dark figures (likely Dwelma, Protto, Ruzza, and Wohn) attacked Fjord, Jester, and Yasha when they moved away from the rest of the Mighty Nein camping for the night. The attack made no noise. After a struggle, Fjord, Jester, and Yasha were all bound and gagged. The Iron Shepherds dragged them to Lorenzo to show off their catches then locked them in cages. The carts with the cages continued along the road.

Beau, Caleb, Keg, Molly, and Nott ambushed the Iron Shepherds on the Glory Run Road. Beau and Molly surrounded Dwelma when they came out of hiding and attacked her. Dwelma helped her allies by dispelling Caleb's Slow spell, but was still knocked unconscious by Beau. No one revived Dwelma and she bled out. The Iron Shepherds put her body on one of their carts after the battle and took her with them.

Keg mentions to the Mighty Nein that Dwelma has "... a weird liking for Lorenzo." and to be ready if Lorenzo goes down first as Dwelma will become very hostile.
entities.short_description: Before the battle at Glory Run Road, Keg described Dwelma as the "creepiest and the craziest" of the Iron Shepherds, as well as "pretty gnarly" to the remaining Mighty Nein.

entities.name: Dweomer
entities.description:
is an Aeormaton who acted as a professional assistant to Laerryn Coramar-Seelie in the flying city of Avalir. As an NPC in Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Dweomer was usually present when Laerryn was working on the Astral Leywright during the final day of Avalir's existence. It was she that noticed that the four taxmen automata brought by Nydas Okiro at Laerryn's request to assist in the Leywright's testing did not bear the glyph of the Armorer Arcane. She participated in the test as well, giving instructions to the taxmen, first noticing the huge and unexpected energy drain, and discovering that the issue was not with the Leywright, but elsewhere in the Etheric Net.

Later, when an argument broke out between the members of the Ring of Brass at the Tree of Names, Dweomer entered the room as Laerryn was under a Hold Person spell cast by Nydas Okiro. Saying, "Within the confines of the Meridian Labyrinth, no harmful spells will be cast upon the Architect Arcane," Dweomer cast Disintegrate at Nydas but was Counterspelled.

Dweomer was still present when the tree was sundered and was caught in the explosion that followed. When Laerryn Dimension Doored away to safety, she was able to watch a glitching and static-filled feed still coming from Dweomer, whose body was on the ground at the foot of the tree, only partially active. Laerryn spoke through Dweomer to the fiendishly-tranformed Zerxus Ilerez, demanding he bring their dead friends back to life, but Vespin Chloras immediately hit Dweomer with a Fireball, destroying her.
entities.short_description: is an Aeormaton who acted as a professional assistant to Laerryn Coramar-Seelie in the flying city of Avalir. As an NPC in Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.description:
Father is a dwarven worshiper of the Changebringer and the contact of The Gentleman in Port Damali. The Gentleman describes him as scraggly in the face and well dressed.

entities.description: Dyamak was an ancient monk and warrior who created and wielded the Wraps of Dyamak, one of the Vestiges of Divergence. So far, they have not appeared nor been mentioned onstream.

entities.name: Dynios
entities.description:
is a mage whose soul is permanently trapped in Prism Grimpoppy's wizard spellbook, which now serves as his body. As an NPC, Dynios is played by Matthew Mercer.

Dynios is now a beautiful brown and black leather spellbook inscribed with silver runes. On its front is a "scrunched" face with only slits for eyes.

Dynios is conceited and proud, and even when sealed in a book he has an air of superiority, having a very good opinion of himself.

Dynios is a mage from the Shadowfell that was trapped in a spellbook during a rivalry. It fell into the hands of the Cobalt Soul, and was sent out with Prism to act as her chaperone while she went on her first fact-gathering assignment for the Soul.

entities.name: Eadwulf Grieve
entities.description:
Eadwulf Grieve is a human Volstrucker. He was a student of Trent Ikithon alongside Caleb Widogast and Astrid Becke. As an NPC, Eadwulf is played by Matthew Mercer.

In 819 PD, when he was approximately seventeen years old, Caleb recalled Eadwulf as having very short cropped black hair and blue eyes. He was taller than Caleb, muscular and strong, with thick black hair on his forearms and a serious look.

When they encountered each other in Trent Ikithon's laboratory at the Vergesson Sanatorium in 836 PD, Eadwulf had changed very little, being tall, wide-shouldered, with short black hair, wearing a dark piece of clothing covering most of his upper body and a stern look. He appears to be a follower of the Raven Queen, referring to her as "The Matron" and wearing a small silver pendant of a raven feather.

Eadwulf has maze-like black tattoos on his forearms and residuum crystals embedded within them, similar to those of Astrid and Owelia.
entities.short_description: Eadwulf Grieve is a human Volstrucker. He was a student of Trent Ikithon alongside Caleb Widogast and Astrid Becke. As an NPC, Eadwulf is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Eaedalus Okiro
entities.description:
Eaedalus Okiro is the Alcald of Cathmoíra, as well as the older brother of Nydas Okiro and a friend of Zerxus Ilerez. As an NPC, Eaedalus is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Eaedalus is a large and handsome human man, muscular and with a big stomach. Like his brother, he has a beard, and his is long and bushy.

In his youth Eaedalus was more realistic than Nydas, and he grew up to be a responsible and trustworthy man, able to manage stressful situations.

Eaedalus and Nydas lived part of their younger years in Cathmoíra, Domunas, where they met Zerxus Ilerez. When they were young boys they spent time in ships, while dreaming about living in floating cities such as Avalir;
