entities.name: Earot
entities.description:
is a reiloran watchman living in Kreviris. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Earot is a hunched and lanky-looking reilora.

Earot is a somewhat restless person who acts as it benefits him, having no defined loyalties. He is quite physical for a reilora, interacting directly with nearby people and objects rather than using his psychic powers.

At some point in his life Earot started working as a watchman in the Overspoke, the highest tower point in The Banners of Kreviris. According to Zhesh he had contact with both the Imperium and the Volition, but was loyal to none, always taking the side of whoever had the advantage in any conflict.
entities.short_description: is a reiloran watchman living in Kreviris. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Earth titan
entities.description:
The earth titans were gargantuan primordial entities made of stone. The Titanstone Knuckles, one of the Vestiges of Divergence, were carved from the heartstone of one of these creatures.

The titan that attacked Vasselheim during the ascension of Vecna to godhood had a gargantuan stone body hundreds of feet tall, with four 150 feet wide arms. After Vecna's defeat by Vox Machina, the titan froze where it was standing and was incorporated into the city by its inhabitants, who began creating shops and homes within its body. Chains, pulleys, and resource elevators dangled down from the body, pulling materials and people up into it, and many gardens had been created within its nooks and shelves. Snowdrops grew alongside its legs.

While Ashton was communing with the spirit of the dead primordial, he had a vision of several mountains of different sizes rising under a purple sky, forming a sort of monolithic crown around him that he felt was looking at him. He heard their voices saying, "We are the rock and stone. We are this world. [...] We've always been. Everything is cyclical."

This was one of multiple earth primordials. In its final battle, this titan was slammed into the ground violently enough to create the Zenwick Mountains and left the titan in an upright position embedded into the mountains.
entities.short_description: The earth titans were gargantuan primordial entities made of stone. The Titanstone Knuckles, one of the Vestiges of Divergence, were carved from the heartstone of one of these creatures.

entities.name: Ebecca D'Antonio
entities.description:
is the eldest daughter and heiress of a prominent family of Kahad.

Ebecca, according to Wick, seems "lovely", at least on paper.

Ebecca was born the daughter of an old man who owned lands with vineyards of special alchemical properties. She had a younger brother too, but as they grew up he renounced his claim to their land, leaving her with a very desirable inheritance.

At some point before the execution of Thjazi Fang Ebecca was betrothed to Light Priest Wicander Halovar, a union arranged by his mother Iris and his grandmother, Photarch Yanessa Halovar.
entities.short_description: is the eldest daughter and heiress of a prominent family of Kahad.

entities.name: Ebenold Kai
entities.description:
is a famous astronomer and professor at the Aydinlan Seminary in Yios.

In 843 PD, Ebenold was getting old for a halfling. He was mostly balding with wavy greying brown hair, a ruddy brown complexion, a wide nose, and a bushy chin beard.

Ebenold Kai is a well-known great astronomer, mentioned by his former associate Roe Estani in the same breath as Planerider Ryn. Estani later told Orym that Ebenold was his old friend and a retired adventurer, strongly hinting that he was also a member of Grim Verity, and gave Orym a letter of introduction to give to him if Bells Hells went to the Aydinlan Seminary in Yios. Estani suggested that he could provide assistance in bringing justice for the murders of Balan and Zeyar, the Lumas twins.

When Bells Hells reached the Seminary they learned Ebenold had cancelled his classes and disappeared a few months earlier, but a receptionist took them to his fairly modest home in a nice gated community nearby. The home seemed deserted, but after the party broke in, they found a hidden staircase leading down, surprising Ebenold and his half-elven companion Baryn Vestisho. The two used a scroll to cast Plane Shift and disappear, hotly pursued by the party. They found themselves in Planerider Ryn's study in the Elemental Plane of Fire and discovered their mutual interests in exploring the ramifications of the coming apogee solstice, the abilities of the growing number of Ruidusborn, and Otohan Thull's apparent efforts to assemble an army of the Ruidusborn in the northern Hellcatch Valley.
entities.short_description: is a famous astronomer and professor at the Aydinlan Seminary in Yios.

entities.name: Eclipse
entities.description:
Eclipse is a deva who serves the Dawnfather in the Material Plane.

Eclipse hides his celestial appearance posing as a humanoid priest.

Eclipse is extremely loyal to his god, to the point where, in his zealotry, he tries to manipulate mortals to achieve the goals he thinks would please Pelor. As Father Larkylai, he's considered an affable man.

At some point before 836 PD Eclipse arrived to Exandria and visited Bronbog, a village in Tal'Dorei with a great devotion to the Dawnfather. Using his powers, Eclipse created a humanoid persona for himself, Father Larkylai, and settled in the village, gaining a good reputation and conducting services from within the town's tavern. His main objective was to brainwash the Bronboggi to create a loyal Army of the Dawn to fight against Pelor's enemies.
entities.short_description: Eclipse is a deva who serves the Dawnfather in the Material Plane.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Edelbern Cleareyes
entities.description:
is the Master of Development on the Tal'Dorei Council as of 836 PD, having succeeded Theadorn Krazz.

Edelbern is a goliath. He is described as having "a remarkable gift of mathematical acuity" and prefers the beauty of stone towers to that of nature. He is also idealistic and dedicated to his work in restoring Tal'Dorei, which has caused him to be easily manipulated by the League of Miracles and granted them increasing power.

Edelbern belonged to the Rivermaw Herd, which absorbed the Herd of Storms in 811 PD. He grew up in Westruun during its occupation by the Herd of Storms, and this is where he discovered that he preferred architecture to nature. He used his skills in math and interest in civic architecture to help restore Westruun. During the second campaign of Critical Role, Edelbern acted as the Master of Development on the Tal'Dorei Council, having taken over the position from Theadorn Krazz. In this role, he is dedicated to restoring Emon and the rest of Tal'Dorei's cities after the devastation of the Chroma Conclave attacks. To help in this endeavor, he has added an "unprecedented" eight lieutenants to his office.

entities.name: Edmuda
entities.description:
was a reiloran enforcer for the Dominion of Cruth's disciplinary division, The Will. As an NPC, she was played by Matthew Mercer.

Edmuda was a very tall, thin female reilora, with dark, shark-like eyes..}} When encountered by Bells Hells, she was wearing tangled robes and shoulder armor that curved upward at the tips, fancy enough to denote her station with ornate metals and bones.

Edmuda was proud and "particularly cruel", and had "a terrifyingly penetrating mind."

When the Imperium doubled production quotas in the outpost of Razora, Edmuda was sent there by the Dominion of Cruth as an enforcer. She was present in the place where the Bloody Bridge touched Ruidus, and joined a caravan of supplies with several members of the Ruby Vanguard, although she didn't speak much during the days it took to reach their destination.
entities.short_description: was a reiloran enforcer for the Dominion of Cruth's disciplinary division, The Will. As an NPC, she was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Edrian Fazir
entities.description:
is the captain of the Arcane Marshals of the Revolutionary Guard. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Edrian is a potbellied older man with a white chinstrap beard. He is a nice man but does not have the soul of a hero and thus is not inclined to rock the boat..}}

The day after Thjazi Fang's execution, Edrian met Sir Harondus Einfasen who planned to reinforce the Revolutionary Guard by reassigning public resources from other offices by shutting them down, thus becoming Dol-Makjar's "security overseer" and Fazir's new superior. A few days later, he told Azune Nayar that Lord Einfasen had requested the Arcane Marshals to investigate the recent events at the Palazzo Davinos, as it appeared House Royce had reopened the doors to Faerie and kidnapped a large number of their servants and retainers when they passed through them. While Captain Fazir agreed with Azune that morale in the Guard was at an all time low, his only suggestion to combat this was to foster camaraderie by a gathering in the mead hall.

Days later, when Azune was promoted to the rank of captain by Lord Otto Einfasen, the latter mentioned that Captain Fazir's space would be given to the Azune, as his office had already been cleared.
entities.short_description: is the captain of the Arcane Marshals of the Revolutionary Guard. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Eduard
entities.description:
is a tiefling who works at the Black Swan in the Erudite quarter of Emon. As an NPC, is played by Aabria Iyengar.

Eduard is a very tall tiefling with skin that is nearly black. He has short white hair and a white goatee. He carries a handkerchief and business cards.

Eduard considers himself a good negotiator. He is very physical with other people to a degree that they find it creepy. According to Gilmore, he is indeed good at business but "falls in love easy".

Eduard approached Dariax, who was in disguise as Tharla Starr, and gave her his card, asking her if she'd be interested in performing at the Black Swan. Dariax, as Tharla, began to negotiate, aided by Fearne and Dorian, but made no commitments. Eduard then left them, disappearing into the crowd.
entities.short_description: is a tiefling who works at the Black Swan in the Erudite quarter of Emon. As an NPC, is played by Aabria Iyengar.

entities.name: Effid
entities.description:
the Fallen () is an older eisfuura who lives near Krook House. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Effid is an older male eisfuura with brown feathers, yellow eyes, and a dark beak. His arms are featherless and the joints appear strange; it seems as though they were broken at some point in the past and never healed properly. He speaks slowly in a working-class London accent.

Ashton brought the yet-to-be-named Bells Hells to Effid's cave-like home to ask some questions about the Lumas twins, The Anger, and Brumestone.

While Effid is reluctant to give up information without payment, he does seem fond of Ashton and calls him "Cracked One." Ashton, for his part, values being in Effid's good books.
entities.short_description: the Fallen () is an older eisfuura who lives near Krook House. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Efterin
entities.description:
is the former leader of a cult named the Hishari and the father of Ashton Greymoore.

Evontra'vir described Efterin as "a broken man of burning purpose" who felt they were owed something by the world because of his lifelong visions that seemed to promise greatness. He was ambitious and wanted to leave his mark in history.

In approximately 793 PD, Efterin arose as a charismatic figure in the region around the small village of Tumilo. He traveled "from town to town, displaying impressive abilities and giving sermons on the elemental spirits of old and the enduring need to restore the Primordial powers." He boasted about having received the blessing of Evontra'vir of the Gau Drashari in the Shattered Teeth, and although some people, such as Keyleth of the Air Ashari, found that hard to believe, it was true that he was given directions to a "shard of power" by Evontra'vir that created the incident that destroyed the Hishari. Evontra'vir showed him a vision of the future, including the relic he would use to usher in "a renewed ancient power" (a shard of the titan Ka'Mort) and directions to the necropolis of Toramunda where it lay.

Eventually, through his words and his charisma, he drew many followers and settled in Tumilo, renaming both it and his followers "Hishari" as a tribute to the historical druid cultures of Exandria. The village was destroyed during a mysterious ritual involving the shard which Efterin was performing with the aid of all of the villagers, including his child Ashton Greymoore and Ashton's mother.
entities.short_description: is the former leader of a cult named the Hishari and the father of Ashton Greymoore.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Eidys Dwendal
entities.description:
Prince Eidys Dwendal is the prince of the Dwendalian Empire, and the heir of his father's throne as of 835 PD.

Eidys is a skilled and physically strong man.

Eidys used to be a happy man who enjoyed an extravagant lifestyle, but he wasn't able to win his father's approval, leaving him jaded, dejected and bitter.

Eidys was born from the marriage of King Bertrand and Queen Duvia, growing up to become the sole heir to the Empire, although less politically skilled than his parents. When he reached an appropriate age he married Suria Saugiss, a member of an influential noble house in the Empire. They were expected to produce the next heir in the line of succession, but so far they have not been able to.
entities.short_description: Prince Eidys Dwendal is the prince of the Dwendalian Empire, and the heir of his father's throne as of 835 PD.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: El-Naumri
entities.description:
was a night angel who served Sylandri and became a psychopomp for the souls of elves in Aramán.

In a vision about their death, El-Naumri's body was humanoid in shape until it turned in autumn leaves.

This angel was described as a "warrior of autumn leaves" with broad wings, a sensitive figure who felt for the mortal children of the goddess of life.

In one version of the story of the origin of the Stone of Nightsong, it was said to have been carved from the rib of El-Naumri, a celestial who died of grief in the moment of the first elf's passing. When he did so, Tezumriel, another angel of Sylandri, carved the Stone from his bones. El-Naumri would not permit the soul of the young elf who died to walk into the shadow alone, and therefore became the first angel of death of the elven people, facilitating their passing into the realms beyond life.
entities.short_description: was a night angel who served Sylandri and became a psychopomp for the souls of elves in Aramán.

entities.name: Ela Lumas
entities.description:
Ginang () is the head of House Lumas, a Mahaan house in Jrusar. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Ela Lumas is a human woman in her late 50s to early 60s with russet skin. She is described as having "a calm beauty and a silent strength" and as carrying herself with weight. Each time the soon-to-be-named Bells Hells spoke with her at the Lumas estate, she was wearing a white dress and veil in mourning in a style indicating her wealth and station.

A kind but sorrowful woman, at the time of her encounter(s) with Bells Hells, Ela Lumas was still mourning the recent deaths of her twin children: Balan and Zeyar.

Ela Lumas is the head of House Lumas, a Mahaan house living the in Lucent Spire of Jrusar. As matriarch of the house, she is titled as "Ginang". She is the member of the family who largely deals with the Chandei Quorum and the other Mahaan houses, and she kept her twin children, Balan and Zeyar, away from complicated politics.
entities.short_description: Ginang () is the head of House Lumas, a Mahaan house in Jrusar. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Elaina
entities.description:
Elaina was a seamstress from Byroden and the human mother of Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia. As an NPC, she was played by Matthew Mercer.

Elaina was described as "a slender human woman with thick dark hair, kind eyes, and gentle hands."

Elaina lived the humble life of a seamstress in the village of Byroden. At some point she encountered an elven diplomat named Syldor Vessar. The details and length of their relationship are unknown, but Syldor eventually left her to return to Syngorn. Elaina later gave birth to half-elven twins and named them Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia.

Elaina and her children lived in a small house, where the twins' room doubled as Elaina's atelier. In Vax'ildan's memories, the house smelled of fabric, chalk, and candles, and his mother often worked late at night by candlelight.
entities.short_description: Elaina was a seamstress from Byroden and the human mother of Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia. As an NPC, she was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Elam Genar
entities.description:
is a middle-aged female earth genasi living in Niirdal-Poc. As an NPC, is played by Aabria Iyengar.

Elam is described as tall. She smells of damp earth, and has rocky skin.

Elam's home is heavily decorated in shades of slightly muted purples, reds, and blues, with statues, pillows, and thick rugs, and she has a dog named Googal.

Elam is extremely hospitable, welcoming in the Crown Keepers immediately after Fy'ra Rai brought them by, making them a meal, and offering them a place to stay. She is an excellent cook, but somewhat nervous of outsiders. However, she warms up to them very quickly.
entities.short_description: is a middle-aged female earth genasi living in Niirdal-Poc. As an NPC, is played by Aabria Iyengar.

entities.name: Elatis
entities.description:
is one of the Somnovem of the mutated Cognouza Ward of the city of Aeor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Elatis's appearance, age and race prior to the flight of Cognouza into the Astral Plane and its subsequent transformation are unknown.

When Lucien was getting closer to the ruins of Aeor and the Immensus Gate he started seeing the Somnovem with more mundane appearances based on the idea he had of each one of them. To him, Elatis looked like a woman with very white teeth.

Elatis was one of the nine leaders, the Somnovem, of the Aeorian neighborhood called Cognouza. In Aeor she worked in the Dawn Crucible, a place where citizens volunteered to have their dreams studied and recorded. The Somnovem led their ward to escape the destruction of Aeor by the gods and transport themselves into the Astral Sea, where they encountered a "psychic storm that wracked every mind and spirit and shattered them until they became one with their own city." "Thousands of people and the Somnovem that guided them were broken, and over time slowly reformed, powerful, the instinct of their dreams driving them, in a place where they could will their dreams to be, were their will not so fragmented."
entities.short_description: is one of the Somnovem of the mutated Cognouza Ward of the city of Aeor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Eldamir
entities.description:
was an ancient elven Archmage of the Librarium Incantatum and one of the seven of the Septarion, the council of Avalir during the Age of Arcanum. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Eldamir was an ancient elf, bowed with age. When Patia met with him on the Eve of The Replenishment, he was wearing a shimmering golden cloak with small glimmering crystals of golden light that shimmered in geometric shapes, turned into motes, and floated away. His eyes were soft and smiling and he leaned on a wooden staff that he had wielded for centuries.

Eldamir was distinguished by his talkativeness, off-target verbosity, and nostalgia, often retelling stories of his past and losing himself in memories. In truth, he did not care about the lives of others and was willing to let an untold number of civilians die as long as the Septarions were protected, himself included.

Eldamir sat on the council since the beginning of Avalir with his exceptional knowledge of the arcane, overshadowing most wizards of the city.
entities.short_description: was an ancient elven Archmage of the Librarium Incantatum and one of the seven of the Septarion, the council of Avalir during the Age of Arcanum. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Eldanwyn
entities.description:
was the high priestess of the temple of the Moonweaver in Vasselheim at the end of The Calamity. As an NPC, she was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Eldanwyn was a mature elven woman who appeared somewhat worn-looking when encountered by Rei'nia Saph and her friends, probably due to the stresses of recent events. She had beautiful but slightly unkempt long, wavy hair worn in silver and plum colored wrappings, and had bags under her eyes. She wore robes of deep plum-purple with flecks of sparkling gemstones, although with muddy tips from walking the streets of Shadowbrook.

Eldanwyn, in her long life, had wielded some of the greatest magics of the Moonweaver and could not understand what had happened to her powers during the goddess's withdrawal during the Divergence. She was frightened and worried, feeling her connection with the divine faltering and blaming herself.

Eldanwyn was a young elf at the beginning of the Calamity. During her long life spent exclusively in Vasselheim, she had seen the face of her goddess many times and felt her actual presence every time her magic was utilized.
entities.short_description: was the high priestess of the temple of the Moonweaver in Vasselheim at the end of The Calamity. As an NPC, she was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Essek Thelyss
entities.description:
is a drow wizard and a senior figure in the Kryn Dynasty. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer, who also voices him in The Mighty Nein.

Essek is a very handsome male drow who holds his head high. He has very short white hair on the sides that come up to a half curved coif to one side. His eyes are violet-blue. He wears an elaborate mantle and deep purple and black robes that almost entirely obscure his body. Under the mantle, he wears comfortable, sleek, well-trimmed Xhorhasian-styled clothing.

Essek moves in a unique way, described as gliding or drifting. His cloak falls to the floor, obscuring his feet. Although in the Mighty Nein's initial meeting with him, they heard and saw his footfalls as he moved, later Jester peeked below his cloak and saw his feet weren't touching the ground. Once, when he came to the Xhorhaus, the party scattered ball bearings on the floor, which separated out around his form like there was some invisible force pushing them outward and generating a strange force keeping them at bay. At Mythburrow, he left two grooves in the snow behind him as he moved, from his toes. At Matthew Mercer's Stockholm Comic Con panel, he clarified that Essek can walk; he simply chooses not to. Later, the party learned that Essek floats because when he was young, he used it as a means of impressing people and now it has become expected of him.

During the battle with Cree in the tunnels beneath Cognouza, Essek acquired a red eye on his right shoulder blade. He acquired four more eyes during the final battle with Lucien, one of which was on his throat. Upon Lucien's death, all five eyes on his body disappeared.
entities.short_description: is a drow wizard and a senior figure in the Kryn Dynasty. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer, who also voices him in The Mighty Nein.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Elias
entities.description:
was the half-elven son of Zerxus Ilerez, who adopted him after marrying his father, Evandrin Alterra. As an NPC, Elias was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Elias was a half-elf teenager with red hair. He looked like a younger version of his father, Evandrin. By the eve of the Calamity he looked gawky and a little awkward.

Elias was an affectionate son who, due to the grief of losing one of his parents, and the fact that the other had to live in a different city due to his job, became somehow resentful towards Zerxus, avoiding contacting him, although he regretted that decision the very same day.

Elias was the son of Evandrin Alterra, an Eldritch Knight that moved to Avalir when his son was still a baby. Shortly thereafter, he met and married Zerxus Ilerez, who fell in love with the knight and loved Elias as his own son, so the couple raised the child together.
entities.short_description: was the half-elven son of Zerxus Ilerez, who adopted him after marrying his father, Evandrin Alterra. As an NPC, Elias was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Elias de Corvo
entities.description:
is a male human and one of the most famous blood hunters in the Claret Orders.

Elias is an older human man with a graying black beard and dark gray hair tied back in a ponytail. His face and forearms are heavily scarred. He typically wears a black leather trench coat and a red scarf.

Elias is a professional and disciplined man, with little patience for weakness and imbeciles.

In Elias's career with the Claret Orders, he successfully hunted many creatures, many of which left him with scars to prove it. In his later years, Elias became more focused on training new members of the order. At some point in his career he met Vess DeRogna, an archmage of the Cerberus Assembly.
entities.short_description: is a male human and one of the most famous blood hunters in the Claret Orders.

entities.name: Elikka
entities.description:
Elikka of Stormpeak was a female cyclops historian who resided in her lair, hidden away in a mountain range in Tal'Dorei, as of 812 PD. As a historian, she was considered an oddity among her people, and it was said that her lair contained documents and treatises on the origins of the cyclops race and that she helped train new cyclops stormcallers in exchange for keeping her updated on what was going on in cyclops society.

So far, Elikka has not appeared nor been mentioned onstream.
entities.short_description: Elikka of Stormpeak was a female cyclops historian who resided in her lair, hidden away in a mountain range in Tal'Dorei, as of 812 PD. As a historian, she was considered an oddity among her people, and it was said that…

entities.name: Elle Gorgofon
entities.description:
As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Elle Gorgofon is a dark-skinned, stern-looking woman with short, ebony hair. She wears heavy plate mail and has a tower shield with a golden inlay in the center intended to mimic a polished mirror.

Gorgofon generally behaves respectfully, especially to those of higher position than her. However, she sometimes acts more forcefully, such as cutting off her superior, Lady Allura Vysoren, mid-sentence. She is a trained soldier with an honest personality. She prefers to simply hear the situation as it is rather than the politics of wordplay, which may be perceived as brash by some people. She has also shown a calm, intelligent side in dealing with the wyvern riders of Thordak's army swiftly and efficiently, despite being harried by them multiple times. She is also unquestionably brave, not even flinching at the thought of dying in a fight with Thordak and his forces.

Allura introduced Vox Machina to General Gorgofon, and Gorgofon immediately asked if Allura knew where Mikael and the rest of the regiment were. Allura informed her they were still in Syngorn. Allura then requested that they speak without guards pointing crossbows at them and Gorgofon brought them inside. Vox Machina questioned her on the state of the fort, their capacity, morale and supplies and she informed them they were low on supplies, especially food. Thankfully, they hadn't seen Thordak but they'd also received very little information from Emon since the attack. Vox Machina then informed her that all of Syngorn was in the Feywild and began planning ways to provide food for the fort. Gorgofon asked Allura if they were to be trusted and Allura assured her they were. They told her they'd already killed three members of the Chroma Conclave. They told her they had a plan and she promised that Fort Daxio would support their efforts. They did some more planning, Gorgofon informing them of the resources available to them.
entities.short_description: As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Ellia Prudaj
entities.description:
Mistress Ellia Prudaj () was a wealthy woman who lived in Jrusar, Marquet. She owned an estate in the Core Spire and a wholesale textile business called Prudaj Textiles located in the Lantern Spire.

Many years ago, she hired the mercenary Ariks Eshteross when he traveled to Jrusar from the battlefields of the Apex War, disillusioned with warfare. They became close friends, and he eventually left his mercenary life to work as her bodyguard. The two maintained an unresolved romance, never acted upon, for years. Eshteross described their friendship as having taught him "true values" beyond searching for money and opening him up to understanding how much others struggled to protect themselves from those who abuse their power. When Ellia died in 823 PD of natural causes, she left her money, estate, and business to Eshteross, who was surprised by the inheritance.

Her estate was occupied by Eshteross and Evelyn Wress, who apparently had also worked for her. Eshteross spent the next twenty years, until his death in 843 PD, keeping her memory alive by using her wealth to defend the people of Jrusar from the Ivory Syndicate and other threats.

There were rumors that Eshteross was responsible for her death. He vehemently denied it, and multiple members of Bells Hells believed he was truthful.
entities.short_description: Mistress Ellia Prudaj () was a wealthy woman who lived in Jrusar, Marquet. She owned an estate in the Core Spire and a wholesale textile business called Prudaj Textiles located in the Lantern Spire.

entities.name: Ellipides Tallbarrel
entities.description:
is a halfling wizard and the fourth dean of the Penteveral of Dol-Makjar. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

In middle-age, Ellipides was quite handsome, with a round belly. During his deanship at the Penteveral, his slightly pointed ears appeared through white curly hair and sideburns. When Murray Mag'Nesson met with him the day he was dismissed, he had bare feet and was wearing a vest and britches.

His office at the university was beautifully appointed with a massive red wood desk carved with wooden gargoyles and panther heads with grapes hanging from their mouths. To one side of it was a small staircase leading from the floor to its top, where a smaller working desk was placed for the Dean.

He had (and possibly still has) a moth familiar named Eustace who spent time hiding in his pocket.
entities.short_description: is a halfling wizard and the fourth dean of the Penteveral of Dol-Makjar. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Elmenore
entities.description:
Lady , also known as Lady Elmenore the Unforgiving, is an Archfey, the High Warqueen of the Burning Vale and the Matriarch of the Seelie Court.

Lady Elmenore is an archfey woman described as beautiful, with dark skin, strong arms, "burning" white eyes with striking golden makeup, and "tall" curly hair of orange-hued "flaming" gold. She dresses in white clothing with metallic decorations in gold tones and a forest theme, and her somewhat darker crown-headdress (which has a yellow gem in the forehead) frames her face.

When Lady Elmenore is angered, her hairline darkens as if burning, and her long, normally dark eyebrows become golden flames.

During the Age of Arcanum, Lady Elmenore was a responsible archfey, concerned for all members of her court, taking whatever steps were necessary to bring them to safety. She was also selfless, willing to suffer if it prevented her from breaking another person's heart.
entities.short_description: Lady , also known as Lady Elmenore the Unforgiving, is an Archfey, the High Warqueen of the Burning Vale and the Matriarch of the Seelie Court.

entities.name: Elodie D'vyen
entities.description:
is a rich merchant and one of the partners of Halandil Fang. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Elodie is a beautiful human woman in her early forties. She dresses in expensive clothes made of rich imported fabric.

Elodie was born in a respectable family from outside of Dol-Makjar. At some point in the last two decades, she began a relationship with the bard Halandil Fang; when they started dating, her grandmother warned her that she should have an answer ready for whenever her actor boyfriend inevitably asked her for money. the couple had a daughter together, Hero. The same year the baby was born Elodie was living with Hal and his two children with Thaisha in the Rookery; back then the relationship was so happy that a wedding was being considered, and Elodie was starting a business in fabrics.

As of the year 71, Elodie had become a rich merchant and lived with her daughter (who was also involved in the business), although still being in a relationship with Hal and in contact with his relatives despite no longer planning to marry him, nor living with him.
entities.short_description: is a rich merchant and one of the partners of Halandil Fang. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Elowen Brist
entities.description:
In , Elowen was described as having tightly-braided reddish hair, with streaks of gray along the sides. When Vox Machina met her a year before, she didn't have the gray streaks, so the trauma with the Dread Emperor kidnapping her son might have taken its toll on her body.

Elowen inherited the Softsky Bakery in Westruun from her family. As its sole employee, she lived a modest life with her son, Simon.

When Simon went missing for a few weeks, Elowen asked Vox Machina to help find him. Vox Machina found and defeated the Dread Emperor, who had kidnapped children from across Tal'Dorei. The party returned most of the missing children to their families, reuniting Simon and Elowen.

Vox Machina travelled from Westruun to the Frostweald in mist form, when they noticed a refugee camp from overhead. When they landed and investigated, Vax'ildan and Vex'ahlia noticed Elowen and her son, Simon, instantly recognizing them from their quest to rescue the children from the Dread Emperor.
entities.short_description: In , Elowen was described as having tightly-braided reddish hair, with streaks of gray along the sides. When Vox Machina met her a year before, she didn't have the gray streaks, so the trauma with the Dread Emperor…

entities.name: Elric Tavelle
entities.description:
was the eldest son of a family of performers of the Greying Wildlands, and the older brother of Lucien Tavelle.

The last memories Lucien had of him were of Elric stiff and ever-smiling, with jet-black eyes that twinkled eyes like beads, always followed by the smell of new shoes.

Elric was a cheerful and helpful boy with a good memory, enthusiastic about his work.

Elric was born at some point before 810 PD as the first son of a married couple of the Greying Wildlands. He had an younger brother, Lucien, and a younger sister, Aldreda. Their parents were artists who usually played music while their children danced, sang or performed plays; Elric was the best performer of all of them, he always remembered his line, and was generally seen as the favorite. However, he had abusive parents who, despite their predilection for him, harshly punished him when they were disappointed, being his younger siblings the ones who consoled him, while they tried to protect themselves from their patents' wrath.
entities.short_description: was the eldest son of a family of performers of the Greying Wildlands, and the older brother of Lucien Tavelle.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Elwend
entities.description:
, the King of Faerie, was the fey ruler of Tír Cruthú.

In the past the King of Faerie had influence over the forests.

The Shaper of Life married Elwend and that, combined with her position as a goddess of the woodlands, made her feel like she knew better than druids and followers of the Old Path, who tried to understand and influence nature without her. The souls of dead elves were sent to the Garden of the Spirit, which was in the land of the King of Faerie.
entities.short_description: , the King of Faerie, was the fey ruler of Tír Cruthú.

entities.name: Emmett
entities.description:
was one of the ogres from the group that attacked Mighty Nein on their way to Berleben. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Category:Articles needing appearance verification
entities.short_description: was one of the ogres from the group that attacked Mighty Nein on their way to Berleben. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Emoth Kade
entities.description:
() is a half-elf noblewoman of Jrusar. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Emoth is pale and very thin. Her hair is dark and very curly and voluminous. When she first appeared, she wore a long gray dress with a train.

After the transformation, her body lost some reproductive features, and breathing holes opened in her back and her shoulders.

After her complete transformation, Imogen Temult could sense a lot of feral anger and a strong devotion to the Shade Mother.
entities.short_description: () is a half-elf noblewoman of Jrusar. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Enmity
entities.description:
is a demon aspirant in the Candescent Creed, and one of the three sisters of Tyranny. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Enmity is extremely tall, with deep speckled red and black skin like lava congealing into stone. She wears very bright white priestly garb, and her horns are curled and ram-like.

Enmity appears to be the leader among the three, frequently being the one to give orders and make the final decision.

Enmity was present at the execution of Thjazi Fang, accompanying Wicander Halovar's father Godard Halovar, and greeted Tyranny. The next day, at the Villa Aurora, Tyranny met all three of her sisters again. Enmity asked if Wicander had acquitted himself well at the funeral. After telling her to "Remember where you are from, and what you are," the sisters moved on to other, more important activities.
entities.short_description: is a demon aspirant in the Candescent Creed, and one of the three sisters of Tyranny. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Enon Brinjay
entities.description:
was a human man in his mid-80s who was the first known victim of Kylre. As an NPC, Enon was played by Matthew Mercer.

When he was human, Enon was visibly elderly and somewhat frail.

After he died, Enon's body grew slightly in size and skin and muscles fell away, leaving a shambling set of bones and organs that attacked without much visible intelligence.

Enon was known for occasionally helping out at the docks, despite retiring years beforehand. Though many people knew him, none of them were that fond of him after he died. He was said to be lonely, having a son who had gotten married and moved up north some thirty-five years ago leaving him behind.
entities.short_description: was a human man in his mid-80s who was the first known victim of Kylre. As an NPC, Enon was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Ephina Parviras
entities.description:
, also known as Effie, is one of the local representatives of the Revolutionary Council of Dol-Makjar. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

She occupies the seat reserved for the orcish Horn Clan and was the first human elected to the Council from the city. Her seat represents the Dol-Makjar districts of Rozigar, Caravan Hill, The Embers, Rubblecliff, and The Fray.

Effie is a tough, wiry, but very small human woman with some silver in her teeth. She is a brass tacks, bare-knuckle, "get it done" person. Off-Balance Cooldown|7:05|Off-Balance}}

Effie is the owner and former tavern keeper at the Napping Tabby tavern. She was elected around the year 63 defending the idea that the Revolutionary Council wasn't doing enough to house people and help the poor, something that made her popular in Caravan Hill but caused the more conservative orcs of the city to feel like she was criticizing the work her predecessors had done. Effie fought for the immigrants and refugees of Dol-Makjar, but her inexperience slowly turned public sentiment against her.
entities.short_description: , also known as Effie, is one of the local representatives of the Revolutionary Council of Dol-Makjar. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Ephred
entities.description:
() is an elf pastry baker of Jrusar known as the Shadow Baker. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Ephred is an elf. He is tall, handsome, and in his thirties; he has dark skin, deep brown eyes, a shaven head, and is described as looking very similar to Lance Reddick. He wears a heavy, gray, patterned woolen cloak across his shoulders.

Ephred has an intense presence; he is described as giving off the impression of being a "powerful creature". He has the charisma of a charming salesman but also maintains a mysterious demeanor. He speaks in a deep voice with a Marquesian accent.

The Shadow Baker regularly sells his "colorful, wonderful-smelling baked goods" at Elder's Post. He keeps them hidden in pouches under his cloak like a seller of contraband, and his true intentions are unclear. Ephred describes himself as a "curator of fine pastries", and says that he does not wish to become a renowned baker but bakes only for "those that need what I have to offer." Amongst his wares are sold a blackberry citrus cinnamon roll with purple and orange icing and purple sprinkles and a bright pink bear claw. He harbors a disdain for pies. Yash Mangal refers to his baked goods as "phantom pastries".
entities.short_description: () is an elf pastry baker of Jrusar known as the Shadow Baker. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Erad Fuckfork
entities.description:
Erad Fuckfork is a member of a Crawler gang and a driver in the Deathwish Run on 16 Sydenstar, 843 PD.

At some point prior to Bells Hells arriving in Bassuras, Erad joined a Crawler gang.

Erad was arguing loudly with another driver before the Deathwish Run.

Category:Articles with verified appearances Category:Bassuras
entities.short_description: Erad Fuckfork is a member of a Crawler gang and a driver in the Deathwish Run on 16 Sydenstar, 843 PD.

entities.name: Ereldra Icozrin
entities.description:
Ereldra Icozrin is a talented harpist of Den Icozrin in the Kryn Dynasty and member of the Children of Malice in 835 PD.

Ereldra was devastated after their family drama, being manipulated to the point of completely changing their ideology and faith through the influence of the Spider Queen.

Ereldra was born as a member of Den Icozrin in the Kryn Dynasty, and growing up worshiping The Luxon. At some point they discovered their talent for music, becoming an acclaimed harpist throughout Rosohna. As an adult, Ereldra fell in love with a woman, and they intended to marry. However, the day of the ceremony was sabotaged by Ereldra's brother, causing them great pain. Lolth took advantage of Ereldra's despair and manipulated them, alienating them from the cult of The Light and affiliating them with her own cause, turning them into a spy for the Children of Malice.

By 835 PD, Ereldra uses their fame as a musician to move through different social circles, spreading rumors and lies that weaken the social foundation of the Dens.
entities.short_description: Ereldra Icozrin is a talented harpist of Den Icozrin in the Kryn Dynasty and member of the Children of Malice in 835 PD.

entities.name: Eric
entities.description:
was the bee companion of the bard Capo. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Eric does not lose his stinger and die after stinging a foe, making him in all likelihood a bumblebee.

Category:Non-player characters Category:Companions Category:Dead Characters Category:Beasts Category:Articles with verified appearances
entities.short_description: was the bee companion of the bard Capo. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Erlich Kerzingblad
entities.description:
Sir is a knight from a vassal house under House Einfasen.

Despite having had some embarrassing moments in public in the past, his reputation and behavior were good and noble enough for Lord Otto Einfasen to praise him and to consider it normal for him to unexpectedly help a fellow knight on a journey.

Erlich was born in a noble house and became a knight in service of House Einfasen. Eventually he joined the Barrowguard, and was meant to establish it in the north. In the year 63 or 64 after the Shapers' War he attended a ball in Dol-Makjar in which he got drunk and made a fool of himself in front of House Halovar.

As of the year 71, days after the execution of Thjazi Fang, Sir Erlich was supposed to be in Equilaine.
entities.short_description: Sir is a knight from a vassal house under House Einfasen.

entities.name: Errevon
entities.description:
Two years after the end of the Scattered War, Errevon and his elemental army invaded Tal'Dorei from the Frostfell, the Elemental Plane of Ice, via a portal in the forest now called the Frostweald. Skysunder, Herald of the Rimelord, was a white dragon who had been sealed within the Frostfell. At some time prior to or concurrent with the Scattered War, Skysunder began acting as a scout to Errevon in order to find the weakest points between the planes. It was with her help that, two years into the reign of Sovereign Zan Tal'Dorei in the new Tal'Dorei Empire, Errevon opened a portal in the forest now known as the Frostweald and plunged Tal'Dorei into a perpetual winter known as the Icelost Years. Errevon then constructed a citadel of ice in the Foramere Basin.

After several years, the Tal'Dorei Council was finally able to convince both Syngorn and Kraghammer—who had been on opposing sides in the Scattered War—to ally with them and fight back the invasion. Together, the peoples of Tal'Dorei and with Ashari druids of Zephrah were able to push Errevon and his servants back into the Frostfell. The Ashari permanently closed the rift between planes, and the storm then quickly subsided, leaving some weaker spirits as the only remains of the Rimelord's army.
entities.short_description: Two years after the end of the Scattered War, Errevon and his elemental army invaded Tal'Dorei from the Frostfell, the Elemental Plane of Ice, via a portal in the forest now called the Frostweald. Skysunder, Herald of…

entities.name: Erwen Dastell
entities.description:
Erwen Dastell is the butler in charge of Greyskull Keep. He handles guest arrivals, cleaning (alongside Laina Yor), payroll, and supplies. As an NPC, he is portrayed by Matthew Mercer.

Erwen has ruddy skin, wears his grey hair in a ponytail, and is clean-shaven. He wears small spectacles across his nose and has a lanky physique.

Erwen greeted Vox Machina as they returned to Greyskull Keep following their adventure in the Underdark, saying he was excited to see them. He shouted for Laina to make some food, but she quickly responded that she was already doing so. Scanlan asked if there had been any visitors or mail, to which Erwen replied that Allura had visited several days prior, and there were no packages or letters for anyone. After this he returned to his quarters.

Vox Machina once again got back from adventuring to have a moment of peace at home. However, the group was missing Pike, who was still working on the temple of Sarenrae. As Vox Machina raised their glasses to her, Erwen entered to say that the meal was ready.
entities.short_description: Erwen Dastell is the butler in charge of Greyskull Keep. He handles guest arrivals, cleaning (alongside Laina Yor), payroll, and supplies. As an NPC, he is portrayed by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Eryn Loathroot
entities.description:
was a teenaged dwarf living on a farmstead in the settlement of Desperloch with her father Garrick. As an NPC, she was played by Matthew Mercer.

Eryn was a dwarven teenage girl with curly dirty-blonde hair who wore a leather breastplate and a tattered cloak.

When she was corrupted by the Umbra, her eyes turned pale, her skin green, and she sprouted tentacles covered in fingers as her mouth developed red tethers and pincers. The transformation reverted for the most part after the monster was defeated, but even her original body retained some marks of the corruption, particularly around the mouth.

She was cheerful and youthfully arrogant, behaving recklessly when it favored her own ambitions, but was loved and appreciated by her neighbors nonetheless.
entities.short_description: was a teenaged dwarf living on a farmstead in the settlement of Desperloch with her father Garrick. As an NPC, she was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Erythiona and Viracheios
entities.description:
Erythiona and Viracheios are two members of the coven of Isharnai, the Prism Sage.

Erythiona was an old woman of fey elven features, with burning red eyes, bull-like horns framed by vibrant orange hair, and numerous tattoos. She wore an armor made of leather and leaves.

Viracheios was a frail and corpse-like woman with long white hair and pale skin and eyes, surrounded by cold, pale energy. She wore a tight shroud-like dress without sleeves.

During their imprisonment each of the witches had a different attitude, with Erythiona being critical and Viracheios being more contemptuous.
entities.short_description: Erythiona and Viracheios are two members of the coven of Isharnai, the Prism Sage.

entities.name: Eselmyr
entities.description:
Eselmyr is a singer in Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe. As an NPC, Eselmyr is played by Matthew Mercer.

Eselmyr is a half-elven woman in her later years. She keeps her hair tied back into a very tight bun.

Eselmyr was singing a song as part of Dr. Dranzel's troupe when Vox Machina ran into them at the Diamond Nest Tavern in Emon.

Eselmyr was with the rest of Dr. Dranzel's troupe when Vox Machina met them at Greyskull Keep. She was mentioned by name for the first (and only) time in this episode.
entities.short_description: Eselmyr is a singer in Dr. Dranzel's Spectacular Traveling Troupe. As an NPC, Eselmyr is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Eskil Ryndarien
entities.description:
Realmseer Eskil Ryndarien is one of the most powerful arcane practitioners in Tal'Dorei. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Eskil is an older human man with round spectacles and a fringe of white hair around his balding top.

Eskil is grumpy, self-important, and unpersonable. Vex once called him a "crotchety old fuck." He usually does as he's asked in the end, but complains often and considers most tasks beneath him.

Eskil once worked within the circle of mages known as the Arcana Pansophical, serving as a Maker, but retired due to frustrations with the political aspects. Until the Chroma Conclave attacked, Eskil lived in Westruun atop his ominous Greystone Tower, attended by his manservant Jekt Wince.
entities.short_description: Realmseer Eskil Ryndarien is one of the most powerful arcane practitioners in Tal'Dorei. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Esmer Balenta
entities.description:
is an explosives manufacturer, operating a black powder business from Finders Takers in Bassuras. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Esmer is a tall, slender, gorgeous woman with jet-black skin and white, almost bleached hair that's parted in the center that goes just past the chin. When Bells Hells first met her, she was clad in a dirty white work shirt and a dark purple-red thick leather vest that cut off mid-torso. She also wore a thick pair of goggles with multiple relatively intricate lenses.

Esmer owns and operates the Finders Takers shop in the East Dregs of Bassuras, and manufactures black powder, firearms, and dynamite. Dancer had frequently sent F.C.G. to Esmer's shop. Esmer had also been dating Dancer, and had last seen her in mid-Brussendar, 843 PD, about a month before meeting Bells Hells.

Accompanied by Dusk and Fearne, who sought supplies to infiltrate the Seat of Disdain, Fresh Cut Grass went to see Esmer to tell her the news of Dancer's death. Esmer was surprised to see FCG and asked if Dancer sent them. FCG tried to gently tell her Dancer was brutally murdered a few months ago, but Esmer spat out her wine and told them they were lying, that was impossible. Dancer came alone to the shop a month ago trying to reconnect with Esmer, and Esmer bought her sad stories and let her stay for a few days. But when things got "a little too intimate", Dancer vanished again. Esmer thought she was probably at The Ends.
entities.short_description: is an explosives manufacturer, operating a black powder business from Finders Takers in Bassuras. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Estella Ladimar
entities.description:
Estella Ladimar was the headmistress of Westhall Academy in Westruun, Tal'Dorei and a descendant of the heroic wizard Atz Yuminor. As headmistress, she supported the Scions of Yuminor and helps guard the Astural Scrolls.

So far, Estella Ladimar has not appeared nor been mentioned onstream.
entities.short_description: Estella Ladimar was the headmistress of Westhall Academy in Westruun, Tal'Dorei and a descendant of the heroic wizard Atz Yuminor. As headmistress, she supported the Scions of Yuminor and helps guard the Astural Scrolls.

entities.name: Ethrand Tachonis
entities.description:
is the brother of Occtis Tachonis. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Ethrand looks like "the most normal" of the Tachonis. He is somewhat muscular, has black hair swept back and frequently wears a vest with bare arms and a cloak. He is described as "severe, petulant, and angry.".}}

Ethrand was born as one of the younger children of Lord Primus Tachonis. As other members of his lineage, he manifested sorcerous abilities at a very young age, and as of the year 59, when he and his family traveled to the Golden Orchard to attend the trial of Thjazi Fang, he stayed behind to tease his youngest brother, Occtis, for not having magic yet. He even threw a stone at him, but that attracted the attention of two of the local pixies, who scared Ethrand away after one of them assured him she had killed members of his family in the Falconer's Rebellion.

Ethrand was in command of a group of six ghouls who appeared at the Palazzo Davinos during a strike that killed Raimond Davinos, the father of Julien. He appeared at the doorway of the room which Aranessa Royce had given to Occtis Tachonis for the night, casting Silence while holding the Stone of Nightsong. He commanded the ghouls: "Put him on the table, open him up and we'll put the stone where it belongs." During the ensuing battle, Ethrand wielded a knife to slice open the pinioned Occtis, reach into his chest, and replace his beating heart with the Stone of Nightsong, as he declared that his brother had always had something wrong with him, and that he should have embraced the gift of their name. After commanding his ghouls to defenestrate Lady Aranessa (something they failed to do) Ethrand moved away with the heart, and when his father got confirmation that he had it, he Shadow Walked to him and Plane Shifted them both away from the battle between the defenders of House Davinos and the horde of summoned undead. He, however, visited the Palazzo again hours later, when Ophelia Seremai was supervising the preparations to clean the place and make it presentable for the Royce gala.
entities.short_description: is the brother of Occtis Tachonis. As an NPC, he is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Evandrin Alterra
entities.description:
was the half-elven First Knight of the flying city of Avalir and the husband of Zerxus Ilerez. As an NPC, Evandrin was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

Evandrin was a half-elf standing about 5'10" with straight red shoulder-length hair. He looked like a mature version of his son, Elias.

After being banished from Exandria and trapped in the Astral Sea, his body became one made of starlight, similar to amethyst, liquid glass, but still palpable..}}

During the meeting with the Ring of Brass in the Palazzo Por'co, Zerxus expressed his distress with his tormenting dreams, which, as he observed himself, led to his poorly performed duties. According to Zerxus, Evandrin would have handled them with a lot more grace.
entities.short_description: was the half-elven First Knight of the flying city of Avalir and the husband of Zerxus Ilerez. As an NPC, Evandrin was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.

entities.name: Evelyn Wress
entities.description:
() is the elven caretaker of Lord Ariks Eshteross at his estate in Jrusar. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Evelyn is a middle-aged elven woman, with light auburn hair that is lighter near her temples. When first encountered by the group later named Bells Hells, she was wearing a shawl and a simple but well-made dress of black and silver.

Evelyn appears attentive to Lord Eshteross and understands intuitively (or from experience) what he wants from her at any given moment. When Bertrand Bell and the newly gathered party arrived unexpectedly, she obtained permission from Lord Eshteross to admit them, escorted them to his room, then left at his nod, locking the door behind her.

Lord Eshteross met Evelyn after he retired from his mercenary career.
entities.short_description: () is the elven caretaker of Lord Ariks Eshteross at his estate in Jrusar. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Everard Dwendal
entities.description:
was king of the Dwendalian Empire immediately preceding Bertrand Dwendal.

He notably relaxed some of the rigid imperial laws limiting freedom of speech that had been in place for generations. However, some political figures took advantage of this and gathered large followings of potential rebels, and King Everard became concerned that they could gather sufficient power to challenge the crown. He founded the Augen Trust, a spy network that could secretly corrupt these politicians through bribery or the uncovering of unsavory secrets, as well as influence the population via propaganda. As of 835 PD, his laws remained in place, but his successor, Bertrand Dwendal, was considering a return to the previous state of affairs.

Category:Kings of the Dwendalian Empire Category:Dwendal family
entities.short_description: was king of the Dwendalian Empire immediately preceding Bertrand Dwendal.

entities.name: Evithorir
entities.description:
the Taker was a dark fey creature entity once sealed beneath Cofferfall Hill in Issylra. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Evithorir is a creature of shadows, appearing as a massive column with a grinning face at its tip. The face is pale gray and pointed, pulled tight against what would be cheekbones, with sunken sockets holding palely glowing blue eyes. They have elongated, crooked and cracked teeth meeting at the center. From the shadowy, hooded depths of their form, the smiling face emerges like a mask from the front that they were able to move through their whole body. In their vicinity, the air seems to grow colder.

A long time ago Evithorir acted in Issylra as a thief of essence and natural magic. They became the enemy of Oma-Dua, a powerful Gau Drashari who fought against them and eventually managed to seal them beneath the rock of Cofferfall Hill, although she was weakened by the Taker's mortal curse which would affect her for the rest of her days.

Centuries later, in 843 PD, the powerful magic of the apogee solstice disturbed the enchantment in Evithorir's imprisonment, freeing them. They traveled to the shrine of the Emerald Tree in the Irriam Canyon, attracted by the power of their old enemy; there, they killed three of the local guardians (Ennorai, Oldaan and Keese), leaving only their bones, and consumed the archdruid Hevestro.
entities.short_description: the Taker was a dark fey creature entity once sealed beneath Cofferfall Hill in Issylra. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Evodon Leeds
entities.description:
is an older human working as one of the Keepers of the Light above Sanctum in Uthodurn. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Evodon has short gray hair, dark skin, and a trimmed beard. His eyes and smile are kind. When Deanna Leimert met with him just after the Apogee Solstice, he seemed nervous and concerned, and was shooing worshippers away.

Although others were not being permitted within the temple following the disruption to magic caused by the solstice, Elder Leeds greeted Deanna familiarly, and referred to her being "the bearer of the miracle" of some of the great deities, presumably referring to her resurrected status. He confessed that his connection with the Dawnfather, in some respects, had been severed, but that he was now convinced the temple should remain open. Deanna gave him 500 gold and noticed as she left he was urging the people waiting outside to enter.
entities.short_description: is an older human working as one of the Keepers of the Light above Sanctum in Uthodurn. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Evon Hytroga
entities.description:
is the proprietor of the Twilight Mirror Museum. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Evon is an older male half-elf. He is tall and very thin, and is described as "spider-like". When Bells Hells first met him, he wore a red and gold mantle with a raised area behind his neck that came to points past his shoulders. Below the mantle, he wore a silver robe and a considerable amount of jewelry. His hair was worn in well-kept sideburns which were going gray, and he had a pencil mustache extending down into a thin horseshoe mustache. His eyebrows were thick and pointed up at the outer edges.

Evon claimed to have spent most of his youth with the Wanderman Assembly, where he earned his fortune, and then spent seven years studying under Prefect Thoshai in Vasselheim. He also claimed to have been a close personal friend of Uriel Tal'Dorei III and to have been present when Uriel died.

Evon Hytroga owned and ran the Twilight Mirror Museum, an "oddities collection" in Heartmoor Hamlet. At some point he developed a rivalry with Jiana Hexum, and since the failed break-in of Hexum Manor by the Nobodies, had bragged about his highly advanced security. Jiana challenged him to a wager: that if she could hire a team to successfully breach his security measures and steal an item of his choosing from the museum, she would win, and he would attempt the same against her manor.
entities.short_description: is the proprietor of the Twilight Mirror Museum. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Evontra'vir
entities.description:
Evontra'vir, also known as the Great Tree of Atrophy, was a powerful Gau Drashari of Toramunda who became a tree spirit in the Shattered Teeth. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.

Evontra'vir looks like a massive tree of maroon-red bark, with weird thin branches full of black leaves and dangling vines, a stocky trunk, and long roots spreading in every direction, with skulls and miscellaneous items between them. When he is conscious, a heavily stretched face appears in the bark as if carved, with a big mouth and two milky white eyes.

The area surrounding the tree is a sinkhole of darkness among three mountains. The Great Tree itself is said to be rooted between realms, a window between life and death. Its nature draws undead shadow creatures toward it that inhabit the island and emerge at nightfall, causing necrotic damage to the living.

A long time ago Evontra'vir, a member of the Gau Drashari, became an archdruid, creating deep bonds with the forces of nature. He was one of the protectors of Toramunda who was present when Imyr Por'co convinced the druids there to allow Mount Ygora to be divided into the flying city of Avalir and the terrestrial Cathmoíra, before the catastrophic explosion that destroyed Domunas and created the Shattered Teeth at the beginning of the Calamity.
entities.short_description: Evontra'vir, also known as the Great Tree of Atrophy, was a powerful Gau Drashari of Toramunda who became a tree spirit in the Shattered Teeth. As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer.
entities.image_credit: Fair-use identification thumbnail via Fandom. Critical Role art © Critical Role (as applicable). Not free or redistributable artwork.

entities.name: Evoroa
entities.description:
https://bsky.app/profile/ariadne-mouse.bsky.social/post/3l2ydbqxnu22d}}

is a bormodo scientist and a Volition ally and spy. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Like other bormodos, Evoroa has a squat figure, with one set of long, muscular arms and a second set of shorter arms with smaller hands. Her head is set between broad, rounded shoulders, such that it was unclear whether she had a neck. She has a wide, pulled-back mouth. She also has, characteristic of bormodos, dark eyes and a nose that is little more than a bump with slits.

Evoroa was a scientist of the Colloquium of Candescense. In 843 PD, when Ludinus Da'leth and his Ruby Vanguard arrived on Ruidus, Evoroa began doing research on the strange technology the Exandrians had brought with them, sharing that information with the Volition. The last the Volition had heard from her, she and others were working on a device and/or weapon specifically for Ludinus. However, she was suddenly abducted by forces of the Imperium, and her cytaa Gona believed she had been taken beneath the Engineering Bay.
entities.short_description: https://bsky.app/profile/ariadne-mouse.bsky.social/post/3l2ydbqxnu22d}}

entities.name: Exalting Blade of Favor
entities.description:
The is a plus six legendary, sentient sword that allows its wielder to resist fire and lightning damage and upon purchase deals 1d10 plus five radiant damage. As Capo walked down a dark pathway, he wished that the sword would begin to emit light, which it promptly accomplished.

The Exalting Blade of Favor has gold and silver inlay with an intricate hilt. When worn in combination with the Crimson Sphere of Generosity, its surge of generosity is doubled.

In the distant past, the sword was wielded by a great hero, Shiona, who defeated Zathkira the Mad but vanished in his underground laboratory, along with his sword.

entities.name: Extovass
entities.description:
Extovass the Gluttonous was a nalfeshnee demon and a servant of Vrudauliun. As an NPC, Extovass was played by Matthew Mercer.

Extovass had a corpulent, dark-furred body standing about 13 feet tall, with massive, long-clawed arms, a wide jaw held in an ape-like grimace exposing massive tusks and teeth, small furry wings, and tiny legs that caused it to walk with an awkward gait.

Bells Hells encountered Extovass at the Iridon Bastion in the Grey Valley of Tal'Dorei, where he was planning to celebrate a feast after having taken the fort from the followers of Bahamut. He had taken several prisoners, and intended to use them (either as food or as sacrifices) and bring more fiendish forces to that place.

The demon succeeded in knocking Imogen Temult unconscious but was driven away and killed by Fearne Calloway shortly thereafter. The rescued prisoners told the party Extovass's name and said that he had yielded himself to a demon prince named Vrudauliun.
entities.short_description: Extovass the Gluttonous was a nalfeshnee demon and a servant of Vrudauliun. As an NPC, Extovass was played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Eye of the Storm
entities.description:
Eyvindr, better know to his cyclops followers as the Eye of the Storm, is a storm giant who is posing as an ancient cyclops avatar of the Stormlord, gathering battalions of followers to carry out revenge on the Council of Seven Scepters.

According to legend, an ancient cyclops gave her only eye in exchange for the power of the storm, becoming the first stormcaller, and came to be known as the Eye of the Storm. It is said that anywhere there is a storm, she can observe the elements as if it were through her own eyes.

In truth, the Eye of the Storm is a vengeful storm giant named Eyvindr, who is posing as a demigod and intent on raising an army to exact retribution on the Council of Seven Scepters. His plan is to conceal his true identity until he believes that his control over the stormcallers is absolute.

Between 812 and 836 PD, a secretive group of stormcallers were active in the Daggerbay Mountains, where they gathered in an old elven temple called the Skyneedle and conducted communal rituals to connect with the entity, who incrementally increased their power.

entities.name: Faeryn Stormwind
entities.description:
Faeryn Stormwind is a silver dragonborn monk and Tiberius Stormwind's brother. Orion Acaba played him in a different campaign concurrently with the Vox Machina campaign.

Faeryn hails from Tyriex, Draconia. He speaks Common, Draconic, and Dwarvish. He comes from a very political family. He is an Open Hand monk. His personality is respectful but impatient, and he likes to do things his own way.

Category:Monks Category:Draconians Category:Draconbloods

entities.name: Fanny Z
entities.description:
is a clothier in Zephrah played by Matthew Mercer.

Fanny's small shop looked almost like a gazebo, with filigreed glass sides and a pointed dome, and was filled with interesting fabrics, leather, and natural objects such as leaves and vines. Fanny was a young woman described as "uniquely" made-up in a spray of color resembling "gorgeous drag", and wore a beehive hairdo.

Fanny greeted Ashton warmly, but he could only rather incoherently describe the vibe he was searching for in his new outfit, which he wanted to reflect his new goal of trying to help and inspire people. She asked for something beyond just an aesthetic, and he gave her some potential samples he had stolen somewhere. She suggested an "antihero chic" look, and they settled on "legendary hero but make it fashion." He trusted her to create it without his approval. The clothing was to be ready in a few days, but she managed to finish it sooner, since it was almost finished the following morning. While she was busy with the last details of the outfit, she complimented Ashton by telling them that, since some of their notes for the clothing design had been so specific, they probably knew who they wanted to be better than they realized.
entities.short_description: is a clothier in Zephrah played by Matthew Mercer.

entities.name: Faramore
entities.description:
is a former employer of Imogen Temult living in Gelvaan.

Faramore wore lots of jewelry with crests and insignias to show who he was.

Faramore was first mentioned when Imogen Temult pretended to be working on his behalf to gain an audience with Vali Dertrana Later, while mind-melding with Fresh Cut Grass Imogen had memories of growing up, rearing and raising horses, and dealing with the frustrations of working in farm pastures under Master Faramore. He apparently was involved in creating new breeds of horses which he sold to travelers passing through Gelvaan. Imogen later described him as one of the most powerful men in town with a lot of businesses around Marquet. She and her father ran his stables in Gelvaan.

Master Faramore became the owner of Imogen's favorite mare, Flora, when Imogen left Gelvaan with Laudna. After the events of Campaign Three, the pair returned to the area and Imogen attempted to purchase Flora from him. Master Faramore had heard of Imogen's fame and happily agreed to sell her the horse if she would sign off on a memoir he had written about everything he had taught her. After Laudna succeeded in frightening and intimidating him, he gave Flora to Imogen free of charge.
entities.short_description: is a former employer of Imogen Temult living in Gelvaan.

entities.name: Faril
entities.description:
The Legend of Vox Machina: The Whitestone Chronicles: Ripley

is a dwarven miner, formerly from Jorenn Village, and a member of the group led by Thorn.

Faril is a dwarven man with brown hair. After Tinyn's death, he began wearing her glasses, which are too big for him, on a chain around his neck. His voice is described as "musical".

According to Thorn, Faril is afraid of ghosts and "has an eye for code". When Vax'ildan first saw him, he noted that Faril walked "with a bounce in his step." In the aftermath of Tinyn's death, Faril was much more serious, spoke little, and, despite previously being a noncombatant, was willing to attempt to free the captured miners on his own, and to stand his ground alongside Thorn. He took up a leadership position among the miners when they were released from jail.

entities.name: Fassbender
entities.description:
Fassbender is a stone golem which could be controlled by the circlet that Vox Machina was asked to retrieve from Westruun, which was under Umbrasyl's control at the time. As an NPC, Fassbender is played by Matthew Mercer.

The name "Fassbender" was given to it by Scanlan. Vex'ahlia suggested naming him Spike.

Fassbender is a twelve-foot-tall humanoid golem built of solid stone. The arms are giant and piston-like and the legs are like tree trunks. Vax'ildan drew a mustache and pointy goatee onto its face, which Keyleth later made permanent with her Stone Shape spell.

Fassbender was originally created by Master Quall, along with the Circlet of Golem Control. When he retrieved items from his house, he forgot to bring the circlet, so he tasked Vox Machina with retrieving it.

entities.name: Fastidan
entities.description:
is one of the Somnovem of the mutated Cognouza Ward of the city of Aeor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.

Fastidan's appearance, age and race prior to the flight of Cognouza into the Astral Plane and its subsequent transformation are unknown.

When Lucien was getting closer to the ruins of Aeor and the Immensus Gate he started seeing the Somnovem with more mundane appearances based on the idea he had of each one of them. To him, Fastidan looked like a man whose beard was golden and shot through with gray; he stood taller than the rest of the Somnovem.

Fastidan was one of the nine leaders, the Somnovem, of the Aeorian neighborhood called Cognouza. In Aeor, despite being at odds with members of the Convocation, he managed to win their respect and receive funds over several years to finance his projects, which included excavating, polishing and constructing threshold crests. He used slaves for such tasks. The Somnovem led the ward to escape the destruction of Aeor by the gods and transport themselves into the Astral Sea, where they encountered a "psychic storm that wracked every mind and spirit and shattered them until they became one with their own city." "Thousands of people and the Somnovem that guided them were broken, and over time slowly reformed, powerful, the instinct of their dreams driving them, in a place where they could will their dreams to be, were their will not so fragmented."

entities.name: Febron Keyes
entities.description:
was an employee of The Gentleman in Berleben. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Febron had one tooth; which was black and crooked from his bottom jaw, cracked lips, a wandering left eye, a balding head and jaundiced skin. By appearance, he looked to have been kicked by a horse a few times, have lived a rough life, and not taken care of himself.

Febron was unpleasant in some manner to every member of the Mighty Nein. His main personality traits seemed to be cowardice, greed, and lecherousness. He had a habit of flirting with his travelling companions, even at the worst of times. He found necromancy scary enough to back away from the Mighty Nein when they were being stalked by a troll.

The Mighty Nein met with Febron in the Keystone Pub under the instruction of The Gentleman. He was passed out drunk, but perked up when the Nein mentioned the Gentleman, only to say that he wanted nothing to do with it. He explained to the group that his job was to meet people, lead them to the safe house, and then escort them back out. However, the last time he returned there, he heard howling and saw corpses strung up outside as a warning and fled. The Nein gave him 100 gp and a drink, which successfully convinced him to escort the Nein there. They made the mistake of paying him on the spot, and realized he could leave without them, so they told him he had to sleep with one of them. He chose Yasha. Yasha shoved the bed across the door and refused to sleep in it, letting Febron take it for himself.
